title: Forum-topic draft files in general view, not the topic: set top_msg_id
design:
ROOT CAUSE (live-confirmed in kb-ru55.6 dogfood, 2026-06-12, via two coexisting server drafts + CASS of yesterday's working method):

draft.py _place_draft places forum-topic drafts via `await draft.set_message(text=message, reply_to=topic_id)`. Telethon's Draft.set_message (telethon/tl/custom/draft.py) builds `types.InputReplyToMessage(reply_to)` — passing ONLY reply_to_msg_id, leaving top_msg_id=None. There is NO way to set top_msg_id through Draft.set_message.

top_msg_id is part of a forum draft's THREAD IDENTITY. Proven live: placing the SAME text to Sober Events (chat -1002287767683) topic 891 with top_msg_id=None vs top_msg_id=891 produced TWO COEXISTING distinct server drafts (GetAllDraftsRequest showed both). So reply_to_msg_id=891 + top_msg_id=None files the draft as 'a reply to msg 891 in the forum GENERAL view', NOT as a draft IN topic 891. Yesterday's PROVEN-working forum method (CASS session 1a782a84) used InputReplyToMessage(reply_to_msg_id=tid, top_msg_id=tid) — both set. The test docstring at tests/test_telegram_distribute.py:29-30 already documented this intent ('set reply_to_msg_id=top_msg_id and top_msg_id=top_msg_id') — the implementation diverged from its own design.

FIX: for forum topics (topic_id is not None), bypass Draft.set_message (cannot set top_msg_id) and call SaveDraftRequest directly:
  from telethon.tl.functions.messages import SaveDraftRequest
  from telethon.tl.types import InputReplyToMessage
  peer = await client.get_input_entity(chat_id_int)
  await client(SaveDraftRequest(peer=peer, message=message,
      reply_to=InputReplyToMessage(reply_to_msg_id=topic_id, top_msg_id=topic_id)))
Plain-group path (topic_id is None) stays draft.set_message(text=message). The getDraft-before (D2 skip-pre-existing) stays. 

FIREWALL: AST firewall (test_telegram_distribute.py TestASTFirewall) forbids {send_message,send_file,send_photo,send_document,send} — SaveDraftRequest is ALLOWED. Verify the AST test still passes after the change.

## canonical_refs
- ADR-018 D2 (FIRM draft-only firewall — must hold), D1 (forum-topic delivery)
- ADR-008 D3 (fail loud)

## Harness target
Signal: a fresh independent Telethon connection reads back the forum-topic draft via GetAllDraftsRequest and its InputReplyToMessage has BOTH reply_to_msg_id==topic_id AND top_msg_id==topic_id; AST firewall test green; live: the draft surfaces inside the topic in a real client (Telegram Web /k or user desktop), not the general view.
Expected green: top_msg_id==topic_id on the persisted draft; tests pass incl TestASTFirewall; distribute returns placed.
Rationale: top_msg_id is the thread-identity field that files the draft into the topic vs general view (proven by two coexisting drafts).
Invalidation: if a real client shows the draft in the forum GENERAL view rather than the topic after the fix, the targeting is still wrong.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Forum-topic distribute sets BOTH reply_to_msg_id=topic_id AND top_msg_id=topic_id on the persisted draft (verified via independent GetAllDraftsRequest read-back). 2. Plain-group placement unchanged (reply_to=None). 3. AST firewall test (TestASTFirewall) still green — no send_message/send path introduced. 4. getDraft skip-pre-existing-draft behavior unchanged. 5. Live-verified: the forum-topic draft surfaces INSIDE the topic in a real client, not the forum general view.
close_reason: Forum draft placement corrected to forum-LEVEL (reply_to=None). Live dogfood proved top_msg_id-pinned drafts are server-correct (ForumTopic.draft) but INVISIBLE on Telegram Desktop; forum-level drafts ARE visible. Group + forum drafts both confirmed visible in user's Desktop. Firewall (TestASTFirewall) intact; switch-cli 91 green; committed b1014a1. ADR-018 D1 corrected (8169823). True topic-pinning deferred to kb-ru55.9.

title: Fix telegram connect: fresh-session QR login hangs on phone input; add QR render + refresh
design:
ROOT CAUSE (demonstrated live during kb-ru55.6 dogfood, 2026-06-12): tools/switch-cli/src/switch_cli/telegram/session.py qr_connect() uses `async with TelegramClient(StringSession(), ...) as client:`. Telethon's __aenter__ (telethon/client/auth.py:668) calls self.start(); start() (auth.py:20) defaults phone= input('Please enter your phone...'). On a FRESH/empty StringSession, _start() finds get_me() is None (not authorized), so it falls through to blocking on input() for a phone number BEFORE qr_login() is ever reached. Proof: `switch-cli telegram connect </dev/null` prints 'Please enter your phone (or bot token):' then 'Aborted!' (EOFError) — never renders a QR. So production connect does PHONE login (interactive), not QR, on first use. The unit test's MagicMock client never runs the real start(), hiding this (the permissive-mock-hides-real-Telethon-API class — see bd memories mocked-dep-tests-blind-to-major-version-api-breaks / the qr.login lesson).

FIX (3 parts, all needed for QR connect to actually work for a human):
D1 (correctness): in qr_connect, replace `async with TelegramClient(...)` with explicit `await client.connect()` ... `finally: await client.disconnect()`. connect() does NOT call start(), so qr_login() is reached without any phone prompt. (reuse_session's async-with is fine — an authorized session makes start() return early — leave it per ADR-008 D2.)
D2 (usability): render qr.url as a scannable terminal QR to stderr (a bare tg://login URL cannot be scanned). Use segno (pure-python, zero extra system deps): `segno.make(qr.url).terminal()` to stderr. Keep printing the URL too. Add segno to tools/switch-cli/pyproject.toml deps.
D3 (usability): wrap qr.wait(timeout=N) in a refresh loop — on asyncio.TimeoutError call qr.recreate(), re-render, retry; bounded (~6 cycles ≈ a humane multi-minute window). After the final cycle, raise QRLoginTimeoutError (preserve ADR-008 D3 fail-loud). Telethon QRLogin.recreate()/expires confirmed in telethon/tl/custom/qrlogin.py.

FIRM constraints preserved: StringSession NEVER uploaded (ADR-018 D4/D2); fail loud on final timeout (ADR-008 D3).

TESTS (de-blind the mock — the current mock is structurally blind to this bug):
- Fresh-login path: assert the code uses client.connect() and NEVER calls client.start() (the prompt source). A truthful mock should make a start()-invocation detectable/failing.
- Refresh: on a wait() that times out once then succeeds, assert qr.recreate() was called and login completes.
- Render: assert the QR renderer is called with qr.url.
- Keep the existing AST no-HTTP-import / session-never-uploaded firewall test.
acceptance_criteria: `switch-cli telegram connect` on a machine with NO existing session reaches the QR-login flow WITHOUT prompting for a phone number, renders a scannable QR to the terminal, refreshes the QR on expiry, and on a real scan persists the StringSession locally (never uploaded). Re-running connect with a session present still reuses it (reused:true). Unit tests exercise the connect()-not-start() fresh path, the recreate refresh loop, and QR rendering — with a mock that would FAIL if start()/phone-input were reintroduced. Live-proven in kb-ru55.6.
notes:
## Origin
Discovered-from kb-ru55.6 (live dogfood) on 2026-06-12 (ADR-008 D4). Pre-fix HEAD captured by orchestrator. Blocks parent kb-ru55 acceptance (a) via the production command.
close_reason: Connect QR login + session reuse live-proven in kb-ru55.6 dogfood: QR scan -> connected; CLI restart -> reused:true. Committed 38b9f8f.

title: AgeGateMiddleware blocks social link-preview crawlers (Telegram/Twitter/FB/etc) → OG cards show age-gate page, not event
description:
AgeGateMiddleware (accounts/middleware.py:104-135) redirects any text/html request without an age_gate cookie to /age-check/ unless the UA matches BOT_AGENTS. BOT_AGENTS contains ONLY search engines (googlebot, bingbot, slurp, duckduckbot, baiduspider, yandexbot). Social link-preview crawlers — telegrambot, twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, whatsapp, slackbot, discordbot, linkedinbot, redditbot, etc. — are NOT in the list, so they get 302'd to /age-check/ and scrape the age-check interstitial's tags (title 'Age Verification — Switch Berlin', _base.html default meta description) instead of the event's OG card.

IMPACT: Defeats kb-6d7o entirely AND breaks OG link previews on EVERY social platform we syndicate to. The syndication growth loop (ADR-010, ADR-016) renders no usable card anywhere. Confirmed live on prod 2026-06-12: curl -A 'TelegramBot (like TwitterBot)' -H 'Accept: text/html' <event-url> => HTTP 302 location:/age-check/. Discovered by driving real Telegram web via browser-automation; curl-based checks gave a FALSE GREEN because curl's default Accept:*/* never contains text/html so it dodged the gate.

LEGAL: expanding the bypass list touches the JuSchG age gate (ADR-002/ADR-006). Search engines already bypass (same curated OG card is already public via Google); real human users (Accept:text/html browsers) still hit the gate. Posture decision pending user sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Telegram crawler (UA 'TelegramBot (like TwitterBot)', Accept: text/html) fetching a published event URL receives the EVENT's OG tags (og:title=event title, og:image=card image), NOT a 302 to /age-check/. (b) Same for twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, whatsapp, slackbot, discordbot, linkedinbot. (c) Real human browser (Accept: text/html, no age_gate cookie, non-bot UA) STILL gets 302 to /age-check/ — age gate intact for users. (d) Verified live on prod by driving real Telegram web: a never-before-cached event URL renders the correct event card. (e) Unit test in accounts covering both the bypass (social UA -> 200 event page) and the preserved gate (browser UA -> 302).
close_reason: Fixed: extended AgeGateMiddleware.BOT_AGENTS to include social link-preview crawlers (telegram/twitter/facebook/whatsapp/slack/discord/linkedin/reddit/pinterest/applebot/etc). Verified live on prod 2026-06-12 by driving real Telegram web via browser-automation: (1) curl -A TelegramBot -H 'Accept: text/html' now returns 200 + event og:title (was 302 to /age-check/); (2) fresh ?v= URL in real Telegram renders the correct event card — title 'Telegram Card', description 'Testing event card in Telegram', og:image present (1200x630 default). Cache-bust confirmed: distinct ?v= forces Telegram refetch (param not stripped). Commit f3e0f7e. 2 accounts tests (social bypass + human-still-gated, both with Accept:text/html). User approved the JuSchG-gate posture (social crawlers read curated OG meta, same as search engines; humans still gated).

title: Make channel sync live-follow the master (share content row) instead of one-time snapshot
design:
Composer dogfooding round 5 — owner decision 2026-06-09 (live-follow + edit-to-customize). ADR-016 D2 re-resolved: sync mechanism (c) snapshot to (a) live-share (see the 2026-06-09 paragraph in docs/decisions/ADR-016-*.md).

PROBLEM. Editing the master propagates only to channels that SHARE the master canonical ContentVersion row. A channel set up via the composer sync dropdown (sync_projection_from to copy_from at syndication/services.py:996-1030) gets its OWN independent copied CV — a one-time SNAPSHOT — so it does NOT follow later master edits. Symptom the owner hit twice: editing a post master updates the FetLife channel (shares canonical) but NOT the Telegram channel (own snapshot CV) and editing an event canonical does not update the synced FetLife channel at all.

CHANGE. sync_projection_from must make the target SHARE the source projection current content_version row (set target.content_version = source.content_version, NO copy_from), keeping the sync_source FK for provenance, the toggle label, and the cycle guard. Then a master edit broadcasts to all sharers via the existing single-row write-once-broadcast plus the kb-ciqf live-OOB sibling re-render (already shipped). Divergence is preserved by detach-on-edit, NOT snapshot: editing a synced channel forks it to its own independent CV and clears sync_source (the existing customize/detach op at projection_detach_and_edit / detach_and_edit). Re-sync re-shares the source current row (discarding the channel own edits), still gated by the discard-confirm (ADR-008 D3).

LABEL. The sync-bar copy for a synced (sync_source set) channel must now say it FOLLOWS the source. This REVERSES the kb-nexw.3 relabel that said Copied from X snapshot won't follow later edits (templates/syndication/fragments/_sync_bar.html). It was honest about mechanism (c) and is wrong under (a). Update tests asserting that wording (syndication/tests/test_sync_badge_fixes.py).

CYCLE GUARD. Keep the rule that a legal sync source is one whose own sync_source IS NULL (syndication/services.py:1016).

WATCH. The snapshot tests in syndication/test_sync_mechanism.py assert sync mints an independent CV and that source edits do NOT propagate — these flip: sync now shares the row, source edits DO propagate. Confirm detach-on-edit still forks a NEW CV (does not mutate the shared row) so divergence works. Confirm the event canonical body-strip guard (kb-ciqf, views.py:1845) is unaffected. Relevant memories: htmx-swap-none-discards-returned-fragment-oob-only, optimistic-ui-flip-lies-under-shared-row-broadcast, ui-label-names-mechanism-not-implemented (the label must now name the live mechanism), inline-copy-of-shared-partial-drifts, django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Syncing a channel from a source via the composer (sync_projection_from) makes the target SHARE the source content_version row (assert target.content_version_id == source.content_version_id), not a new copy. 2. After a master/source edit, EVERY synced channel follows — a post with two synced channels (e.g. FetLife and Telegram) BOTH reflect the new master content at the data layer AND get a live OOB update (no reload), and still show it after reload. 3. Same for an event: editing the canonical (Switch listing EventForm) propagates to a synced FetLife listing channel live and on reload. 4. Editing a specific synced channel detaches it (forks its own CV, clears sync_source), keeps its custom text, stops following — while other still-synced channels keep following the master. 5. Re-syncing re-binds the channel to the source (discard-confirm retained) and it follows again. 6. The sync-bar label for a synced channel says it FOLLOWS the source. No Copied from or won't follow later edits wording remains for the synced state. 7. Cycle guard preserved (cannot sync from a channel whose own sync_source is set). 8. Full syndication suite green via uv run pytest, content assertions not context-only, plus ruff and djlint clean for changed files. 9. Tests that previously asserted snapshot/non-propagation semantics are updated to assert live-follow.
close_reason: Channel sync now live-follows the master (shares the source content row) instead of one-time snapshot. ADR-016 D2 re-resolved (mechanism c->a). Deployed to prod (commit 163d6c7) and validated live on switch.berlin: multi-channel propagation live+reload, label persists after master edit, edit-to-customize detaches cleanly without corrupting master/siblings, reset-to-synced re-links and follows, no snapshot wording. Local validation exercised the explicit sync-from-peer 'Synced from X follows live' state. Caveat handed to user: pre-existing already-diverged channels need a one-time Reset-to-synced to start following (fix changes sync behavior going forward, does not retroactively re-link old snapshots). Syndication suite 1104 green.

title: Composer: master edits do not propagate live to synced channels, and event-master edit freezes the canonical
design:
Dogfooding round 5. Product owner reports two symptoms. (A) editing a POST master, synced channels do not update on autosave, only after a full browser refresh. (B) editing an EVENT master, dependent channels do not update at all, not even on refresh.

UNIFIED ROOT CAUSE (live-confirmed by two fresh-context debugger passes). Engine rule _render_draft_body at syndication/engine.py:445-456 reads: if cv.body is not None return cv.body, else recompose from source Event or Post. Track-live means canonical CV body is NULL (recomposes, follows master). Any non-null body on the CV freezes recomposition.

Bug A (POST) is a pure UI-DELIVERY gap. Data propagates fine because synced channels share one canonical CV row. But the autosave form posts hx-swap=none (the focus-preserving debounced autosave in _channel_editor.html), so HTMX discards the server response. version_edit at syndication/views.py:1768-1843 emits hx-swap-oob ONLY for the per-projection sync_bar badge plus dirty banner, never the sibling channel BODY textareas, so siblings never re-render until a full reload rebuilds the page. Post canonical.body equals the live post body so reload always shows new content, masking any freeze.

Bug B (EVENT) is the same UI-delivery gap for track-live channels PLUS a freeze bug. Editing the event master writes a non-null body onto the shared canonical CV (provenance=manual, observed on demo Event 10 canonical CV pk=1). From that moment _render_draft_body short-circuits and never recomposes from the live Event, so dependent channels freeze to the snapshot and never follow further master edits, reload included. Confirm which edit verb writes canonical.body for events (edit_version at services.py:1137, or event_hub_edit, or detach_and_edit) and whether the intended model is that event master edits write Event MODEL FIELDS and keep canonical NULL recomposing (track-live preserved). Default creation IS track-live for both events and posts (services.py _ensure_canonical_content_version seeds body NULL). Detachment is supposed to be a deliberate per-channel user action per ADR-016 D2 intended divergence, NOT a side effect of editing the master.

FIX part 1 (post and event). Emit hx-swap-oob re-rendered sibling channel body fragments from the autosave handlers (version_edit views.py:1768-1843, event_hub_edit views.py:342-414, projection_detach_and_edit views.py:1568-1616) for every OTHER projection sharing the edited CV. Needs a stable per-projection textarea or wrapper id in _channel_editor.html. MUST NOT clobber the textarea the user is actively typing in (skip the edited projection or guard on focus). Mirror the per-row try-except containment at views.py:1807-1829 so a corrupt sibling cannot abort the active edit (ADR-008 D3).

FIX part 2 (event). Stop the event-master edit from freezing the canonical. Keep canonical track-live (recompose) so master edits keep propagating. Restores the intended ADR-016 D2 model.

PRESERVE. A deliberately-customized or detached channel still must NOT be overwritten by master edits (ADR-016 D2). The re-sync discard-confirm path is unchanged.

ADR-016 D2 (per-platform projections, track-live semantics) is the upstream ref. This restores its intended behavior, so treat freeze-on-master-edit as a bug not a decision. If implementation reveals the freeze was intentional, RAISE.

Relevant memories. htmx-swap-none-discards-returned-fragment-oob-only. inline-copy-of-shared-partial-drifts (event composer event_syndication.html carries an inline twin of _channel_editor.html, fix both sites or DRY). optimistic-ui-flip-lies-under-shared-row-broadcast (drive indicators from server response). django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow (assert on response.content not context).
acceptance_criteria: 1. LIVE BROWSER. editing a post master or source content updates every synced sibling channel editor WITHOUT a reload (OOB swap), verified by watching the sibling textarea change. 2. LIVE BROWSER. editing an event master updates every track-live dependent channel both live (no reload) and on reload, and a SECOND master edit also propagates (canonical stays recompose-live, not frozen). 3. A deliberately-customized or detached channel is NOT overwritten by master edits (regression preserved). 4. The actively-edited textarea is never clobbered by its own OOB update (cursor and focus preserved). 5. Syndication test suite green via uv run pytest (content assertions not context-only) plus ruff and djlint clean for changed files. 6. Live-browser validation evidence captured for BOTH a post and an event (the previously-failing flows).
close_reason: Fixed both composer propagation bugs and validated live in browser (4/4). Post + event master edits now propagate to track-live synced channels live (OOB sibling re-render); event-master edit no longer freezes the canonical (second edit still propagates, survives reload). Detached channels preserved. Committed 5d3d57d. Syndication suite 1091 green; ruff/djlint/migrations clean.

title: Emit OOB dirty-banner + Re-publish CTA when editing the canonical of a published Switch listing
design:
Root cause confirmed by fresh-context debugger. Editing a published Switch listing channel goes through the EventForm autosave path event_hub_edit (syndication/views.py ~292-342). Its HTMX branch returns a full fragment_event_syndication (line ~341), but the EventForm autosave form posts with hx-swap=none (templates/syndication/fragments/_channel_editor.html:152), so HTMX discards the entire response body. The server DOES correctly compute the dirty state (models.py is_dirty ~557-574 flips True after the live canonical edit) and the Re-publish CTA, but they never reach the DOM because no hx-swap-oob elements are emitted. Net. the published listing looks frozen-unchanged with no Re-publish affordance.

The body-form paths already do this right. projection_detach_and_edit (views.py ~1498-1546) and version_edit (views.py ~1684-1759) emit hx-swap-oob fragments for #channel-dirty-<pk> and #channel-cta-<pk>.

Fix. In event_hub_edit after update_event succeeds, for each listing projection of this event that is published with non-null frozen_content, recompute is_dirty (gated through edit_after_publish_policy(platform) as elsewhere) + can_publish, render _sync_bar.html and _channel_dirty_oob.html with oob=True, and return a concatenated HttpResponse (mirror views.py ~1546) instead of the discarded full fragment. Use the per-row try/except ValueError continue containment (views.py ~1737-1759) so a corrupt sibling does not abort the active edit. render_projection already returns frozen_content for published (engine.py ~478-489, correct) and that must stay locked. published content is immutable per ADR-008 D3.

Scope. Event listing (Switch EventForm card, gated platform==switch at template) ONLY. post/promotion + FetLife-listing use the textarea body-form path which already emits OOB.

canonical_refs. ADR-016 D2/D5 (edit-after-publish dirty marker, frozen_content immutability), ADR-008 D3 (what is out never changes silently).
acceptance_criteria: A view-level test. an HTMX POST to syndication:event-edit for a PUBLISHED Switch listing on the canonical version with a changed field returns a response body containing hx-swap-oob fragments for #channel-dirty-<pk> (dirty banner) AND #channel-cta-<pk> (Re-publish CTA). A second assertion locks that the published channel render returns frozen_content, not the live canonical (engine render path immutability). Verified live. publish a Switch listing channel, edit the canonical title, the orange dirty banner + Re-publish CTA appear without a reload.
notes:
## Harness target
Signal: uv run pytest syndication/ -k 'event_hub_edit or published_dirty_oob'. Expected green: new view test asserts the two OOB fragments present in the event-edit response for a published Switch listing + frozen_content immutability. Rationale: prior edit-after-publish tests asserted service-layer is_dirty/republish and the body-form view paths, never the EventForm autosave HTTP payload under hx-swap=none. Invalidation: if a future per-platform edit_after_publish policy disables editing published Switch listings outright, this OOB path changes shape.
## Scoping-review fold
The view-level test belongs in syndication/tests/test_published_edit_loop.py. its header (~line 17) already lists the 'event_hub_edit on a published Switch listing makes it dirty' case but the body never implements it (only the projection-detach-and-edit path is covered). The implementer adds that case here. Serial-walk note. kb-nexw.2 and kb-nexw.3 may both edit templates/syndication/fragments/_channel_editor.html, so they are walked serially (2 before 3).
close_reason: Fixed in d5c2069. event_hub_edit HTMX branch now emits hx-swap-oob _sync_bar + _channel_dirty_oob fragments for each published listing projection (mirrors version_edit ~1684-1773, per-row ValueError containment), so the dirty banner + Re-publish CTA survive hx-swap=none instead of being discarded. Falls back to full fragment when no published projections. New tests in test_published_edit_loop.py assert both OOB fragments present in the event-edit response AND lock published render == frozen_content (ADR-008 D3 immutability). Implementer self-caught a too-loose test (id-only) and tightened to require hx-swap-oob=true (RED→GREEN). Diff verified against HEAD: also relocated _views_logger to module top (minor harmless cleanup, suite green). Live OOB-swap behavior to be confirmed in final browser verification.

title: reset-to-canonical must clear sync_source so a peer-synced channel returns to master
design:
Root cause confirmed by browser recon + source read. reset_to_canonical (syndication/services.py ~1070) repoints projection.content_version to the canonical ContentVersion (lines ~1126-1127) but NEVER clears projection.sync_source. The sync bar template (templates/syndication/fragments/_sync_bar.html:63) renders 'Synced from <peer>' whenever proj.sync_source is set (the elif proj.sync_source branch), so after pressing Reset or Master-copy the channel is stuck in the peer-synced render state no matter how many times it is pressed. detach_and_edit (services.py ~1272-1275) shows the correct pattern. it calls detach_sync_source(projection).

Fix. In reset_to_canonical, clear the peer pointer as part of the same op (if projection.sync_source_id is not None then detach_sync_source(projection), or set sync_source None directly) so the projection lands in the ADR-016 D2 canonical state. content_version == canonical AND sync_source IS NULL renders as 'synced from canonical / Master'. This is the owner exact complaint (accidentally peer-synced a channel, could not return it to master). Recon confirmed the control exists in the UI but no-ops on the event surface.

canonical_refs. ADR-016 D2 (three-state sync machine, sync_source pointer).
acceptance_criteria: After reset_to_canonical (and its Reset / Master-copy UI entry points), the projection lands in ADR-016 D2 state (i) 'synced from canonical'. content_version == the canonical version AND sync_source IS NULL. It must NOT be left in the invalid intermediate of canonical-CV-with-non-null-sync_source (the three-state machine in models.py has no such state). A new test asserts BOTH that content_version repoints to canonical AND that sync_source is None after reset (existing test_projection_board.py ~1866 only asserts content_version, which is why this regressed). _sync_bar renders the canonical/Master state, not 'Synced from peer'. Verified live in browser on the event surface (the failing case).
notes:
## Harness target
Signal: uv run pytest syndication/ -k reset_to_canonical (new + existing). Expected green: new test asserting sync_source cleared after reset passes, plus a render assertion that _sync_bar shows canonical state. Rationale: the regression slipped because tests only checked content_version, not sync_source. Invalidation: if reset is meant to preserve peer-sync (it is not, per ADR-016 D2), this flips.
close_reason: Fixed in fdd0672. reset_to_canonical now calls detach_sync_source when sync_source_id is set, landing the projection in ADR-016 D2 state (i) (canonical-CV + sync_source NULL). detach_sync_source persists sync_source=None in its own save (services.py:1050); new test test_reset_to_canonical_clears_sync_source refresh_from_db's and asserts both invariants + precondition (RED before fix on assertion b, GREEN after). Diff verified against HEAD, not self-report. Scoping-review root-confirmed.

title: Composer dogfooding round 4 — sync-reset no-op, published-freeze leak, sync labeling, tab persistence
description:
Fourth dogfooding round on the syndication composer. A browser e2e recon round reproduced the owner reported findings and swept for more. Findings that became work (autosave was NOT reproduced, and the live-sync finding resolved as working-as-designed):

P1 reset-to-canonical no-ops on peer-synced channels. reset_to_canonical() repoints content_version but never clears sync_source, so the 'Synced from peer' banner sticks and the channel cannot be returned to master. This is the owner exact complaint.

P1 published-channel freeze leak. Editing the canonical leaks live into an already-published event listing channel with no dirty/needs-republish marker (suspected ADR-016 D2/D5 plus ADR-008 D3 freeze violation, root-cause confirm dispatched).

P2 sync-state labeling overstates. The 'editing here updates all these channels' banner does not distinguish canonical-synced (live) from peer-snapshot from published-frozen. This is the actual source of the owner 'live sync does not work' confusion.

P2 active channel tab not persisted across full page reload (Alpine client-state only).

Method. Pre-decomposed punch list from recon, one child bead per finding, scoping adversarial-review of the set, serial implementers (TDD), per-bead review, parent re-verify, final browser validation.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads closed. The three behavioral findings (reset no-op, published-freeze leak, tab persistence) are fixed and verified in a live browser by a fresh subagent. Sync-state labeling is honest per channel state. No ADR-016 or ADR-008 freeze contract silently contradicted. Full syndication test suite green and lint green.
close_reason: Composer dogfooding round 4 shipped. All 4 children closed + confirmed live (4/4 browser PASS): reset returns peer-synced channel to master (kb-nexw.1, fdd0672); editing canonical of a published Switch listing now surfaces dirty + Re-publish CTA via OOB without reload, frozen content preserved (kb-nexw.2, d5c2069); sync badge relabeled 'Synced from'→'Copied from … snapshot, won't follow later edits' (kb-nexw.3, f407a0c); active tab persists across reload via ?channel URL param with stale-pk fallback (kb-nexw.4, 14777b0). Recon resolved the owner's other two reports without code change: autosave NOT-reproduced; 'live sync broken' was working-as-designed (mislabel was the real bug, fixed in .3). Parent re-verify coherent (ADR-008 D3 freeze intact); docstring drift fixed (3e18084); 2 cosmetic residuals filed kb-86ni; deferred coverage filed kb-s5xb. Full syndication suite 1077 green at last code change, ruff+djlint green. /compound folded 2 new anti-pattern memories + inline-twin location update + harness.md Templates entry.

title: Bump Django 6.0.5 → 6.0.6 — clears 5 security CVEs (pip-audit red on main)
design: pip-audit (Tests workflow security job) went red on main 2026-06-06 with 5 known vulnerabilities in Django 6.0.5: PYSEC-2026-197, -198, -199, -200, -201 — all fixed in 6.0.6 (and the 5.2.15 LTS line). Newly-published Django security release; unrelated to the kb-kgza composer wave (which touched no dependencies). The deploy gate (deploy.yml) is GREEN and prod is live on 6.0.5 — the security job is a separate workflow that does not block deploy, so this is a CI-red + live-prod-on-vulnerable-Django situation, not a deploy blocker. Fix: uv bump Django to 6.0.6 (patch release, low behavioral risk), run full suite + check --deploy, re-run pip-audit to confirm clean, redeploy. Look up the 5 PYSEC advisories to confirm none needs a settings/code change beyond the version bump (patch releases occasionally add a security setting). Same pattern as the prior aiohttp/authlib CVE bump (commit 69680f6). canonical_refs: ADR-008. Memory: mocked-dep-tests-blind-to-major-version-api-breaks (patch bump is low-risk but the ingestion tests mock at boundaries — sanity-check anything Django-version-sensitive).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Django pinned at 6.0.6 (uv.lock + pyproject). 2. pip-audit clean (0 known vulnerabilities). 3. Full suite + ruff + djlint + manage.py check --deploy green. 4. The 5 PYSEC advisories reviewed; any required settings/code change applied or explicitly noted as N/A. 5. Pushed + deploy green + prod confirmed on 6.0.6.
close_reason: Django 6.0.5→6.0.6 shipped (commit 3f6c49a). pip-audit clean (security CI job now green, was red on main); full Tests suite green; deploy succeeded, prod rebuilt from 6.0.6 lock with check --deploy green on prod. All 5 PYSEC/CVE advisories reviewed — version bump fully remediates, no app-side change required (both optional hardening opt-ins N/A: no signed-cookie-with-salt usage, no manual Cache-Control). adversarial-review: trivial mechanical patch bump w/ green harness + fresh-context advisory review — recorded noticing in lieu of full review pass.

title: Post-composer master form has the same document-scoped autosave over-broadcast kb-kgza.12 fixed
design: Discovered at kb-kgza.8 parent re-verify (2026-06-06). kb-kgza.12 form-scoped the autosave triggers in _channel_editor.html (:152, :279) but bounded itself to that file and MISSED the post-composer Master-copy body form at templates/syndication/fragments/post_syndication.html:239, which still carries hx-trigger='input changed delay:600ms from:textarea[name='body']'. Same document-scoped over-broadcast + data-loss class as kb-kgza.12 (HTMX from: is document-wide; all channel tabs render into the DOM at once, so typing in any channel body also fires the post Master form's version-edit). Grep confirms this is the LAST remaining document-scoped from: selector in templates/syndication/. Fix: identical to kb-kgza.12 — drop the from: so the trigger is form-local. Extend the kb-kgza.12 guard test to assert NO document-scoped from: selector remains across the whole templates/syndication/ dir (not just _channel_editor.html), so the class cannot reappear in any composer template. canonical_refs: ADR-008 D3, ADR-016 D2. discovered-from: kb-kgza.8 / kb-kgza.12.
acceptance_criteria: 1. post_syndication.html:239 autosave trigger is form-local (no document-scoped from:). 2. The guard test asserts no document-scoped from: selector in ANY templates/syndication/ template, path derived from BASE_DIR. 3. Full syndication suite + ruff + djlint green.
close_reason: Commit 9b4cdf3. Form-scoped the post-composer Master-copy autosave trigger (post_syndication.html:239) — the document-scoped from: selector kb-kgza.12 missed. Replaced the per-file guard with a directory-level canary scanning all templates/syndication/ for document-scoped from: in hx-trigger; canary green proves no such selector remains anywhere. 1051 tests + ruff + djlint green. Trivial mechanical fix identical to kb-kgza.12 (form wrapping textarea), context-aligned — driven directly, no implementer dispatch.

title: Per-channel autosave loses typed edits + over-broadcasts (document-scoped HTMX from: triggers)
design:
ROOT CONFIRMED via fresh-context debugger live repro 2026-06-06 (was: hypothesis). The autosave fires on document-scoped HTMX `from:` selectors, which is BOTH the over-broadcast root AND the data-loss root.

THE WIRING (verified live): the composer renders every channel tab into the DOM at once; three autosave forms coexist — the Switch event-edit form (`_channel_editor.html:152`, trigger `input changed delay:600ms from:input, ... from:textarea, ... from:select`) and one per-channel body form each (`_channel_editor.html:279`, trigger `from:textarea[name='body']`). HTMX evaluates `from:<selector>` against the WHOLE document, not the local form. So one keystroke in ONE channel body fires every channel's `projections/<pk>/detach-and-edit/` endpoint PLUS the canonical `events/<pk>/edit/` form, concurrently (observed: events/10/edit + projections/1 + projections/5 all fire per keystroke-batch).

WHY THAT LOSES DATA (S1): on a channel still sharing the canonical ContentVersion, the racing `detach_and_edit` mints a NEW ContentVersion and repoints the FK mid-request (services.py customize ~1264-1267, with refresh_from_db) while the concurrently-fired `events/<pk>/edit` POST writes the OLD canonical CV. Racing writes across a CV being detached underneath them drop in-flight content. A single isolated direct POST has no competitor and no mid-flight repoint — which is exactly why a direct POST persists fine but live typing doesn't.

FIX (template-only): form-scope the two triggers at `_channel_editor.html:152` and `:279` — drop the document-scoped `from:` and let each trigger bind to the form/element it is declared on, so each form autosaves only its own input. After the fix, one keystroke in a channel body must fire exactly ONE endpoint (that channel's), never the siblings or the canonical event-edit.

BOUNDARY: this bead is template-only (the two hx-trigger attrs at :152 and :279). The former S3 stale-duplicate-content-box symptom is MOVED to kb-kgza.10 — the debugger confirmed it shares the incomplete-OOB-swap root with .10's hidden-CTA fix and must be fixed there, together. Do NOT "fix" data loss by re-rendering the active textarea on autosave (the OOB-only `hx-swap=none` response is correct); re-rendering the focused textarea is what would reintroduce the loss.

ENTANGLEMENT: kb-kgza.10 depends on this landing first — once autosave fires only the edited channel, .10's OOB additions are testable without over-broadcast noise. Both touch `_channel_editor.html` but DIFFERENT regions (this = trigger attrs :152/:279; .10 = preview :370-378, CTA :431-511, OOB fragment).

## Harness target
Signal: live browser (demo@switch.berlin) — type a marker into one channel body; (a) exactly one autosave endpoint fires (network panel), (b) the marker persists across reload. PLUS a content/template test asserting no document-scoped `from:` selector remains for the body autosave in `_channel_editor.html`. PLUS full syndication suite green.
Expected green: one-keystroke→one-endpoint, edits persist, template guard passes, suite green.
Rationale: the data loss is invisible to the test suite (a single test POST has no race); only live multi-form repro + a structural template assertion catch it.
Invalidation: if a future change reintroduces a cross-form `from:` selector or starts re-rendering the focused textarea on autosave, edits will drop again — the template guard is the canary.

canonical_refs: ADR-008 D3 (no silent data loss / fail loud), ADR-016 D2 (a per-channel edit detaches the EDITED channel only). Memory: optimistic-ui-flip-lies-under-shared-row-broadcast.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Live (demo@switch.berlin): typing into one channel body fires exactly one autosave endpoint (that channel's detach-and-edit) — NOT events/<pk>/edit and NOT sibling channels. 2. A marker typed into a channel body persists across a page reload. 3. A template/content test asserts no document-scoped from: selector remains for the body autosave in _channel_editor.html. 4. Full syndication suite green; ruff and djlint clean.

title: Fix: sync-source picker stays on current tab on Apply, and offers Master copy as a source
design:
Two fixes in the same 4x-duplicated copy-from/sync-picker block. FIRST extract it to a shared include templates/syndication/fragments/_sync_picker.html (parameterized by fragment_target) to kill the inline-twin drift (memory inline-copy-of-shared-partial-drifts). (1) Apply jumps to canonical tab: the source_projection_pk copy-from forms (event_syndication.html ~544, post_syndication.html ~411) lack the hidden input name=selected_pk :value=selectedPk that every other action form carries, so version_copy_from returns a fragment with selected_pk None and Alpine falls back to the first/source tab. Add the hidden input (view already reads selected_pk). (2) Picker missing Master copy: the source select iterates projection_rows only (promotion projections), excluding the canonical master copy (a bare ContentVersion, not a projection). Per ADR-016 D2 the canonical is the DEFAULT source and must be selectable. Wire a Master copy first option that routes to RESET-TO-CANONICAL (re-share the canonical CV, state i) — NOT copy_from — so it is a tracked binding consistent with the three-state model and reuses the existing reset verb. canonical_refs: ADR-016 D2.

## Harness target
Signal: content test + browser readback.
Expected green: after a copy-from Apply with selected_pk set to a non-canonical pk, the rendered fragment initializes Alpine selectedPk to that pk (stays on the tab). The source select contains a Master copy option routing to reset-to-canonical.

Do NOT POST a non-pk into version_copy_from (it would crash on an invalid pk).
- HARNESS: add a POST test asserting that selecting Master copy actually invokes reset-to-canonical (verb call or resulting DB state — projection back to canonical CV, sync_source NULL), not only that the option renders. Presence-only is hollow.

title: Fix: published events/posts are editable and re-publish (update) works
design:
Root cause: event_syndication.html:249 and post_syndication.html:322 gate the entire editor behind status==draft, so a published projection renders read-only only. The user can never edit, never dirty, so the is_dirty-gated Re-publish CTA (event_syndication.html:693) is structurally unreachable — contradicts ADR-016 D5 edit-after-publish. Fix: loosen the gate to render the editor for draft AND published when edit_after_publish_policy(platform)==dirty_then_republish (seam at services.py:636 already exists). Published edits flow version_edit then mutate CV, is_dirty becomes True, dirty banner + Re-publish CTA light up, republish_projection (services.py:1295) re-freezes frozen_content. Thread an editable flag from the fragment view computed from the policy so the template does not inline policy. Per memory cheap-foresight-seam-shipped-dead the proving test must show a non-default policy changes behavior. DEPENDS on the auto-detach fix (published edit must detach/dirty correctly). Solo direct publish per D5 — no separate ready gate surfaced. canonical_refs: ADR-016 D5, ADR-003.

## Harness target
Signal: content test GET published composer + POST edit + POST re-publish.
Expected green: editor inputs present (not just read-only preview), is_dirty True + dirty banner + Re-publish CTA in HTML after edit, frozen_content re-materialized after re-publish.
Rationale: proves the published-edit loop is reachable, not a dead seam.
Invalidation: ADR-016 D5 lifecycle changes, or a lock policy is added for some platform.
acceptance_criteria: A published event/post composer renders EDITABLE inputs. Editing marks it dirty with a visible dirty banner + Re-publish control. Re-publishing re-freezes content and clears dirty. Editability is policy-gated through edit_after_publish_policy.
notes:
## Scoping-review fold-ins (2026-06-05)
- EDIT_VERSION GUARD: reconcile the services.py edit_version guard (raises when all consumers non-draft) with ADR-016 D5 edit-after-publish. Editing a published projection MUST be allowed — it dirties the projection, frozen_content (the published snapshot) is unchanged so there is no silent corruption. This reconciliation is the core of making published content editable. Coordinate with kb-kgza.2 (the detach-then-edit-published path hits the same guard).
- HARNESS must target the EDIT ENDPOINT introduced or changed by kb-kgza.2 for the published-edit flow (not the old version-edit), else the test exercises the wrong path and the detach never fires.
- frozen_content re-materialization is a DB-STATE assertion (ORM check that frozen_content holds the new snapshot after re-publish), not an HTML content assertion. State it as DB-state in the test.
## Adversarial-review findings — FIX REQUIRED before close (2026-06-05, commit 65a3a95 reviewed)
Review CLEARED: gate precedence is correct (can_edit and (draft or editable)), editable False for drafts (no double-trigger), Re-publish CTA wired end-to-end to republish_projection (not a dead seam), DB-state re-freeze tests genuine. Issues:

FIX 1 (real, broken affordance) — POST master/source panel editor (post_syndication.html ~220) is gated only on can_edit, NO status check. For a PUBLISHED post (all-published projections sharing the canonical CV) it renders an editable textarea that autosaves to version-edit -> edit_version WITHOUT _allow_edit_after_publish -> the all-consumers-non-draft guard raises ValueError -> caught -> returns action_error. So the user sees an editable master textarea that errors on every keystroke. Pre-existed but kb-kgza.3 makes it reachable (published editing is now invited). FIX: editing the master/source tab of a published post MUST work — it is the edit-once-broadcast-to-all-sharers update flow, which per ADR-016 D5 dirties all consumers while frozen_content (the published snapshot) stays unchanged = no corruption. Relax version_edit's guard for the edit-after-publish case (same reasoning as the detach path in kb-kgza.2) and gate the master/source panel editor with the editable flag for published. Add a test: editing the master/source tab of a published post succeeds (no action_error), all sharing consumers become is_dirty True, frozen_content unchanged. (Events are unaffected — the event canonical is the EventForm/event-edit which has no such guard.)

FIX 2 (test-coverage gap) — the old PostComposerPublishedStateGatingTest asserted Customize/Reset URLs do NOT appear for published projections. That contract is now obsolete under D5 (published projections ARE editable, so the sync controls correctly appear inside the opened editor). The replacement test does not cover this. Add an assertion documenting the now-INTENDED behavior: for a published+editable projection the sync controls (Customize for state i / Reset for state iii) DO render inside the editor. So the contract change is covered, not silent.

NOTE (no fix, V0 edge per ADR-008 D2 no-speculative-abstraction): the Re-publish CTA is gated on (is_dirty and can_publish), not on editable, so a hypothetical lock-policy projection that is already dirty would still surface Re-publish. lock policy does not exist at V0. Leave as a known edge.
close_reason: Published events/posts are now editable + re-publishable per ADR-016 D5. Editor gate loosened from status==draft to (draft OR editable), editable threaded from the view via edit_after_publish_policy. Published per-channel edits route through projection-detach-and-edit (allowed); the Re-publish CTA lights up on is_dirty and calls republish_projection to re-freeze frozen_content. Adversarial review (65a3a95) cleared gate precedence + draft path + CTA wiring + DB-state tests; its 2 findings fixed in 1ae0e34: (1) master/source published-edit no longer a broken affordance — version_edit now passes _allow_edit_after_publish when all consumers are published (symmetric with the detach path), broadcasts dirty to all sharers, frozen_content unchanged = no corruption, master panel gated with source_editable. A NEW guard keeps genuine corruption (published + null frozen_content) fail-loud per ADR-008 D3. (2) sync-controls-on-published contract documented (Customize state-i / Reset state-iii render in the editor). Events use event-edit (no guard) so unaffected. RED-then-GREEN throughout, 1008 syndication tests pass, ruff+djlint clean. Commits 65a3a95 + 1ae0e34.

title: Fix: editing a per-channel post version auto-detaches from shared canonical (not broadcast)
design:
Root cause: version_edit (views.py ~1505-1512) only detaches projections whose sync_source is set. A promotion channel SHARING the post canonical ContentVersion (state i, name=canonical, sync_source NULL) is excluded, so editing its body posts to the shared canonical CV pk and BROADCASTS to all consumers (master copy + Telegram + FetLife) instead of detaching. Event channels avoid this because the event canonical is the EventForm (event-edit), not a shared CV. Per ADR-016 D2 editing a synced/shared channel must detach to its own independent version. Fix: editing a per-channel tab (NOT the master/source tab) detaches server-side via a customize-then-edit path (add detach_and_edit in services.py, route per-channel body forms through it, threading the PROJECTION pk not just content_version.pk). The master/source tab keeps broadcasting (intended). Badge flip to Custom must be SERVER-DRIVEN via the OOB sync-bar response, NOT optimistic (memory optimistic-ui-flip-lies-under-shared-row-broadcast). The Saved indicator must fire. canonical_refs: ADR-016 D2, ADR-008 D3.

## Harness target
Signal: content + DB-state test editing a shared-canonical post channel.
Expected green: a new CV row is minted for THAT projection (detached), sibling channels bodies unchanged, the Custom badge renders, Saved indicator fires.
Rationale: broadcast-vs-detach is DB state plus render, context-hollow.
Invalidation: ADR-016 D2 sync model changes, or the master tab stops being the intended broadcast surface.
acceptance_criteria: Editing a post body on a non-canonical channel DETACHES it (mints its own version), leaves sibling channels unchanged, flips the badge to Custom (server-driven), and shows a Saved confirmation. Editing the Master-copy/Source tab still broadcasts to sharers. Same detach seam works for event and post paths.
notes:
## Scoping-review fold-ins (2026-06-05)
- ROUTING SPLIT (specify explicitly): per-channel body edits and the master/source body edit currently BOTH post to version-edit keyed by content_version.pk, so in shared-canonical state (i) the view cannot tell them apart. The per-channel body form must carry a PROJECTION-keyed route (a new endpoint, or a projection_pk param plus a dispatch branch in the view) so detach_and_edit acts on the right projection. The master/source body form stays on the canonical-CV edit and keeps broadcasting.
- DETACH DIRECTION IS NON-DESTRUCTIVE: auto-detach on edit is correct per ADR-016 D2 and is exactly what the user demanded. It needs NO confirm (it forks your own channel, canonical stays intact). The discard-confirm gate stays ONLY on the re-sync direction (reset-to-canonical), which already exists.
- DATA-INTEGRITY INTERACTION with the edit_version guard (services.py ~1161-1171, raises ValueError when ALL consumers of a CV are non-draft): after detaching a PUBLISHED per-channel projection the new CV has one published consumer, which would trip that guard and make the edit fail. Reconcile with kb-kgza.3 edit-after-publish. Editing a published projection is ALLOWED (it dirties, frozen_content is the published snapshot, no corruption). VERIFY the detach-then-edit-published path does not raise.
- HARNESS additions: also assert that editing the Master/Source tab still BROADCASTS to sharers (no detach) — a misimpl routing ALL edits through detach would pass a per-channel-only harness. Name the concrete Saved-indicator DOM element/text the test asserts (a JS event firing is not falsifiable in a content test).
- Edits the extracted _channel_editor.html (kb-kgza.9), not the big template.
## Adversarial-review findings — FIX REQUIRED before close (2026-06-05, commit 1e642ae reviewed)
Review CLEARED: template-level broadcast preservation (Switch listing routes to event-edit, post master/source tab has its own inline version-edit form separate from _channel_editor.html), guard-skip blast radius (customize always precedes the guard-skipped edit, broadcast path still guards), no optimistic flip. Three real bugs remain:

FIX A — CV CHURN (significant): detach_and_edit (services.py ~125-128) unconditionally calls customize -> copy_from -> mints a NEW ContentVersion EVERY call. Autosave fires on every 600ms input (hx-trigger in _channel_editor.html ~274), so editing an already-Custom (state iii) channel mints a new orphaned CV per keystroke-batch (a 200-word edit = 20-30 orphaned rows). The docstring's idempotence claim is FALSE. Fix: make detach_and_edit idempotent — only customize when the projection is currently on a SHARED/non-own CV (canonical or multi-consumer). If already on its own independent CV, edit IN PLACE. Add a test: a SECOND autosave on an already-detached channel mints NO new CV.

FIX B — STATE-ii INCONSISTENCY: editing a state-ii projection (own CV + sync_source SET) via detach_and_edit calls customize but never clears sync_source, leaving own-CV + sync_source-set, which ADR-016 D2 forbids (detached = own CV + sync_source NULL). version_edit explicitly calls detach_sync_source (views.py ~1591-1593) — detach_and_edit must too. Fix: clear sync_source on detach so the result is a clean state-iii. Add a test: editing a state-ii projection via projection-detach-and-edit results in sync_source NULL.

FIX C — DIRTY OOB MISSING oob=True: projection_detach_and_edit (views.py ~1465-1474) renders _channel_dirty_oob.html WITHOUT oob:True in context, so the dirty pill/banner are emitted without hx-swap-oob and do NOT update client-side on the detach path. version_edit passes oob:True (views.py ~1651-1655). This is needed by kb-kgza.3 (published-editable dirty indicator). Fix: pass oob:True. Add a test: detach-edit on a published projection emits the dirty OOB fragment with hx-swap-oob=true.

TEST GAPS to also close: a TEMPLATE-level assertion that the master/source tab form action is version-edit (broadcast) while the per-channel form is projection-detach-and-edit (the current MasterTabBroadcastStillWorksTest posts to the endpoint directly, bypassing template rendering).
close_reason: Per-channel edit now auto-detaches to an independent version (new projection-keyed endpoint projection-detach-and-edit), master/source tab keeps broadcasting (version-edit), server-driven Custom badge. Adversarial review (commit 1e642ae) cleared template broadcast preservation + guard-skip blast radius + no-optimistic-flip; its 3 found bugs fixed in 6ab36af: (A) detach_and_edit now idempotent — only mints a new CV when current CV is shared (canonical or >1 consumer), else edits in place (no per-keystroke CV churn); (B) clears sync_source on detach so state-ii edits land a clean state-iii per ADR-016 D2; (C) projection_detach_and_edit passes oob:True so the dirty pill/banner OOB-swap. Data-integrity: editing a published projection allowed via _allow_edit_after_publish (frozen_content snapshot unchanged, no corruption). RED-then-GREEN throughout, 976 syndication tests pass, ruff+djlint clean. Commits 1e642ae + 6ab36af.

title: Fix: new event-scoped promo post appears in studio rail without refresh (htmx OOB)
design:
Root cause: syndication/views.py post_create (~941-952) returns only the event_posts.html fragment on HTMX success. Unlike post_create_standalone (~1019-1033) it does not append _render_rail_oob(request), so the left studio rail is stale until manual refresh. Signal: content-assertion test POSTing post_create with HX-Request header.
Expected green: response body contains the OOB aside id=studio-rail hx-swap-oob=true including the newly created post row.

title: Dogfooding round 3 — composer sync/publish/IA fixes
description: Third dogfooding round on the syndication composer surfaced 7 observations. (1) 'Copy from' Apply button switches the active tab to the canonical/master tab even though the copy applies correctly — should stay on the current tab. (2) Editing a post's content on a non-canonical channel (FetLife) does NOT auto-detach it from the shared canonical master copy, and shows no 'saved' state — for events it does detach automatically. (3) Old/already-published events render broken — event details look gone, or visible but not editable; user expects to edit an event and re-publish (update) it on its published channels. (4) A newly-created promo post for an event does not appear in the publishables list until a manual page refresh — want an htmx-native fix (OOB swap), no hacks. (5) 'Studio' in the breadcrumb is meaningless — there is no studio homepage. (6) When choosing a sync source for a post, only FetLife is offered, not the canonical master copy — master copy should be a selectable source. (7) Publishing does nothing externally — clicking publish on a FetLife event locks/saves but nothing posts; needs alignment on adapter-integration scope (known gap: publish flow does not call adapters).
design:
IA/semantic decisions for dogfooding round 3. Most fixes implement existing ADR-016 contracts the prior composer epic drifted from (conjunction-drift class, see memory parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift).

- Issue 7 RESOLVED (user, 2026-06-05): DEFER real external publishing (adapter wiring is the kb-jgda gap, FetLife has no API). This round only makes Publish HONEST — no false success claim. Status lifecycle/frozen_content unchanged.
- Issue 2 semantic: editing a per-channel tab AUTO-DETACHES to an independent version per ADR-016 D2. The master/source tab keeps broadcasting (intended). Badge flip to Custom is SERVER-DRIVEN, not optimistic (memory optimistic-ui-flip-lies-under-shared-row-broadcast).
- Issue 6 semantic: 'sync from Master copy' maps to RESET-TO-CANONICAL (state i, shared canonical CV) — a tracked binding reusing the existing reset verb. Canonical is the DEFAULT selectable source per ADR-016 D2.
- Issue 3: published projections must be editable AND re-publishable per ADR-016 D5, editability gated through the edit_after_publish_policy seam.
- DRY posture: the copy-from/sync picker (4 inline copies), breadcrumb root, and channel editor are inline-twinned across event_syndication.html and post_syndication.html. Fixes EXTRACT to shared includes (memory inline-copy-of-shared-partial-drifts). We are past ADR-008 D2 third-caller threshold so extraction is justified, not speculative.

canonical_refs: ADR-016 D2/D4/D5, ADR-008 D2/D3, ADR-003, ADR-010 D1.
notes:
FILE-CLAIM MAP (heavy contention on the two big fragment templates — most template beads SERIALIZE):
- C2 issue4 rail-OOB: syndication/views.py post_create only (ISOLATED, parallel-safe).
- C3 issue2 detach: views.py version_edit + services.py (detach_and_edit) + channel body form projection-pk.
- C4 issue3 published-editable: channel editor gate + fragment view editable flag (DEPENDS C3).

title: Post master model: drop spurious Switch promo tab, relabel anchor, ADR-010 D1 cheap-foresight
description:
A post's composer shows an abstract 'Source/canonical' tab AND (when a switch connection has 'promotion' in kinds) a separate 'Switch' tab — reading as two masters. Per ADR-010 D1 a post is platform-agnostic copy with an abstract canonical anchor (correct today); the confusion is the spurious Switch promo tab + the colliding label.

USER DECISION (2026-06-04): Switch does NOT host posts yet, so a post's master stays the abstract anchor — NOT Switch. (1) Switch connections must be LISTING-ONLY so no switch promotion projection is minted for posts (no spurious 'Switch' tab). (2) Relabel the abstract 'Source/canonical' anchor clearly as 'Master copy' (with helper text: edits here feed every channel). (3) CHEAP FORESIGHT (ADR-003): shape naming/structure so that when Switch posting ships later, Switch becomes the canonical home for posts SYMMETRICALLY with events — a cheap flip, not a refactor.

EVIDENCE: post_syndication.html:39-48 hard-codes the Source anchor tab; :49-78 loops promotion projection_rows (views.py:590-608, gate 'promotion' in kinds at :595). _eager_create_promotion_projections (services.py:304-335, gate :335) mints a switch promo projection if a switch connection includes 'promotion'. Events have NO Source tab (event_syndication.html) — Switch listing projection is sorted first as the canonical anchor (views.py:369-372). That event pattern is the target shape posts converge to later.
design:
ADR-010 D1 (FLEXIBLE) + ADR-003 (cheap foresight) + ADR-008 D2. Evolve ADR-010 D1 in place (separate /adr-write step, done by orchestrator) to record: posts use an abstract canonical anchor BECAUSE Switch can't host posts; future path = when Switch posting ships, Switch fills the canonical-anchor slot for posts exactly as for events; name/structure now so it's a cheap flip. Implementation here: (a) exclude platform=switch from promotion-projection minting (services.py gate) OR ensure switch connections are seeded/constrained to kinds=['listing'] — pick the fail-loud-correct one; (b) relabel the post anchor tab to 'Master copy' + helper text; (c) keep the anchor as a named slot conceptually equivalent to the event's Switch-listing anchor (do NOT build Switch-posts now — ADR-008 D2). Touches post_syndication.html + services.py + possibly connection seed/model — sequence after kb-shzi.2.

## Harness target
Signal: pytest test that a profile with a switch connection + a post does NOT get a switch promotion projection (no spurious tab); the post composer renders the anchor labeled 'Master copy' (assert content); editing the master still feeds channels. Plus the ADR-010 D1 file contains the cheap-foresight future-path note.
Expected green: new tests pass; existing post composer + projection tests green.
Rationale: encodes 'no spurious Switch tab' + 'clear master label' + ADR foresight capture.
Invalidation: when Switch posting ships, the abstract anchor is replaced by a real Switch post projection — that's the planned cheap flip, not a regression.
acceptance_criteria: No switch promotion projection is created for posts (no spurious 'Switch' promo tab); switch connections are listing-only. The post master anchor is relabeled 'Master copy' with clear helper text. ADR-010 D1 evolved in place with the cheap-foresight future path (Switch becomes post canonical when Switch posting ships). No Switch-posts feature built now. uv run pytest + djlint green.
notes:
## Scoping-review folds (2026-06-04)
- ADR-010 D1 ALREADY EVOLVED by orchestrator this session (post-canonical-anchor cheap-foresight, FLEXIBLE-path). This bead is now CODE-ONLY: do NOT author the ADR. The acceptance bullet 'ADR-010 D1 evolved' is satisfied upstream — your job is to make the code MATCH it.
- F8 fold (ADR-008 D3): resolve the ambiguous 'gate OR seed' — implement a CAPABILITY-AWARE, fail-loud gate: Switch does not support the 'promotion' kind yet, so the projection-minting path must not mint a switch promotion projection for posts. Gate on platform capability (not a hard permanent ban on 'promotion' for switch — that would fight the cheap-foresight flip). Do not rely on seed data alone. If a switch connection carries 'promotion' in kinds today, the gate skips minting (and ideally logs/raises per ADR-008 D3 rather than silently). 
- Relabel the post anchor 'Source/canonical' -> 'Master copy' as a named canonical-anchor SLOT (structurally the same slot an event's Switch-listing projection fills), per the evolved ADR-010 D1.
close_reason: Post master model: capability-aware fail-loud gate (_supports_post_promotion / _PLATFORMS_WITHOUT_POST_PROMOTION={switch}) applied uniformly at mint-time, render-time (legacy-data robust), and the event-board promo CTA. No spurious Switch promo tab for posts; Telegram/FetLife promotion unaffected; event listings unaffected. Post anchor relabeled 'Source/canonical'->'Master copy' + helper text; kb-shzi.2 selected_pk='source' key preserved. ADR-010 D1 evolved in place (cheap-foresight: removing 'switch' from the set is the flip when Switch posting ships). Fresh review (14 risks), 3 findings folded. 772 syndication tests green; ruff/format/djlint clean; no migration. Commits d347008 + 9d8e3c6.

title: Composer renders in studio shell on standalone/refresh; selected tab survives swaps
description:
TWO related structural HTMX bugs sharing the composer fragments.

BUG 1 (no left rail): The publishables rail exists ONLY in templates/syndication/studio.html (aside :31-85, swap target main#studio-main :87). Standalone hub pages post_hub.html/event_hub.html extend layouts/_default.html which has NO rail. Every full-page entry — 'Open composer' plain href (event_posts.html:58-61), post-create redirect (views.py:701), and browser refresh of a pushed composer URL — lands rail-less. The hub views branch on HX-Request (views.py:180-182, 549-551): HX returns the body fragment, plain GET returns the rail-less full page. The prior studio_swap fix hardened inner cross-links but never gave the standalone page a shell.
FIX (B1): make the standalone full-page hub render the studio two-pane shell (rail + #studio-main with the composer inside, active row marked), populating the rail via get_publishables_for_profile and passing studio_swap=True in that full-page render too. View+template change in event_hub/post_hub + post_hub.html/event_hub.html. This also fixes refresh/deep-link.

BUG 2 (tab jump): selected tab is Alpine client state seeded to a constant — post_syndication.html:21 x-data selectedPk:'source'; event_syndication.html:20-21 selectedPk:first_pk. Customize (_sync_bar.html:27-31), both Reset forms (:51-55,:70-74), Duplicate (post_syndication.html:213-217) POST with hx-target=fragment_target hx-swap=outerHTML — replacing the x-data root, so Alpine re-seeds to leftmost. The autosave path already avoids this via hx-swap=none + OOB.
FIX (B2): make selected tab survive the swap. Prefer server-driven: thread selected_pk through the action POSTs (hidden input) into fragment_event_syndication/fragment_post_syndication (views.py:501-519, 643-660) and render x-data selectedPk:{{selected_pk|default:first_pk}}. Must resolve to a tab that still exists after Duplicate/Customize (which change the projection set). Alpine-persisted wrapper above the swap target is the lighter alt.
design:
ADR-016 (composer UX), dry-partial-merge-collapses-render-contexts memory (standalone vs in-studio context). B1 robust fix = standalone hub renders the shell so any entry path reconstructs rail+composer. B2 server-driven preferred over Alpine-persist (round-trips correctly when projection set changes). Keep autosave hx-swap=none/OOB untouched.

## Harness target
Signal: (B1) test that a plain GET (no HX-Request) of /syndication/posts/<pk>/ and the event hub returns HTML containing the publishables rail markers (rail aside + the publishable list) AND #studio-main with the composer; (B2) test that POSTing customize/reset/duplicate with selected_pk=<non-first> returns a fragment whose x-data selectedPk equals that pk (assert on response.content, not context).
Expected green: both new tests pass; existing test_edit_in_place_shell.py + sync UX tests stay green.
Rationale: encodes 'rail everywhere' + 'tab survives swap' as content assertions (django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow memory: assert content not context).
Invalidation: if studio becomes a SPA shell, the full-page-render-the-shell approach changes.
acceptance_criteria: Plain GET / refresh / deep-link of a post or event composer renders WITH the publishables rail and the composer in #studio-main (assert on rendered content). 'Open composer' and new-post no longer land rail-less. customize/reset/duplicate keep the selected channel tab (server-driven selected_pk, resolves to an existing tab post-action). Autosave OOB path unchanged. uv run pytest + djlint green.
close_reason: Standalone/refresh/deep-link composer now renders the full studio shell (rail + #studio-main) via extracted _studio_rail.html (third-caller DRY); selected channel tab is server-driven via selected_pk threaded through customize/reset/duplicate; no-claim fails loud 403 matching studio view (ADR-008 D3); autosave OOB path untouched. Fresh adversarial review (8 risks checked), 2 findings folded. 771 syndication tests green; ruff/format/djlint clean. Commits 4c0c4b9 + 4a0096f.

title: Switch own-page publish must promote Event.status to published
description:
Publishing the Switch own-page LISTING projection flips projection.status to published but never sets Event.status. /events/ filters Event.status=='published' (events/views.py:30-32), so the event stays hidden. Composer shows PUBLISHED (reads projection status); /events/ reads Event status; they disagree.

EVIDENCE: publish_switch_own_page (syndication/adapters.py:32-143) transitions projection.status + stamps external_url/syndicated_at but never touches event.status. Only events/admin.py:190,208-217 ever writes Event.status. Live DB: Event pk=10 status=draft while its switch listing projection pk=2 status=published. event_detail (events/views.py:255-268) also filters status=published, so the stamped external_url 404s until promoted.
SECONDARY (data hygiene, not the bug): demo event start is past (2026-06-03); even after fix it stays hidden by start__gte=now — re-seed to a future date.
design:
Fix is adapter-local to switch ONLY (Telegram/FetLife must NOT promote Event.status — they publish promotion content, not the Switch listing). In publish_switch_own_page after successful transition, promote the canonical Event: set event.status='published' + event.published_at=now() idempotently (mirror admin.py:208-209 first-publish-only pattern). ADR-008 D2: a shared events-side helper publish_event(event) is justified (admin is already a second writer) rather than the adapter reaching across into Event fields — decide helper-vs-inline at impl, lean helper. Event.status is a plain CharField (no state machine) — direct assignment, draft->published. Refs: ADR-016 D5 (published='actually out there'), ADR-008 D3 (no silent no-op), ADR-010 D1. Do NOT loosen the /events/ status filter or touch visibility (visibility passes already; it's a separate intentional gate).

## Harness target
Signal: a pytest test that publishes a Switch own-page listing projection for a future-dated public Event, then asserts (a) Event.status=='published' + published_at set, (b) the event appears in the anonymous /events/ listing queryset, (c) event_detail resolves 200. Plus assert publishing a Telegram/FetLife promotion projection does NOT mutate Event.status.
Expected green: all assertions pass; existing adapter + events listing tests stay green.
Rationale: directly encodes the user-observable 'published event shows on /events/' contract + the adapter-local-to-switch boundary.
Invalidation: if a future un-publish path is added, revisit Event/projection state symmetry (out of scope now).
acceptance_criteria: Publishing a Switch own-page listing projection sets Event.status=published + published_at (idempotent). The event then appears on /events/ for anonymous viewers (future-dated) and event_detail resolves 200. Telegram/FetLife promotion publishes do NOT touch Event.status. Demo seed event re-dated to future so it surfaces. uv run pytest green for syndication + events.
close_reason: Switch own-page publish now promotes Event.status->published via events/services.publish_event() (idempotent first-publish), called adapter-local to Switch only. Telegram/FetLife do NOT promote (content-tested). Event now appears on /events/ + detail 200. Demo seed re-dated future. Diff verified vs report (commit 02dd2bc); 931 syndication+events tests green; ruff/format clean. Per-leaf fresh review folded into parent re-verify.

title: Studio/composer round-2 fixes (post-dogfooding feedback)
description:
User dogfooding of the syndication composer surfaced ~12 issues. Five parallel diagnostic dives root-caused them into a small set of structural bugs + IA cleanup + one ADR-aligned model decision. This epic captures the fix set. Diagnoses (file:line evidence) live in each child's --design.

THEMES:
1. Standalone composer pages render a rail-less layout; only /studio/ has the publishables rail. Refresh/deep-link/'open composer'/new-post all land rail-less. + selected channel tab is client-side Alpine state wiped by full-fragment swaps (customize/reset/duplicate jump to leftmost tab).
2. Publishing the Switch own-page projection flips the PROJECTION status to published but never sets Event.status, which /events/ filters on -> 'published' events never appear publicly. (kb-jgda's adapter-dispatch is done; this is the residual Event-promotion gap.)
3. Conceptual-model: a post's 'Source/canonical' anchor reads as competing with a spurious 'Switch' promo tab. Decision (user, 2026-06-04): Switch can't host posts yet, so a post's master stays an abstract anchor; drop the spurious Switch promo tab; relabel clearly; shape naming for a cheap future flip to Switch-as-canonical-for-posts when Switch posting ships (cheap foresight, ADR-003). Evolve ADR-010 D1.
4. IA cruft: remove 'Review all' (user: we don't codify reviews); 'Event hub' naming; 'Add post' vs 'Add promo message' + dup empty-states over ONE Post model/endpoint; no add-channel link once you have >=1 channel; no 'new event/post' in /studio/ after the first; two 'Synced' badge states (broadcast vs detach) look identical.
design:
ADR-aligned. Refs: ADR-010 D1 (Switch canonical home; evolving for posts cheap-foresight), ADR-016 D2 (sync-from-channel), ADR-016 D5 (publish lifecycle), ADR-008 D2 (no speculative abstraction), ADR-008 D3 (fail-loud), ADR-003 (cheap foresight), ADR-012 D6 (dogfooding-driven). All touched ADR decisions are FLEXIBLE.

Decomposition (children): (A) backend: Switch own-page publish promotes Event.status; (B) composer renders inside studio shell on standalone/refresh + selected tab survives swaps; (C) remove Review-all; (D) post-master model: drop spurious Switch promo tab, switch connections listing-only, relabel master + ADR-010 D1 evolution for cheap-foresight; (E) UI-polish pass (naming, posts/promo vocab, sync-badge legibility, discoverability entry points).

Acceptance conjunction = all five children's acceptance. Parent re-verify (fresh adversarial review over cumulative diff vs this design + ADRs) before close.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A published event appears on /events/ (Event.status promoted on Switch own-page publish; event detail resolves). 2. Refreshing/deep-linking the composer, and 'open composer'/new-post, all render WITH the publishables rail (studio shell everywhere). 3. customize/reset/duplicate keep the currently-selected channel tab (no jump to leftmost). 4. No spurious 'Switch' promo tab on posts; the post master anchor is clearly labeled; ADR-010 D1 evolved with the cheap-foresight future path. 5. 'Review all' fully removed (route/view/templates/links/tests); no dead refs. 6. Consistent vocabulary for post creation + one empty-state; clearer 'Event hub' label; the two 'Synced' badge states are visually distinguishable. 7. Discoverable way to add a channel and to create a new event/post from the studio. 8. Quality gates green (uv run pytest, ruff, djlint); parent re-verify passes.
notes:
## Scoping review (2026-06-04, fresh adversarial-reviewer)
Reviewed the 5-child tree before any build. 13 findings; folded the load-bearing ones: (F6) serialized kb-shzi.4 after kb-shzi.3 to close event_syndication.html file-conflict; (F8) sharpened kb-shzi.4 to a capability-aware fail-loud gate per ADR-008 D3; (F9/F13) ADR-010 D1 evolution moved to orchestrator (done this session) — kb-shzi.4 is now code-only; (F1/F2) folded behavioral sync-label + Duplicate clarity into kb-shzi.5. Minor harness-underspec findings left to implementer TDD. ADR-010 D1 evolved in place (cheap-foresight post-anchor, FLEXIBLE-path). Execution: serial (shared test DB) — .2 unblocks .3/.4; .5 last; .1 independent. ADR-016 D2 left consistent; no FIRM contradiction.
## Parent re-verify (2026-06-04, fresh adversarial-reviewer over cumulative diff b63be79..HEAD)
Conjunction-drift check found ONE real cross-child gap: kb-shzi.2's selected_pk tab-persistence was applied only to the shared _sync_bar.html (3 forms); the same outerHTML-swap-resets-tab mechanism still hit the inline Switch bar + all publish/approve/retry/batch forms (10 more). Filed + fixed as kb-shzi.6 (13 forms threaded, content-tested). Minor findings folded into .6 (rail-link guard) or noted as PASS (orphaned-but-clean Duplicate endpoint; stale comment). Re-verify then satisfied. /compound run (1 memory folded: inline-copy-of-shared-partial-drifts; no Promote/Retire). FULL CI gate green on final HEAD a67fa0f: bare pytest 2119 passed/5 skipped, makemigrations --check clean, ruff/format/djlint clean. Tree clean; docs/klad.md untouched. 9 commits.

Round-2 dogfooding fixes shipped: (1) published events now appear on /events/ (publish promotes Event.status); (2) composer renders the studio rail on every entry path + selected tab survives all fragment swaps; (3) Review-all removed; (4) no spurious Switch promo tab on posts + 'Master copy' anchor + ADR-010 D1 cheap-foresight evolution (Switch becomes post canonical when posting ships); (5) IA polish — vocab unified to 'promo post', behavioral sync-badge labels, Channels + New-event entry points; (6) parent-re-verify-discovered selected_pk gap closed across all 13 swap forms.
