title: Prod deploy red ~4 days: init container exits 1 on VPS (migrations/check --deploy) — passes Tests workflow but fails against prod env/data
description:
The deploy workflow has failed on every commit since 2026-05-29 (last green: 392b731 'track /events/ redesign epic'; first red: 9e24092, the close of the kb-wz8m syndication epic). It fails at the 'Recreate app + run migrations + check --deploy' step: the prod 'init' container exits 1. The GH Actions log does NOT capture the init container's stderr (only 'service init didn't complete successfully: exit 1').

KEY SIGNATURE: the SAME code passes the Tests workflow's migrate + makemigrations --check + check --deploy steps (Tests is fully green on HEAD), but fails in the prod init container. That points to a prod-ENVIRONMENT/DATA-specific failure, not a code bug CI can see. Prime suspect: a migration from the kb-wz8m epic (ContentVersion model + content_version cutover + override_data drop + backfill — landed exactly in the break window) failing against REAL prod data, OR a prod env var the init's check --deploy needs. This is the migration-green-on-fresh-test-DB / broken-against-prod-data failure class (see memories data-migration-backfill-default-regresses-prior-visibility, migration-introducing-unhandled-rows-lands-with-its-code-path).

CONSEQUENCE: switch.berlin has likely not deployed for ~4 days.

DIAGNOSIS BLOCKED ON: the init container's actual error. Need either (a) SSH the VPS + 'docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs init', or (b) add a 'docker compose logs init' dump-on-failure step to deploy.yml and re-run.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy workflow green on HEAD: prod init container completes (migrations + check --deploy succeed against prod DB), app recreated, site serves. Root cause identified and fixed at the correct layer (migration / prod env / init script). deploy.yml emits init container logs on failure so future init breaks are diagnosable from CI alone.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-06-03. Root cause: syndication/0001_initial was edited in place across 3 commits (cb8a2ea create, e940abb connection-FK refront, 738fb72 frozen_content) AFTER prod had already applied an early version on 2026-05-26. Prod's schema froze at the late-May shape (platform_id string, no connection_id, no frozen_content, no platformconnection table) while the migration graph claimed 0001-0004 applied — irreconcilable divergence, no migration file describes prod-actual to current. Fix: (1) committed 93bd319 making 0005's four column-drops idempotent (DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS + state_operations) — necessary but not sufficient. (2) All 6 syndication tables were EMPTY on prod (0 rows), so dropped them + cleared syndication django_migrations history, then redeployed: init replayed 0001-0007 from current files into the correct schema. Verified: 7 migrations applied, platformprojection has connection_id+frozen_content (no platform_id), platformconnection table exists, switch.berlin/events 200. (3) committed c723383 adding if:failure() init+app log dump to deploy.yml so the next init break is diagnosable from the Actions log without SSH. Prod was dark ~4 days (2026-05-29 to 2026-06-03); now serving latest code.
close_reason: Prod deploy fixed + verified green (3 deploys green on c723383); switch.berlin serving latest code after ~4 days dark. Root cause: in-place edits to already-applied 0001_initial diverged prod schema from the migration graph; resolved by rebuilding the (empty) syndication schema from current migrations + idempotent 0005 drops + deploy log-dump on failure.

title: CI security job red: pip-audit runs under py3.12 (project needs 3.13) masking 8 real CVEs in 5 deps
design:
Discovered 2026-06-02 while driving CI green after kb-f17n (ruff lint, green) and kb-va4a (Telegram token tests, green). The CI security job's pip-audit step (.github/workflows/test.yml: `uvx pip-audit -r /tmp/reqs.txt`, where reqs.txt = `uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project`) is RED.

TWO STACKED PROBLEMS:

(1) VERSION SKEW (the visible crash). pip-audit's ephemeral venv runs under python3.12 (seen in CI log path `/tmp/.../bin/python3.12`), but the project is `requires-python = ">=3.13"`. The lockfile hashes are for 3.13-resolved wheels; pip-audit's 3.12 resolution picks cp312 wheels whose hashes aren't in the file -> "THESE PACKAGES DO NOT MATCH THE HASHES FROM THE REQUIREMENTS FILE" -> exit 1. This is a CI-config bug: pip-audit must run under 3.13. Likely fix: pin `uvx --python 3.13 pip-audit ...` (verified locally: under 3.13 the hash error disappears and pip-audit runs cleanly).

(2) 8 REAL CVEs masked behind the crash. Running pip-audit locally under 3.13 (the fix for #1) exposes real advisories the gate would then fail on:
  - django 6.0.4 -> PYSEC-2026-54 (fix 5.2.14 / 6.0.5)
  - pydantic-ai 1.84.0 -> CVE-2026-46678 (fix 1.99.0)  <-- 15-minor-version jump, breakage risk, needs test-suite verification
  - pyjwt 2.12.1 -> PYSEC-2026-175/177/178/179 (fix 2.13.0)
  - python-multipart 0.0.26 -> CVE-2026-42561 (fix 0.0.27)
  - starlette 1.0.0 -> PYSEC-2026-161 (fix 1.0.1)

So fixing the config alone does NOT green the job — it reveals these 8 CVEs which must be remediated (bump deps) or explicitly ignored (pip-audit --ignore-vuln with rationale, per-CVE).

SCOPE / SEQUENCING:
- Sub-A: CI-config fix (pin pip-audit to 3.13). Mechanical, low-risk.
- Sub-B: dependency bumps. django/pyjwt/python-multipart/starlette are patch/minor and likely safe (verify suite). pydantic-ai 1.84->1.99 is the risk — review changelog for breaking changes to the agent/syndication code paths before bumping; may need code adjustments. Each bump verified against `uv run pytest`.
- Decision needed from user: appetite for the pydantic-ai upgrade now vs. ignore-with-rationale + separate upgrade bead.

canonical_refs: ADR-008 D4 (discovered-from filing). May touch kb-dle (deploy-posture ADR: CI-managed secrets / dev-prod parity) if a CI-python-version-pinning convention emerges.
close_reason: Two stacked problems fixed. (1) CI config: pinned pip-audit to py3.13 (was py3.12, project requires 3.13 -> wheel-hash-mismatch crash). (2) 10 CVEs cleared: django->6.0.5, pydantic-ai->1.105 (CVE-2026-46678), explicit transitive floors starlette/pyjwt/python-multipart + urllib3/idna (surfaced on re-run; pydantic-ai tree didn't pull patched transitives). The pydantic-ai 1.84->1.105 jump was NOT API-compatible: fresh-context adversarial review REJECTED the first attempt (result_type=/result.data removed, mocked ingestion tests blind to it). Migrated ingestion/extraction.py to output_type=/result.output and de-blinded the mocks; verified Agent construction against the real installed library (no UserError). Verified: pip-audit 3.13 = 0 vulns, pytest 1991 passed, makemigrations clean, ruff clean. Committed f4064da. verdict:pass (post-fix; the REJECT was on the pre-fix attempt, repaired and re-verified against real library).

title: CI security job red: gitleaks reports 2 secrets in git history
design:
Discovered while pushing kb-33do (2026-06-02). The CI security job is RED: `gitleaks detect --source . --no-banner --redact` (fetch-depth 0, full history) reports "leaks found: 2" across 448 commits scanned. NOT introduced by kb-33do (history scan; the kb-33do commits add no secrets). Pre-existing.

P1 because committed secrets are security-sensitive. Remediation (do NOT expose the values in tickets/transcript): (1) run gitleaks locally to identify WHICH commits/files (handle output as sensitive); (2) ROTATE the exposed credentials first (assume compromised once in history); (3) scrub from history if warranted (git filter-repo / BFG) — note history rewrite is hazardous on a shared remote, coordinate; OR (4) if they are false positives / test fixtures, add a .gitleaks.toml allowlist with rationale. The repo currently has no custom gitleaks ruleset.

Use the secrets-via-stdin skill discipline for any token-touching steps; keep values out of context.
acceptance_criteria:
- The CI security job's gitleaks step exits clean (0 leaks) — either the 2 findings are remediated (rotated + scrubbed) or allowlisted as confirmed false-positives/fixtures with a documented .gitleaks.toml rationale.
- Any genuinely-exposed credential is rotated (treated as compromised), with values never landing in tickets/transcript.
close_reason: Both gitleaks findings were generic-api-key false positives on Django ORM syntax (request.auth, <field>__<lookup> filter kwargs in syndication/api.py) — no real credential, so no rotation/history-rewrite needed. Fixed with .gitleaks.toml allowlist extending the default ruleset (useDefault=true). Verified: CI-equivalent scan 0 leaks; positive control (fake github-pat) still trips, proving the gate stays live. Committed 1466e89. Adversarial-review skipped: trivial single-file config edit, verification is empirical (CI-equivalent green + positive control is the strongest possible check that the gate isn't weakened); allowlist regex is self-evidently ORM-specific and cannot match a generic credential line.

title: Fix parent-re-verify conjunction drift: post-scoped publish-all + post-composer navigation
design:
Parent re-verify of kb-q4u9 found two MATERIAL conjunction-drift defects invisible to each child in isolation, plus two cosmetics. Fix all.

MATERIAL:
1. Post workspace "Publish all ready" fires the EVENT-scoped batch-publish. post_syndication.html (~line 21-23) hx-posts to `projection-batch-publish` with event_pk; urls.py (~85-87) only has the event-scoped `events/<event_pk>/projections/publish-all-ready/`; views.py (~1094-1124) calls `publish_all_ready_projections(user, event)` which batches ALL of the event listing + every post under the event — NOT just this post. On success it returns `_syndication_fragment_response(request, event)` (the EVENT fragment, id event-syndication) into the post template hx-target `#post-syndication` (wrong fragment, wrong slot). Violates parent acceptance bullet 5 / harness probe 1 ("publish-all-ready over the POSTs projections, each adapter invoked with its own body"). FIX: add a post-scoped publish-all-ready service path (publish only the posts ready projections) + a post-scoped URL+view that returns the POST fragment; wire the post template button to it with hx-target #post-syndication.

2. Flat publishable list navigation missing. event_posts.html (~46-62) renders posts as static article cards with NO link to the post composer; nothing links to the post-hub route child C built. Parent acceptance bullet 1 + D1 ("a flat list of publishables is navigable; selecting one opens its composer"). FIX: link each post card to `syndication:post-hub pk=post.pk` so selecting a post opens its composer.

COSMETIC:
3. services.py `_unique_copy_name` docstring (~722-724) says "(event, name) is UNIQUE-constrained" — stale after 0006 split into two partial constraints. Update.
4. event_facts.html (~16-78) renders title/date but NOT venue/location; parent bullet 8 says "title/date/location". Add venue/location (Event.venue FK).

HARNESS: extend syndication/test_e2e_publishable_workspace.py with a publish-all-ready-over-a-post test (the path that hid finding 1): create a post with ≥2 ready promotion projections with divergent bodies, POST the post-scoped publish-all-ready endpoint, assert each adapter invoked with its OWN channel body AND the returned fragment is the post fragment (not the event fragment). Plus a Client/test assertion that a post card in the event hub links to the post-hub.

canonical_refs: ADR-016 D2/D5 (publish lifecycle, post-scoped projections); ADR-010 D1 (Switch canonical); ADR-008 D3 (fail-loud).
acceptance_criteria:
- Post workspace "Publish all ready" publishes ONLY the current posts ready projections (not the whole events), each adapter invoked with its own channel body, and returns the POST fragment into #post-syndication (not the event fragment).
- A post card in the event hub links to the post composer (post-hub); selecting a post opens its composer (parent bullet 1 / D1).
- _unique_copy_name docstring reflects the split partial unique constraints.
- event_facts.html renders venue/location alongside title/date.
- New e2e test: publish-all-ready over a post with ≥2 divergent ready channels routes each channel its own body and returns the post fragment; a test asserts the post-card→post-hub link.
- Full syndication suite green (618+ pass, only pre-existing FetLife red kb-33do); touched templates djlint-clean.
close_reason: Fixed two parent-re-verify conjunction-drift defects + two cosmetics. (1) Post workspace 'Publish all ready' now hits a post-scoped service (publish_all_ready_projections_for_post) + view + URL (post-projection-batch-publish) that publishes ONLY the post's ready projections and returns the POST fragment — verified: adapter invoked per channel with own body, sibling post + event listing NOT published, #post-syndication fragment returned. (2) Post cards in event hub now link to the post-hub composer (parent bullet 1 / D1 navigability). Cosmetics: _unique_copy_name docstring updated for split partial constraints; event_facts header renders venue/location. 619 pass (1 pre-existing FetLife red kb-33do); templates djlint-clean. Commit 0675b91.

title: E2E integration probe: customize-in-UI diverges + publishes per channel
design:
The conjunction the parent's harness **Invalidation** clause names that no single-layer probe exercises: customizing a post channel in the **live UI** actually writes the post version and renders a divergent body, and publishing from the UI routes the divergent body to the adapter. This is the integration-test bead (decompose DoD #5 — children A→B→C all compose here; a service-layer test alone can pass while the composer never writes the post version, and a browser render test alone can pass while the body never diverges).

`browser-automation` (authenticated `runserver`) end-to-end. New test file `syndication/test_e2e_publishable_workspace.py`.

## canonical_refs
- ADR-016 D2 — per-channel divergence at the data layer, exercised through the UI seam.
- ADR-016 D5 — publish invokes the adapter with the channel's own (frozen) body.

## Harness target
- **Signal:** `browser-automation` e2e. Select/create a post; customize its Instagram channel and edit the body; assert the live preview diverges from the still-synced Telegram channel (the composer actually writes the post version — catches "the composer never writes the post version"). Publish the customized channel from the UI; assert the adapter mock received that channel's own body (not the canonical/other channel's). In the same live run, confirm the event workspace's Switch-tab anchor and the post workspace's Source-tab anchor (ties probe 3's render to the data layer).
- **Expected green:** live customize→diverge→publish routes the channel's own body; both anchors confirmed live.

## Origin
/decompose kb-q4u9 round 1 — see parent's `## Decomposition record`.
acceptance_criteria:
- In the live UI, customizing a post Instagram channel and editing its body renders a divergent live preview vs the still-synced Telegram channel — i.e. the composer actually writes the post version (catches "the composer never writes the post version").
- Publishing the customized channel from the UI invokes the adapter with that channel own body.
- In the same live run, the event workspace Switch-tab anchor and the post workspace Source-tab anchor are both confirmed (ties probe 3 render to the data layer).
close_reason: E2E integration probe shipped (test-only, syndication/test_e2e_publishable_workspace.py). 4 Client-level tests hitting real HTTP endpoints: customize seam (POST customize→edit mints a post-scoped CV, repoints proj_1's FK, leaves proj_2 on canonical = isolation, divergent body renders in response.content), publish seam (adapter httpx.post invoked with channel's own divergent frozen body, not canonical — ADR-016 D5 routing), and both anchors (Switch event / Source post). Browser-automation read-back visually confirmed live divergence (divergent tab shows EDITED badge + diverged preview + 'live on' banner gone; synced tab unchanged). Probe found NO bugs in A/B/C — seams correctly wired. 617 pass (1 pre-existing FetLife red kb-33do). Commit 4901736.

title: Rebuild the syndication hub as a Typefully composer workspace
design:
Replace the stacked card-board (`templates/syndication/fragments/event_syndication.html`, the as-built that shipped the rejected card-list) with a Typefully-shaped publishable workspace.

- **Flat list** of publishables (events + posts, **no nesting**); selecting one opens its composer.
- **Focused composer** with **horizontal channel icon-tabs**; each tab carries a **sync toggle** (synced = shares canonical + "live on `<channels>`" cue; customize = own diverged version; reset = back to synced); a **live preview** reskins to the selected platform (reuse `_channel_preview.html`).
- Canonical anchored as a tab: an **event's** canonical = the **Switch tab** (ADR-010 D1, Switch is the event's native home); a **post's** = an abstract **"Source" tab**.
- **Slim shared event-facts header** (D5) — repurpose `event_facts.html`; edited via "edit event", distinct from the per-channel body. Fold `event_posts.html` into the flat publishable list (no separate posts section).
- **No platform-owned-LLM "generate" affordance** (carried kb-wz8m D-B).
- **Post-scoped hub/fragment views + routes** — today `urls.py` (18-121) has only `post-create`, no post hub or fragment route; add them. `views.py` `event_hub`/`fragment_event_syndication` (89-107, 221-329) + `review_all` (808-852) read `source_version.event`/`version.event` (null for posts) → resolve publishable-scoped.
- **Version-op view redirect-dispatch (folded from adversarial review):** the version-op POST views (`version_copy_to`, `version_edit`, `version_reset`, `version_duplicate`, … at `views.py:647-808`) hardcode `redirect("syndication:event-hub", pk=event.pk)` at 663/712/750/etc. — for a post-owned version `event` is null → `event.pk` AttributeErrors. Dispatch the redirect target by publishable type (event-hub vs the new post-hub).

Depends on Child B: the post-scoped consumers-map, `create_post` seeding, and the resolve-owner service paths the views call must exist first.

## canonical_refs
- ADR-016 D1 — Event structured facts (platform-neutral) vs Post communication artifact; facts header is shared, edited once.
- ADR-016 D2, D4, D5 — channel tabs bind to per-connection ContentVersions; publish lifecycle.
- ADR-010 D1 — event canonical anchors at the Switch tab (growth-loop posture).
- ADR-008 D2 — flat list (no nested hierarchy before PMF); "Switch"/"Source" two concrete labels, not an abstraction.

## Harness target
- **Signal:** browser read-back — runserver + `browser-automation` screenshot, authenticated session, **both** an event's and a post's workspace. At desktop width assert on **rendered HTML / screenshot** (not `response.context`): flat publishable list; composer with channel icon-tabs; a visible sync toggle; event workspace anchors canonical at the **Switch tab** with event facts as a header; post workspace anchors canonical at the **"Source" tab**; no "generate" affordance present; a version op (e.g. reset) on a post channel redirects to the post hub (not a 500 on `event.pk`). Plus `djlint --check` clean and no multi-line `{# #}` comment bleed (the two kb-wz8m failure classes). The post workspace is seeded by creating a post via the service layer (Child B).
- **Expected green:** both workspaces render with tabs + sync toggle + anchored canonical (Switch / Source) + facts header; no generate affordance; post version-op redirect lands on the post hub.

## Origin
/decompose kb-q4u9 round 1 — see parent's `## Decomposition record`.
acceptance_criteria:
- At desktop width, an event workspace renders on rendered HTML / screenshot (not response.context): flat publishable list, composer with channel icon-tabs, a visible sync toggle, canonical anchored at the Switch tab, event facts as a header.
- A post workspace renders the same composer shape with canonical anchored at the "Source" tab; a version op (e.g. reset) on a post channel redirects to the post hub, not a 500 on event.pk.
- No "generate" (platform-owned-LLM) affordance is present in the UI.
- djlint --check clean; no multi-line {# #} comment bleed in rendered output (the two kb-wz8m failure classes).
close_reason: Typefully composer workspace shipped: flat publishable list, horizontal channel icon-tabs, per-channel sync toggle (customize/reset/duplicate/copy-from gated on draft), live preview, event canonical anchored at Switch tab (Switch-first ordering enforced per ADR-010 D1) and post canonical at Source tab, slim event-facts header, no generate affordance. Post-scoped hub+fragment routes/views added; version-op + lifecycle error-path redirects dispatch publishable-scoped (no 500 on post versions). 613 pass (1 pre-existing FetLife red kb-33do); C templates djlint-clean; browser read-back confirmed Switch-first + published-state gating. Two review rounds: round-1 found redirect-dispatch + Client-test honesty surface; round-2 fixed 6 findings (error-path dispatch, Switch-first ordering, published-state toggle gating, strengthened canonical test, post-scoped test helper, composer parity). Commits 0e3d4bb, caac9df, eb98db4.

title: Publishable-scope the service/engine layer + data-backfill migration (fail-loud)
design:
Generalize the event-hardcoded service/engine cluster in `syndication/` to resolve the owning Event **OR** Post and **fail loud** (ADR-008 D3) rather than silently resolve a post-owned version to its event, AND write the data migration that backfills existing dogfood data. This child is the atomic "posts are publishable at the data layer" unit — it both introduces post-owned rows (via migration `0007`) and makes every service path handle them, so the tree never has a red intermediate state.

**Service functions (`services.py`):**
- `_ensure_canonical_content_version` (192-213) — add a post-keyed `get_or_create` path.
- `_eager_create_promotion_projections` (260-300) — FK the **post's** canonical, not `post.event`'s.
- `create_post` (487-517) — seed the **post's** canonical (the `create_post → _ensure_canonical(event) → _eager_create_promotion_projections` chain at 512-515 is the latent smell D4 fixes).
- `_resolve_projection_event` (557-585) — resolve the owning Post for a promotion canonical, not collapse to event.
- `_gate_can_edit_for_cv` (615-628) — `content_version.event` is null for post versions; resolve the post owner (via `post.event`) through `can_edit`; never `can_edit(user, None)`.
- `content_version_consumers_map` (644-662) — add a post-scoped path (today `filter(event=…)` returns empty for post-owned versions, silently breaking the "live on" cue).
- `reset_to_canonical` (811-846) — for a promotion projection resolve the **post's** canonical (`get(event=…)` at 836 would silently return the event's — the exact bug).
- `edit_version` (849-906) + freeze guards — re-verify draft-vs-frozen propagation on post-owned canonicals.
- `copy_from`/`copy_to`/`duplicate`/`customize` cluster (678-792) — construct `ContentVersion` for post versions correctly (today `ContentVersion(event=source_version.event)` → for a post source `event=None`, `post=None` → **violates the check constraint A added**); guard cross-publishable equality.

**Engine (`engine.py`):**
- `generate_projection` (196-281, esp. `get_or_create(event=canonical_event)` at 240-244) — for a promotion use the **post's** canonical, not `source_post.event`'s.
- `render_projection` (442-466) — verify post-owned canonical render + frozen path.

**Data migration `0007`** (depends on `0006`) — backfill: mint a canonical `ContentVersion` per existing `Post`; repoint each promotion `PlatformProjection.content_version` from the event's canonical to the post's new canonical. Mirror-then-invert the existing `0005` backfill helper (lines 8-49) which routes promotion projections to `source_post.event`'s canonical. Safe for `ready`/`published` projections (rendered content in immutable `frozen_content`, ADR-016 D2); `on_delete=PROTECT` retains orphaned event-canonical rows (not cascaded — acceptable). `atomic=False` if a pending-trigger requires (0005 precedent, line 69). Authz contract (`authz.py` `can_edit`/`can_publish`, takes an Event) unchanged — funnel a resolved Event.

## canonical_refs
- ADR-016 D2 — promotion projections FK the post's canonical; post canonical seed (this child does the service+data half).
- ADR-016 D5 — explicit publish lifecycle; freeze at draft→ready preserved on post-owned canonicals.
- ADR-008 D1 — clean data migration (no back-compat shim).
- ADR-008 D3 — fail loud: post-owned version resolving to its event raises, never silent-fallback.
- ADR-017 D1, D2 — `can_edit`/`can_publish` chokepoint; post path resolves an Event owner via `post.event`, never `can_edit(user, None)`.

## Harness target
- **Signal:** two probes. (1) **Data integration** (pytest, Django test client; extends `test_version_ops.py` / `test_hybrid_content_model.py`): create a Post with ≥2 promotion projections; assert both start on the post's own canonical (`ContentVersion.post` set, `event` null); customize one + edit body, assert the still-synced channel unaffected; assert the copy/duplicate cluster on a post source constructs `post=…` not `event=source.event`; reset → re-points at the post's canonical; edit the shared canonical → propagates to a synced draft channel but NOT to one already `ready`/`published`; `content_version_consumers_map` reports both synced channels; per-channel publish AND `publish-all-ready` invoke the adapter with each channel's own body; any service resolving a post-owned version to its event raises. (2) **Migration probe** (`MigrationLoader` + `RunPython.code()` per `tests/test_organizer_lia_migration.py`; `test_content_version_cutover.py`): on a DB seeded with a pre-generalization Post whose promotion projections FK the event's canonical, post-migration every such projection FKs the post's canonical and each Post has its own canonical row — asserted raw-ORM, independent of the post-scoped service path.
- **Expected green:** both probes pass; full suite green (post rows now handled on every path).

## Origin
/decompose kb-q4u9 round 1 — see parent's `## Decomposition record`.
acceptance_criteria:
- create_post seeds the post own canonical; its promotion projections FK the post canonical (ContentVersion.post set, event null).
- Customize one promotion channel + edit its body; a second still-synced channel is unaffected (per-channel divergence isolation for posts).
- The copy_from/copy_to/duplicate cluster, run on a post-owned source version, constructs ContentVersion(post=…, event=None) — not event=source.event (which would raise the check constraint).
- Reset a customized post channel → it re-points at the post canonical (not the event).
- Editing the post shared canonical propagates to a still-synced draft channel but NOT to a channel already ready/published (freeze, ADR-016 D2).
- content_version_consumers_map for the post reports both synced channels (data behind "live on").
- Per-channel publish AND publish-all-ready over the post projections each invoke the adapter with its own channel body.
- Any service resolving a post-owned ContentVersion to its event raises rather than silently falling back (ADR-008 D3).
- Migration 0007 probe: applied on a DB seeded with a pre-generalization Post whose promotion projections FK the event canonical → post-migration every such projection FKs the post canonical and each Post has its own canonical row; asserted raw-ORM via MigrationLoader/RunPython.code(), independent of the service path.
close_reason: Service/engine layer publishable-scoped + fail-loud (8 functions + engine.generate_projection); data migration 0007 backfills existing posts (mint post canonical, repoint promotion projections event→post). All probe-1 bullets green incl. publish/publish-all-ready per-channel adapter routing; probe-2 migration backfill green against historical registry. 591 pass (1 pre-existing FetLife red, kb-33do). Fresh-context review of 5a679d6 + 2943576: fail-loud confirmed, branching exhaustive, migration idempotent; material publish-probe gap closed, minors folded (dead code, migration test fidelity, copy_to N=2). Commits 5a679d6, 2943576.

title: Generalize ContentVersion schema to publishable (schema-only, no backfill)
design:
Schema-only generalization of `ContentVersion`. Add `post` FK (nullable), make `event` nullable, add a DB `CheckConstraint` enforcing exactly-one-of `event`/`post` non-null (mirror `PlatformProjection.source_event`/`source_post`, syndication/models.py:408-421). Split the `(event, name)` `UniqueConstraint` (models.py:344-349) into two partial constraints: `(event,name) WHERE event IS NOT NULL` and `(post,name) WHERE post IS NOT NULL`. Update `__str__`/docstring (209-229, 351-352). Write **schema migration `0006`** (depends on `0005`) — fields + constraints only, **no data backfill** (the backfill is Child B's data migration `0007`, landing with the service code that makes post-owned rows safe). No `Publishable` base model (ADR-008 D2).

**Why schema-only (independently green):** after this child, no post-owned `ContentVersion` rows exist; all existing code still creates event-only rows (event non-null, post null → check satisfied; the `(event,name)` partial unique preserves event uniqueness). The full existing suite stays green and this child is independently shippable. This split resolves the adversarial-review finding that a backfill-in-A leaves a red intermediate state (existing service code reads `content_version.event` without a None-guard).

## canonical_refs
- ADR-016 D2 — ContentVersion generalized to publishable (this child does the schema half).
- ADR-008 D1 — clean pre-launch migration (schema migration, no back-compat shim).
- ADR-008 D2 — no `Publishable` base model; two concrete FKs.

## Harness target
- **Signal:** a schema/constraint test constructing `ContentVersion` via raw ORM — both `event` and `post` set raises; neither set raises; the two partial unique constraints hold (two posts each carry a `name="canonical"` row; an event and a post each independently carry `name="canonical"`). Plus `makemigrations --check --dry-run` clean and the full existing suite green.
- **Expected green:** constraints enforce at write-time (ADR-008 D3) and no existing event-path test regresses.

## Origin
/decompose kb-q4u9 round 1 — see parent's `## Decomposition record`.
acceptance_criteria:
- ContentVersion has a nullable event + nullable post FK; a DB check constraint enforces exactly-one-non-null — a row with both set OR neither set raises at write-time (ADR-008 D3).
- The (event,name) unique is split into two partial constraints: two posts can each hold a name="canonical" row, and an event + a post can each independently hold name="canonical".
- makemigrations --check --dry-run is clean; the full existing test suite stays green (no post rows exist yet; event-path behavior unchanged); model + schema-refactor tests updated for the new shape.
- Schema migration 0006 exists, depends on 0005, and contains fields + constraints only (no data backfill).
close_reason: Schema generalized: ContentVersion gains nullable post FK + nullable event, XOR check constraint, two partial unique constraints; schema migration 0006 (depends 0005, no backfill). 45 constraint tests green; full syndication suite green under Postgres (571 pass, 1 pre-existing FetLife fail filed as kb-33do); makemigrations --check clean; fresh-context adversarial review of diff 90898df found no defect. Committed 90898df.

title: Rebuild syndication hub as a publishable workspace — flat list + composer with channel tabs + per-channel post versioning
design:
## Context

The per-event syndication hub (`/syndication/events/<id>/`) shipped as a stacked single-column wall — event facts, promotional posts, then a vertical projection card-list. Dogfooding (2026-06-01) confirmed it is far from the Typefully-grade workspace the work intended: epic kb-wz8m D-D specified a composer + channel rail, but only the vertical card-list shipped; the focused composer pane was never built (the template carries a `composer + channel-rail` comment over markup that is the "pure card-board" alternative D-D explicitly rejected). The user re-opened the IA at design altitude. This bead is the realignment design — a Typefully-shaped publishable workspace.

Two upstream ADRs were evolved in place to canonicalize the content-model + posture this design depends on (committed `694d79d`, both FLEXIBLE, announce + proceed): **ADR-016 D2** (ContentVersion generalized Event-only → publishable Event-or-Post) and **ADR-010 D1** (Switch-as-canonical-home growth-loop posture).

This supersedes kb-wz8m's D-D layout (composer+rail → composer + channel icon-tabs) and D-A presentation (abstract canonical → anchored at the Switch tab). It carries forward kb-wz8m's committed core: publish invokes the platform adapter, no platform-owned-LLM affordance.

## Decisions

### D1 — Flat publishable list is the navigation primitive (FLEXIBLE)

The left-hand navigation is a **flat list of publishable primitives** — an Event OR a Post, each independently publishable. **No nesting** of posts under their event yet.

- **Rationale:** `external:` user direction 2026-06-01 — *"the most simple composable thing is for it to just be a publishable primitive like either an event or a post, either one can be published… I wouldn't do nesting of posts under events just yet, let's start simpler and more composable, a little less opinionated for as long as we don't have clear PMF."* `reasoned:` flat list defers the event→posts hierarchy (ADR-008 D2 — don't build the structure until PMF demands it).
- **Alternatives:**
  | Alternative | Why rejected |
  |---|---|
  | Events-only navigation (posts reached only inside an event) | `reasoned:` posts are independently publishable artifacts (ADR-016 D1); hiding them under events makes a promo post you want to edit hard to reach. |
  | Two-level nested (events at top, posts nested under selected event) | `reasoned:` premature hierarchy — opinionated structure before PMF; `external:` user explicitly deferred nesting. |
- **What would invalidate:** dogfooding shows users can't find the right post without seeing it grouped under its event (flat list gets noisy at scale) → add nesting/grouping.

### D2 — Composer + horizontal channel icon-tabs + per-channel sync toggle (FLEXIBLE; supersedes kb-wz8m D-D layout)

Selecting a publishable opens a **focused composer**. Channels are **horizontal icon-tabs** (Typefully shape), not a right-hand rail. Each channel tab carries a **sync toggle** that realizes the existing customize / reset-to-shared ops. A **live preview** reskins to the selected channel.

- **Rationale:** `external:` Typefully scout (kb-wz8m) + user 2026-06-01 — channel icon-tabs + the "Sync with Bluesky" toggle map exactly to our channels + customize/reset. `reasoned:` icon-tabs read cleaner than a rail for 2–3 channels; the sync toggle is a more intuitive expression of live-on-canonical vs diverged than the current buried buttons.
- **Alternatives:**
  | Alternative | Why rejected |
  |---|---|
  | Right-hand channel rail (kb-wz8m D-D as specified) | `reasoned:` superseded — a rail of cards is heavier and less Typefully than icon-tabs for a few channels; the tab is also where the per-channel sync toggle naturally lives. |
  | Per-card inline editors (the as-built card-list) | `direct:` kb-wz8m D-D already rejected this ("cramped writing surface; degrades writing quality"); the as-built shipped it anyway — this bead corrects that. |
- **What would invalidate:** channel count per publishable grows beyond what a tab row holds (~6+) → tabs overflow; revisit (overflow menu or rail).

### D3 — Canonical anchored per publishable type (FLEXIBLE; realizes ADR-010 D1 + ADR-016 D2)

There is **no separate "canonical section"** above the hub — one hub. The canonical content-version is **anchored as a tab**:
- **Event** canonical = the **Switch tab** (Switch is the event's native home — ADR-010 D1 growth-loop posture). Presentation-only: the existing abstract canonical row is *presented as* the Switch tab; zero schema churn on the event side.
- **Post** canonical = an abstract **"Source" tab** (a post has no native-home channel).

Other channels sync/diverge from the anchor.

- **Rationale:** `external:` user 2026-06-01 — *"the canonical is kinda just one channel/version (it's actually the Switch version)"* + the growth-loop framing (facilitators publish full events to Switch as canonical home). `reasoned:` collapsing the canonical into a tab removes the redundant "why is Switch both canonical and a board" confusion the stacked layout produced. **"Source" is a concrete label for the post's existing canonical anchor, not a generalized abstraction** — there is no shared "canonical-anchor" base type; events label their anchor "Switch", posts label theirs "Source" (ADR-008 D2 cleared — two concrete labels, not one abstraction over N callers).
- **Alternatives:**
  | Alternative | Why rejected |
  |---|---|
  | Anchor a post's canonical at one of its channels too (e.g. its first/primary promotion channel) by symmetry with events | `reasoned:` a promo post has no native-home channel — unlike an event, which genuinely lives on Switch (ADR-010 D1). Picking an arbitrary channel as "master" would be a false anchor and mislead which channel an edit propagates from. |
  | Keep the canonical as a separate "canonical/original" section above the channel tabs (don't anchor it as a tab) | `direct:` the as-built stacked layout did exactly this and produced the user's "why is Switch both the canonical and a board" confusion (2026-06-01 dogfooding). `reasoned:` one-hub requires the canonical to be a peer tab, not a section. |
- **What would invalidate:** facilitators treat Switch as just-another-channel (author elsewhere, cross-post to Switch equally) → canonical-home framing wrong (mirrors ADR-010 D1 invalidation).

### D4 — Generalize ContentVersion to publishables; posts get per-channel versioning (FLEXIBLE; = ADR-016 D2 evolution, this bead implements)

`ContentVersion` gains mutually-exclusive `event` / `post` FKs (exactly one non-null, DB check constraint — mirrors `PlatformProjection.source_event`/`source_post`). Posts get their **own** auto-created canonical seed (A1, parallel to events). Promotion projections point at the **post's** canonical (fixes the latent smell where they FK'd the event's). **No formal `Publishable` base model** (ADR-008 D2). Pre-launch clean/squashable migration (ADR-008 D1); a post's canonical seed is explicit, never silent-defaulted to the event's (ADR-008 D3).

- **Rationale:** `external:` user 2026-06-01 — *"we definitely need per-channel versioning for posts since people want to post something similar on both Telegram and Instagram… but their ToS are wildly different."* Identical ToS-divergence rationale that justified ContentVersion for events.
- **What would invalidate:** posts never diverge per channel in dogfooding (one body for all channels) → per-post versioning over-built; collapse posts to a flat body. (Full predicate set lives in ADR-016 D2.)

**Implementation surface — service-layer blast radius (folded in from adversarial review 2026-06-01).** The generalization is not "add a FK" — a cluster of services in `syndication/services.py` currently hard-code event-scoping (`content_version.event` / `filter(event=…)`) and will misbehave or fail for a post-scoped `ContentVersion` (where `event` is null). All of these must become publishable-scoped (resolve the owning Event *or* Post), and each must **fail loud** (ADR-008 D3) rather than silently resolve to the event for a post projection:
- `_ensure_canonical_content_version` (currently `get_or_create(event=…, name="canonical")`) — needs a post-keyed path; `create_post` must seed the **post's** canonical, not call the event path (the current `create_post` → `_ensure_canonical_content_version(event)` → `_eager_create_promotion_projections` chain is the exact latent smell D4 fixes).
- `_eager_create_promotion_projections` — must FK the post's canonical, not `post.event`'s.
- `reset_to_canonical` — for a promotion projection must resolve the **post's** canonical (today it resolves the event's via `_resolve_projection_event`).
- `content_version_consumers_map(event)` — must gain a post-scoped path or it returns empty for post-owned versions, silently breaking the **"live on" cue for post channel tabs**.
- `_gate_can_edit_for_cv` — `content_version.event` is null for post versions; must resolve auth via the post's owner or raise (never `can_edit(user, None)`).
- `edit_version` / freeze guards — confirm the draft-vs-frozen propagation semantics hold for post-owned canonicals (ADR-016 D2 freeze rule is unchanged but must be re-verified on the post path).

**Schema + data migration (folded in).** Pre-launch clean migration (ADR-008 D1) must: (a) add `ContentVersion.post` FK + the mutually-exclusive `event`/`post` check constraint; (b) **split the `(event, name)` unique constraint** into two partial constraints — `(event, name) WHERE event IS NOT NULL` and `(post, name) WHERE post IS NOT NULL` — so two posts can each hold a `name="canonical"` row without relying on Postgres NULL-distinctness as an implicit guard; (c) **backfill existing dogfood data**: mint a canonical `ContentVersion` for each existing `Post` and repoint each existing promotion `PlatformProjection.content_version` from the event's canonical to the post's new canonical. The repoint is **safe for already-`ready`/`published` projections** because their rendered content lives in immutable `frozen_content` (ADR-016 D2), not the live version; `on_delete=PROTECT` means orphaned event-canonical rows are retained, not cascaded — acceptable.

### D5 — Event facts as a slim shared header (FLEXIBLE)

Platform-neutral event facts (title / date / location) render as a **slim shared header**, distinct from the per-channel editorial body the composer edits. Facts are edited once (via "edit event") and shared across all channels; only the body/editorial diverges per channel.

- **Rationale:** `reasoned:` facts are platform-neutral (ADR-016 D1 — the Event's structured facts don't change by where they're announced); foregrounding them as a full section (the as-built) wastes vertical space and confuses facts-vs-copy. A header keeps them present but subordinate to the composer.
- **What would invalidate:** a platform needs structurally different facts (e.g. a channel-specific date display) → facts become per-channel too.

## Acceptance contract

Observable end-state (epic-level; decomposed later):

- A **flat list of publishables** (events + posts, no nesting) is navigable; selecting one opens its composer.
- The composer shows **horizontal channel icon-tabs**; selecting a tab binds the editor + a **live preview reskinned to that platform** to that channel's content version.
- Each channel tab has a **sync toggle**: synced = shares the canonical row (edits propagate; a "live on \<channels\>" cue names them); customize = the channel's own diverged version; reset = back to synced.
- An **event's** canonical is anchored at the **Switch tab**; a **post's** at an abstract **"Source" tab."**
- **Posts support per-channel content versions**: `ContentVersion` has mutually-exclusive `event`/`post` FK (check constraint enforced); a post gets its own canonical seed; promotion projections FK the **post's** canonical; a post customized on Instagram renders a different body than on Telegram, with divergence isolated (editing one channel does not change another).
- **The post sync/customize/reset ops and the "live on" cue work on post-owned versions** the same as events — reset returns a customized post channel to its post's canonical (not the event's); editing a post's shared canonical propagates only to its still-synced draft channels and the "live on" cue names them; a post channel already `ready`/`published` is unaffected by later canonical edits (freeze, ADR-016 D2).
- **Existing dogfood data is migrated**: every existing Post has a canonical `ContentVersion` of its own, and every existing promotion projection FKs its post's canonical (not the event's) after migration — no promotion projection is left pointing at an event canonical.
- **Event facts** (title/date/location) render as a shared header, edited once, shared across channels.
- **Publish** (per-channel + publish-all-ready) invokes the platform adapter (carried from kb-wz8m).
- There is **no platform-owned-LLM "generate" affordance** in the UI (carried from kb-wz8m D-B).

## Harness target

- **Signal:** two probes (conjunction).
  1. **Data integration test (pytest, Django test client):** create a Post with ≥2 promotion projections; assert both start on the **post's own** auto-created canonical `ContentVersion` (not the event's), that `ContentVersion.post` is set and `event` is null with the mutually-exclusive check constraint enforced (a row with both or neither raises at write-time, ADR-008 D3); customize projection_1 and edit its body; assert projection_2 (still synced) is **unaffected** (per-channel divergence isolation for posts); **reset projection_1 and assert it re-points at the post's canonical** (not the event's — catches the `reset_to_canonical` event-scoping bug); edit the post's shared canonical and assert it propagates to the still-synced draft channel but **not** to a channel already published (freeze, ADR-016 D2); assert `content_version_consumers_map` for the post reports both synced channels (the data behind the "live on" cue). Then per-channel publish projection_1 **and** `publish-all-ready` over the post's projections, asserting each ready projection's adapter is invoked with **its own** channel's body.
  2. **Migration probe (pytest against a populated DB):** apply the migration on a DB seeded with a pre-generalization Post whose promotion projections FK the event's canonical; assert post-migration every such projection FKs the **post's** canonical, each Post has its own canonical row, and the two partial unique constraints hold (two posts can each carry a `name="canonical"` row). This is the `.claude/harness.md` "data migration" fit-profile signal — a service-layer test alone cannot prove the backfill of existing rows.
  3. **Browser read-back (runserver + `browser-automation` screenshot, authenticated session):** at desktop width, **both** an event's workspace and a post's workspace render correctly — flat publishable list, composer with channel icon-tabs, a visible sync toggle; the **event** anchors its canonical at the **Switch tab** and the **post** anchors its canonical at the **"Source" tab**; event facts render as a header — asserted on **rendered HTML / screenshot**, not `response.context` (the kb-wz8m fit-profile failure classes: context-not-content hollow tests, multi-line-comment bleed).
- **Expected green:** all three probes pass. Green = posts diverge per channel at the data layer with correct routing (create, customize, reset, freeze, publish-all-ready), existing data is backfilled, AND both the event and post Typefully workspaces render (tabs + sync toggle + anchored canonical + facts header).
- **Rationale:** the data probe must assert **post-owns-its-canonical** because a naive unit test on `ContentVersion` passes even if promotion projections still FK the *event's* canonical (the exact latent smell ADR-016 D2's generalization fixes); the reset + consumers-map assertions catch the event-scoped service functions (`reset_to_canonical`, `content_version_consumers_map`) that the blast-radius note names. The migration probe is separate because a service-layer test on freshly-created objects never exercises the backfill of *pre-existing* rows (`.claude/harness.md` data-migration fit-profile). The browser read-back is load-bearing per the syndication fit-profile — two failure classes (view tests asserting `response.context` over `response.content`; multi-line `{# #}` comments bleeding as raw page text) each recurred twice in kb-wz8m and only a rendered read-back catches them; it must cover **both** the event and post workspaces because the Source-tab anchor is post-only.
- **Invalidation (signal-shaped):** the harness is the wrong altitude if all three probes pass while a real user still hits a broken state — e.g. the data + migration probes pass but a post channel customized in the live UI does not actually render a divergent body (the composer never writes the post version), or the event read-back passes but the post workspace renders the Switch tab / no Source anchor. Either observation means a probe is asserting structure without exercising the user path, and the harness must be extended (or, on `/decompose`, the relevant child re-authors it at its altitude).

## canonical_refs

- [ADR-016 D2](docs/decisions/ADR-016-outbound-syndication-architecture-event-post-projections.md) — content-version generalization to publishable (committed 694d79d); this bead implements it (mutually-exclusive event/post FK, post canonical seed, promotion projections → post canonical).
- [ADR-010 D1](docs/decisions/ADR-010-event-based-product-posture.md) — Switch-as-canonical-home growth-loop posture (committed 694d79d); the UI anchors an event's canonical at the Switch tab per this.
- [ADR-016 D4, D5](docs/decisions/ADR-016-outbound-syndication-architecture-event-post-projections.md) — PlatformConnection destinations + explicit actor-attested publish lifecycle; unchanged, carried (publish invokes adapter).
- [ADR-008 D1, D2, D3](docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md) — clean pre-launch migration; no `Publishable` base model + flat (not nested) list; post canonical explicit seed (no silent default).
- `kb-wz8m` (closed epic) — superseded: D-D composer+rail → composer + channel icon-tabs; D-A *presentation* → canonical anchored at Switch/Source tab. **Carried in scope (the version-ops service layer this epic reuses and extends to posts):** the `customize` / `copy-from` / `copy-to` / `reset-to-canonical` snapshot ops, `content_version_consumers_map` + the "live on" cue, the freeze-at-`draft→ready` rule, the publish-invokes-adapter core, and D-B (no platform-owned LLM). This epic does not rebuild these — it generalizes them from event-scoped to publishable-scoped (see D4 blast radius).
- `.claude/harness.md` — syndication/template fit-profile (browser read-back load-bearing; the two recurred failure classes).
acceptance_criteria: A publishable workspace where a flat list of events and posts (no nesting) opens a focused composer with horizontal channel icon-tabs and a per-channel sync toggle (customize/reset-to-shared); an event's canonical anchors at the Switch tab and a post's at an abstract Source tab; posts support per-channel content versions (ContentVersion gains mutually-exclusive event/post FK with a check constraint, posts get their own canonical seed, promotion projections FK the post's canonical) so a post diverges Instagram-vs-Telegram with divergence isolated; event facts render as a slim shared header; publish invokes the platform adapter; no platform-owned-LLM affordance. Verified by a pytest data probe (post owns its canonical, divergence isolated, adapter routed) plus an authenticated browser read-back of the rendered workspace.

title: Build the composer pane — finish kb-wz8m composer+rail two-pane (acceptance clause 1 unshipped)
design:
## Context

Epic kb-wz8m (Redesign event syndication as a per-channel board) was CLOSED claiming 'composer+channel-rail board, all 9 acceptance clauses met'. Dogfooding /syndication/events/<id>/ shows acceptance clause 1 — 'a focused composer bound to the selected channel's version, its preview reskinned to that platform' — was NOT actually shipped. What rendered is a stacked single-column card list (the 'pure card-board' shape D-D explicitly REJECTED), with per-card inline 'Edit' expanders. No composer pane exists in the markup; the template carries only a comment labelled 'composer + channel-rail board'.

Result: surface reads as one long narrow column, feels far from Typefully, and the canonical source vs destinations distinction is invisible (user confusion: 'why a separate Switch board when Switch is canonical?').

## Scope

Build the missing half of kb-wz8m D-D: restructure event_hub from stacked single column into a two-pane **composer + channel rail**:
- **Composer pane** (left/primary): a focused, wide editor bound to the currently-selected channel's ContentVersion (headline/body/imagery/cta/voice), with a live preview that reskins to the selected platform. Lift the existing per-card inline editor (showVersionOps panel) OUT into this persistent pane.
- **Channel rail** (right): the existing per-platform projection cards as a compact column — status pill, platform-styled preview thumbnail, per-channel publish, select-to-edit. Switch-own-page stays a peer rail card (it is a real publish destination); the composer carries the 'canonical source' role visually, which resolves the Switch-double-up IA confusion.
- **'Live on <channels>' cue** (D-D, load-bearing): when the selected version is shared across channels (A1 default), the composer must name which channels an edit propagates to, and highlight those rail cards.

Reuse existing working endpoints (all verified functional): version-edit, projection-reset-to-canonical, version-copy-from, version-duplicate, batch-publish, per-channel publish. This is a template/Alpine/HTMX restructure + studio-grade polish, not new backend.

## canonical_refs
- kb-wz8m D-D (composer + channel rail; build posture: reuse events/ styling + cotton component library)
- kb-wz8m D-A (content-version sharing semantics behind the 'live on' cue)
- ADR-016 (render contract), ADR-008 D2 (no speculative abstraction — build the composer the design specified, nothing more)

## Verification
Browser-verified in the UI build loop (auth via minted session cookie). The data-layer behavior is already covered by kb-wz8m's integration harness; this bead is the UI surface.
close_reason: Superseded by kb-q4u9. This bead built a two-pane composer+rail checkpoint, but the syndication-hub IA realignment (kb-q4u9) replaces the rail with horizontal channel icon-tabs + per-channel sync toggle and adds per-post versioning. The checkpoint's composer-editor + source-vs-destination markup is reusable reference for kb-q4u9's implementation; its specific layout is not the destination. Uncommitted template diff (event_hub.html, fragments/event_syndication.html) left in the working tree as reference.

title: Close integration-test coverage gaps from epic parent re-verify
description:
Parent re-verify of the syndication epic (ADR-009 D5) found two acceptance behaviors exercised only at unit level, not across the integration seam. Functionality is believed correct (unit tests + e2e pass) — these tests prove the seam or surface a hidden bug.

Gap 1: customize then reset-to-canonical round-trip. notes:
## Content-derivation semantics (orchestrator-resolved, 2026-05-29)

Faithful relocation of the existing override_data hybrid onto ContentVersion — NOT a snapshot-at-seed model:

- ContentVersion's editorial fields (headline/body/imagery/cta/voice + listing/promotion content) act as overrides-on-a-shared-row: a field that is NULL/unset means 'derive from the live canonical Event/Post at render time' (the role override_data key-absence played); an explicit value overrides.
- A1 canonical version is seeded EMPTY (all editorial fields null = track-live). So editing the Event still flows into draft projections' render output — NO regression of the current draft-tracks-canonical behavior. 'Seeded from the event' = the canonical version represents the event by tracking it live; rail is never empty because the version row exists and renders the event's content.
- Editing the VERSION (setting a field, e.g. via composer/customize) = divergence; propagates to every projection sharing that row. This is what the harness assertion 'editing the canonical version changes a draft projection render' tests.
- render_projection(draft) = compose from the version's explicit fields, falling back to live canonical for null fields (mirror the current _render_draft_body, reading the version instead of override_data).
- Freeze at draft->ready UNCHANGED: materialize (version explicit fields + live canonical for nulls) into projection.frozen_content; ready/published render returns frozen_content; fail-loud preserved (ADR-008 D3).
- If the kb-wz8m.1 ContentVersion field shape cannot express null-means-derive (e.g. non-nullable CharFields with '' indistinguishable from unset), the implementer raises — we adjust the field nullability rather than guess.

Adversarial review PASS after folds (non-null FK, agent_assisted dedicated version, apps.get_model migration, template/api refs).

title: Redesign event syndication as a per-channel board over a content-version model
design:
## Context

The v0 outbound-syndication MVP (epic kb-a4u) shipped functional but with poor UX. Dogfooding this session surfaced that the event→syndication hub has had essentially no syndication-UX thought: it's a wall of disconnected fragments, not a place an organizer can confidently review and publish what each platform will receive.

We scouted the field before redesigning: Buffer + Planable + Typefully (live authenticated browser scouts), BrightBean Studio (full source read — it is our exact stack: Django + HTMX + Alpine + Tailwind), and Mixpost (source read for its data model). Convergent patterns:

- **The preview card IS the review surface** — the thing you approve is rendered as the real platform post (avatar/handle/chrome), inline, not behind a modal (Planable feed-as-preview, Typefully editor-as-preview fusion, BrightBean per-platform cards).
- **Content model = canonical + per-channel override with fallback** (Mixpost and BrightBean converged independently).
- **Editorial status lives on the per-channel child**, parent status *derived* by aggregation, so one channel can be published while another is still in review (BrightBean).

The decisive **divergence from the market**: every scouted tool assumes destination platforms have *aligned* content rules, so per-channel divergence is a minor inline tweak. **Switch's destinations are ToS-divergent** — Hipsy must censor explicit language, FetLife allows uncensored, the Switch own-page is unconstrained. So distinct *content versions* ("long uncensored", "censored", "short") are structural, not an edge case. None of the four tools model this; it is genuinely ours to design.

This bead designs the v0.5 syndication redesign: a per-channel review/publish board over a reusable content-version model, with the publish action actually invoking the platform adapters. Decomposition is deferred (a later `/decompose` call); this bead is the single design artifact.

## Decisions

### D-A — Content-version model (FLEXIBLE)

**Core (v0):** introduce a `ContentVersion` entity (per `Event`): a named editorial copy variant (headline / body / imagery selection / cta / voice). Each per-connection `PlatformProjection` points at exactly one version via a new `content_version` FK; a version is reusable across many channels (many projections → one version).

**Sharing semantics (v0):** because many projections can point at the *same* row, editing that row propagates to every projection pointing at it — single-row shared-edit across channels **is** the v0 default (A1 starts all channels on one canonical version; write-once-broadcast), made visible by the D-D "live on" cue rather than silent. Divergence is opt-in via the snapshot-copy affordances below (each mints a new, independent row). What v0 does **not** ship is syncing edits across two *already-separate* rows — that is the deferred cross-row "Link" (needs merge/conflict UX).

**v0 affordances, snapshot-semantic:** `duplicate` (new version seeded from an existing one), `copy-from` (a channel pulls a fresh copy from a chosen source), `copy-to` (push a version's content into multi-selected target channels, each an independent copy — first caller: pushing one variant to a ToS-aligned cluster of channels at once, a user-requested workflow).

**Reconciliation with ADR-016 D2 (load-bearing):** the current `PlatformProjection` carries inline per-field overrides in an `override_data` JSONField (verified: `syndication/models.py:279`), with absent-key = use canonical, and a `frozen_content` snapshot taken at publish (`models.py:292`). D-A **replaces `override_data` with the `content_version` FK**: editorial content moves onto the shared, named `ContentVersion` (Mixpost content/delivery split). Content-authorship signals ADR-016 D2/D3 placed on the projection (`provenance` auto-vs-edited, `generated_by`, `last_generated_at`) **move onto `ContentVersion`** — they describe the *content*, so they travel with it and power the "your agent drafted this / you edited it" marker (ADR-016 D3). The projection keeps delivery-state only (`status`, `external_id`, `syndicated_at`, `frozen_content`) plus the FK. Per ADR-008 D1 (pre-launch: refactor hard, squash migrations, no back-compat), this is a clean schema refactor — there is no production override content to preserve (v0 just shipped; only disposable dogfood data exists).

**Sub-decision A1 — never-empty board (load-bearing, has a first caller):** creating an `Event` auto-creates **one** canonical `ContentVersion` seeded from the event's primary fields, and every eagerly-created projection (ADR-016 D4) points at it by default. So the board always renders ≥1 card; additional versions are created by the organizer or their agent. This is the minimum to make the board usable, not speculative.

**Sub-decision A2 — version mutability + publish freeze (data-integrity, ADR-008 D3):** a `ContentVersion` is **mutable while its projection(s) are pre-publish**; at publish the existing freeze-at-publish path snapshots the rendered content into the projection's `frozen_content`, so a published record is an immutable artifact and is unaffected by later edits to the version. No silent divergence — published = frozen, draft = live version.

**Deferred (explicitly NOT v0, per ADR-008 D2 — the FK substrate supports adding each without rework, but none has a first caller yet):**
- **Cross-row "Link"** — keeping two *already-separate* version rows in sync going forward (cross-row propagation with merge/conflict UX). NOT to be confused with single-row sharing (many projections → one row), which **is** v0 (see Sharing semantics above). What v0 omits is syncing edits across distinct rows.
- **`derived_from` lineage** provenance — rides in with Link, when a feature actually reads it.
- **Per-Profile preset reuse** (save the {versions + channel mapping}, pre-fill new events). This is behavioral abstraction (save + apply actions), not just data shape; add it once dogfooding shows organizers genuinely recur the same configuration.

- **Rationale:** ToS-divergent destinations make multi-version the present (not future) need — Hipsy-censored is a first caller today. A named, reusable version + a single `content_version` FK is the maximally-reshuffleable substrate: it degenerates to fully-independent (every channel its own version) or one-size-fits-all (all channels → one version) with no schema change, and share-vs-snapshot becomes two UI affordances on one FK rather than two data models. The deferred items are real cheap-foresight (ADR-003) deliberately left unbuilt (ADR-008 D2).
- **Alternatives:**
  | Option | Rejection | Warrant |
  |---|---|---|
  | Keep ADR-016 D2 inline `override_data` only | Forces re-editing identical censored copy on every ToS-aligned channel; no reusable grouping | reasoned: ToS-divergent destinations cluster into shared editorial variants inline-per-channel cannot express without duplication |
  | Cross-row Link (sync edits across two already-separate version rows, with merge/conflict UX) | Genuinely more complex (merge semantics) + no v0 first caller — single-row sharing (default) + customize + reset-to-canonical cover v0 needs | reasoned: single-row sharing needs no merge; cross-row sync does — defer until a feature reads it. (NB: single-row shared-edit IS adopted as the v0 default, made non-silent via the "live on" cue — not rejected here) |
  | Channel-owns-content + copy-from pointer (DAG, no version entity) | No shared-edit path ever; conflates "copy" (snapshot) with "share" (live) into one ambiguous pointer | reasoned: separating the version entity from the FK keeps both mental models cleanly expressible |
- **What would invalidate this:** if dogfooding shows organizers never create more than one version (always one-size-fits-all), the version primitive is over-built (ADR-008 D2) — collapse to a single canonical copy on the Event.

### D-B — Agentic posture: no platform-owned LLM in the UI (FLEXIBLE; matches ADR-016 D3, which is FLEXIBLE)

No platform-owned LLM is embedded in the UI — no "generate draft with our model" button. Drafting/AI capability lives in the **user's own agent**, which acts through the **co-equal API** using agent-credential auth (an agent acts with the identical authority of its user, ADR-017 D1; the agent layer is additive, ADR-011 D1). The UI stays a human review/publish surface. This is the UI consequence of ADR-016 D3's existing "BYO-agent at v0; bundled-agent deferred." AI transforms a market tool would expose as buttons (condense, censor, rewrite-as-announcement — cf. Typefully's AI palette) are **agent-side via the API**, not UI features.

- **Rationale:** a platform model barely knows the user; their own agent is far better-informed. The co-equal-API + agent-credential seam we already built (ADR-016 D3) *is* the personal-agent integration mechanism (ADR-011 D1, additive). Not building UI-side AI is also less to build and on-posture.
- **Alternatives:**
  | Option | Rejection | Warrant |
  |---|---|---|
  | Embed a platform "generate draft" LLM button in the UI | Off-posture; platform model under-informed about the user; re-introduces a private UI fast-path the agent doesn't share | external: ADR-016 D3 (BYO-agent v0, co-equal API, no private fast-path) |
  | No AI assistance at all (pure manual text entry, no agent) | Forecloses the agent integration that is the platform's long-term differentiator | external: ADR-011 D1 (agent layer is additive, not absent) |
  | UI affordance that triggers the *user's own* agent via the API (deep-link / "ask my agent") | Premature — depends on a personal-agent integration we haven't built; revisit long-term | reasoned: keep the API seam, defer the UI bridge until a personal-agent target exists |
- **What would invalidate this:** if dogfooding shows users *without* a personal agent are blocked from drafting and churn, revisit — an explicit ADR-016 D3 mutation warrant, routed through `/adr-write`.

### D-C — Lightweight review model (FLEXIBLE; within ADR-017 D1)

Review is lightweight and social, not an enforced workflow. Teammates are multiple users with verified `ProfileClaim`s to the same organizer `Profile` (the team-membership seam, ADR-017 D3; through-tables carry the permission semantics, ADR-007 D2). Co-claimants share visibility of the event + its versions/board and self-organize who drafts and who eyeballs. An optional "looks good" exists; there is **no enforced multi-stage approval gate**.

- **Rationale:** Switch organizers are mostly solo or small trusted teams sharing one Profile; BrightBean's none/optional/internal/internal+client policy machinery is built for agencies-with-clients and is friction without value here.
- **Alternatives:**
  | Option | Rejection | Warrant |
  |---|---|---|
  | BrightBean-style configurable approval policy (none/optional/internal/internal+client) | Agency-with-clients machinery; over-built for solo/small-team organizers | reasoned: our team unit is co-claimants of one Profile who trust each other; enforced gates add steps without catching real errors at this scale |
- **What would invalidate this:** if multi-claimant teams emerge needing enforced review, widen via `ProfileClaim.role` (the seam ADR-017 D3 reserves).

### D-D — Per-channel review/publish board: composer + channel rail; publish invokes the adapter

The event hub is redesigned to a **composer + channel rail** (FLEXIBLE shape). The **rail** is always-visible per-channel cards — one per destination projection — each carrying its assigned `ContentVersion`, a status pill, a platform-styled preview thumbnail, and a per-channel publish. The **composer** is a Typefully-grade focused editor bound to the currently-selected channel's version, with a live preview that reskins to that platform (editor-as-preview fusion). Publish is **per-channel** with a **publish-all-ready** convenience. A secondary **Review-all** mode lays every channel's rendered preview side-by-side for the pre-publish cross-channel check — its first caller is the ToS-divergence check (confirming the Hipsy-censored and FetLife-uncensored variants are each correct before publish), the highest-stakes review moment and the core value of this redesign (see Context). Editorial status lives on the projection; the Event's status is derived by aggregation (BrightBean "lowest-state-wins").

**Composer+rail is NOT the rejected "Composer-first" (below).** The rejected option is *one shared box that blasts all channels, with per-channel adaptation hidden behind a mode-switch that clears the box* (the Buffer AVOID finding). Honest scope: in the A1 default state (all channels on canonical), editing the composer *does* propagate to every channel still on canonical — that is the intended single-row shared-edit (D-A). The distinction from the rejected blast-box is not "no shared editing"; it is (a) per-channel adaptation is the always-visible rail, never a hidden mode that clears on toggle, and (b) the "live on <channels>" cue names exactly which channels an edit touches, with per-channel divergence one click away. The tradeoff it resolves is writing-focus (Typefully's editor was the strongest scouted UX, and the event description is critical) vs. simultaneous cross-channel review — the latter recovered via Review-all.

**Sharing UX (this restates D-A's sharing model for the board):** a channel's connection to content IS the `content_version` FK. By A1 every channel starts pointed at the *same* auto-created canonical version row — so editing canonical propagates to all of them (write-once-broadcast; this single-row sharing is v0 per D-A, not the deferred cross-row Link). **Customize** = duplicate into the channel's own row (opt-in divergence). **Reset-to-canonical** = repoint the FK back at the canonical row (re-enters v0 single-row sharing — pure FK assignment, still not the deferred cross-row Link). **Legibility cue (load-bearing):** because shared-row editing propagates, the composer MUST show "live on <channels>" and highlight those rail cards, so propagation is explicit, never silent.

**Committed core (not flexible — subsumes bead kb-jgda):** the publish action **must actually call the platform adapter** for that destination. Today publish only transitions DB status while `publish_switch_own_page` / `publish_telegram_promotion` sit wired-but-uncalled; this is the gap the redesign must close. Publish stays actor-attested, never auto-on-ready (ADR-016 D5).

**Build posture:** wire to real models (not a throwaway prototype); reuse and extend the existing events/ page styling and the `cotton` component library as a clean, expandable design system.

- **Rationale:** preview-is-the-review-surface is the convergent best practice; per-channel publish matches all four scouted tools (publishing genuinely differs per platform); status-on-child lets one channel ship while another waits; the focused composer adopts Typefully's editor-as-preview — the strongest writing UX scouted — without the Buffer blast-box failure.
- **Alternatives:**
  | Option | Rejection | Warrant |
  |---|---|---|
  | Composer-first (one shared box → blast all; per-channel edits behind a "customize" mode-switch) | Hides per-channel adaptation behind a mode switch that resets/clears the shared box | direct: Buffer live scout AVOID finding — the "Customize for each network" mode-switch resets/clears the shared box |
  | Pure card-board (every channel card is its own inline editor, no focused composer) | Cramped writing surface; the event description is critical and deserves a focused editor, not a narrow card field | reasoned: writing quality is a primary task here; narrow per-card editors degrade it |
  | Versions-first two-pane (versions list + channel→version assignment grid) | Foregrounds version management over authoring; leans into the deferred per-Profile preset layer | reasoned: premature for v0 — channel-primary matches "canonical first, channels copy from it"; version-primary is the preset mental model deferred in D-A |
  | Auto-publish on "ready" (no explicit publish action) | Removes the actor-attested publish step | external: ADR-016 D5 (publish is actor-attested, never auto-on-ready) |
- **What would invalidate this:** if dogfooding shows the focused composer is unused (organizers always one-shot canonical, never customize), the composer is over-built — degrade to the rail alone. If the board is too heavy for a 2-channel solo organizer, degrade gracefully to a per-channel list (data model unchanged).

## Acceptance contract

End-state (system behavior, observable; decomposed later):

- An organizer authors an `Event` and lands on a **composer + channel rail**: a rail of one card per destination projection (each rendering its assigned `ContentVersion` as that platform's real post preview, with a status pill and per-channel publish) plus a focused composer bound to the selected channel's version, its preview reskinned to that platform. Event creation auto-seeds one canonical version so the rail is never empty.
- The organizer can **create/duplicate** content versions, **copy-from** a source into a channel, **copy-to** (multi-select) push a version into several channels, **customize** a channel into its own version, and **reset-to-canonical** to reconnect — all snapshot-semantic — and each projection carries exactly one version via `content_version` FK. While channels share a version, the composer shows which channels that version is **live on**.
- A secondary **Review-all** mode shows every channel's rendered preview side-by-side for the pre-publish cross-channel check.
- Editing a version updates its draft projections' previews; a **published** projection's `frozen_content` is unchanged by later version edits.
- **Publish (per-channel and publish-all-ready) invokes the platform adapter** for that destination — the projection transitions to `published` with that channel's *assigned version's* content posted, not merely status-flipped. (Subsumes kb-jgda.)
- Co-claimants of the same Profile share visibility of the event/board; there is no enforced approval gate.
- There is **no platform-owned-LLM "generate" affordance** in the UI.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** an end-to-end integration test (Django test client) that walks the real v0 path — start-shared → customize → publish:
  1. Create an Event with ≥2 eager projections; assert **both start on the *same* auto-created canonical `ContentVersion`** (A1 shared default) and that the canonical version reports both projections as consumers (the data behind the "live on" cue).
  2. **Customize** projection_1 (duplicate canonical into projection_1's own row) and edit it; assert projection_2 (still on canonical) is **unaffected** by that edit (single-row divergence isolation).
  3. Trigger per-channel publish on projection_1; assert (a) projection_1's adapter is invoked (mock/spy) with **projection_1's customized content specifically** (not canonical's — catches a routing swap), and (b) projection_1 → `published` with `frozen_content` populated while projection_2 stays draft.
  4. Trigger **publish-all-ready**; assert each ready projection's adapter is invoked once.
- **Expected green:** that test passes (shared default + consumer set verified; divergence isolated; adapter invoked with correctly-routed customized content; publish-all fans out; freeze correct). Green = the start-shared→customize→publish→adapter path is wired end-to-end with correct per-channel routing. (The "live on" cue's *visual* render is browser-verified in the UI build loop, not here; this Signal covers the *data* behind it.)
- **Rationale:** unit tests on the models pass even when the wiring is broken — the kb-jgda defect is exactly "status flips but the adapter is never called," and a routing bug would pass a naive "adapter called" assertion. The goal-faithful altitude is an integration probe walking the *actual* v0 path (start shared, then diverge) — testing two already-distinct versions would miss the shared-default + divergence-isolation behavior D-D adds. Model/unit altitude misses the wiring; live-platform posting is too transport-flaky for a harness (ADR-008 D4 territory).
- **Invalidation:** if the publish path is later refactored to an async task queue, re-anchor the probe on task-enqueue + the adapter call inside the worker. If D-A's version primitive is collapsed (its invalidation fires), the version-routing and divergence-isolation assertions no longer apply and the harness reduces to the kb-jgda invocation check.

- docs/decisions/ADR-007-profile-centric-schema.md — D2 (organizer through-tables carry permission semantics — D-C)

title: Wire publish flow to per-platform adapters (publish_projection → adapter dispatch)
description:
DISCOVERED during kb-a4u.14 build. The platform adapters (publish_switch_own_page kb-a4u.10, publish_telegram_promotion kb-a4u.14) are standalone functions that NOTHING in the user/agent flow calls. publish_projection (syndication/services.py:603) and the publish API/view endpoints only do can_publish + transition_status(ready→published) — they never invoke an adapter. So clicking Publish on a Telegram/Switch-own-page projection flips status to published WITHOUT performing the actual Bot API send / URL resolution. The adapters are effectively dead code from the publish button's perspective.

This was a deliberate build-order choice (adapters built standalone + test-green first, per ADR-008 D2 'abstraction emerges from divergence'). With three divergent shapes now present — switch own-page (no external call, auto-confirm), telegram (push-API send, auto-confirm + message_id, ADR-008 D4 retry), fetlife (no-API, copy-paste + mark_published attestation) — the divergence threshold IS met, so the cross-platform dispatch is now warranted rather than speculative.

SCOPE: route publish by projection.connection.platform → the correct adapter (push-API platforms call their adapter which auto-confirms; no-API platforms like FetLife keep the copy/mark_published attestation path — do NOT force them through an auto-confirm send). Decide whether the gate (can_publish) wraps the dispatch, and whether the publish endpoint auto-invokes the adapter or stays a two-step (publish-intent then adapter). This introduces the adapter-dispatch abstraction — likely a thin platform→callable map, NOT a base-class/plugin-registry (keep ADR-008 D2 minimal). Surface to user: this is a design decision (dispatch shape + auto-invoke vs two-step) before building.
