title: step-1: Schema + config + first consumer
description:
Design: /workspace/docs/plans/2026-04-21-bundle-a-post-0.5-code-sprint-design.md#data-model-deltas

Ships four schema changes + unified whole-row cache + data migration + first call-site replacement in one bead to prevent dead-code antipattern.

## Changes required

### 1. New model: a_core.ModerationAction
Add to /workspace/a_core/models.py:

  class ModerationAction(models.Model):
      moderator = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
      flag = models.ForeignKey('reviews.Flag', null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL)
      target_type = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=[
          ('event','Event'),('organizer','Organizer'),('review','Review')
      ])
      target_id = models.IntegerField()
      target_repr = models.CharField(max_length=200,
          help_text='Snapshot of target label at action time; preserved after deletion')
      action = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=[
          ('no_action','No action'),('hide','Hide target'),
          ('delete','Delete review (soft)'),('suspend','Suspend organizer'),('resolved','Mark resolved')
      ])
      reason = models.TextField(blank=True)
      created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
      class Meta:
          indexes = [models.Index(fields=['target_type','target_id'])]

### 2. New field: reviews.Review.hidden
Add to /workspace/reviews/models.py, inside class Review(models.Model):
  hidden = models.BooleanField(default=False, db_index=True)

All existing Review.objects display queries must filter hidden=False after this migration.

### 3. Extended model: a_core.FeatureFlag.numeric_value
Add to FeatureFlag in /workspace/a_core/models.py:
  numeric_value = models.IntegerField(null=True, blank=True,
      help_text='For threshold-style flags; None means boolean-only')

### 4. New field: events.Event.avg_rating
Add to Event in /workspace/events/models.py (alongside existing rating_count at line 90):
  avg_rating = models.FloatField(null=True, blank=True)

Update recompute_aggregates in /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py to compute avg_rating for events:
  from django.db.models import Avg
  avg = Review.objects.filter(event=event).aggregate(avg=Avg('rating'))['avg']
  Event.objects.filter(pk=event.pk).update(
      attendance_count=...,
      interested_count=...,
      rating_count=rating_count,
      avg_rating=avg,
  )

This field is required by step-7a (event star chip) which uses event.avg_rating. Confirmed: Event currently has rating_count (line 90) but no avg_rating field.

### 5. Unified whole-row cache + get_numeric helper
CURRENT state: cache key is 'feature_flag:{key}', stores only the boolean .enabled value (see /workspace/a_core/models.py lines 20-25 and 48-55).

CHANGE: migrate to 'feature_flag_row:{key}' which stores the entire FeatureFlag model instance (pickle-serialized by Django's cache framework — standard behavior). Both get_flag and get_numeric project from this single cached row.

In /workspace/a_core/models.py:

  a) FeatureFlag.save() line 20: change cache.delete('feature_flag:{self.key}') to cache.delete('feature_flag_row:{self.key}')
  b) FeatureFlag.delete() line 24: change cache.delete('feature_flag:{key}') to cache.delete('feature_flag_row:{key}')
  c) Rewrite get_flag() (lines 46-56) to project .enabled from cached row.
     The stored value changes from bool to a FeatureFlag model instance:
       def get_flag(key: str, default: bool = False) -> bool:
           cache_key = f'feature_flag_row:{key}'
           row = cache.get(cache_key)
           if row is None:
               try:
                   row = FeatureFlag.objects.get(key=key)
                   cache.set(cache_key, row, timeout=60)
               except FeatureFlag.DoesNotExist:
                   return default
           return row.enabled
  d) Add new function get_numeric():
       def get_numeric(key: str, default: int) -> int:
           cache_key = f'feature_flag_row:{key}'
           row = cache.get(cache_key)
           if row is None:
               try:
                   row = FeatureFlag.objects.get(key=key)
                   cache.set(cache_key, row, timeout=60)
               except FeatureFlag.DoesNotExist:
                   return default
           if row.numeric_value is None:
               return default
           return row.numeric_value

Cache stale-key note: After deploy, old 'feature_flag:{key}' entries naturally expire within 60s TTL — no manual cache-bust needed. Both old and new keys coexist briefly during this window; the new code only reads 'feature_flag_row:{key}', so there is no split-brain risk post-deploy.

NOTE: MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY (line 18 of reviews/views.py, imported at organizers/views.py line 8) is NOT replaced in this step. Only AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD is replaced now. MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY will be replaced when step-4 upgrades the organizer reviews UI (step-4 will add get_numeric('threshold.organizer_ratings_display', default=3) and update organizers/views.py). Do not remove MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY in this step.

### 6. Data migration seeding 8 new flag rows
Migration numbering (based on existing migrations):
  - a_core: existing 0001, 0002, 0003 → create 0004_featureflag_numeric_value_moderationaction (schema) + 0005_seed_bundle_a_flags (data)
  - reviews: existing 0001, 0002, 0003 → create 0004_review_hidden (schema)
  - events: existing 0001–0005 → create 0006_event_avg_rating (schema)

Create /workspace/a_core/migrations/0005_seed_bundle_a_flags.py. Must depend on 0004 AND on ('a_core', '0003_seed_featureflags'). Uses get_or_create with defaults to preserve admin-flipped values on re-run.

New rows to seed (the 6 original rows from 0003_seed_featureflags.py are NOT re-seeded here):

  - threshold.event_ratings_display: numeric_value=3, enabled=True

  - threshold.follower_display: numeric_value=5, enabled=True
  - EVENT_REVIEWS_DISPLAYED: enabled=False
  - TRENDING_SORT_ENABLED: enabled=True
  - INGESTION_PAUSED: enabled=False

### 7. First consumer: replace AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD in /workspace/reviews/views.py
  - Line 19: remove 'AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD = 3'
  - Add 'from a_core.models import get_numeric' to imports
  - Line 148: replace 'if auth_flag_count >= AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD:' with 'if auth_flag_count >= get_numeric("threshold.auto_hide_flag", default=3):'

title: Brainstorm: business model for the agent harness + platform (free/managed tiers, open-source posture, BYOK, transaction fees)
design:
## Question
How do we monetize, relatively short-term, given the product is an agent harness (skills/CLI) + Switch as system of record? Not to settle in one sitting — run /brainstorm with the user.

## Starting hypotheses (first instincts, 2026-07-07 session — challenge these)
1. DON'T MONETIZE THE WEDGE: charging for skills taxes adoption exactly where the cold-start needs zero friction; skills are copyable text, subscription enforcement is hostile + flimsy. Weakest option on the table.
2. MONETIZE THE SERVICE (near-term): managed pi agent as THE paid tier — set up, configured, hosted, kept up-to-date, we do LLM routing (margin on tokens); BYOK as a cheaper middle tier. Most facilitators will never run Claude Code — BYO-agent's named failure mode (ADR-016 D3 revisit signal) is the market for this. Open-core / managed-hosting pattern (Ghost, Plausible).
3. MONETIZE THE TRANSACTION (long-term): ticketing is where two-sided event-marketplace revenue naturally sits (Eventbrite, not Buffer). Ticket Tailor = the transaction rail today (composed); own rail or fee-share later. Adjacent: ADR-015. Also right-sizes expectations: the Berlin facilitator base is small — harness subscriptions could never be the business; they are wedge + modest service revenue.
4. OPEN-SOURCE: near load-bearing here, not just nice — the harness handles the user's own Telegram session (MTProto) in a privacy-sensitive kink community; auditability is close to a trust requirement. Does not conflict with the managed-service model; strengthens distribution.

## To explore in the brainstorm
- Tier shape + pricing (free skills / BYOK / fully-managed); what exactly the managed tier includes (setup, updates, LLM routing, support SLA).
- Open-source license + what stays closed (the platform? nothing?); OSS contribution vs product-harness publishing path (ADR-019 D4b, deferred).
- When transaction-fee revenue becomes real (depends on payments strategy, ADR-015 / Stripe cutover research beads).
- Willingness-to-pay signals to collect during challenge walks with closest-circle facilitators.

## canonical_refs
- ADR-019 (esp. D6 wedge/moat frame; D4b product-harness publishing deferred)
- ADR-015 (payment-processor strategy — the transaction-rail leg)
- ADR-010 D1 (canonical-home growth loop — what the free wedge is for)
notes: Refinement 2026-07-07 (user): NOT fully hosted/managed — agents work far better on the user's local device, and ADR-018 D4 already binds capability to local install (platform never custodies the Telegram session), so hosting would contradict existing decisions. The paid tier = 'we make local trivial': assisted install of a pi agent, kept-up-to-date channel, possibly a desktop GUI wrapper (Claude-Cowork-style) around pi so non-technical facilitators get a friendly interface instead of a TUI. Monetize convenience/setup/support + optionally LLM routing (BYOK discount), all local-first.

title: placement-report verb resolves connection by destination_id alone — MultipleObjectsReturned 500 for multi-topic forums
design:
## Context

Discovered-from the kb-56c2 parent re-verify (ADR-009 D5 conjunction-drift pass). Per-child tests never seeded two forum-topic connections of one forum, so the four child greens all missed this.

## The bug

`report_telegram_placements` (syndication/services.py:~362) resolves the PlatformConnection with `get(organizer, platform='telegram', destination_id=...)` — IGNORING topic_id. But the schema `TelegramPlacementItemIn` (api.py) accepts topic_id, C3c (switch-cli draft.py) SENDS it, and the model's unique constraint is on (organizer, platform, destination_id, topic_id). A forum with multiple subscribed topics has multiple PlatformConnection rows sharing destination_id with different topic_id. The `.get()` then raises PlatformConnection.MultipleObjectsReturned — which is UNCAUGHT (only DoesNotExist is caught) → an unhandled 500.

Two violations: (1) ADR-008 D3 fail-loud — a 500 crash, not a structured error item; (2) the C3c↔C3a contract seam — topic_id is in the schema but dropped on the floor during resolution.

## Decision

Resolve the connection by the FULL unique key (organizer, platform, destination_id, topic_id) — extract topic_id from the item (None for channels/groups; set for forum topics). Catch BOTH DoesNotExist AND MultipleObjectsReturned and append a structured error item (fail-loud per ADR-008 D3), never let either propagate as a 500.

## Acceptance

report_telegram_placements resolves PlatformConnection by (organizer, platform, destination_id, topic_id) — the model's unique key. A payload item referencing a forum destination_id that has multiple topic-connections resolves the correct one via topic_id (no MultipleObjectsReturned). A not-found resolution appends a structured error item and continues (no 500). Verified by a unit test that seeds two forum-topic connections sharing destination_id with distinct topic_id, POSTs a placement for one, and asserts the correct connection's record is written and NO 500/uncaught exception occurs; plus a test that an unresolvable (destination_id, topic_id) yields a structured error, not a crash.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Django unit tests on report_telegram_placements with multi-topic-forum seeding.
- **Expected green:** (a) two connections sharing destination_id (distinct topic_id) seeded; a placement item with topic_id=X writes the record on the topic_id=X connection, not the other; (b) no MultipleObjectsReturned propagates; (c) an unresolvable (destination_id, topic_id) appends a structured error item and the verb still returns (no 500); (d) the existing single-connection (topic_id=None) path still resolves correctly.
- **Rationale:** The 500 only fires with ≥2 same-destination connections — a state per-child tests never seeded. The fix must be proven against that exact multi-topic-forum state.
- **Invalidation:** If resolution still ignores topic_id, OR MultipleObjectsReturned/DoesNotExist can propagate as a 500, the fix is wrong.

## canonical_refs
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md — D3 (fail-loud structured error, not a 500)
- Parent kb-56c2; bug in kb-56c2.1's service; contract with kb-56c2.3 (sends topic_id)
acceptance_criteria: report_telegram_placements resolves PlatformConnection by the full unique key (organizer, platform, destination_id, topic_id). A forum destination_id with multiple topic-connections resolves the correct one via topic_id (no MultipleObjectsReturned). An unresolvable (destination_id, topic_id) appends a structured error item and the verb continues (no 500). Verified by a unit test seeding two forum-topic connections sharing destination_id with distinct topic_id (placement for one writes the right record, no crash) + a test that an unresolvable key yields a structured error not a 500 + the existing topic_id=None path still resolves.

title: Integration: seeded end-to-end coverage read-back
design:
## Context

Integration child (C3d) of kb-56c2 (Telegram coverage tracker), per ADR-005:10 (N≥2 cross-referencing children). Verifies the composed end-to-end coverage surface over seeded data and pins the cross-surface contract between the agent report (C3c) and the server verb (C3a). Depends on C3a, C3b, C3c. See kb-56c2 --design.

## Decisions

- **Contract mechanism is explicit:** the C3a placements verb's Django-Ninja input schema (the artifact C3a builds — available once C3a ships; the C3d→C3a dep enforces ordering) is THE contract artifact; C3c's report-payload builder is validated against that schema object directly (import + validate), so the assertion fails if either side drifts. The Ninja input-schema pattern is the one already used for the ingest verb (`TelegramInventoryItemIn`, syndication/api.py).
- **Agent-closeable:** seeds placement records server-side rather than requiring a live MTProto account. The full live-real-Telegram dogfood is DEFERRED to an epic-level user-paired pass (mirroring kb-ru55.6) — noted, not required by this bead's contract.
- **Seed scenario spans all tiers:** own channel (bot), private group (agent), forum (agent), AND a public destination (deep-link) — so the four machine states co-occur and the public-tier affordance is exercised.

## Acceptance

With placement records seeded server-side as if reported by both observable writers (bot-tier inline + agent-tier reported) for a distribution run spanning an own channel (bot), a private group (agent), a forum (agent), AND a public destination (deep-link), the coverage view read back in a browser shows each destination's honest status: the four machine states co-occurring, forum-level granularity, a `pending` bot/agent destination (selected, no record), the public destination as a deep-link affordance (not placed/pending), and the send-checklist listing the human-action set (agent-tier placed + public) — with NO "sent" badge. The C3c report payload is asserted against the C3a verb's request schema (the Django-Ninja input schema for `POST /api/telegram/placements`) — a concrete shared-contract validation, not a round-trip. Verified by a browser read-back over seeded data + the schema-validation assertion.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Browser read-back over seeded placement data + a schema-validation contract assertion.
- **Expected green:**
  (a) all four machine states co-occur honestly in one rendered coverage view;
  (b) forum-level granularity holds end-to-end;
  (c) a pending (selected bot/agent no-record) destination renders;
  (d) a public destination renders as a deep-link affordance (not placed/pending);
  (e) send-checklist lists the human-action set (agent-tier placed + public);
  (f) no "sent" badge;
  (g) the C3c report payload validates against the C3a Ninja input schema object (named artifact).
- **Rationale:** Per-child tests pass in isolation but cross-surface contract drift (payload ↔ schema, reconciliation ↔ render, public-tier handling across model+UI) only shows when composed — the recurring conjunction-drift failure mode (parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift). Seeded read-back is the agent-closeable e2e altitude; validating against the named Ninja schema makes (g) falsifiable.
- **Invalidation:** If the composed view diverges from the per-child contracts, OR the report payload fails the verb schema, OR a state/tier is unreachable or mishandled end-to-end — the composition is wrong.

- Parent kb-56c2; C3a (verb schema), C3b (render), C3c (report payload); kb-ru55.6 (deferred live dogfood pattern)

title: Update switch-cli distribute to report placement outcomes
design:
## Context

Agent child (C3c) of kb-56c2 (Telegram coverage tracker). Updates `switch-cli telegram distribute` to report each placement outcome back to the C3a placement-report verb. This re-touches the agent built in kb-ru55 (its distribute command). Depends on C3a (the verb contract). See kb-56c2 --design (agent-tier reporting) and kb-ru55 --design (the distribute command + draft-only firewall).

## Decisions

- **Report-after-place:** emit the outcome immediately after each getDraft→saveDraft attempt resolves — `placed` on saveDraft ack, `skipped-pre-existing-draft` when getDraft finds a pre-existing draft (no clobber), `failed` (with error_detail) on error.
- **Payload = the C3a verb's contract shape** (destination_id, topic_id?, status, error_detail?), NO session/content fields (ADR-018 D4).
- **Reuse the existing identity-token client** from sync/ingest (kb-ru55.3) — keep report logic in the existing switch-cli client/distribute modules so it stays inside the existing AST-firewall scan. If a new module is unavoidable, add it to the firewall scan target list.
- **Draft-only firewall stays FIRM** (ADR-018 D2): this change introduces no auto-send path. Re-assert the AST-parse firewall (no sendMessage/forward_messages) over all distribute code including any new report module (kb-ru55.10 hardening discipline).
- **Forum-level outcome** (one report per forum connection — kb-56c2 D5 / kb-ru55.8).

## Acceptance

The agent's `switch-cli telegram distribute` command POSTs each destination's outcome to the C3a placement-report verb: `placed` on saveDraft ack, `skipped-pre-existing-draft` when getDraft finds a pre-existing draft, `failed` (with error_detail) on error. The report payload is the verb's contract shape (destination_id, topic_id?, status, error_detail?) and contains NO session/content fields. The existing draft-only firewall is intact — no auto-send path is introduced. The report logic lives in the existing switch-cli client/distribute modules (reusing the identity-token client from kb-ru55.3); if any new module is added, the firewall AST-scan scope is extended to cover it. Verified by switch-cli unit tests against a mocked server: the three outcome types POST the correct payload (incl. the skipped case), no session/content in payload, and the AST firewall assertion (no sendMessage/forward_messages) still holds over ALL distribute code including any new report module.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** switch-cli unit tests against a mocked report server + AST firewall scan over all distribute code.
- **Expected green:**
  (a) saveDraft ack → POST status=placed with correct payload;
  (b) getDraft pre-existing → POST status=skipped-pre-existing-draft (NOT failed), no saveDraft, no clobber;
  (c) error → POST status=failed with error_detail;
  (d) payload contains no session/content fields;
  (e) AST/structural firewall assertion (no sendMessage/forward_messages) passes over ALL distribute code including any new report module (scan scope extended if a new file is added).
- **Rationale:** The report call is the agent half of the contract seam; a mocked-server unit test pins the payload shape against C3a's verb without a live account. The firewall re-assertion (kb-ru55.10 discipline) guards against the change introducing an auto-send; extending the AST scope guards the new-module escape.
- **Invalidation:** If a report mislabels skipped as failed, OR the payload carries session/content, OR the change introduces any auto-send path, OR a new report module escapes the firewall scan — wrong.

- docs/decisions/ADR-018-channel-push-mechanisms-and-draft-only-mtproto-posture.md — D2 (FIRM firewall stays intact), D4 (no session/content in payload)

title: Build the coverage view + send-checklist UI (browser read-back)
design:
## Context

UI child (C3b) of kb-56c2 (Telegram coverage tracker). Renders the coverage surface + send-checklist from C3a's reconciliation service. Depends on C3a (model + reconcile). See kb-56c2 --design for the coverage model (four machine states, D6 public-tier affordance, D3 send-checklist).

## Decisions

- **Drive status from server reconciliation, never an optimistic client flip** (memory: optimistic-ui-flip-lies-under-shared-row-broadcast — a status surface that flips client-side lies under shared-row states).
- **Assert rendered CONTENT, not `response.context`** (memory: django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow — Django view-context tests pass on broken templates; .claude/harness.md Templates §).
- **Public-tier row = deep-link affordance** ("open & post manually"), never placed/pending (kb-56c2 D6).
- **Send-checklist filter** = `PlatformConnection.postability` ∈ {agent (only when `placed`), public}; bot-tier excluded; agent-tier `pending` excluded (no draft to send yet — kb-56c2 D3). Ticking is client-only, no persistence — checking a box does not mutate any coverage record.
- **Forum rows are forum-level** (one row per forum connection, not per-topic — kb-56c2 D5 / kb-ru55.8).
- **Vanished (flagged_missing) destinations render flagged-loud**, mirroring the picker, not silently dropped (ADR-008 D3).

## Acceptance

A coverage view renders per-destination status for a distribution run, reading the reconciliation service from C3a. Each bot/agent-tier destination row shows one of {placed, failed, pending, skipped-pre-existing-draft} with an honest label — NO "sent" badge anywhere in the rendered HTML. Public-tier destinations render as a deep-link affordance ("open & post manually"), never as placed/pending. Forum destinations render at forum-level (one row per forum connection, not per-topic). A vanished (flagged_missing) destination renders flagged-loud, mirroring the picker, not silently dropped. A send-checklist renders alongside, listing the human-action destinations — agent-tier `placed` AND public-tier — filtered by `PlatformConnection.postability` (bot-tier and agent-pending excluded), with tickable items that do NOT mutate coverage state. Verified by: Django view/template tests asserting rendered content (not just context) + a browser read-back confirming no "sent" badge, honest labels, public-tier-as-deep-link, forum-level rows, and the send-checklist.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Django view/template tests (rendered content) + browser read-back of the coverage view.
- **Expected green:**
  (a) each of the four machine states renders with an honest label in the rendered HTML;
  (b) NO "sent" string in any rendered template/response;
  (c) public-tier renders as a deep-link affordance (not placed/pending);
  (d) forum rows are forum-level (one per forum connection);
  (e) a flagged_missing destination renders flagged-loud;
  (f) the send-checklist renders the human-action set (agent-tier placed + public-tier), filtered by postability, and ticking does not POST a coverage mutation;
  (g) browser read-back confirms (a)–(f) visually.
- **Rationale:** Coverage UI is rendered HTML — the "no sent badge", public-tier-affordance, and send-checklist assertions must verify in the rendered template, not the view context (Django view-context tests pass on broken templates — .claude/harness.md Templates §). Browser read-back is the goal-faithful altitude for a status surface.

title: Build the TelegramPlacement model + placement-report API verb + bot-tier inline write
design:
## Context

Foundation child (C3a) of kb-56c2 (Telegram coverage tracker, end-to-end). Builds the server-side truth layer: the `TelegramPlacement` model, the co-equal placement-report API verb the agent calls, the inline bot-tier write in the existing publish path, and the reconciliation service that C3b renders and C3d composes. See kb-56c2 --design for the full coverage model (four machine states, three delivery tiers, D6 public-tier-as-affordance).

## Decisions

The model shape and verb contract are load-bearing:

- **Stored status enum = exactly three values** {placed, failed, skipped-pre-existing-draft}. `pending` is NEVER stored — it is computed at reconciliation. "sent" does NOT exist (ADR-018 D2 / ADR-008 D3). This enum is the single resolution point, server-side, 422-guarded — mirror the kb-ru55.2 TelegramPostability/TelegramDialogType pattern (single source, no CLI-duplicated vocabulary).
- **Key:** unique on (PlatformProjection × PlatformConnection); nullable error_detail; timestamp.
- **Tier discriminator = `PlatformConnection.postability`** (no duplicated `writer` field). postability is the resolved distribution tier, so a public-tier connection never receives a bot/agent record — reconciliation routing and record presence never disagree (kb-56c2 D2).
- **Public-tier is outside the four-state machine** (kb-56c2 D6): reconciliation returns a `deep-link` human-action affordance for a selected public-tier destination — NOT placed, NOT pending. Excluded from the pending computation.
- **Bot-tier inline write** lives in the existing `publish_telegram_promotion` adapter, ordered so the placement-record write and the projection `status`/`external_id` transition cannot silently diverge: a Bot-API success with a failed placement write raises (ADR-008 D3 fail-loud), it does not leave a `published` projection with a phantom-`pending` destination. Write in the same transaction / fail loud.
- **Placement-report verb** `POST /api/telegram/placements`: accepts a list of {destination_id, topic_id?, status, error_detail?}, identity-token auth, writes/updates records, rejects forbidden fields (session/content) with 422 — reuse the ingest verb's rejection pattern (ADR-018 D4). The Ninja input schema is the cross-surface contract C3c/C3d validate against.

## Acceptance

A `TelegramPlacement` Django model exists, keyed on (PlatformProjection × PlatformConnection), unique on that pair, with a stored status enum of exactly three values {placed, failed, skipped-pre-existing-draft}, nullable error_detail, timestamp. (`pending` is never stored; "sent" does not exist in the enum.) A co-equal API verb `POST /api/telegram/placements` accepts a list of {destination_id, topic_id?, status, error_detail?}, writes/updates records under identity-token auth, and rejects forbidden (session/content) fields with 422. The web Bot-API publish path (`publish_telegram_promotion`) writes a placed/failed record inline at call-return; this write does not silently diverge from the existing projection status transition (fail-loud). A reconciliation service computes per-selected-destination status: bot/agent-tier selected connections return placed/failed/skipped from records and `pending` for no-record; public-tier selected connections return a `deep-link` affordance (not placed, not pending); flagged_missing destinations are surfaced flagged. Tier is derived from `PlatformConnection.postability`. No "sent" value exists in the enum or any API response. Verified by unit tests: the three stored states + computed pending reachable across the bot-tier inline write + a simulated agent report; report verb writes correct record; report verb 422 on forbidden fields; reconciliation returns pending for selected bot/agent no-record AND a deep-link affordance (not placed/pending) for a selected public-tier destination.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Django unit tests (model + reconciliation service + report verb + bot-tier adapter write).
- **Expected green:**
  (a) model persists a record per (projection,connection) with the THREE stored states {placed, failed, skipped-pre-existing-draft} + unique constraint; "sent" absent from the enum;
  (b) report verb writes/updates a record under identity auth and returns 422 on session/content fields;
  (c) bot-tier publish path writes placed on Bot-API ok / failed on error inline, and fails loud if the placement write diverges from the status transition;
  (d) reconciliation returns placed/failed/skipped from records, `pending` for a selected bot/agent connection with no record, a `deep-link` affordance for a selected public-tier connection (not placed, not pending), and surfaces flagged_missing;
  (e) no "sent" string in enum/model/serializer.
- **Rationale:** This is the contract seam the agent (C3c) and UI (C3b) both consume; the verb's field contract + 422 guard need a unit test mirroring the ingest verb's cross-surface discipline (kb-ru55.2). pending-as-computed and public-as-deep-link-affordance are the subtle correctness points a model-only test would miss; the bot-tier atomic-write check guards the ADR-008 D3 phantom-pending gap.
- **Invalidation:** If "sent" appears in the enum, OR pending is stored as a row, OR a public-tier destination is classified placed/pending, OR the verb accepts session/content fields, OR reconciliation drops selected-no-record destinations, OR a Bot-API-success-with-failed-write passes silently — wrong.

title: Wire picker selection -> kinds=[promotion] + names/tags writer
design:
Mutation layer on Child B's rendered picker surface (SERIAL after B — shares destination_picker.html + syndication/views.py + syndication/urls.py). Two write paths:

1. SELECT / DESELECT a postable destination (topic leaf / channel / group): select sets `kinds=["promotion"]` (ADDITIVE — preserve any existing "listing") + `enabled=True` on that PlatformConnection; deselect removes "promotion" from kinds. This is the connection-management responsibility the ingest verb deliberately deferred (synced rows land kinds=[]). Note: "select for promotion" adds the KINDS dimension — distinct from the existing `connection_toggle` view, which flips `enabled`.
2. EDIT friendly-name + theme-tags (Child A overlay): persist, and immediately drive the tag-filter.

Server-side selectability guard is LOAD-BEARING (ADR-008 D3 fail-loud, FIRM): a locked/agent-tier row (when no agent) or a forum cluster label must REJECT a forged selection POST (4xx, no kinds mutation) — never trust client-side disabling; the visual non-interactivity from Child B is NOT a security boundary. Optimistic UI flips can lie under shared-row broadcast (memory optimistic-ui-flip-lies-under-shared-row-broadcast) — drive the selected/locked indicator from server state. HTMX autosave: the uncheck->False case needs a hidden-companion guard or it is silently lost (memory htmx-autosave-checkbox-uncheck-discard-needs-hidden-companion); hx-swap=none returned fragments must be OOB (memory htmx-swap-none-discards-returned-fragment-oob-only). Don't ship a kinds/overlay field with no observable v1 behavior (L2A calibration) — selection MUST yield an observable projection on the next Post-create.

## canonical_refs
- ADR-008 D3 — fail-loud server-side selectability guard (FIRM)
- ADR-016 D2/D4 — kinds=promotion -> per-destination projection
- ADR-018 D1 — only reachable tiers selectable

## Harness target
- Signal: live `browser-automation` read-back driving the real picker — click-select a topic leaf; toggle a tag; AND a crafted POST (real client, not curl-default-Accept — memory curl-default-accept-dodges-content-negotiated-gate) against a locked/agent-tier row and a forum cluster label. To verify projection-eligibility END-TO-END: after selecting a destination, CREATE a Post for an event owned by that profile and confirm a PlatformProjection row exists for the newly-enabled connection (projections fire at Post-create via services.py `_eager_create_promotion_projections`, NOT at selection time — verified: the gate is `"promotion" in conn.kinds AND conn.enabled`, called from create_post).
- Expected green: (a) selecting a topic leaf persists kinds=["promotion"] + enabled=True, and a subsequent Post-create produces a PlatformProjection for that connection; deselect removes "promotion"; (b) a tag edit persists and re-filters the tree; (c) uncheck->False round-trips (not silently lost); (d) a crafted select POST against a locked row OR a forum cluster label is REJECTED server-side (4xx / no kinds mutation).
- Rationale: autosave + selection round-trips are HTMX/Alpine behaviors invisible to view-context tests (the uncheck-discard and hx-swap=none traps surface only in a live browser). Projection-eligibility requires the Post-create step because `_eager_create_promotion_projections` fires at Post creation, not at picker selection — a select-only read-back would green on kinds being set while nothing observable happens (the exact no-observable-behavior trap the L2A calibration warns about). Server-side guard rejection must use a crafted POST (client disable is not a boundary).
- Invalidation: selecting a destination does NOT yield a PlatformProjection on the next Post-create, OR an uncheck is silently lost, OR a crafted POST can set kinds=promotion on a locked row or a forum cluster label.
acceptance_criteria: From the rendered picker (Child B), the facilitator can: (a) SELECT a postable destination (topic leaf/channel/group) — selection sets kinds=['promotion'] (preserving existing kinds) + enabled=True, making it projection-eligible (a subsequent Post-create produces a PlatformProjection via services.py _eager_create_promotion_projections); DESELECT removes 'promotion'; (b) EDIT a friendly name + theme tags (Child A overlay) which persist and immediately drive the tag-filter. title: Render the destination picker (tree + tag-filter + capability ladder + vanished-loud)
design:
Build the destination-picker RENDER surface, extending the existing syndication web pattern (Django template + Alpine for tree expand/collapse + tag-filter reactivity + HTMX; NO React island — matches connections_list.html / connection_create.html). Render-ONLY: no mutation endpoints (those are Child C). Intended route: a new picker view — name it in syndication/urls.py (e.g. `destinations/` or an extension of `connections/`) and use that exact URL as the harness read-back target.

Renders the synced Telegram inventory (PlatformConnection rows where type in TelegramDialogType) as:
(a) categorized tree — Channels / Groups / Forums->Topics;
(b) theme-tag filter — chips + text search, reading Child A's overlay tags;
(c) forum rows as "Group > Topic": the forum/group name is a NON-interactive cluster label with NO checkbox; each topic is a selectable leaf. THE FORUM-TOPIC TRAP is the canonical footgun (memory telegram-forum-topic-draft-not-pinnable-on-desktop; kb-mztq): a forum group cannot receive a post without a topic_id; a forum-level checkbox lands the draft nowhere or in the wrong topic;
(d) capability ladder from `postability` (TelegramPostability: bot/agent/public) — when NO agent is connected, agent-tier (private) destinations render VISIBLE-but-LOCKED with an "agent required" indicator (not hidden, not selectable). UX expression of ADR-018 D1/D4 (FLEXIBLE); locked-not-hidden keeps targets legible on reconnect;
(e) vanished destinations (`flagged_missing=True`) rendered with a LOUD flag (ADR-008 D3 FIRM) — not silently shown, not silently hidden.

READ canonical enums (TelegramDialogType, TelegramPostability) from syndication/models.py — do NOT coin picker-local variants (memory adr-enum-vocabulary-drift-invisible-per-bead). Lock/vanished LABELS must name the actual mechanism (memory ui-label-names-mechanism-not-implemented). Reuse shared row/badge partials via `{% include %}`, not hand-copy (memories inline-copy-of-shared-partial-drifts, dry-partial-merge-collapses-render-contexts — audit context flags). Alpine directives are inert without an `x-data` ancestor (memory alpine-3-x-directives-mouseenter-click-class-x) — only a live browser surfaces this. No Audiences layer (ADR-008 D2 FIRM).

Scope note (L2A calibration — this class is underestimated ~2x): B bundles five render concerns (tree, tag-filter, capability-ladder, vanished, forum-rows), but they share one view + one template + one browser-read-back pass, so they close as a unit; budget for the underestimate at implementation time rather than splitting (no technical interface between the five render concerns to carve a separate bead on).

## canonical_refs
- ADR-008 D2 (no Audiences — FIRM), D3 (vanished-loud — FIRM)
- ADR-018 D1/D4 (capability ladder — FLEXIBLE)
- ADR-016 D4 (PlatformConnection-routed)
- .claude/harness.md Templates section (browser read-back required for rendered HTML)

## Harness target
- Signal: live `browser-automation` read-back of the picker route (the new view named in syndication/urls.py) against a SEEDED synced inventory — seed (via fixture/factory or the ingest verb) at least: one channel, one group, one forum with >=2 topics, one `flagged_missing=True` row, one agent-tier (postability=agent) row — with NO agent connected. Invocation: browser-automation start -> nav to the picker URL -> screenshot + DOM read-back. Precondition: dev Postgres carries HEAD migrations (run migrate) + restart the `app` container after template edits (Django cached.Loader serves stale templates), per .claude/harness.md.
- Expected green: (a) tree renders the three categories + forum->topic nesting; (b) forum/group cluster label has NO checkbox, only topic leaves bear a checkbox; (c) the flagged_missing row renders a loud vanished flag; (d) with no agent, agent-tier rows render visible + locked + "agent required" label (not hidden, not selectable); (e) tag chips render from overlay tags and filter the tree.
- Rationale: picker is rendered HTML; Django view-context tests pass on broken templates (memory django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow). Only a live browser read-back confirms rendered state + Alpine reactivity. A response.content render-regression test is the cheap pre-filter, NOT the ground-truth signal.
- Invalidation: a forum group renders as a selectable post target, OR a vanished destination renders as a normal selectable row (or is silently hidden), OR the no-agent floor HIDES private destinations entirely instead of locking them.

title: ADR-006 D4: canonicalize the JuSchG age-gate crawler-exemption posture
description: The decision that social link-preview crawlers (Telegram/Twitter/FB/WhatsApp/etc.) bypass the JuSchG age gate to read curated OG meta — the same exemption search engines already have, while real human browsers stay gated — is currently stranded in: (a) a code comment + the BOT_AGENTS tuple in accounts/middleware.py, (b) the kb-t93r close-reason. No ADR canonicalizes it. ADR-006 (legal gate execution) is the structural-fit home (its scope is JuSchG gate execution); ADR-002 only mentions 'crawlers bypass' as a 2026-04 test step, never a reasoned binding decision. Surfaced by /compound on kb-t93r (Promote P1). Risk of leaving it in code: a future security/privacy-hardening pass re-tightens BOT_AGENTS to 'just search engines' and silently re-breaks OG previews on every platform (the exact kb-t93r regression in reverse); and a DPA/legal reviewer asking 'why do 18 bot UAs skip your youth-protection gate' has no citable reasoned decision. User explicitly approved the posture 2026-06-12.
design: Route via /adr-write. Add ADR-006 D4 (FIRM): JuSchG age gate (AgeGateMiddleware, active under PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED) gates real human browsers (Accept:text/html, non-bot UA, no age_gate cookie) but EXEMPTS automated link-preview/index crawlers (search + social unfurlers in BOT_AGENTS). Rationale: a crawler renders only curated OG meta (already public via Google) into a link-preview card — it does not expose a human to gateable content; the human who clicks STILL hits the gate on the actual page. Gating crawlers instead breaks every OG card across all syndication platforms (defeats ADR-010/ADR-016 growth loop) for zero youth-protection gain. Scope boundary: exemption is UA-list-based, curated-meta surface only; does not weaken the gate for human navigation. Reverse-link kb-t93r in canonical_refs; cite ADR-010/ADR-016 as downstream interest. Firmness FIRM (legal posture, user-signed-off, revisitable only on Berlin legal advice). Promote countermand reasoning in kb-t93r /compound audit.

title: Live-dogfood the full Telegram connect→sync→ingest→distribute flow against a real account (USER-PAIRED, gates parent)
design:
## Context

Integration-test bead carrying the parent kb-ru55's live-dogfood harness — the conjunction unit tests cannot prove (spec ≠ live client, kb-mztq). USER-PAIRED: the live MTProto session needs the user's account + hands (api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org + QR scan + a real private group + a real forum topic). Per the overselling anti-pattern (memory overselling-validation-before-representative-case-demonstrated), the LOAD-BEARING cases are the private group + forum topic — NOT public/own-channel; the dogfood must exercise those specific cases, not extrapolate. Depends on A, B, C, D. THIS BEAD GATES PARENT kb-ru55 CLOSURE — children A–D reaching unit-green does NOT close the parent.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** live dogfood against a real Telegram account (the parent's harness).
- **Expected green:** parent acceptance (a)–(e), each observed live against ≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic (the representative cases): (a) QR login completes + session persists across CLI restart; (b) sync pushes a metadata-only inventory incl ≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic; (c) the ingest verb accepts + stores it (no content in payload, verified server-side); (d) distribute places a draft (not a sent message) in ≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic; (e) the pre-existing-draft path records `skipped-pre-existing-draft` without clobber.
- **Rationale:** the spike proved the primitives in isolation; this proves the integrated CLI↔server flow live. Mocked-Telethon unit tests structurally cannot replace the live MTProto session test.
- **Invalidation:** if saveDraft silently sends, or the payload contains content/session creds, or pre-existing detection fails to warn, the implementation is wrong.

## File-claim

none new (drives the live flow); optional `tools/switch-cli/DOGFOOD.md` checklist.

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-018-channel-push-mechanisms-and-draft-only-mtproto-posture.md — D2 (FIRM draft-only firewall verified live), D4 (agent-side)
- kb-mztq (spike proved primitives; live integration is this bead)

## Origin

acceptance_criteria: Against a real Telegram account: (a) QR login completes + session persists across CLI restart; (b) sync pushes a metadata-only inventory incl ≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic; (c) the ingest verb accepts + stores it (no content in payload, verified server-side); (d) distribute places a draft (not a sent message) in ≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic; (e) the pre-existing-draft path records `skipped-pre-existing-draft` without clobber. Requires the user (api_id/api_hash + QR scan + real private group + forum topic) — NOT agent-closeable alone; this bead gates parent kb-ru55 closure.
notes:
## Forum-topic top_msg_id risk (from kb-ru55.4 review, 2026-06-12) — VERIFY LIVE

Telethon's `Draft.set_message(reply_to=topic_id)` (used by kb-ru55.4's distribute) builds `InputReplyToMessage(reply_to_msg_id=topic_id)` with `top_msg_id=None`. Per the MTProto forum-topic spec, targeting a topic thread may require BOTH `reply_to_msg_id=top_msg_id` AND `top_msg_id=top_msg_id` set. Unit tests cannot adjudicate this (Telethon's wrapping is behind the mock boundary) — only this live dogfood can.

**Live check to add:** after distribute places a forum-topic draft, confirm in the real client that the draft lands IN THE SPECIFIC TOPIC THREAD, not at channel/group level.

**Known fix path if it mis-targets:** bypass `Draft.set_message` and call the raw `telethon.tl.functions.messages.SaveDraftRequest(peer=..., message=..., reply_to=InputReplyToMessage(reply_to_msg_id=top_msg_id, top_msg_id=top_msg_id))` directly (still draft-only — SaveDraftRequest is NOT a send, firewall intact). If applied, file as a discovered-from child of kb-ru55.4.
## Recommended pre-live mocked smoke test (from parent re-verify, 2026-06-12)

Before the live session, a cheap mocked end-to-end test (connect→sync→push→distribute, all Telethon + HTTP mocked) would catch any wiring gap and save live-session time. Parent re-verify hand-verified the seams (session config_dir consistent across commands; sync payload matches the ingest schema exactly), so this is insurance, not a known gap.

## What the live session needs from the user

- A QR scan from the user's phone (Telegram → Settings → Devices → Link Desktop Device).
- At least one real PRIVATE group + at least one real FORUM TOPIC the user can post in (the load-bearing cases — do NOT extrapolate from public/own-channel per memory overselling-validation-before-representative-case-demonstrated).
- The running Switch server (the ingest verb POST /api/telegram/inventory) reachable with a valid switch-cli identity token.
Verify (a)-(e) in this bead's acceptance, PLUS the forum-topic top_msg_id risk noted above (does the forum draft land IN the topic, not at channel level).

title: Build switch-cli telegram distribute — multi-destination getDraft→saveDraft with draft-only firewall
design:
## Context

The distribute command — the parent acceptance's "on distribute, places saveDraft in ≥1 private group AND ≥1 forum topic." Iterates a placement set, applying the per-destination getDraft→saveDraft mechanism + firewall. The web cockpit (sibling picker/coverage beads) later decides *which* destinations + content; this child owns the agent-side multi-destination placement execution. For this bead's scope, the CLI interface is explicit: `--message <body>` + repeatable `--dest <chat_id>[:<topic_id>]`, destinations resolved against the locally-cached synced inventory (a `--dest` not in the inventory fails loud, ADR-008 D3). The server-pull-of-pending-distributions loop (agent fetches what the web cockpit queued) is NOT this child. Depends on A (session).

## Decisions

- **D1 (FIRM, ADR-018 D2):** draft-only firewall — never sendMessage/auto-send. **Verified two ways:** (structural) a test AST-parses the placement module (`ast.walk`, not a string grep — a string scan misses `getattr(client, 'send'+'_message')`) and asserts no attribute access / call to `send_message`/`send`/any auto-send Telethon method — proves no path CAN reach it; (behavioral) across all branches (empty-draft, pre-existing-draft, forum-topic, private-group) the mocked client's `send_message` is asserted not-called.
- **D2 (FLEXIBLE, ADR-018 D4 / ADR-008 D3):** getDraft before saveDraft per destination; pre-existing → `skipped-pre-existing-draft`, warn, no clobber.
- **D3 (FLEXIBLE):** forum-topic placement via reply_to=top_msg_id; iterate the full placement set (≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic in the dogfood).

## Harness target

- **Signal:** unit test with mocked Telethon getDraft/saveDraft over a multi-destination fixture + a structural AST-parse source-scan test; live placement in the integration child E.
- **Expected green:** (structural) the placement module source has zero attribute access / calls to sendMessage/auto-send (AST-parse). (behavioral) over a placement set with an empty-draft private group + an empty-draft forum topic, `distribute` calls saveDraft for each (reply_to=top_msg_id for the topic) and never send_message; for a destination whose getDraft returns a pre-existing draft, it does NOT call saveDraft and records `skipped-pre-existing-draft`. (live, E) real saveDraft places reviewable (not sent) drafts in ≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic; pre-existing path warns.
- **Rationale:** the getDraft→saveDraft branch + firewall is unit-testable by asserting which Telethon method is (not) called PLUS a structural scan that no send path exists at all; the actual draft landing + device-sync needs a live account (E). ADR-018 D2 is FIRM — "never sends" must be proven structurally, not only on the happy path.
- **Invalidation:** if any path can call sendMessage/auto-send (AST scan finds a reference), or a pre-existing draft is clobbered, or forum drafts miss reply_to=top_msg_id, the firewall/placement is wrong.

## File-claim

`tools/switch-cli/src/switch_cli/telegram/draft.py`, `tools/switch-cli/src/switch_cli/cli.py` (add `distribute` cmd — SERIAL after A and C), `tools/switch-cli/tests/test_telegram_distribute.py`

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-018-channel-push-mechanisms-and-draft-only-mtproto-posture.md — D2 (FIRM draft-only firewall), D4 (agent-side execution)
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md — D3 (fail loud; warn-don't-clobber)
- Parent kb-ru55

## Origin

/decompose kb-ru55 round 2. Deps: A (session).
acceptance_criteria: `switch-cli telegram distribute --message <body> --dest <chat_id>[:<topic_id>] [--dest …]` (destinations resolved against the locally-cached synced inventory; `--dest` repeatable, `:topic_id` suffix targets a forum topic) builds a placement set and, for each destination, calls getDraft first; if a draft pre-exists it records `skipped-pre-existing-draft` and does NOT clobber; if clear it calls saveDraft (reply_to=top_msg_id for forum topics). Over a placement set containing ≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic, it places drafts in both. No code path in the placement module references or reaches sendMessage or any auto-send variant (draft-only firewall — verified structurally via AST-parse AND behaviorally via mock-not-called across all branches). A `--dest` absent from the synced inventory fails loud. Unit-verified with a multi-destination fixture (≥2 `--dest`, one with `:topic_id`); live placement folds into the integration child E.
close_reason: Multi-dest distribute implemented; getDraft→saveDraft per destination, pre-existing→skipped-pre-existing-draft (no clobber), fail-loud on unknown --dest before any placement. FIRM ADR-018 D2 draft-only firewall verified via AST-parse scan (canary-proven non-vacuous) + behavioral send_message-not-called across all branches. Real Telethon draft API confirmed from source; spec=Draft truthful mocks. Fresh review PASS (commit f1a382b). 84 unit tests green. KNOWN forum-topic top_msg_id risk deferred to live dogfood kb-ru55.6 (see its notes).

title: Build switch-cli telegram sync — postable-dialog enumeration + metadata-only push to ingest verb
design:

The can-post filter + forum-topic expansion is the load-bearing enumeration logic (per memory telegram-fanout-destination-can-the-user-post-filter, validated in kb-mztq). Exclude broadcast-only subscriptions; include private no-username groups; expand forum groups to per-topic (group_id, topic_id, topic_title) rows (the forum group itself is NOT a postable destination; reply_to/top_msg_id targeting recorded for the distribute child). Dialog `type` values emitted MUST be the canonical `TelegramDialogType` set defined by child B (single-resolution-point — do not coin local variants).

title: Build the Telegram-inventory ingest API verb + PlatformConnection model fields (metadata-only upsert)
design:
## Context

The metadata-only sync spine (epic kb-fj4m D6): the agent is the sole writer; the web picker (kb-sbhs) reads these rows. Per the parent's cross-child seam resolution (user decision 2026-06-12), this child lands the PlatformConnection model migration **implementing kb-sbhs's D1 decision** (one PlatformConnection per postable dialog; chat_id + nullable topic_id; no server-side saveDraft credential per ADR-018 D4) — NOT a re-design — plus the ingest verb that writes it. The names/tags overlay (kb-sbhs D2) is NOT landed here — kb-sbhs owns it (it has the writer UI). kb-sbhs gains a dependency on this child and is descoped from model-BUILDING to model-review+refine + picker.

## Decisions

- **D1 (FIRM, ADR-016 D4):** destinations ARE PlatformConnection rows. Add `topic_id` (nullable) + dialog-metadata fields (`type`, `title`, `postability`) via migration. No lighter staging table.
- **D1a (FIRM — enum-vocabulary single-resolution-point):** the `type` enum is a CANONICAL vocabulary shared across three surfaces — the sync child emits it, this child stores it, kb-sbhs's picker categorizes by it. Define the enum values ONCE (e.g. a `TelegramDialogType` choices class in `syndication/models.py`) matching kb-sbhs D3's tree categorization (channel / group / supergroup / forum_topic — the picker's Channels/Groups/Forums→Topics buckets). `postability` likewise matches kb-sbhs D4's capability-ladder reads. A test asserts stored `type` values equal this canonical set (cross-surface equality, NOT substring — per commit e93c4ec). Rationale: enum drift across writer/storage/reader is invisible per-bead and only surfaces at parent re-verify (see memories adr-enum-vocabulary-drift-invisible-per-bead, parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift).
- **D2 (FIRM, ADR-018 D4 / parent bead D3):** metadata-only. Reject any payload field carrying message content, access_hash, or session_string — fail loud (ADR-008 D3).
- **D3 (FLEXIBLE, ADR-008 D3):** vanished-destination reconciliation = flag, not delete (epic acceptance "vanished destination flagged loud"). The flag field is read by kb-sbhs's vanished-destination picker rendering (D3).
- **D4 (FLEXIBLE, ADR-016 D3):** co-equal API verb following the existing Ninja + identity-token auth pattern (`syndication/api.py`), service logic in `services.py`.
- **D5 (alignment, per user seam decision):** model fields serve BOTH the ingest write AND kb-sbhs's picker reads. Do NOT add overlay (names/tags) fields here — no dead fields (anti-pattern cheap-foresight-seam-shipped-dead); kb-sbhs adds them with the overlay UI.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Django/pytest unit test against the ingest verb with a fixture inventory payload (no live session).
- **Expected green:** the migration adds topic_id + type + title + postability to PlatformConnection; POST of a metadata-only inventory upserts one PlatformConnection per postable destination (topic_id set for forum topics); a payload with content/access_hash/session is rejected 422 (fail-loud); re-POST is idempotent (no dup rows, asserted by row count); a destination dropped from a later sync is flagged, not deleted; the stored `type` values equal the canonical `TelegramDialogType` set kb-sbhs's picker reads (cross-surface equality assertion per D1a) — a divergent value (e.g. `forum_group` not in the set) fails the test.
- **Rationale:** the ingest seam is fully server-side and unit-testable with fixtures — it is the C1↔C2 integration contract, so it must be pinned by a real DB-state assertion (Django view-context tests pass on broken templates — assert stored rows per `.claude/harness.md` Templates §).
- **Invalidation:** if the verb stores content or session creds, or creates duplicate rows on re-sync, or silently drops vanished destinations, or stores a `type` value outside the canonical set, the metadata-only sync spine is wrong.

## File-claim

`syndication/models.py` (+ migration: PlatformConnection.topic_id + type/title/postability + TelegramDialogType choices), `syndication/migrations/` (new migration), `syndication/api.py` (ingest verb), `syndication/services.py` (ingest service), `syndication/tests/test_telegram_ingest.py`. Disjoint from CLI children → may run in PARALLEL with child A.

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-016-outbound-syndication-architecture-event-post-projections.md — D3 (co-equal API), D4 (PlatformConnection destination, no bypass)
- docs/decisions/ADR-018-channel-push-mechanisms-and-draft-only-mtproto-posture.md — D4 (metadata-only sync; agent sole writer)
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md — D3 (fail loud)
- kb-sbhs D1/D2/D3/D4 (model-read requirements this child aligns to; kb-sbhs depends on this child)
- Parent kb-ru55

## Origin

/decompose kb-ru55 round 2 (see parent ## Decomposition record). Model ownership pulled into this child per user seam decision 2026-06-12.
acceptance_criteria: The PlatformConnection model gains the fields needed to store a postable Telegram destination per kb-sbhs's D1 spec (nullable `topic_id`; dialog `type`; `title`; `postability`) via migration — one PlatformConnection per postable destination, no server-side credential. The `type` values come from a single canonical `TelegramDialogType` choices set matching kb-sbhs's picker categorization (channel/group/supergroup/forum_topic). A co-equal API verb accepts a metadata-only inventory payload (list of {chat_id, title, type, topic_id?, postability}) and upserts these rows (topic_id set for forum-topic rows). A payload carrying message content / access_hash / session material is rejected loud (422). Re-POST of the same inventory is idempotent (upsert, no duplicate rows, asserted by row count). A destination absent from a later sync is flagged (not silently deleted). title: Build switch-cli telegram connect — Telethon QR login with local session custody
design:
## Context

Foundation child of kb-ru55. Enumerate (sibling sync child) and distribute (sibling distribute child) both require an authenticated Telethon session. Reuses the kb-mztq spike's validated QR-login pattern (api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org → QR in terminal → reusable StringSession). No phone-code flow.

## Decisions

- **D1 (FLEXIBLE, ADR-018 D1):** QR login via Telethon `qr_login()`; StringSession persisted to switch-cli config dir (`~/.config/switch-cli/`), not `.env`, not server. api_id/api_hash read from local config (user provides once).
- **D2 (FIRM, ADR-018 D4 / parent bead D3):** session string NEVER enters a server-bound payload. A test asserts the sync/ingest payload contains no session material.
- **D3 (FIRM, ADR-008 D3):** fail loud on QR timeout / session-corruption / missing api creds — raise visible error, no silent re-login loop.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** unit test with a mocked Telethon client; live QR handshake folds into the live-dogfood integration child (E).
- **Expected green:** (unit) the `connect` command drives the Telethon QR-login codepath, persists the returned StringSession to the config dir, and a reload reads it back; a second invocation reuses the stored session (no re-login); no server-bound payload carries the session. (live, in E) a real QR scan completes and the session is reused across a CLI restart.
- **Rationale:** QR + StringSession custody plumbing (storage location, reuse, no-upload) is unit-testable with a mocked Telethon client; the actual MTProto handshake needs a live account, deferred to E (spec ≠ live client, kb-mztq).
- **Invalidation:** if the StringSession is written to a server-bound payload, or the command re-logins every run (no persistence), the custody model is wrong.

title: Build Telegram Audiences (saved destination sets) fast-path
design:
## Context

Saved named destination sets ("Audiences") for the Telegram distribution cockpit (kb-fj4m). This feature is DEFERRED per ADR-008 D2 -- build only once at least one real selection-reuse is observed in production. The data shape is kept audience-ready by C2 (ADR-003 cheap foresight).

## Decisions

### D1 -- Audiences are persisted pick-sets ("save this selection as an audience")

An audience is a named, saved set of PlatformConnection destinations. "Save this selection as an audience" in the picker closes the loop: presets are a byproduct of doing the work once, not a separate chore. Cold-start: run one in the tree; run two is one tap on a saved audience.

title: Build WYSIWYG Telegram composer: live-edit the styled preview (one surface, no editor/preview split)
design:
## Context

**Reframed 2026-06-13.** The owner redirected from the original "read-only faithful preview" to WYSIWYG live-edit-the-preview, modeled explicitly on Typefully: the styled platform preview IS the editing surface. The original READ-ONLY premise (old D1/D2/D3) is dead — superseded by **ADR-016 D7 (FIRM)**. What survives from the original bead is the *per-destination-type faithful Telegram render* and the *shared card_image_url resolver* reuse — now realized as the editable surface rather than a read-only twin.

Child of epic kb-fj4m (Telegram distribution cockpit). Depends on kb-y209 + kb-6d7o (both closed; shared resolver at events/og.py:18). Governing memory: composer-is-wysiwyg-live-edit-the-preview-never-split-editor-and-render.

## Current state / the gap
- `templates/syndication/fragments/_channel_preview.html` — read-only styled Telegram render (chat-bubble + link-preview card). Branches only on `proj.connection.platform`, NOT destination type — so channels/groups/forum-topics all render identically (the faithfulness gap).
- `templates/syndication/fragments/_channel_editor.html` — separate `<textarea>` editing surface, gated so the read-only preview is hidden when editable (kb-kgza.10 stale-duplicate prevention — the split D7 dissolves).
- The collapse: ONE editable styled surface, no textarea + read-only twin.

## Decisions

### D1 — One editable styled surface (FIRM, ADR-016 D7)
Collapse `_channel_editor.html` textarea + `_channel_preview.html` read-only render into a single editable styled surface for the Telegram branch. The facilitator types directly into the rendered, platform-skinned post body (contenteditable or styled-textarea — implementer-chosen). No separate textarea; no separate read-only preview element for the same channel.

### D2 — Per-destination-type render (FLEXIBLE)
Branch on `proj.connection.type` (TelegramDialogType): channel-post framing for CHANNEL (own/admin channels — channel name shown, post framing, not a chat bubble); group-message + link-preview card for GROUP/SUPERGROUP/FORUM_TOPIC. Faithfulness is judged by browser read-back against a real placed draft, not by prose.

### D3 — Reuse the shared card_image_url resolver (FIRM)
Import events/og.py `card_image_url`; never duplicate. The link-preview card image == the live event og:image. Card reflects live content as edited.

### D4 — Cheap foresight for overflow-into-thread; do NOT build splitting (ADR-003 + ADR-016 D7)
Shape the content/naming to hold an ordered set of segments for one channel. Build NO splitting logic now (v0 platforms Telegram/FetLife/Switch have no tight char limit). Additive when a thread-native platform (Twitter/Bluesky) lands.

## Acceptance contract
The Telegram composer surface is WYSIWYG: the facilitator edits by typing directly into the styled, platform-skinned post body — ONE surface, no separate textarea and no separate read-only render for the same channel. The surface renders per destination type (channel-post framing for own/admin channels; group-message + link-preview card, image via the shared card_image_url resolver, for groups/forum topics). The link-preview card reflects the live content. Edits persist through the save path (reload shows the edit). Content is shaped to accommodate ordered segments (cheap foresight; splitting NOT built). Verified by browser read-back.

## Harness target
- **Signal:** browser read-back of the live composer (Templates § of .claude/harness.md — rendered HTML + Alpine/HTMX behavior only confirmed live).
- **Expected green:** (a) typing into the styled Telegram body edits content and persists (reload shows the edit); (b) correct format per destination type (channel-post vs group-message+card) in live read-back; (c) the link-preview card image URL matches card_image_url resolver output for the same event; (d) exactly ONE surface — no separate textarea and no separate read-only preview element for the same channel (assert on rendered HTML); (e) no console / HTMX-target errors on the live surface.
- **Rationale:** WYSIWYG editability + per-type framing are behavioral/rendered, not view-context; Django view-context tests pass on broken templates (see harness.md). preview==reality for the card is the load-bearing equality.
- **Invalidation:** a separate textarea or read-only twin reappears; channel-post and group-message render identically; the card image URL diverges from the live og:image.
