title: Build the Telegram coverage tracker
design:
## Context

This child of epic kb-fj4m builds the **coverage tracker**: the honest truth surface for what the machine can confirm about a distribution run, rendered in the cockpit. It is the C3 child.

**Realigned 2026-06-14 (end-to-end scope, after a state-drift review).** When this bead was first authored (2026-06-12) the agent-side plumbing was hypothetical. It is now built and live-dogfooded (kb-ru55): the local agent connects, syncs a metadata-only inventory to the server ingest verb, and places `saveDraft` drafts in private groups and forum topics. The synced-inventory ingest API and the destination picker (kb-sbhs) are live. So this bead's dependencies are real — but the **placement-report seam the tracker needs does not exist**: the agent places drafts and reports nothing back, and there is no server verb to receive a placement outcome. This bead builds that seam end-to-end.

**Three delivery tiers, two machine-observable (ADR-018 D1).** Own/admin-channel posts go out via the Bot API, **web-executed** — the web knows the outcome at call-return (bot tier). Private-group and forum-topic drafts are placed by the **agent**, whose outcome the server cannot see unless it reports back (agent tier). Public destinations get a zero-auth **deep-link** the human opens and posts manually — like the native send, this is **outside machine observation** (public tier). The tracker reconciles the two machine-observable tiers (bot: web-written inline; agent: reported via a new co-equal verb) into the four-state coverage surface, and renders public-tier destinations as honest human-action affordances (D6) — never as a fabricated machine state, never as a silent `pending` ghost.

See kb-fj4m --design for the shared epic context (coverage status set, draft-only honesty firewall). C1 (kb-ru55, agent plumbing) and C2 (kb-sbhs, picker) are the upstream surfaces this composes against.

## Decisions

### D1 — Coverage status set: {placed, failed, pending, skipped-pre-existing-draft}; no fabricated "sent"
**Firmness: FIRM** (ADR-008 D3 / ADR-018 D2). **Unchanged by the realignment.**
Exactly four machine-observable states are tracked per destination per distribution run:
- `placed` — bot-tier: Bot API post acked; OR agent-tier: `saveDraft` acked (server-confirmed via report verb);
- `failed` — bot-tier: Bot API post failed; OR agent-tier: `saveDraft`/getDraft call failed (with error detail);
- `pending` — destination selected but no resolved record yet;
- `skipped-pre-existing-draft` — agent's getDraft found a pre-existing draft; `saveDraft` skipped to avoid clobber.

A fifth state, "sent", is NEVER added — the human's native send is outside our observation (ADR-018 D2 FIRM draft-only firewall). A send-checklist is shown alongside the coverage view for the facilitator to track the manual send step.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Show a "sent" status | `direct:` ADR-008 D3 | Fabricated state — the machine cannot observe the human's native send. Silent-integrity violation. |
| Merge skipped-pre-existing-draft into "failed" | `reasoned:` | The skipped case is semantically distinct (no error; deliberate non-placement); merging into "failed" is misleading and loses actionable information. |

**What would invalidate this:** if Telegram exposes a read-back API that confirms human sends, a real "sent" state could be added (but only then).

### D2 — One uniform placement record per (projection × destination), two writers; pending = absence
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.** **Revised by the realignment** (was: single agent-reported write path).
A `TelegramPlacement` record is keyed on (PlatformProjection × PlatformConnection): status ∈ the D1 set, plus nullable `error_detail` and a timestamp. Two writers populate the same table:
- **Bot tier (web-written, inline):** the existing web Bot-API publish path (`publish_telegram_promotion`) writes a `placed`/`failed` placement record when its call returns. No agent involved. The placement-record write and the existing projection `status`/`external_id` transition must not silently diverge — if the Bot API succeeds but the placement write fails, that fails loud (ADR-008 D3), it does not leave a `published` projection with a phantom-`pending` destination.
- **Agent tier (reported):** the agent's distribute command POSTs placement outcomes via the new report verb (D4); the server writes the record.

`pending` is not a stored row — it is the **reconciled** state of a selected machine-observable destination (a bot- or agent-tier PlatformConnection the picker marked for promotion) that has no placement record yet. **Public-tier destinations are excluded from the `pending` computation** (D6) — they are never machine-pending. No `DistributionRun` envelope is modeled (ADR-008 D2: no speculative abstraction); "run" is implicitly the set of placements for a projection's selected destinations. Re-distributing updates records in place.

The tier of a placed destination is **derived from `PlatformConnection.postability`** ({bot, agent, public}), not a duplicated `writer` field on the placement record — postability is the **resolved distribution tier**: each destination is distributed via exactly one tier (its postability), so a bot destination is bot-posted, an agent destination is saveDraft-placed, and a public destination is deep-link-only. A public-tier connection therefore never receives a bot/agent placement record, so reconciliation has no ambiguity (postability routing and record presence never disagree). This is also the single source for the send-checklist filter (D3).

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Reuse `PlatformProjection.status` for coverage | `reasoned:` | Projection status is per-projection-per-platform; it cannot express per-destination outcome across many Telegram dialogs. A distinct per-(projection,connection) record is required. |
| Client-side only coverage | `reasoned:` | Client state is losable (refresh, close); server-confirmed placement is the robust truth (validated against the kb-mztq pre-existing-draft anomaly where client display was flaky). |
| A `DistributionRun` envelope model now | `direct:` ADR-008 D2 | No speculative abstraction before the need is earned; per-(projection,connection) records carry coverage without an envelope. |

**What would invalidate this:** if facilitators need cross-run history (re-distribute audit trail), a run envelope with append-only placements replaces in-place update.

### D3 — Send-checklist is a facilitator-facing UI aid, not a machine-tracked state
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.** **Unchanged by the realignment.**
The send-checklist is a visual list of the destinations that still need a **human action**: agent-tier `placed` destinations (a draft is waiting — the facilitator opens it and sends natively) AND public-tier destinations (the facilitator opens the deep-link and posts manually, per D6). The filter is derived from `PlatformConnection.postability` (agent or public; bot-tier needs no entry — the bot already sent). An agent-tier destination that is still `pending` is NOT on the checklist — there is no placed draft to send yet, so there is nothing for the human to action; the `pending` status shows on the coverage surface itself, and the destination joins the checklist only once it becomes `placed`. It is NOT machine-tracked — checking a box does not change any coverage record. Its purpose is task-management scaffolding for the human-completed steps.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Machine-track checklist ticks as coverage state | `reasoned:` | Would fabricate "sent" semantics through the back door; the checklist is human scaffolding, not machine observation. |

**What would invalidate this:** if facilitators want checklist ticks to persist, a lightweight self-reported "personally acknowledged" field could be added — but labeled self-reported, never machine-confirmed.

### D4 — Placement-report co-equal API verb; agent distribute reports each outcome
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE** (ADR-016 D3 co-equal API). **New decision from the realignment.**
A new co-equal API verb (mirroring the ingest verb's shape) receives agent-tier placement outcomes: per destination, `{destination_id, topic_id?, status, error_detail?}`. The agent's distribute command (`switch-cli telegram distribute`) is updated to POST the outcome of each getDraft→saveDraft attempt — `placed` on saveDraft ack, `skipped-pre-existing-draft` when getDraft finds an existing draft, `failed` (with detail) on error. The verb rejects any forbidden fields (session/content) like the ingest verb (ADR-018 D4). Identity-token auth, same as the other agent verbs.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Agent does not report; web infers placement | `direct:` ADR-008 D3 | The web cannot observe agent-side saveDraft outcome; inferring it would fabricate state. The agent must report. |
| Re-derive coverage by re-querying Telegram | `reasoned:` | Per-render live MTProto queries are slow and re-introduce session exposure; report-on-place is the co-equal seam (ADR-016 D3). |

**What would invalidate this:** if the agent and web later share a push channel, a streamed report could replace request/response POST.

### D5 — Coverage destination granularity is forum-level (matches shipped placement reality)
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.** **New decision from the realignment.**
A live-dogfood finding (kb-ru55.8) flipped forum placement from per-topic to forum-level: top_msg_id-pinned per-topic drafts were invisible in Telegram Desktop, so the agent now places one forum-level draft. Coverage granularity follows: a forum's coverage is tracked on the forum's PlatformConnection, not per-topic. The known multi-topic-collapse bug (kb-ru55.11, separate ticket) is OUT OF SCOPE here — the tracker honestly reflects whatever the agent placed.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Track coverage per forum-topic | `reasoned:` | Would diverge from shipped placement reality (forum-level drafts); coverage must mirror what was actually placed, not an aspirational granularity. |

**What would invalidate this:** if kb-ru55.9 (true per-topic forum pinning) lands, coverage granularity re-follows placement back to per-topic.

### D6 — Public/deep-link tier is a human-action affordance, not a machine state
**Firmness: FIRM** (ADR-018 D2 / ADR-008 D3). **New decision from the realignment review.**
ADR-018 D1 has three delivery tiers. The public tier delivers a zero-auth `tg://` deep-link the human opens and posts manually — the machine never executes the post and cannot observe whether it happened. Like the native send, a public placement is therefore **unobservable**, and must NOT receive any of the four machine states: not `placed` (fabricated — same class as a "sent" badge), and not `pending` (a silent ghost indistinguishable from never-distributed, an ADR-008 D3 violation). Instead, a selected public-tier destination renders as an explicit deep-link affordance ("open & post manually") and joins the send-checklist (D3). It is excluded from the `pending` reconciliation (D2).

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Give public-tier a `placed` state when the deep-link is offered | `direct:` ADR-018 D2 | The machine offered a link; it did not place anything it can confirm. A `placed` badge here is fabricated state — the same firewall violation as "sent". |
| Leave public-tier as `pending` (no record) | `direct:` ADR-008 D3 | A permanent silent `pending` is indistinguishable from never-distributed — a silent-integrity gap. Public-tier must be honestly distinct. |
| Drop public-tier from the cockpit entirely | `reasoned:` | The no-agent capability floor (epic D1) reaches bot + public from the browser alone; dropping public removes a first-class tier. |

**What would invalidate this:** if Telegram exposes a deep-link callback confirming the human posted, public-tier could gain a real machine-confirmed state.

## Acceptance contract

For a distribution run, per-destination coverage is reconciled and rendered honestly end-to-end. The bot-tier web publish path writes a `placed`/`failed` `TelegramPlacement` record inline when its Bot API call returns (failing loud if that write diverges from the projection status transition). The agent's distribute command reports each agent-tier outcome via the new co-equal placement-report verb, and the server writes the matching record. All four machine states ({placed, failed, pending, skipped-pre-existing-draft}) are reachable and correctly assigned across the two observable tiers; a simulated pre-existing-draft case produces `skipped-pre-existing-draft` (not `failed`). `pending` is the reconciled state of a selected **bot- or agent-tier** destination with no record. Public-tier destinations render as deep-link human-action affordances (never `placed`, never `pending`) and join the send-checklist. No "sent" status exists anywhere in the model, API, or rendered UI. The send-checklist lists the human-action destinations (agent-tier `placed` + public-tier), filtered by `PlatformConnection.postability`. Forum coverage is forum-level. A vanished (flagged_missing) destination is flagged loud, mirroring the picker.

Verified by: (a) unit tests asserting all four state assignments across both observable writers (web bot-tier inline + agent-reported); (b) unit test asserting no "sent" status in the Django model or any API response, and that a selected public-tier destination is neither `placed` nor `pending` but a deep-link affordance; (c) the placement-report verb rejecting forbidden (session/content) fields with 422 and writing the correct record; (d) the agent distribute command POSTing outcomes (mocked server) including a skipped-pre-existing-draft case; (e) browser read-back of the coverage view confirming honest status labels (no "sent" badge), the send-checklist (agent-tier placed + public-tier), and forum-level rows.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Unit tests for both placement writers + the report verb + the agent report call (mocked), AND browser read-back of the coverage view.
- **Expected green:**
  (a) all four coverage states reachable and correctly assigned in unit tests, across BOTH the web bot-tier inline write and the agent-reported write;
  (b) `skipped-pre-existing-draft` is assigned on a simulated pre-existing draft (not `failed`);
  (c) the placement-report API verb writes the correct record and rejects forbidden (session/content) fields with 422 (mirrors ingest-verb guard, ADR-018 D4);
  (d) the agent distribute command POSTs the correct outcome per destination against a mocked server (incl. the skipped case), with the draft-only firewall intact (no auto-send introduced);
  (e) no "sent" status exists in the Django model, any API response, or any rendered template; a selected public-tier destination is neither `placed` nor `pending` but a deep-link affordance;
  (f) browser read-back of the coverage view shows honest status labels (no "sent" badge), renders the send-checklist for human-action destinations (agent-tier placed + public-tier), and shows forum-level rows.
- **Rationale:** Coverage UI is rendered HTML; the "no sent badge" assertion must be verified in the rendered template, not just the model (Django view-context tests pass on broken templates — see `.claude/harness.md` Templates §). The report verb is a contract seam the agent depends on, so its field-contract + forbidden-field guard need a unit test, mirroring the ingest verb's cross-surface discipline (kb-ru55.2 re-verify).
- **Invalidation:** If any coverage state renders as "sent", OR `skipped-pre-existing-draft` collapses into `failed`, OR a selected bot/agent destination with no record fails to show `pending`, OR a public-tier destination renders as `placed` or as a silent `pending` ghost, OR the report verb accepts session/content fields, OR the agent change introduces an auto-send — the tracker is wrong.

title: Build the Telegram destination model + web picker (tree + tags)
design:
## Context

This child of epic kb-fj4m builds the server-side destination model and the web picker UI. The destination model resolves the open modeling question from the epic: how to represent a facilitator's many postable Telegram dialogs (groups, channels, forum topics) as `PlatformConnection` records. The picker UI renders the synced inventory as a tree + tag-filter (no Audiences layer yet — deferred per ADR-008 D2).

See kb-fj4m --design for the open modeling question, the shared epic context, and the Audiences deferral rationale.

## Decisions

### D1 — Resolve the one-account-many-dialogs modeling question via PlatformConnection (ADR-016 D4; no lighter-record bypass)
**Firmness: FIRM** (ADR-016 D4).
Each postable dialog — including each forum topic — is represented as its own `PlatformConnection` record. A forum topic connection carries chat_id + topic_id (top_msg_id); the session is agent-side (ADR-018 D4), so NO saveDraft credential is stored server-side. If this shape strains ADR-016 D4 in any way, this bead RAISES an ADR-016 D4 note explicitly rather than bypassing silently. Do not author an ADR — raise the note and surface it for the session owner to resolve.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Lighter destination record | `direct:` ADR-016 D4 | ADR-016 D4 explicitly targets PlatformConnection; bypassing it without a formal ADR revision is not acceptable. |
| One PlatformConnection per Telegram account, dialogs as sub-records | `reasoned:` | Loses the projection-per-destination model (ADR-016 D4 links projections to connections); each postable target needs its own connection for coverage tracking to work per-destination. |

**What would invalidate this:** a formal revision of ADR-016 D4 that allows a sub-connection model.

### D2 — Names/tags overlay is additive metadata on PlatformConnection; audience-ready data shape
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE** (ADR-003 cheap foresight for audience-readiness; the additive-only constraint is FIRM per ADR-008 D3).
Friendly names and theme tags are stored as overlay metadata on the `PlatformConnection` record (or a related table). They are additive decoration — never message content, never a replacement for the connection identity. The data shape is kept audience-ready (ADR-003): a future Audiences feature can read the same overlay without reshaping.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Names/tags as message content fields | `direct:` ADR-016 content-default | Names/tags are metadata, not content; embedding them in the message body would corrupt the single-shared content model. |

**What would invalidate this:** if Audiences requires a structurally different overlay shape, revisit at the Audiences implementation bead.

### D3 — Picker UI: tree + tag-filter only (no Audiences); forum rows are topic-leaves
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE** (Audiences deferred per ADR-008 D2).
The picker renders the synced inventory as: (a) a tag-filter (theme chips + search); (b) a full categorized tree (Channels / Groups / Forums→Topics). Forums render as flattened "Group > Topic" rows — the forum name is a visual cluster label with NO checkbox (a forum group is not postable; only a specific topic is). Vanished destinations (present in overlay but absent from synced inventory) are flagged loud, not silently shown (ADR-008 D3).

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Forum-level checkbox | `direct:` kb-mztq | A forum group cannot receive a post without a topic_id; a forum-level checkbox lands the draft nowhere or in the wrong topic. |
| Audiences layer now | `direct:` ADR-008 D2 | Deferred until real selection-reuse is observed. |

**What would invalidate this:** if forums routinely have one obvious target topic, an auto-pick-default could reduce rows — but the explicit (group, topic) row stays the safe baseline.

### D4 — Capability-ladder rendering: no-agent shows only bot + public tiers
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE** (UX expression of ADR-018 D1/D4).
When the facilitator has no connected agent, the picker only shows destinations reachable via bot (own/admin channels) + public (deep-link) tiers. Private groups and forum topics are shown as locked/unavailable with an "agent required" indicator — not hidden, not selectable. This makes the capability ladder visible rather than presenting a confusing empty state.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Hide private destinations when no agent | `reasoned:` | Hides available targets on reconnect; the locked state is more legible. |

**What would invalidate this:** if the locked-state UI creates more confusion than the hidden-state alternative, revisit with a real user feedback signal.

## Acceptance contract

The `PlatformConnection`-routed destination model stores each postable Telegram dialog (incl. each forum topic as its own record with chat_id + topic_id) with names/tags overlay. The web picker, read back via live browser automation, renders: the tag-filter + full tree (no Audiences); forum-topic rows as "Group > Topic" with the forum name as a non-interactive label and NO forum-level checkbox; a vanished destination flagged loud (not silently shown); private destinations locked (not hidden) when no agent is connected. Verified by browser read-back.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Browser read-back of the picker against a synced inventory.
- **Expected green:**
  (a) the picker renders the tree + tag layers correctly in a live browser read-back (NOT a Django view-context assertion);
  (b) no forum group appears as a selectable post target — only its topic rows are selectable (the forum-topic trap);
  (c) a destination present in overlay but absent from the synced inventory renders as flagged/vanished (loud, not silectable);
  (d) with no agent connected, private destinations are visible but locked (bot + public only are selectable).
- **Rationale:** The picker is rendered HTML; Django view-context tests pass on broken templates (see `.claude/harness.md` Templates §). Only a live browser read-back confirms the rendered state.
- **Invalidation:** If a forum group renders as a selectable post target, OR a vanished destination renders as selectable, OR the no-agent floor hides private destinations entirely — the model/rendering is wrong.

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-016-outbound-syndication-architecture-event-post-projections.md — D4 (projection → PlatformConnection destination, no bypass), content single-row-default / opt-in divergence
- docs/decisions/ADR-018-channel-push-mechanisms-and-draft-only-mtproto-posture.md — D1 (tiered push), D4 (agent-side session; no server-side saveDraft credential)
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md — D2 (no speculative abstraction: no Audiences layer), D3 (fail-loud: vanished destinations flagged)
- docs/decisions/ADR-003-cheap-foresight-patterns.md — destination model kept audience-ready
- .claude/harness.md — Templates § (browser read-back required for rendered-HTML picker)
- Epic kb-fj4m (parent)

title: Build switch-cli Telegram connect + enumerate + sync (and the server ingest verb)
design:
## Context

This child of epic kb-fj4m builds the agent-side plumbing: QR login into a Telegram account via Telethon, enumeration of all postable dialogs (groups, channels, forum topics), a metadata-only sync push to the server ingest API, and — on distribute — agent-side saveDraft placement into private groups and forum topics (with pre-existing-draft detection).

This is the "local agent" half of the capability ladder (ADR-018 D4). The web cockpit renders from what this child syncs. See kb-fj4m --design for the shared epic context and the open modeling question around PlatformConnection shape.

## Decisions

### D1 — Telethon QR login, reusing the kb-mztq spike pattern
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.**
`switch-cli telegram connect` opens a QR login flow using the kb-mztq spike's validated Telethon approach (api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org + QR code in terminal → reusable StringSession). No phone-code flow (QR is frictionless for desktop). Session stored locally by switch-cli; never uploaded to the server.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Phone-code login | `reasoned:` | More friction, no advantage for a desktop-first CLI tool; QR was proven in the spike. |

**What would invalidate this:** if QR login proves incompatible with the user's account 2FA setup, phone-code becomes the fallback.

### D2 — Enumerate postable dialogs via can-post filter; forum topics as (group, topic) pairs
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.**
After login, enumerate all dialogs and apply the can-post filter (broadcast-channel subscriptions where the user cannot post are excluded). For forum groups, enumerate topics and yield one (group_id, topic_id, topic_title) tuple per topic — the forum group itself is NOT a postable destination. Result: a flat inventory of postable destinations.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Enumerate without can-post filter | `reasoned:` | Would include broadcast channels the user cannot post to — a silent-integrity issue (ADR-008 D3). |

**What would invalidate this:** if Telegram's getDialogs API changes the postability signal, re-validate the filter against live data.

### D3 — Metadata-only sync: push ids/titles/types/topic-ids/postability to server ingest verb; NEVER message content
**Firmness: FIRM** (ADR-018 D4).
The sync payload is metadata only: chat_id, title, type (channel/group/supergroup/forum_topic), topic_id where applicable, and postability flag. No message content, no access_hash, no session data. The co-equal ingest API verb (defined here, owned by C1) receives this inventory and stores it for the web picker (C2) to read.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Sync full dialog objects including access_hash | `direct:` ADR-018 D4 | Access_hash is session-credential material; syncing it to the server violates the agent-side session custody principle. |

**What would invalidate this:** if the web cockpit needs additional metadata fields to render correctly, add them to the inventory schema (keeping the metadata-only principle).

### D4 — saveDraft placement: getDraft check before saveDraft; warn-don't-clobber; forum via reply_to/top_msg_id
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE** (ADR-018 D2 FIRM draft-only; warn behavior FLEXIBLE).
On distribute, for each private group/forum-topic destination: (1) call getDraft to check for a pre-existing draft; (2) if one exists, warn and record `skipped-pre-existing-draft` status — do NOT clobber; (3) if clear, call saveDraft with the message body (and reply_to=top_msg_id for forum topics). The draft-only firewall is FIRM (ADR-018 D2): never call sendMessage or any auto-send variant.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Clobber pre-existing draft silently | `direct:` ADR-008 D3 | Destroying the user's existing draft without warning is a data-integrity violation. |

**What would invalidate this:** if getDraft proves unreliable (flaky, stale), an explicit warn-and-confirm UX replaces the automated check.

## Acceptance contract

`switch-cli telegram connect` completes QR login and stores a reusable session. `switch-cli telegram sync` enumerates all postable dialogs (incl. forum topics as (group, topic) pairs) and pushes a metadata-only inventory to the server ingest API verb (defined here). On distribute, the agent places saveDraft in at least one private group and at least one forum topic; getDraft is checked first and a pre-existing draft produces a `skipped-pre-existing-draft` warning (no clobber); no auto-send occurs. Verified by live dogfood against a real account asserting metadata-only upward sync incl. at least one private group + at least one forum topic; saveDraft places (not sends); pre-existing-draft path warns.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Live dogfood against a real Telegram account.
- **Expected green:**
  (a) QR login completes and the session persists across CLI restarts;
  (b) sync pushes a metadata-only inventory to the server including at least one private group and at least one forum topic;
  (c) the server ingest API verb accepts and stores the inventory (no message content in the payload);
  (d) saveDraft places a draft (not a sent message) in at least one private group and at least one forum topic;
  (e) the pre-existing-draft detection path fires correctly and records `skipped-pre-existing-draft` without clobbering.
- **Rationale:** The spike (kb-mztq) proved the Telethon primitives; this harness proves the integrated CLI flow + server ingest seam. Unit tests cannot replace the live MTProto session test.
- **Invalidation:** If saveDraft silently sends (auto-send), or the sync payload contains message content or session credentials, or pre-existing-draft detection fails to warn — the implementation is wrong.

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-018-channel-push-mechanisms-and-draft-only-mtproto-posture.md — D1 (tiered push), D2 (FIRM draft-only firewall), D4 (agent-side execution + metadata-only sync)
- docs/decisions/ADR-016-outbound-syndication-architecture-event-post-projections.md — D3 (co-equal API: the ingest verb is a co-equal API endpoint)
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md — D3 (fail-loud: warn on pre-existing draft, never clobber)
- Spike kb-mztq (live validation of Telethon saveDraft primitives — closed)
- Epic kb-fj4m (parent)

On distribute, the agent places saveDraft in >=1 private group and >=1 forum topic; getDraft is checked first and a pre-existing draft produces skipped-pre-existing-draft warning (no clobber); no auto-send occurs. Verified live against a real account.

**User-pairing gate:** "Full conjunction coverage" REQUIRES .6 green, and .6 is user-paired (api creds + QR scan + real account) — NOT agent-closeable alone. Children .1–.4 reaching unit-green does NOT close the parent; kb-ru55 closure is gated on the user-paired .6 dogfood.
## Parent re-verify (2026-06-12) — code children .1-.4 conjunction

Fresh-context adversarial re-verify over the cumulative diff of the four closed code children vs parent --design + ADR-018/016/008. **No wire-breaking drift:** sync payload ↔ ingest schema match field-for-field; `type` vocabulary identical across the CLI↔server boundary; ADR-018 D2 draft-only firewall holds across the whole composition (not just draft.py); ADR-018 D4 metadata-only holds on every upward call; connect→sync→distribute session handoff consistent.

Findings + disposition:
- [1] postability was unconstrained server-side → FIXED in kb-ru55.2 (now a 422-guarded TelegramPostability enum, mirroring type). 
- [2] ingest creates kinds=[] connections (inventory-only) → BY DESIGN (picker-selects-destinations); documented in service docstring + flagged on kb-sbhs as its enablement responsibility.
- [3] no single cross-subproject test pins CLI CANONICAL_DIALOG_TYPES == server TelegramDialogType → ACCEPTED: with type+postability both 422-guarded server-side, a CLI vocabulary drift now fails loud at sync time (runtime guard). Static cross-surface test is belt-and-suspenders (subprojects have separate envs).
- [4] no mocked end-to-end (connect→sync→push→distribute) test → ACCEPTED: the live-dogfood child kb-ru55.6 is the designed e2e; review hand-verified the wiring. A pre-live mocked smoke test recommended on .6.

**Parent closure gated on kb-ru55.6 (live dogfood, user-paired) — see below.** All four code children unit-green + fresh-review PASS + conjunction verified.
## Core delivered + dogfooded (2026-06-12)
connect/sync/ingest/distribute verb built (.1-.4), connect QR fix (.7), forum-level draft fix (.8), live dogfood (.6) all closed. Acceptance (a)-(e) verified live against a real account (private group lust berlin + forum topic Sober/Raves&Parties), confirmed in user's Telegram Desktop + independent server read-back. Draft-only firewall (ADR-018 D2) intact. KEY FINDING: top_msg_id-pinned forum drafts are invisible on Telegram Desktop -> forum-level placement adopted; ADR-018 D1 corrected. Remaining (non-blocking): kb-ru55.9 (true per-topic pinning, DEFERRED), firewall-hardening follow-up (forward_messages), multi-topic-same-forum collapse follow-up.

title: Build the Telegram destination-picker + connection-setup UX for the syndication cockpit
design:
## Context

The Telegram distribution cockpit (epic **kb-fj4m**) needs a **destination picker** and the **connection-setup flow** it sits on. Transport + risk are decided (ADR-018): own/admin channels → Bot API; private groups + forum-topics the user can post in → MTProto `saveDraft` placed by a local agent, human sends; public → also a deep-link; draft-only firewall is FIRM. The facilitator earlier reported feeling "lost" in the target hierarchy (channels vs groups vs topics-inside-forum-groups). This bead designs the UX that makes that hierarchy legible and selectable, plus the first-connect flow — the parts the cockpit epic flagged but did not detail.

The picker is the easy half; **getting a user connected is the load-bearing half**, and its custody/execution model is governed by ADR-018 D4 (elaborated 2026-06-11 alongside this brainstorm). This bead is the UX/flow design feeding kb-fj4m; per the standing instruction it is not to be decomposed here.

## Decisions

### D1 — Hybrid destination inventory: live enumeration is truth, persisted overlay decorates it
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.** Every distribution re-enumerates what the user can actually post to (the source of truth, fetched by the local agent's session). A persisted overlay decorates that live set with friendly names, theme tags, audiences, and last-used selections. A saved destination that has vanished from the live set (left the group, topic archived) is **flagged loud, never silently shown** (ADR-008 D3). "Choosing targets" is therefore *not* a setup gate — inclusion is automatic from live enumeration; curation (names/tags/audiences) is continuous in the picker.

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Curated-once cached list | `reasoned:` a purely cached destination list drifts stale (groups/topics change); showing a destination the user can no longer post to is a silent-integrity failure (ADR-008 D3). |
| Live each time, no overlay | `reasoned:` loses presets, friendly names, and tailoring/coverage memory — the efficiency win for recurring fan-out. |

**What would invalidate this:** if live enumeration proves too slow/expensive to run per distribution, a time-boxed cache with explicit staleness surfacing would replace pure-live.

### D2 — Layered picker: saved Audiences → tag filter → full categorized tree
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.** One picker, three zoom levels: **Audiences** (saved named selections — the fast path) on top; a **tag filter** (theme chips + search) in the middle; the full categorized **tree** (Channels / Groups / Forums→Topics — the source of truth, always reachable) at the bottom. The unifying move: **an audience is just a persisted pick-set** — "save this selection as an audience" closes the loop, so presets are a byproduct of doing the work once, not a separate chore. Cold-start dissolves: run one is in the tree; run two is one tap on an audience.

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Tree-only browse | `reasoned:` every event becomes a manual sweep of ~40 destinations — the "lost" feeling, merely structured. |
| Presets-first only | `reasoned:` cold-starts empty (must build the first preset before any value) and is the most to build; the layered model gets there organically. |
| Tags-only, no audiences | `reasoned:` recurring fan-out (same ~8 groups every tantra event) earns a one-tap saved set immediately; tags alone re-do the multi-select each time. |

**What would invalidate this:** if facilitators never reuse selections (every event a unique set), the Audiences layer is dead weight and the picker collapses to tag-filtered tree.

### D3 — Forums render as flattened "Group › Topic" rows; the forum name is a label, never a checkbox
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.** Because a forum *group* is not postable (only a topic inside it is — the draft carries a `topic_id`/`top_msg_id`), the destination's real identity is the **(group, topic) pair**. Each forum-topic is its own selectable row ("Conscious Events Berlin › Love"); the forum name is a visual cluster label with **no checkbox**, so there is nothing non-postable to mis-click. Uniform with plain groups; tags/audiences treat a topic like any other destination. Many-topic forums collapse extras behind "+ N more topics."

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Expandable forum node with a forum-level checkbox | `direct:` (kb-mztq) a forum group cannot receive a post without a topic; a forum-level checkbox is a lie that lands the draft nowhere or in the wrong (General) topic. |
| Check forum → prompt for topic | `reasoned:` two-step per forum, clumsy under multi-select and when replaying a saved audience. |

**What would invalidate this:** if forums routinely have one obvious target topic, an auto-pick-default could reduce rows — but the explicit (group, topic) row stays the safe baseline.

### D4 — Connection setup + execution: web orchestrates and runs the no-session tiers; the local agent runs the private hop (governed by ADR-018 D4)
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE** (UX of an ADR-018 D4 decision). The web is the full cockpit (author, pick, distribute, coverage) and **directly executes the two tiers needing no session** — bot auto-post to own channels, public deep-links. The session-required tier (private groups + forum topics) is executed by the user's **local agent** (`switch-cli`), which holds the MTProto session locally and syncs **destination metadata only** (ids/titles/types/topic-ids/postability — never message content) up to the web picker. Result is a **capability ladder, not a wall**: no agent → bot + public reach from the browser alone; connect an agent → unlock private-community + forum-topic reach. We never custody user sessions; a server-held session is deferred behind explicit opt-in. Setup = (web) add the Switch bot to your own channel [largely exists] + (local) `switch-cli telegram connect` (QR login → enumerate → sync inventory). The framing is **your own account, automated, draft-only — not a "userbot"** (ADR-018 D3).

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Server-held session (web-executes-private) | `reasoned:` concentrates every facilitator's full personal-account Telegram session on the platform — a severe breach/liability surface for a solo operator; a stolen session string is full account control, not draft-only. Deferred opt-in only (ADR-018 D4). |
| CLI-only (no web cockpit) | `reasoned:` non-technical facilitators are shut out of even bot + public reach; co-equal API (ADR-016 D3) wants the web as a first-class client of the orchestration. |

**What would invalidate this:** if local-agent friction provably blocks adoption, revisit the deferred server-held-session opt-in tier (an ADR-018 D4 evolution, eyes open).

### D5 — The picker is selection + coverage only; per-destination content tailoring lives in the composer
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.** The picker does not edit content. Per ADR-016, content is single-shared by default with opt-in per-destination divergence, and that divergence is authored in the composer, not the destination picker. Keeps the picker focused on *where*, the composer on *what*.

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Inline per-destination tailoring in the picker | `reasoned:` conflates *where* with *what*, bloats the picker, and duplicates the composer's divergence affordance (ADR-016 single-row-default / opt-in-divergence). |

**What would invalidate this:** if tailoring is almost always per-destination in practice, merging a lightweight tailor-on-select into the picker could be reconsidered.

### D6 — Coverage confirms "placed", not "sent" (draft-only honesty)
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE.** The machine can confirm a draft was **placed** (the agent's `saveDraft` acked) but **cannot observe the human's native send** (the human's tap in the official app is invisible to us, by the FIRM draft-only firewall). Coverage therefore shows **placed ✓ / failed ✗ / pending** per destination as machine fact, plus a **send-checklist** the facilitator works through (or visually confirms) — never a fabricated "sent" status. Server-confirmed placement is the cockpit's own truth, robust to client display flakiness (the pre-existing-local-draft surfacing anomaly from kb-mztq); detect a pre-existing draft before placing (warn, don't clobber).

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Show a "sent" status | `reasoned:` the send is a native human action outside our observation (ADR-018 D2 firewall); a machine "sent" badge would be fabricated — an ADR-008 D3 silent-integrity violation. |

**What would invalidate this:** if Telegram exposes a read-back that confirms human sends, coverage could add a real "sent" state.

## Acceptance contract

Given a facilitator with the Switch bot on their own channel and a connected local agent: opening the cockpit shows the layered picker (Audiences / tag-filter / tree) populated from live-enumerated postable destinations with the saved overlay applied; forums appear as flattened "Group › Topic" rows with no forum-level checkbox; a vanished destination is flagged, not silently shown. They select a mix (own channel + ≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic), optionally save it as an audience, and distribute: the own channel auto-posts via the bot (web-executed), the private group + forum topic receive agent-placed synced drafts (human sends), public destinations also offer deep-links. Coverage shows placed/failed/pending per destination (never a fake "sent"), with a send-checklist. A facilitator with **no** agent connected still sees and can distribute to bot + public tiers from the browser. Tailoring is absent from the picker (composer owns it).

## Harness target

- **Signal** — end-to-end dogfood against the real account + a live browser read-back of the picker. (a) `switch-cli telegram connect` performs QR login, enumerates dialogs, and syncs the metadata inventory; (b) the web picker, read back via browser-automation (not just a Django view-context assertion), renders the three layers, flattened "Group › Topic" rows with the forum name as a non-interactive label, and a loud flag on a deliberately-removed destination; (c) a real distribution places synced drafts in ≥1 private group and ≥1 forum topic (human-send firewall intact) and bot-posts the own channel; (d) coverage reflects server-confirmed placement and shows no "sent" status; (e) with the agent disconnected, the picker still offers bot + public tiers.
- **Expected green** — all five hold in a live browser + real account: layered picker renders correctly, forum rows are topic-identity leaves with no postable container checkbox, drafts land in the representative private + topic destinations, coverage is placement-truthful, and the no-agent capability floor (bot + public) is reachable.
- **Rationale** — the goal-faithful altitude is a live browser read-back + real fan-out, because (i) the picker is rendered HTML where Django view-context tests pass on broken templates (recurring hollow-test class — see `.claude/harness.md` Templates §), and (ii) the private-draft hop + human-send loop cannot be captured by unit tests (the spike proved the primitives; this proves the integrated UX). Unit tests alone would go green on a picker that mis-renders the forum-topic distinction or fakes a "sent" badge.
- **Invalidation** — if coverage status diverges from server-confirmed placement, or the picker lets a forum group be selected as a target (topic-less draft), or a vanished destination renders as selectable, the inventory/coverage model needs rework. If the no-agent path cannot reach bot+public, the capability-ladder split is wrong.

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-018-channel-push-mechanisms-and-draft-only-mtproto-posture.md — D1 (tiered push), D2 (FIRM draft-only firewall), D3 (under-observation + "not a userbot" framing), **D4 (agent-side execution + capability ladder + metadata-only sync — elaborated 2026-06-11 with this brainstorm)**.
- docs/decisions/ADR-016-outbound-syndication-architecture-event-post-projections.md — D3 (co-equal API: web is a first-class client), D4 (projection → PlatformConnection destination), content single-row-default / opt-in divergence (D5 governs tailoring boundary).
- docs/decisions/ADR-011-personal-agent-layer-additive.md — D1 (agent-extended scope may be agent-only — the private-draft hop).
- docs/decisions/ADR-010-event-based-product-posture.md — Switch own-page is the canonical home; syndication is downstream promotion.
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md — D2 (concrete-not-speculative: audience = persisted pick-set, no preset engine before earned), D3 (fail-loud: vanished destinations flagged, no fake "sent").
- docs/decisions/ADR-003-cheap-foresight-patterns.md — shape the distribute-job seam so a friendly local app / future server-held tier can slot in without reshaping the web side.
- Cockpit epic **kb-fj4m** (this design feeds it). Spike **kb-mztq** (live validation). Depends on **kb-y209** (cover field-parity → card image) + **kb-6d7o** (preview cache-bust → fresh card) for faithful preview.
- `.claude/harness.md` — Templates § (browser read-back catches rendered-template bugs view-context tests miss); "Live spike against a third-party platform API" pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Given the Switch bot on the user's own channel + a connected local agent: the cockpit shows a layered picker (saved Audiences / tag-filter / full tree) populated from live-enumerated postable destinations with a persisted name/tag/audience overlay; forums render as flattened 'Group › Topic' rows with NO forum-level checkbox; a vanished destination is flagged loud, not silently shown. User selects own channel + ≥1 private group + ≥1 forum topic, optionally saves the set as an audience, and distributes: own channel bot-auto-posts (web-executed), private group + forum topic receive agent-placed synced drafts (human sends natively), public destinations also offer deep-links. Coverage shows placed/failed/pending per destination with a send-checklist and NO fabricated 'sent' status. A user with NO agent connected can still see and distribute to bot + public tiers from the browser alone (capability ladder). Tailoring is absent from the picker. Verified via live browser read-back of the picker + an end-to-end real-account dogfood.
notes: Superseded: design distributed into kb-fj4m children kb-ru55 (C1: switch-cli connect+enumerate+sync+ingest), kb-sbhs (C2: destination model+web picker), kb-56c2 (C3: coverage tracker), kb-6yyp (C4: faithful preview) + deferred Audiences kb-gx96 after joint adversarial review (collapsed the picker/cockpit overlap into one epic).

title: Route live event-page og:image through card_image_url resolver (realize the single resolution point; preview==reality)
design:
## Context — discovered at parent re-verify (ADR-008 D4)

kb-6d7o's design premise: events/og.py::card_image_url is THE single card-image resolution point, consumed by BOTH the live event-page og:image AND the studio preview, so preview==reality is structurally guaranteed (ADR-003). Parent re-verify found this is NOT realized: kb-6d7o.1 added a PARALLEL inline implementation in templates/events/detail.html (lines 12-18: {% if cover_image %}...{% else %}{% static 'img/og-default.png' %}{% endif %}) instead of calling the resolver. kb-6d7o.3's preview DOES call card_image_url. So there are two parallel code paths.

Outputs match today for cover events on standard ports, but:
- The no-cover default URL diverges latently: template uses '{scheme}://{get_host}{% static %}' vs resolver's request.build_absolute_uri(static(...)) — different on non-standard ports / SCRIPT_NAME prefix.
- The default path 'img/og-default.png' is hard-coded in the template, parallel to og.py's DEFAULT_OG_IMAGE_STATIC constant — silent drift point.
- The 'preview==reality guaranteed structurally' comments in events/og.py and syndication/views.py are factually false (live page doesn't use the resolver).

## Fix
- events/views.py event_detail: compute og_card_image_url = card_image_url(event, request) and add to template context.
- templates/events/detail.html: replace the {% if cover_image %}...{% else %}...{% endif %} og:image block with a SINGLE line: <meta property="og:image" content="{{ og_card_image_url }}" /> (no branching, no hard-coded path). Keep the PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED gate.
- Fix the now-true comments in events/og.py and syndication/views.py (they ARE structurally guaranteed once live page uses the resolver).

## canonical_refs
- ADR-003 (single resolution point — the guarantee this realizes)
- ADR-008 D2 (extract-at-third-caller — live page + preview are now 2 callers of one resolver, not 2 implementations), D4 (discovered-from)

## Harness target
- **Signal:** uv run pytest events/tests/test_og_meta.py syndication/ -k 'og_image or card or preview'
- **Expected green:** the live event detail page's rendered og:image content EQUALS card_image_url(event, request) for BOTH a cover event and a no-cover event (exact equality, not substring); existing og + preview tests stay green.
- **Rationale:** preview==reality is only real if the live tag and the resolver produce byte-identical URLs; an exact-equality test (not substring) is the only assertion that proves the single resolution point.
- **Invalidation:** hollow if the test asserts a substring (e.g. just the filename) instead of exact equality to the resolver output; or if detail.html still branches on cover_image / hard-codes the default path.
acceptance_criteria: The live public event detail page's og:image is produced by events/og.py::card_image_url (the view passes card_image_url(event, request) to context; detail.html emits a single <meta property="og:image"> with no cover/default branching and no hard-coded default path). A test asserts the rendered live og:image content is byte-EQUAL to card_image_url(event, request) for both a cover event and a no-cover event. The misleading 'structurally guaranteed' comments in events/og.py and syndication/views.py are now accurate. Existing og + preview tests stay green.
close_reason: Live event-page og:image now routes through events.og.card_image_url (view passes og_card_image_url; detail.html emits a single <meta og:image> with no branching/hard-coded path). Both live page + studio preview consume the one resolver — single resolution point realized (ADR-003), preview==reality structurally guaranteed. Exact-equality regression test (rendered og:image == resolver output, cover + no-cover) guards future drift; misleading comments corrected. Discovered at parent re-verify (ADR-008 D4). Harness green: 43 og/card/preview tests; events/+syndication/ 1343 passed. Committed 7dfa238.

title: Telegram distribution cockpit — faithful preview + tiered fan-out (bot / saveDraft incl. private groups & topics / deep-link) as UI + agent
design:
## Context

Slice-1 of the Typefully-grade syndication UX: a **Telegram distribution cockpit**. The job-to-be-done — author an event once → faithful per-destination preview → fan out to the facilitator's own channel plus their (mostly private) community groups and forum topics → track coverage. Authoring (studio composer), the Event/Post/PlatformProjection model, and the co-equal HTTP API already exist. This epic builds the full distribution cockpit + agent-side saveDraft driver.

The transport mechanics and risk posture were validated live (spike **kb-mztq**) and canonicalized in **ADR-018**. The destination-picker and connection-setup UX was jointly designed with adversarial review (brainstorm 2026-06-11, picker bead kb-ethw superseded into this epic after the designs converged into one coherent scope). This epic decomposes into four children (C1–C4) plus a deferred Audiences bead.

**Open modeling question (to be resolved by C1/C2, not here):** A facilitator has ONE Telegram account but MANY postable dialogs — groups, private channels, and individual forum topics inside forum-groups. The open question is whether each postable dialog (or each forum topic) should be its own `PlatformConnection` record (carrying chat_id + optional topic_id, and NO server-side saveDraft credential since the session is agent-side per ADR-018 D4) or whether another shape better fits. C2 resolves this; if the chosen shape strains ADR-016 D4, C2 RAISES an ADR-016 D4 note rather than bypassing silently.

## Decisions

### D1 — Tiered delivery per destination
**Firmness: FIRM** (governed by ADR-018 D1/D2).
- Own/admin channels → Bot API auto-post (web-executed).
- Postable groups, supergroups, forum-topics (incl. private) → MTProto `saveDraft` placed by the local agent; human sends on their official client (draft-only firewall is FIRM, ADR-018 D2).
- Public destinations → also a zero-auth deep-link convenience.
- Capability ladder: no agent → bot + public tiers from the browser alone; connect an agent → unlock private-community + forum-topic reach.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Server-held MTProto session | `reasoned:` | Concentrates every facilitator's full personal-account session on the platform — severe breach/liability for a solo operator. Deferred opt-in only (ADR-018 D4). |
| Agent-only, no web cockpit | `reasoned:` | Non-technical facilitators cannot reach even bot + public tiers; co-equal API (ADR-016 D3) demands the web as a first-class client. |

**What would invalidate this:** if local-agent friction provably blocks adoption, the deferred server-held-session opt-in tier (ADR-018 D4 evolution) becomes the re-evaluation path.

### D2 — Destinations route through PlatformConnection (no bypass)
**Firmness: FIRM** (governed by ADR-016 D4).
All destinations — channels, groups, forum topics — are `PlatformConnection` records. The "or a lighter destination record" hedge from the old epic design is DELETED. Names/tags overlay is additive metadata on top of the `PlatformConnection` record, never a replacement or a message-content field. The open modeling question (one connection per dialog vs. another shape) is resolved by C2; if that resolution strains ADR-016 D4, C2 files a note rather than silently bypassing.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Lighter destination record | `direct:` ADR-016 D4 | ADR-016 D4 explicitly targets PlatformConnection; a lighter record is a bypass, not a shortcut. |

**What would invalidate this:** if ADR-016 D4 is formally revised, the destination model follows.

### D3 — Coverage status set: {placed, failed, pending, skipped-pre-existing-draft} + send-checklist
**Firmness: FIRM** (governed by ADR-008 D3 / ADR-018 D2).
The machine can confirm a draft was placed (`saveDraft` acked, server-confirmed) but cannot observe the human's native send. Coverage therefore shows exactly four machine-observable states plus a send-checklist — never a fabricated "sent" badge. Pre-existing-draft detection: getDraft check before saveDraft; warn, don't clobber; produces `skipped-pre-existing-draft` status.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Show a "sent" status | `direct:` ADR-008 D3 | The send is a native human action outside our observation; a machine "sent" badge is fabricated state. |

**What would invalidate this:** if Telegram exposes a read-back that confirms human sends, a real "sent" state becomes possible.

### D4 — Faithful preview is READ-ONLY; may embed in the picker
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE** (F7 review finding).
The faithful preview renders the message as it will land per destination type (channel-post format vs. group message + link-preview card). It is READ-ONLY; preview does not equal tailoring, so embedding it in the picker does not violate ADR-016 content-editing boundaries. Depends on kb-y209 (cover field-parity) + kb-6d7o (cache-bust/preview card) for a correct, fresh card.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Preview implies tailoring controls | `reasoned:` | Conflates *where* (picker) with *what* (composer); ADR-016 governs tailoring in the composer. |

**What would invalidate this:** if facilitators routinely need per-destination content customization at preview time, tailoring-in-picker is a composer-scope change, not a preview change.

### D5 — Audiences (saved destination sets) deferred
**Firmness: FIRM** (governed by ADR-008 D2).
Ship tree + tag-filter only. The Audiences layer (saved named pick-sets) is deferred until at least one real selection-reuse is observed in production. The destination model in C2 is kept audience-ready (ADR-003 cheap foresight) so the data shape does not need reshaping when Audiences ships.

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Ship Audiences now | `direct:` ADR-008 D2 | No speculative behavioral abstraction before the need is earned. |

**What would invalidate this:** observing at least one real selection-reuse in production (the gating condition for the deferred Audiences bead).

### D6 — Server-side sync ingest API verb (co-equal, agent-calls-web)
**Firmness: FLEXIBLE** (governed by ADR-016 D3).
The agent syncs metadata-only inventory (ids, titles, types, topic-ids, postability flags — NEVER message content) up to the web cockpit via a co-equal API ingest verb. The web picker reads from this server-side inventory for rendering; the agent is the sole writer. This is the metadata-only sync spine that connects C1 (agent enumerates + pushes) to C2 (web picker reads + renders).

| Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Agent calls Telegram directly per distribution; no server sync | `reasoned:` | The web cockpit cannot render the picker without a server-side inventory; the co-equal API is the integration seam (ADR-016 D3). |

**What would invalidate this:** if real-time agent enumeration per distribution is fast enough to replace the synced inventory, a live-enumerate-on-open model could replace the sync verb.

## Acceptance contract

A facilitator with the Switch bot on their own channel and a connected local agent: opens the distribution cockpit, sees the picker (tag-filter + full tree, no Audiences layer yet) populated from the synced postable destination inventory; forums render as flattened "Group > Topic" rows with NO forum-level checkbox; a vanished destination is flagged loud, not silently shown. They select a mix (own channel + at least one private group + at least one forum topic) and distribute: the own channel auto-posts via the bot (web-executed), the private group + forum topic receive agent-placed synced drafts the facilitator reviews and sends natively; coverage shows {placed, failed, pending, skipped-pre-existing-draft} per destination with a send-checklist and NO fabricated "sent" status. A facilitator with NO agent connected still sees and can distribute to bot + public tiers from the browser alone (capability ladder). Tailoring is absent from the picker. A faithful per-destination-type preview (READ-ONLY) renders the card as it will land.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** End-to-end dogfood against a real account + live browser read-back.
- **Expected green** requires ALL of:
  (a) picker renders the tree + tag layers (no Audiences) correctly in a live browser read-back;
  (b) forum rows are topic-leaves with NO selectable forum-level post target (the forum name is a visual label only);
  (c) synced drafts land in at least one private group AND at least one forum topic with the human-send firewall intact (no auto-send);
  (d) bot posts the own channel (Bot API, web-executed);
  (e) coverage is placement-truthful including a `skipped-pre-existing-draft` case, and shows NO "sent" status;
  (f) the no-agent capability floor reaches bot + public tiers from the browser alone.

title: Embed versioned ?v=<rev> canonical Switch URL in Telegram promotion body at publish-freeze; bump publish_rev on (re)publish, not on pre-publish edits
design:
## Context
**Send-sequence fact (load-bearing — caught in review R2):** `publish_telegram_promotion` calls `render_projection(projection)` while status is still `ready` (adapters.py:260), builds the payload (adapters.py:264), sends it, and ONLY THEN calls `transition_status(projection, "published")` (adapters.py:331). So the body Telegram receives is the `draft→ready` frozen body — the `ready→published` re-freeze happens AFTER the send and never reaches Telegram. Therefore the versioned URL + rev must be in the `draft→ready` freeze, and the test must assert the sent payload, not the post-publish snapshot.

`_compose_promotion_body(post, platform)` (engine.py:176-186) composes headline/body/cta and embeds NO URL today; `post.cta` is blank in v0. The promotion chain is `PlatformProjection(kind=promotion).source_post → Post.event → Event` (models.py:121-136, 373-439). `publish_event` (events/services.py:16) is first-publish-idempotent with NO Event-level republish hook — so rev lives on the PROJECTION.

## Decisions
- **rev = `PlatformProjection.publish_rev`** (NOT on Event). Bump sites = the body-freezes that feed a send: the `draft→ready` branch of `transition_status` (engine.py ~92-99) and `republish_projection`'s re-materialize (services.py:1438). NOT bumped at `ready→published` (that re-freeze happens after the send; bumping there would desync the sent body's rev from the snapshot) and NOT on draft ContentVersion edits (ADR-016 D2 freeze rule). Factor `_bump_publish_rev(projection)`, called immediately BEFORE `_materialize_effective_fields` at each freeze site so the frozen body carries the bumped rev.
- **Path-completeness (verified R3):** every send-producing path routes through a bump+embed freeze site. First-publish: `draft→ready` (freeze+bump) then `publish_projection`→adapter sends the ready body. Direct-publish (`publish_projection_direct`, services.py:1527-1533) routes draft→`approve_projection`(→`transition_status("ready")` freeze+bump)→`publish_projection`→adapter — so it IS covered. `draft→published` is NOT a legal transition (engine.py `_LEGAL_TRANSITIONS`). Edit-after-publish: `republish_projection` re-materialize+bump.
- **URL embedding** lives in the promotion branch of `_materialize_effective_fields` (where the projection — thus `source_post.event` + `publish_rev` — is in scope), appended to the composed body so every freeze embeds the current rev. Because rev is stable between the `draft→ready` bump and the later `ready→published` re-freeze, the sent body and the post-publish snapshot carry the SAME `?v=` (consistent).
- **Canonical URL** via `reverse("event-detail", kwargs={"org_slug": event.organizer.slug, "event_slug": event.slug})` — route name confirmed at events/urls.py:12 (hyphen `event-detail`). NOTE: events/sitemap.py:39 calls `reverse("event_detail")` (underscore) — a pre-existing latent bug; do NOT copy it (follow-up filed). Make absolute via the EXISTING `settings.SITE_URL` (a_core/settings.py:92 — already present with a default; do NOT add a new setting). Append `?v=<publish_rev>`.
- **Republish re-dispatch is OUT OF SCOPE / deferred** (matches the existing v0 deferral at services.py:1480-1489): `republish_projection` re-materializes + bumps rev but does NOT re-send to Telegram. Child C delivers the rev + URL-in-frozen-body so re-dispatch (when it lands) carries the right URL; the actual Telegram re-send on republish is a follow-up bead. End-to-end "edited event's card refreshes" requires that follow-up.
- Versioned-URL is THE cache-bust mechanism (ADR-008 D2, one path) — no WebpageBot, no manual refresh.
- Adding the URL changes the posted promotion message (previously URL-less); any existing promotion-body test asserting exact body content must be updated as part of this child.

## canonical_refs
- ADR-016 D5 (`republish_projection` edit-after-publish path), D2 (freeze rule; frozen_content freeze sites)
- ADR-010 D1 (canonical Switch event URL is the embedded target)
- ADR-008 D2 (single mechanism; inline reverse, no premature extraction)

## File claims
- `syndication/models.py` (+ migration in syndication/migrations/: `PlatformProjection.publish_rev`)
- `syndication/engine.py` (`_bump_publish_rev` + draft→ready bump + promotion freeze URL-embed)
- `syndication/services.py` (`republish_projection` bump; verify `publish_projection_direct` freeze path)
- `syndication/tests/test_promotion_url.py` (new)
- updates to any existing promotion-body test asserting exact body
- (Reads `event.organizer.slug` / `event.slug` read-only — no `events/` edits.)

## Harness target
- **Signal:** `uv run pytest syndication/ -k "publish_rev or versioned or cache_bust or promotion_url"`
- **Expected green:** (1) FIRST-PUBLISH: mocking the Bot API HTTP send in `publish_telegram_promotion`, the sent payload text contains the canonical event URL + `?v=<publish_rev>`; (2) REPUBLISH: after an edit-after-publish, `republish_projection` increments `publish_rev` and the re-materialized `frozen_content["body"]` carries the new `?v=` (frozen body is the correct observable — re-send is deferred); (3) a draft ContentVersion edit leaves `publish_rev` unchanged.
- **Rationale:** cache-bust correctness IS the rev-bump-at-send contract; first-publish is observable in the actual Bot API payload (the message Telegram receives), republish in the re-frozen body (re-send deferred).
- **Invalidation:** hollow if the FIRST-PUBLISH assertion targets the post-`published` frozen snapshot instead of the sent payload (would pass even if Telegram got no URL); or asserts `publish_rev` increments without asserting `?v=` in the body; or bumps on a draft edit.
acceptance_criteria: A new PlatformProjection.publish_rev (PositiveIntegerField, default 0) increments by 1 at each body-freeze that feeds a send — on the draft->ready freeze (in transition_status) and on the republish_projection re-materialize — and does NOT change on a draft ContentVersion edit. The canonical absolute Switch event URL (built from source_post.event via the event-detail route) carrying ?v=<publish_rev> is embedded into the promotion body at freeze, so it is present in the body the Telegram adapter actually sends. Covered by tests asserting: (1) FIRST-PUBLISH — against the body the adapter SENDS (Bot API payload text, mocked HTTP send in publish_telegram_promotion, NOT the post-publish snapshot): the sent payload contains the canonical event URL with ?v=<rev>; (2) REPUBLISH — republish_projection increments publish_rev AND the re-materialized frozen_content['body'] carries the new ?v= (republish is re-freeze-only in v0; actual Telegram re-dispatch is a deferred follow-up, so the frozen body is the correct observable); (3) a draft ContentVersion edit leaves publish_rev unchanged.
notes:
## Review correction (post-impl, 2026-06-11)

Fresh-context review found two Important issues; design tightened:
1. **Telegram-gate the URL embed.** The ?v= versioned URL is a Telegram-link-preview cache-bust artifact. Embed ONLY for telegram promotion projections (guard on projection.connection.platform == 'telegram') — not the platform-agnostic promotion branch. Non-telegram (fetlife/switch) promotion bodies stay unchanged.
2. **Fail loud on missing organizer (ADR-008 D3).** When a telegram promotion's event lacks the organizer/slug needed to build the event-detail URL, RAISE at the freeze site with a clear message — do NOT silently omit the URL (silent omission = the cache-bust silently fails with no error).
close_reason: Versioned ?v=<publish_rev> URL embedded in the Telegram promotion frozen body; publish_rev bumps on draft->ready freeze + republish_projection, not on ready->published or draft edits. Telegram-gated (non-telegram promotion bodies unchanged); fails loud per ADR-008 D3 on organizer-less telegram promotions. First-publish test asserts the SENT Bot API payload; republish test asserts re-frozen body. Reviewed fresh-context (REVISE x1: telegram-gate + D3 raise -> both fixed). Harness green: 15 passed; full syndication suite 1159 passed. Committed 3e4597a. Follow-ups: kb-rsl4 (republish Telegram re-dispatch), kb-wd6e (sitemap reverse-name bug).

title: API event field-handling rigor: PATCH null-clear semantics + enum validation (co-equal + fail-loud residuals from kb-y209)
design:
## Context

Surfaced by the kb-y209 parent re-verify (conjunction-drift pass over the cover/field-parity epic). These are PRE-EXISTING API-rigor gaps that kb-y209 exposed but did not introduce — kb-y209.3 (venue+tags) made the API strictly better (you can now SET venue; bad ids fail loud), but two adjacent residuals remain on the API event surface that the web form does not share. Filed rather than inline-fixed to avoid scope-creeping kb-y209 into an API-semantics redesign.

## Residual 1 — PATCH cannot null-clear optional fields (ADR-016 D3 co-equal)

`events_update` (syndication/api.py ~740) filters `patch_kwargs` with `if v is not None`, so `PATCH {"venue": null}` (or `age_restriction`, `capacity`, `end`, etc.) silently drops the key — there is no API path to CLEAR an optional field to null. The web form CAN clear (e.g. blank venue → clean_venue returns None → update_event sets venue=None). So agent ≠ web for the clear operation. Also no `DELETE /events/{id}/cover` to remove a cover (web can only replace, so cover is symmetric-ish, but the agent can't remove either). Decide a PATCH null-clear convention (e.g. an explicit sentinel, or accept null-means-clear for a named subset) consistent with ADR-016 D3.

## Residual 2 — API accepts unvalidated enum strings (ADR-008 D3 fail-loud + enum-drift)

`EventCreateIn`/`EventUpdateIn` type `category`/`visibility`/`language`/`currency` as bare `str` with no validation against the canonical choices. So `category="party_play"` (a typo) is silently accepted and stored — the web form's ChoiceField rejects this. This contradicts ADR-008 D3 (fail loud on invalid data) on the API surface and is exactly the `adr-enum-vocabulary-drift-invisible-per-bead` trap. Additionally `EventForm.CATEGORY_CHOICES` and `Event.CATEGORY_CHOICES` are not co-defined against a shared constant (forms.py:217 carries a `""` option the model choices don't). Validate API enum fields against the canonical vocabulary; consider co-defining the choice lists.

## Decisions

- **FLEXIBLE** — both are API-side rigor improvements on syndication/api.py; the web form is already correct. Fix-loud and parity-restore per the cited ADRs.

## Acceptance contract

API PATCH can clear an optional event field to null via an agreed convention (co-equal with the web form's clear). API event create/update reject invalid enum values for category/visibility/language with a 4xx (fail loud), validated against the canonical choices. Enum choice lists co-defined (no form/model drift).

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-016-*.md D3 (co-equal API)
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-*.md D3 (fail loud, no silent accept of invalid data)
acceptance_criteria: API PATCH can clear an optional event field to null via an agreed convention (co-equal with the web form's clear). API event create/update reject invalid enum values for category/visibility/language with a 4xx (fail loud, validated against canonical choices). Enum choice lists co-defined (no form/model drift).

title: Add venue + tags to event API schemas (EventCreateIn/UpdateIn/Out) for ADR-016 D3 co-equal parity
design:
## Context

Parent: kb-y209. ADR-016 D3 co-equal API parity is violated: the web `EventForm` accepts `venue` (id → Venue, `forms.py` clean_venue ~82-97) and `tags` (comma slugs → Tag pks, clean_tags ~99-112), but the API schemas `EventCreateIn` / `EventUpdateIn` / `EventOut` (`syndication/api.py` ~410-503) **omit both**. An agent cannot set or read back venue/tags. `update_event` / `create_event` services (`services.py` ~418, ~479) ALREADY accept `venue` + `tags` kwargs — so this is purely an API schema + handler-resolution gap, no service change.

## Decisions

- **FLEXIBLE** — add `venue: int | None = None` and `tags: list[str] | None = None` to `EventCreateIn` and `EventUpdateIn`; add venue + tags to `EventOut` readback (e.g. `venue_id` + `tags` list). In the create/update handlers, resolve venue-id → Venue and tag-slugs → Tag pks before calling the service, mirroring `clean_venue` / `clean_tags`.
- **ADR-008 D3 (fail loud)** — an invalid/unknown `venue` id must fail loud at the API (4xx), NOT silently drop to None — mirroring `clean_venue` raising ValidationError. Unknown tag slugs follow the form's lenient skip (tags are optional, no hard fail).

## File claims

- `syndication/api.py`
- `syndication/test_co_equal_api.py`
- `syndication/test_api.py`

## Harness target

- **Signal:** `uv run pytest syndication/test_co_equal_api.py syndication/test_api.py -k "venue or tags or co_equal"`
- **Expected green:** new tests assert, with a **DB round-trip** (not schema-shape only): (a) POST/PATCH an event with a `venue` id persists `Event.venue`; (b) POST/PATCH with `tags` slugs persists the `Event.tags` M2M; (c) `GET` (EventOut) returns the venue + tags that were written (read-back parity); (d) POST/PATCH with an **invalid venue id returns 4xx** (fail-loud error path, not a silent drop).
- **Rationale:** API parity is exactly an HTTP request/response + DB-persistence contract; pytest over the Ninja test client is the precise harness. The 4xx error-path is a named acceptance bullet and must have its own assertion.
- **Invalidation:** hollow if tests assert Pydantic schema acceptance only without round-tripping through `update_event` to the DB and back via `EventOut`, OR if the invalid-venue-id 4xx path is not asserted.
acceptance_criteria: POST/PATCH to the event API endpoints accepts venue (id) and tags (list of slugs); update_event/create_event persist them; EventOut reads venue + tags back (read-back parity). An invalid venue id fails loud (4xx), not a silent drop. Verified by DB-round-trip tests in syndication/test_co_equal_api.py + test_api.py — co-equal with the web form's venue/tags handling.

## Context

- **ADR-010 D1** — the Switch card IS the canonical listing/edit surface.

title: Telegram link-preview card: cache-bust on publish + default og:image fallback
design:
## Context

Verified 2026-06-11: switch.berlin event pages are reachable by Telegram's crawler past the age-gate (cookieless GET w/ Telegram UA -> 200, no redirect, OG tags present; gated on `PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED`, on in prod). Two card-quality problems surfaced live:

1. **Stale cache.** Telegram caches link previews per-URL aggressively. An event page crawled earlier (serving `_base.html` default site-level meta) shows a STALE card even after correct event-specific OG tags deploy. Telegram won't re-fetch on its own.
2. **No image without a cover.** `og:image` only emits when the event has a cover image. No currently-published event has one, so cards carry no event image.

## Decided strategy (2026-06-11, confirmed by user)

**Cache-bust = versioned URL param.** @WebpageBot automation ruled OUT: it has no Bot API, our backend bot cannot message it (bot-to-bot needs mutual opt-in it hasn't enabled), and the only programmatic path is an MTProto userbot driving a real account — against Telegram's automation rules. Decision: when we syndicate an event to Telegram, the embedded Switch event URL carries a `?v=<rev>` param where `<rev>` strictly increases on each (re)publish and does NOT bump on pre-publish edits. Telegram caches per full URL, so a new rev forces a fresh crawl -> current OG card. Per ADR-008 D2 (simplest mechanism, one path) — no WebpageBot ping, no manual-refresh action.

- Version key: a monotonic publish revision that bumps on each ready->published transition; pre-publish edits do not bump. Implementer picks the cleanest tie-in to the existing projection/event publish model (events/services.py:16 publish_event is first-publish-idempotent on published_at, so a dedicated publish-revision counter is likely needed).

**Default og:image fallback.** When an event has no cover image, emit a site-level default OG card image (~1200x630, asset to be created — current static/img/logo.png is 705 bytes, too small). ADR-008 D3-clean: 'event has no cover' is a fact, not a data-integrity error (cf. zero-reviews-is-a-fact precedent in the D3 audit) — intentional branding default, not silent masking.

**High-fidelity studio preview.** The Telegram studio preview must render the actual link-preview CARD (image incl. default fallback, og:title, og:description) — not just the message body. Today the preview (templates/syndication/fragments/_channel_preview.html:26-42) is message-body-only, so authors can't see the card and get surprised on Telegram. The card-image resolver (default-fallback logic) is SHARED between the live event-page og:image (templates/events/detail.html:6-18) and the studio preview so preview == reality.

## Discovery (load-bearing)

The Telegram promotion body (`_compose_promotion_body`, syndication/engine.py:176-186) currently embeds NO event URL — only headline/body/cta. The versioned Switch URL must be embedded in the syndicated post for the cache-bust (and the link-preview card itself) to apply. URL-embedding is a mechanic of the approved versioned-param mechanism, not a separate decision.

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-016-*.md D5 (publish lifecycle), D2 (ContentVersion freeze rule)
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-*.md D3 (fail loud / no silent stale), D2 (simplest mechanism, one path)
- docs/decisions/ADR-012-*.md D3 (public tier robot-indexing — only public events' cards reach the crawler)
acceptance_criteria:
(a) Cache-bust strategy decided + documented in --design — DONE.
(b) An event with no cover image renders og:image = the site-level default on its public event detail page (PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED on).
(c) The syndicated Telegram post embeds the Switch event URL with a ?v=<rev> param; republishing the event bumps rev; pre-publish edits do not bump it.
(d) The Telegram studio preview renders a link-preview card mockup (image incl. default-when-no-cover, og:title, og:description) matching what Telegram will render, driven by the SAME image-resolution logic as the live event page.

## Harness target
pytest. Expected-green: tests asserting (1) no-cover event detail emits og:image = site default; (2) syndicated Telegram URL carries ?v=, and the rev bumps across a republish but not across a pre-publish edit; (3) the studio preview fragment renders the card image (default when no cover) + title + desc.
