title: Spike: validate Telegram fan-out mechanics live (deep-link prefill, unfurl card, bot own-channel post)
design:
## Context

Moving syndication toward Typefully-grade UX, the first vertical slice is Telegram: faithful per-channel preview + a "distribution cockpit" that fans one authored event/post out to a facilitator's own channel (auto, via bot) and the community groups they're a member of (one-tap deep-link for public, copy-paste for private), with an opt-in userbot automation tier seam designed-for-but-deferred.

The cockpit design rests on several Telegram client behaviors that two doc-research passes confirmed *in spec* but which must be confirmed *in a live client* before building (per user-pref "study it live, don't design from memory"). The research agent itself flagged that client behavior can drift from spec and that `?text=` prefill is conditioned on "if the user can write in the chat."

This is a validation spike: kill the load-bearing unknowns hands-on against the user's own Telegram + throwaway test fixtures, driven via Telegram Web (browser-automation) so the user's involvement is ~one QR login. Findings feed the slice-1 cockpit bead.

## Decisions (under test — this spike confirms or corrects them)

- FLEXIBLE — Destination model = own/admin channels (bot auto-post) + groups the facilitator is a member of (public = one-tap `t.me/<username>?text=` open-with-draft; private = copy-paste). Subscriber-only broadcast channels drop out (can't post). Invalidation: if deep-link prefill doesn't work live, the "one-tap" tier collapses to copy-paste everywhere.
- FLEXIBLE — Cover image rides as a link-preview card via the event page's OG tags (og:image/title confirmed present in templates/events/detail.html), not a manually-attached photo. Invalidation: Telegram's crawler can't fetch the page past the age-gate → blank card → need a different image strategy.
- FLEXIBLE — Tier-1 bot posts to the facilitator's own channel as a native channel post (channel name shown, bot hidden) via the existing adapter + PlatformConnection connect UI. Invalidation: post shows bot identity / fails.

## Acceptance contract

Each of the six unknowns below has a documented finding (yes/no + evidence, marked Web-only where applicable), captured in the spike bead and ready to feed the slice-1 cockpit design:

- A. `t.me/<public-group-username>?text=…` opens that exact chat with an editable, non-auto-sent draft.
- B. Same prefill works in the facilitator's own channel (admin/can-write) — the "if user can write" condition.
- C. Private group has no open-with-draft path → copy-paste is the honest fallback (note the friction).
- D. A public Switch event URL unfurls into a card (cover image + title) AND Telegram's crawler reaches the page past the age-gate.
- E. The Switch bot, added as admin to the test channel + connected via the existing UI, posts a native channel post.
- F. Reference screenshots of the real rendered channel post + unfurl card captured as the pixel target for the faithful preview.

## Harness target

- Signal: live Telegram Web session driven via browser-automation (nav to deep-links, eval composer state, paste URL, read unfurl DOM, screenshot) + a real publish fired through the existing Telegram adapter against a connected test channel.
- Expected green: A–F each resolved with concrete observed evidence (DOM/screenshot/sent-message), not doc-spec inference.
- Rationale: the goal-faithful altitude is observed client behavior, not unit tests or doc reading — the whole point of the spike is that spec ≠ live client. Telegram Web is the altitude I can drive autonomously; mobile-only deltas get flagged for a 30-sec phone confirm rather than blocking.
- Invalidation: if Telegram Web diverges materially from mobile on the prefill behavior (A/B), the Web finding is non-authoritative and must be re-confirmed on a native client before the cockpit is built.

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-016-*.md D3 — co-equal API (cockpit must be reachable by agent + UI alike); D4 — PlatformConnection owned by organizer.
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-*.md D2 (concrete per-channel, no speculative abstraction), D3 (fail loud on render/fetch error).
- docs/decisions/ADR-017-*.md D1 — agent is the user's delegate (relevant to the deferred userbot tier).
acceptance_criteria: Each of A-F has a documented live finding (yes/no + observed evidence, Web-only marked): A deep-link prefill opens public group with editable draft; B prefill works in own channel; C private group = copy-paste fallback; D event URL unfurls to card past age-gate; E bot posts native channel post via existing adapter; F reference screenshots captured. Findings feed the slice-1 Telegram cockpit design.
notes:
SPIKE FINDINGS (2026-06-11, driven via cookieless crawler probe + Telegram Web):

D (unfurl past age-gate) — CONFIRMED HARD. Cookieless GET of real event page (switch.berlin/events/iksk-berlin/turning-men-into-furniture-jun-2026/) with Telegram crawler UA returned HTTP 200, 0 redirects, OG tags present (og:title/description/type/url). Age-gate does NOT block the crawler (og block gated on PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED, on in prod). CAVEAT: og:image is conditional on event cover_image; NONE of currently-published events have a cover, so today's card is title+description only (no image). Image strategy works mechanically but needs cover-setting driven at authoring, or a default OG image fallback.

A/B (deep-link t.me/<username>?text= prefill) — SPEC-CONFIRMED; native-only. Telegram Web cannot faithfully reproduce native deep-link prefill, so a faithful test needs a ~60s phone tap (pending from user). Spec (core.telegram.org/api/links) says yes, conditioned on user-can-write.

C (private group no deep-link) — SETTLED by logic. Private groups have no @username → no t.me/<username> to address → copy-paste is the only path.

E (bot native channel post) — DEFERRED. Local TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is a 401 placeholder; adapter can't fire locally. Needs real prod token (or run against prod). sendMessage path already covered by green suite; only live unknown is appearance (channel posts hide bot unless sign-messages on — standard TG behavior).

F (reference capture) — Got editorial event-page screenshot. TG card render derivable from confirmed OG tags; visual card screenshot deferred (webk automation low-ROI).
RESOLUTION (2026-06-11, native tests via Telegram Desktop tg:// + user glances):

title: Persist the active channel tab across a full page reload
design:
Recon A2. The active channel tab is Alpine client-state (selectedPk on the composer shell, templates/syndication/fragments/event_syndication.html and post_syndication.html) with no URL or server persistence. Any full page reload, or a deep-link, drops the user back to the first/Master tab. (Distinct from kb-kgza.11 which locked tab persistence across the publish HTMX swap as a separate, already-handled case. this is the full-reload case.)

Fix (simplest thing that fits, ADR-008 D2). thread the selected channel through a URL query param (e.g. ?channel=<pk>). Alpine inits selectedPk from the param on load and updates it on tab switch via history.replaceState, so reload and deep-link both restore the active tab. URL-param beats a server/session store here. it is lighter AND makes channel tabs deep-linkable for free. Apply to both the event and post composer shells (watch for the inline-twin pattern between them).

canonical_refs. ADR-008 D2 (simplest thing that fits).
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a channel tab updates the URL (?channel=<pk> or equivalent). Reloading the page, or opening the deep-link directly, restores that channel as the active tab. A stale or invalid channel param (a pk that no longer exists on this publishable, e.g. after a channel is removed) falls back gracefully to the default/first tab, never a blank editor. Works on both event and post composers. Existing publish-swap tab persistence (kb-kgza.11) not regressed. Verified live. select a non-default channel tab, reload, the same tab is active.
notes:
## Harness target
Signal: live browser verification (Alpine client-state) is primary. plus a pytest/template assertion that the composer shell wires selectedPk from a URL param. Expected green: reload restores the selected tab in the browser. Rationale: tab state is client-side, so the authoritative signal is a real reload in the browser, not a server test. Invalidation: if the composer moves to server-rendered per-tab routes, the persistence mechanism changes.
close_reason: Fixed in 14777b0. Active channel tab now persists across full reload + deep-link via ?channel=<pk> URL param. Alpine x-init IIFE reads the param, validates against the rendered pk list (validPks for events, validKeys incl 'source' for posts) so a stale/removed channel falls back to the server-seeded default tab, never blank; setTab() helper writes the param via history.replaceState on every tab click. Applied symmetrically to both event_syndication.html and post_syndication.html. Existing kb-kgza.11 publish-swap persistence (selected_pk server var + hidden input) preserved. 11 wiring tests + full suite 1077 passed, ruff + djlint green. Diff verified: Alpine expressions syntactically valid, no Django/JS quote collision. Live browser confirmation in the epic's final validation phase.

title: Make the sync-state banner honest per channel state (canonical-live vs peer-snapshot vs published-frozen)
design:
This is the actual source of the owner 'live sync does not work' confusion. Recon Finding 3 verdict. canonical to synced-draft-channel propagation DOES work (verified on a clean event), so finding 3 is NOT a sync bug. The problem is the banner copy overstates and conflates three genuinely different states.

The three ADR-016 D2 render states and what editing the master actually does to each.
(i) canonical-synced draft. content_version == canonical AND sync_source IS NULL. editing the master DOES live-propagate here.
(ii) peer-synced. own content_version AND sync_source set. a one-time snapshot, the source later edits do NOT propagate by design (divergence is the point for ToS-divergent destinations).
(iii) published. frozen, editing the master marks it dirty / needs re-publish (covered by sibling kb-nexw.2).

Current banner says things like 'editing here updates all these channels' / 'SHARED' without distinguishing these, so the owner edited a channel that was peer-synced or published and concluded live sync is broken. Recon A3. the 'updates all these channels' promise even stays shown after a sharer is published.

Fix. Make _sync_bar.html (templates/syndication/fragments/_sync_bar.html) copy state-accurate. canonical-synced reads as live-from-master, peer-synced reads as a snapshot that will not follow later edits, and the master/shared banner must NOT promise 'updates all these channels' when a sharer is published or peer-snapshot. MUST grep for inline twins of the sync bar first (memory inline-copy-of-shared-partial-drifts. event_syndication.html ~156-235 hand-copies the three-state badge with a 'must match _sync_bar.html' comment). Either replace the twin with an include or apply identical copy to both AND add a content test asserting twin parity (surface-wide guard per .claude/harness.md Templates section).

canonical_refs. ADR-016 D2 (three render states), ADR-008 D3.
acceptance_criteria: The sync-bar copy distinguishes the three states accurately. canonical-synced says edits to the master flow here live, peer-synced says it is a snapshot that will not follow later master edits, and no banner promises 'updates all these channels' when a sharer is published or peer-snapshot. If an inline twin of the sync bar exists it carries identical state-branch copy, guarded by a content test (assertContains on rendered HTML, not response.context). Verified live. the three states read correctly in the browser.
notes:
## Harness target
Signal: uv run pytest syndication/ -k 'sync_bar or sync_label'. Expected green: a content test (assertContains on rendered output) asserts each of the three sync states renders its correct, non-overstated label across _sync_bar.html AND any inline twin. Rationale: template-rendered copy is invisible to context-only assertions (memory django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow) and twins drift (inline-copy-of-shared-partial-drifts). Invalidation: if the three-state model collapses (ADR-016 D2 invalidation), labels change.
## Pre-dispatch brain findings
Twin location confirmed. the inline three-state badge twin is in templates/syndication/fragments/_channel_editor.html:84-135 (the Switch-listing EventForm card, comment 'must match _sync_bar.html'), NOT event_syndication.html as an older memory said. It CANNOT be collapsed to {% include _sync_bar.html %} because _sync_bar's outer div carries id=sync-bar-proj-<pk> and that include already renders at _channel_editor.html:267 (duplicate id breaks OOB). So this is the unavoidable two-site-edit arm. update both _sync_bar.html AND the _channel_editor.html twin + add a parity content test.

Core deliverable narrowed. state (ii) currently reads 'Synced from <platform>' + '· editing detaches'. The word 'Synced' is the lie that caused finding #3 (owner edited the source, expected the snapshot to follow). Relabel to snapshot language: main 'Copied from <platform>', sub '· snapshot, won't follow later edits'. State (i) 'Shared' is accurate (canonical broadcast is live to draft sharers) — leave it. published-sharer honesty (A3) is delivered by kb-nexw.2's per-channel dirty/published badge, not this bead.
close_reason: Fixed in f407a0c. State-(ii) sync badge relabeled from 'Synced from <platform>' + '· editing detaches' (which falsely implied ongoing live sync) to 'Copied from <platform>' + '· snapshot, won't follow later edits' — truthful to ADR-016 D2 mechanism c (one-time copy_from, source edits never propagate). This was the confirmed root of the owner's finding #3 confusion. Applied identically to both _sync_bar.html and the _channel_editor.html Switch-card twin (can't be de-duped to an include — duplicate sync-bar id would break OOB), with a BASE_DIR-derived twin-parity guard + rendered-content tests (RED before, GREEN after). title: Fix silent error-swallows + stale frozen_content in syndication edit/publish paths (ADR-008 D3 / ADR-016 D5)
design:
VERIFIED via fresh-context parent re-verify + debugger confirmation 2026-06-06. Three correctness findings on the edit/publish surface; all code-level, grouped because they share that surface.

FINDING 1 (ADR-008 D3 silent swallow) — TWO sites, not one. Both coerce the is_dirty invariant-violation ValueError to a clean False, hiding data corruption:
  (a) `projection_detach_and_edit` views.py:1521-1522 — `except ValueError: _content_is_dirty = False`
  (b) `version_edit` views.py:1728-1729 — identical swallow (`except ValueError: _content_is_dirty = False  # Invariant violation`)
The is_dirty property raises for a PUBLISHED projection with null frozen_content (an invariant violation — see test_edit_after_publish.py case 4, line 180). Swallowing it to False hides that corruption. Both sites should surface/raise per ADR-008 D3, not default to a clean state. [The original bead cited only ~1530; the second site at :1728-1729 was found by scoping review and confirmed by the debugger.]

FINDING 2 (ADR-008 D3) — `version_copy_from` legacy path views.py:~1832 swallows a ValueError without surfacing `action_error` to the user (the non-legacy path DOES surface it). FIRST confirm whether this legacy path is still reachable. If dead → DELETE it (ADR-008 D1, no backward-compat shims), do not fix. If live → surface the specific error like the non-legacy path.

FINDING 3 (ADR-016 D5 re-freeze gap) — LOCATION CORRECTED. The freeze decision lives in `engine.py transition_status`, NOT services.py:1455-1484 as the original bead claimed. engine.py:92-99 materializes frozen_content on draft→ready ONLY; ready→published hits the bare `else: save(update_fields=["status","updated_at"])` at engine.py:105-106 with NO re-freeze. Every publish path routes ready→published through that else: `publish_switch_own_page` (adapters.py:139), the Telegram path, the FetLife attestation path (services.py:1377), and mark_published. So if the source ContentVersion was edited AFTER consumers reached 'ready' (permitted by `version_edit`'s `_allow_edit_after_publish=True` when all consumers are non-draft, views.py:1658-1660), the first publish freezes nothing new → published frozen_content is STALE (pre-edit snapshot). NOTE `republish_projection` already DOES re-freeze (services.py:1427-1429), so the gap is FIRST-publish only, not re-publish.
FIX: add a ready→published re-freeze branch in `engine.py transition_status` (~:105-106), mirroring the draft→ready freeze, so EVERY path to published captures the current effective content. Engine is the single status-writer, so fixing there covers all callers; a services-only fix would miss the adapter + mark_published paths.

canonical_refs: ADR-008 D1 (delete dead paths), ADR-008 D3 (fail loud, no silent fallback), ADR-016 D5 (frozen_content snapshot at publish). Memory: 2026-05-18-adr-008-d3-silent-fallback-audit.

NOTE: this bead edits `projection_detach_and_edit` and `version_edit` (the two swallow sites) — the SAME functions kb-kgza.10 adds OOB CTA emission to (~:1528, ~:1735). Sequence this bead before kb-kgza.10 to avoid collision.

## Harness target
Signal: a test asserts a PUBLISHED projection with null frozen_content surfaces an error (not a silent clean False) through BOTH the detach-and-edit and version_edit paths; a test proves engine ready→published re-freezes (edit source CV after a consumer reaches 'ready', publish, assert published frozen_content reflects the post-edit content); the existing republish re-freeze test stays green; version_copy_from legacy path is covered (error surfaced) or proven removed. Full syndication suite green; ruff + djlint clean.
Expected green: both swallows fail loud, first-publish re-freezes, legacy path resolved, suite green.
Rationale: these are silent-fallback / stale-snapshot bugs invisible to happy-path tests; each needs an explicit invariant-violation or edit-then-publish test.
Invalidation: if a new publish caller bypasses engine.transition_status, the re-freeze guarantee breaks — the engine-level fix is what prevents that.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Both is_dirty swallow sites (views.py projection_detach_and_edit ~1521 and version_edit ~1728) surface/raise the invariant violation instead of coercing to False; a test asserts a published projection with null frozen_content surfaces an error through both paths. 2. version_copy_from legacy path is either deleted (if proven unreachable) or surfaces action_error like the non-legacy path, with a test. 3. engine.transition_status re-freezes frozen_content on ready to published; a test proves editing the source content version after a consumer reaches ready then publishing yields fresh frozen_content; existing republish re-freeze test stays green. 4. Full syndication suite green; ruff and djlint clean.
notes: ## Origin: discovered-from kb-kgza parent re-verify (2026-06-06). Reviewer findings: views.py:1832 (version_copy_from ValueError swallow), views.py:1530 (projection_detach_and_edit is_dirty swallow→False), views.py:1649-1656+888-915 / services.py:1455-1484 (ready→published no re-freeze → stale frozen_content). Provenance: detach view is in this epic's diff (kb-kgza.2, 6ab36af); copy_from legacy path may predate the epic — confirm at fix time.

title: Verify/fix publish keeps the active channel tab (prior jumps-to-canonical likely publish-from-canonical)
design:

(i) NOT-A-BUG: the original kb-kgza.8 observation ("re-renders with selectedPk:2") was simply Publish FROM the canonical tab (pk2 = first_pk), which is indistinguishable from a jump.

title: Complete dirty-state live refresh: platform-aware label + Re-publish CTA + stale preview must reach the OOB edit path
design:
VERIFIED via fresh-context debugger live root-cause 2026-06-06. The autosave/edit OOB response (`_channel_dirty_oob.html`, emitted by `projection_detach_and_edit` views.py:1528 and `version_edit` views.py:1735) swaps ONLY the status dot (`#channel-dot-N`) and dirty banner (`#channel-dirty-N`). Three edit-dependent things therefore never refresh on a LIVE edit — only on a full page reload. All three share that one incomplete-OOB-swap root:

PROBLEM A — label honesty + DRY. The dirty-banner copy is generic "Edited — re-publish to update the live post" at `_channel_dirty_oob.html:20` (tooltip) and `:32` (banner). It should be platform-aware: FetLife → "...your FetLife post manually" (FetLife has no publishing API), else → "...the live post". The same generic copy is hand-twinned at FIVE template locations (resolves the prior 4-vs-5 ambiguity): `_channel_dirty_oob.html:20`, `_channel_dirty_oob.html:32`, `_channel_editor.html:393/395` (full-render banner, already platform-aware-fixed in kb-kgza.6), `event_syndication.html:97` (tab-dot tooltip), `post_syndication.html:86` (tab-dot tooltip). title: Edit-after-publish dirty marker + explicit re-publish
design:
Realizes ADR-016 D5 (edit-after-publish). A projection is "dirty" = `status == 'published'` AND effective body (from content_version) != `frozen_content`. **CORRECTION (gate first — ADR-008 D3 but no spurious fire): the null-frozen_content fail-loud check applies ONLY when status=='published'; a DRAFT projection legitimately has null frozen_content and is NEVER dirty — gate on status=='published' BEFORE the null check, so authoring drafts never raise.** **CORRECTION (cheap foresight per ADR-003, just added to ADR-016 D5): read the edit-after-publish behaviour through a SINGLE named policy resolution point (e.g. an `edit_after_publish` policy resolved from the connection's platform, default `dirty_then_republish` for all v0 platforms) rather than inlining dirty logic at each call site — so a future per-platform "lock editing on no-edit-API channels" is a capability value, NOT a rewrite. Do NOT build the alternate behaviours now (ADR-008 D2) — only make the single seam.** Derive `is_dirty` (property on PlatformProjection or in the view row-builder; prefer derivation, no new DB column). UI: orange status dot (the C3 dot's added case) + an inline "Edited — re-publish to update the live post" banner below the editor; Publish CTA stays visible for dirty published projections labelled "Re-publish"; re-publish reuses the existing publish verb (`publish_projection` ~services.py L603, which re-freezes frozen_content). Extend `_sync_bar.html` with the 4th state.

## Canonical refs
- ADR-016 D5, ADR-003, ADR-008 D2/D3

## Harness target
- **Signal:** (a) pytest unit tests for `is_dirty` property and the policy resolution point; (b) Playwright browser read-back on a published projection that has been edited.
- **Expected-green:** (a) pytest: `is_dirty` True when published & body != frozen_content; False when equal; a DRAFT projection with null frozen_content has `is_dirty == False` and does NOT raise; a PUBLISHED projection with null frozen_content raises or surfaces an error. `grep -r "edit_after_publish"` shows exactly ONE resolution site (policy seam). (b) Browser: editing a published channel's body causes its pill dot to turn orange (computed background-color = orange/amber) and an "edited" or "re-publish" banner appears in the DOM — without full page reload. Clicking Re-publish returns the dot to green.
- **Rationale:** The `is_dirty` property gate (draft never raises) and the single policy seam are unit-testable; the orange dot + banner appearance without reload requires a live DOM read-back after an HTMX partial update.
- **Invalidation:** If a draft projection raises on `is_dirty`, or if the policy logic is duplicated across multiple call sites (grep finds >1 resolution site), or if the orange dot doesn't appear after editing in the live browser, the respective signal fires red.
acceptance_criteria: pytest: is_dirty True when published and effective body != frozen_content, False when equal; a DRAFT with null frozen_content is is_dirty=False and does NOT raise; a PUBLISHED projection with null frozen_content surfaces an error. The edit-after-publish behaviour is read from one named policy point (grep shows a single resolution site, default dirty_then_republish). Browser read-back: editing a published channel's body turns its pill dot orange / shows the 'edited—re-publish' banner without reload; clicking Re-publish returns it to green. CI green.
close_reason: Edit-after-publish dirty marker shipped + browser-verified (commit 728e880): is_dirty derivation gated on status==published (drafts never dirty/never raise; published+null-frozen raises); orange dot + 'edited — re-publish' banner + Re-publish CTA appear on editing a published channel without reload (OOB swap); re-publish re-freezes frozen_content. Cheap-foresight single edit_after_publish_policy seam (default dirty_then_republish, one resolution site). 854 tests pass, djlint --check clean.

title: Add-channel: backend add_projection/reconcile + '...' toggle UI
design:
Realizes D-IA5 + ADR-016 D4 (post-hoc projection reconciliation). Backend `syndication/services.py`: `add_projection(publishable, connection)` — mints a draft PlatformProjection for an existing Event/Post × connection if none exists (mirror `_eager_create_listing_projections` ~L262 / `_eager_create_promotion_projections` ~L324); idempotent; raise ValueError on wrong-kind (fail-loud ADR-008 D3); never deletes a published projection. `reconcile_projections(publishable)` batch version. Views/urls (`syndication/views.py`, `syndication/urls.py`): `POST .../add-channel/` (connection_pk → add_projection → HTMX swap of syndication fragment; requires can_edit per ADR-017); `DELETE/POST .../remove-channel/` disables/removes an UNPUBLISHED projection. **CORRECTION (ADR-008 D3 fail-loud): remove-channel on a PUBLISHED projection returns 400 WITH a visible surfaced reason in the response body (not empty, not generic) — render a visible error state.** UI: an Alpine "…" dropdown at the end of the pill row listing enabled connections with toggles (checked = projected); toggle ON → add-channel POST, OFF → remove.

## Canonical refs
- ADR-016 D4, ADR-008 D3, ADR-017 D1

## Harness target
- **Signal:** (a) pytest unit tests for `add_projection` and the remove-channel view; (b) Playwright browser read-back for the "…" toggle interaction.
- **Expected-green:** (a) pytest: `add_projection(event, fetlife_conn)` creates exactly one draft projection (assert count=1), returns the same object on re-call; raises `ValueError` on wrong-kind mismatch; remove-channel POST on a published projection returns HTTP 400 with a non-empty body containing the reason string. (b) Browser: clicking "…" opens a dropdown; toggling ON for an unprojected-but-enabled connection triggers an HTMX swap and a new pill appears in the pill row without full page reload (`window.performance.navigation.type !== 1`).
- **Rationale:** The idempotency and fail-loud contracts (ADR-008 D3) are unit-testable; the HTMX partial-swap UX (pill appears without reload) requires a live browser to confirm.
- **Invalidation:** If idempotency breaks (second call creates a duplicate projection) or remove-channel on a published projection silently returns 200, the pytest signal fires red. If the full page reloads on toggle, the browser signal fires red.
acceptance_criteria: pytest: add_projection(event, fetlife_conn) creates exactly one draft projection when none exists, returns the same on re-call (idempotent); raises ValueError on wrong-kind. View test: POST add-channel returns 200 with the new channel's platform in the content; DELETE/remove on a published projection returns 400 with a non-empty reason string. Browser read-back: clicking '...' on a composer with an enabled-but-unprojected connection shows a toggle; toggling ON makes a new pill appear without full page reload. CI green.
close_reason: Add-channel shipped + browser-verified for BOTH event and post composers (commits 553cb5a + 1cf65e9): add_projection/reconcile service verbs (idempotent, raise-on-wrong-kind, never-touch-published); add_channel_event + add_channel_post views + generic remove_channel (400+visible-reason on published); '…' kebab dropdown toggle on both composers minting projections for enabled-but-unprojected connections — fixes the FetLife-added-later gap. 847 tests pass (33 add-channel tests).

Replace the tall stacked vertical tab buttons (`event_syndication.html` ~L62-116; `post_syndication.html` ~L41-120) with compact single-line pills: platform identity + a status dot (draft=amber, ready=blue, live/published=green, failed=rose; the dirty/edited-needs-republish=orange state is ADDED by C5 — author the dot as a SINGLE status→color resolution point so C5 adds one case, not a re-architecture). Active pill = filled, inactive = ghost. Move "Publish all ready" CTA adjacent to the pills (right end), not below.

- D-IA4, ADR-016 D5

title: Composer IA consolidation — single-bar + edit-in-place + add-channel (Typefully-grade, dogfooding round 2)
design:
## Context

Second dogfooding round on the syndication composer (after kb-ide0 redesign + kb-shzi fix epic) surfaced ~8 IA/UX complaints that all trace to one root: the composer is built as a stack of slabs (status eyebrow + big serif title + promo list + tall tab row + a BODY block + a SEPARATE preview block) where the reference product (Typefully) is one composer bar over one edit-in-place surface. A live browser study of the user's own Typefully session (2026-06-05) confirmed Typefully's shape: ONE 64px composer bar = platform pills (left) + "…" + Schedule/Publish (right); the editor IS the styled post (one TipTap element, no textarea-vs-preview pair); per-platform divergence is a "Sync with <primary>" toggle; "+ New draft" is one-click into an empty editor; draft rows are wholly clickable.

Most of the underlying machinery already exists: the per-channel sync engine (content_version FK + customize/copy_from/reset + sync_source pointer per ADR-016 D2), the studio rail, the post composer's edit-in-place bubble. What never landed is the single-bar consolidation and the event composer's edit-in-place unification; the genuinely new gaps this round added are add-a-channel-to-an-existing-publishable (the FetLife-added-later problem), a prominent "+ New", and clickable promo cards.

This epic is the IA/UX realization. The data-model + lifecycle decisions live in ADR-016 (D2 sync-from-channel; D4 post-hoc projection reconciliation, evolved 2026-06-05; D5 edit-after-publish dirty-marker + per-channel status surfacing, evolved 2026-06-05). This epic's --design carries only the IA/layout decisions, per the ADR-016 precedent (Consequences/Direct: "UX/IA detail lives in those beads' --design, not this ADR").

## IA decisions (this epic owns)

- **D-IA1 — One consolidated composer bar.** Collapse the per-publishable chrome into a single row directly under the global navbar: channel pills (left) · breadcrumb (center, e.g. "Studio › Nightfall" for a post, linking to its event) · Schedule/Publish CTA (right). Drop the standalone status eyebrow and the big serif title element. Global navbar unchanged.
- **D-IA2 — Edit-in-place everywhere.** The channel's rendered preview IS the editor. Finish the event/listing composer (currently shows a BODY textarea AND a separate rendered preview = the same content twice); the post composer already edits in place. No standalone read-only-mirror block.
- **D-IA3 — Title model.** No standalone big serif title. For a Post, the headline is the first line of the editable body (Typefully-exact). For an Event listing, the structured fields (title, date, venue) render inline-editable WITHIN the first channel's preview card, not as an H1 above everything.
- **D-IA4 — Pill tabs + per-channel status.** Replace the tall stacked vertical tab buttons with compact pills (platform identity + a small status dot: draft / live / edited-needs-republish / failed). Active pill = filled. Status lives on the pill per ADR-016 D5 — there is no publishable-level status header.
- **D-IA5 — "…" add-channel.** A "…" at the end of the pill row opens a per-channel toggle list ("Channels for this <listing|post>") — Typefully's "Draft Platforms" analog. Toggling an enabled-but-unprojected connection ON mints its projection (ADR-016 D4 add_projection verb) = the FetLife-added-later fix. Toggling off disables/removes an unpublished projection.
- **D-IA6 — "+ New" in the rail.** Prominent "+ New" at the top of the publishables rail → choose [New event / New promo post] (we fork by type since we have two publishable kinds, unlike Typefully's single draft type); opens the create surface inline in the studio pane (#studio-main hx-target), not a full-page navigation.
- **D-IA7 — Clickable cards + drop redundant nav.** The promo-post card under an event becomes wholly clickable (hx-get into the studio pane, matching studio_rail_row); drop the "Open composer ↗" text link and the redundant "Event Workspace ↗" button (the centered breadcrumb in D-IA1 is the way back).
- **D-IA8 — Event composer block order.** The listing/edit surface is primary; the promo-post list becomes a compact clickable strip BELOW the channel composer, not stacked on top of the event body.

## Reference contrast (Typefully, live-studied 2026-06-05)

Typefully has no parent/child publishables → no breadcrumb (we keep one, centered, because post→event parentage is real); a single draft type → one-click "+ New" (we fork by type); a single-primary sync model → "Sync with <primary>" (we already generalized to sync-from-any-channel per ADR-016 D2, which is richer). The bar layout, edit-in-place, pill tabs, "…" platform toggle, clickable rows, and Schedule/Publish-on-the-right are lifted directly.

## Out of scope (explicit)

Scheduling backend, undo, keyboard shortcuts, media upload, per-channel char counters, mobile/responsive rail (existing backlog beads kb-dsgd / kb-g89u / kb-mbb7 / kb-a3md / kb-5ok6 — link, don't absorb). OAuth/credential capture for connections (separate open backend). This epic is IA/layout + the two small backend verbs ADR-016 D4/D5 named (add_projection reconcile; edit-after-publish dirty marker).
acceptance_criteria: The per-Event and per-Post composer reads as ONE bar (pills · breadcrumb · Schedule/Publish) over an edit-in-place surface — verified live in the browser on both an event and a post. Specifically: (1) no standalone status eyebrow or big serif title; status is per-channel on the pill (ADR-016 D5). (2) The event/listing composer edits in place — no separate BODY+preview double-render (closes kb-fzqn). (3) Channel tabs are compact pills with a status dot; a '…' opens a per-channel toggle that can ADD a channel to an existing publishable (an enabled-but-unprojected FetLife connection becomes a channel — ADR-016 D4). (4) Editing an already-published channel marks it 'edited — re-publish needed', never silently re-broadcasts (ADR-016 D5). (5) A prominent '+ New' in the rail creates either an event or a promo post inline. (6) Promo cards under an event are wholly clickable; the redundant 'Open composer' link and 'Event Workspace' button are gone; the promo strip sits below the channel composer. CI green (lint + test + security); no raw double-render or duplicate-title regressions in a browser read-back.
notes: Dogfooding round 2 on the composer. Live Typefully study screenshots: /tmp/typefully-study/. Current-IA inventory with file:line mapping captured in orchestrator context. ADR-016 evolved 2026-06-05 (D4 post-hoc reconcile, D5 edit-after-publish + per-channel status). Decompose into child beads; absorb kb-fzqn (event double-render) as the edit-in-place child; LINK (do not absorb) the deferred-feature backlog kb-dsgd/kb-g89u/kb-mbb7/kb-a3md/kb-5ok6/kb-p0hl/kb-xpun.
close_reason: Composer IA consolidation shipped + verified. All 8 feature children (.1-.8) + 3 parent-re-verify repairs (.9 one-bar consolidation, .10 post double-render, .11 policy seam) closed. 6 epic bullets delivered + browser-verified: (1) one bar pills·breadcrumb·publish, no eyebrow/title; (2) event edit-in-place, no double-render, venue inline; (3) pill tabs+status dot + '…' add-channel (FetLife-added-later fix); (4) edit-after-publish dirty marker + explicit re-publish; (5) prominent +New event/post inline create; (6) clickable promo cards + strip below composer. ADR-016 D4/D5 evolved in place. Parent re-verify (fresh-context) run; found 3 conjunction-drift issues (D-IA1 partial, post double-render twin-drift, dead policy seam) — all fixed + re-verified. Full CI green: 2220 pytest pass, ruff check+format, djlint --check ., makemigrations --check clean. NOT yet pushed (awaiting authorization — push triggers prod deploy).

title: Studio IA polish: naming, post-create vocab, sync-badge legibility, add-channel/new-publishable entry points
description:
Final UI-polish pass over the studio/composer surface (one surface — ui-craftsman, runs AFTER the structural children land). Five UX items diagnosed:

1. NAMING: visible 'EVENT HUB' kicker (_event_hub_body.html:19) reads oddly — user wants 'open/edit event'. Post side already says 'Post Workspace' (_post_hub_body.html:19); studio main pane says 'workspace'. Standardize on one vocabulary (recommend 'Event'/'Post' workspace or drop the kicker). Also fix page title event_hub.html:3 ('Switch Syndication Hub') and cross-link labels 'Event hub' (_post_hub_body.html:22-29, post_syndication.html:90,95). DEFER route/view/file renames (event-hub etc., ~40 sites) — visible-label only.
2. POST-CREATE VOCAB: ONE Post model + ONE endpoint (syndication:post-create) but six strings: '+ Add post'/'Add post'/'Add promo message'/'No posts yet'/'No promo posts yet'/'Promotional posts' (event_posts.html:6,12,41,67; event_syndication.html:47,54,562,566) + two interaction styles (inline form vs full-page nav). Standardize one term + one empty-state + prefer the inline form. (Model is clean per ADR-016 D1 — no Post.kind needed.)
3. SYNC-BADGE LEGIBILITY: states (i) shared-canonical (broadcasts on edit) and (ii) peer-synced (detaches on edit) BOTH render 'Synced' (_sync_bar.html:37 vs :48) — user asked 'is it two-way sync?'. Behavior is correct per ADR-016 D2 (do NOT change semantics). Disambiguate labels: state (i) -> e.g. 'Shared · edits broadcast' / state (ii) stays 'Synced from <peer>'. Surface 'editing here updates N channels' near the edit point when the canonical CV has >1 consumer (content_version_consumers_map, services.py:689).
4. ADD-CHANNEL DISCOVERABILITY: no link to connections (urls.py:57-58) from navbar/studio once you have >=1 channel (the 'Connect platforms' CTA only shows at zero channels, event_syndication.html:39-42). Add a persistent 'Channels' link (navbar.html, gated like Studio) and/or studio rail nav slot (studio.html:41 reserved studio-nav-sections div).
5. NEW-PUBLISHABLE DISCOVERABILITY: 'Create event' only shows in the rail/studio EMPTY state (studio.html:81,101); vanishes after the first event. Add a persistent '+ New event' in the rail header (studio.html:46-48). New-post is correctly event-scoped (keep inside event composer, unified label per item 2).
design:
ADR-010/ADR-016 (FLEXIBLE; none codify a review/approval flow). ADR-003 reserved studio-nav-sections slot is the cheap-foresight home for the Channels nav. tailwind-v4-component-layer-loses-to-utilities + alpine-3-x-directives memories apply for any CSS/Alpine. Match existing dark-editorial design system (kb-mono, serif headings). This is the LAST child — depends on kb-shzi.2/.3/.4 so it polishes final markup, not a moving target. ui-craftsman owns build->screenshot->critique on the live app (localhost:8000, demo@switch.berlin/demo).

## Harness target
Signal: live-browser read-back (ui-craftsman) confirms: rail has persistent '+ New event' + a 'Channels' link; event composer kicker no longer says 'Event Hub'; post-create uses one consistent term + one empty-state; the two sync states render visually distinct labels. Plus uv run pytest + djlint green and a content assertion test for the relabeled sync states + unified post-create string.
Expected green: browser read-back passes the slop/clarity check; suite green; no raw 'Event Hub'/dup-vocab strings remain (grep).
Rationale: UI legibility is only verifiable in a real browser (django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow, django-multiline-hash-comment memories) — content tests can't see rendering quality.
Invalidation: route/file renames deferred; if undertaken later that's a separate mechanical bead.
acceptance_criteria: 'Event Hub' visible label + page title + cross-links replaced with clear vocabulary (no route/file rename). Post-create uses one consistent term + one empty-state + one interaction style. The two 'Synced' badge states are visually distinguishable; broadcast consequence surfaced near the edit point (semantics unchanged). A persistent 'Channels'/add-channel affordance and a persistent '+ New event' affordance exist in nav/studio. Browser read-back confirms clarity. uv run pytest + djlint green.
notes:
## Scoping-review folds (2026-06-04)
- F1 fold: the sync-badge relabel must convey the BEHAVIORAL difference, not just a color/icon — directly answering the user's 'is it two-way sync?'. State (i) shared-canonical -> label like 'Shared · editing updates N channels' (broadcast); state (ii) peer-synced -> 'Synced from <peer> · editing detaches'. The user must be able to read the consequence of editing, not just see two distinct chips.
- F2 fold: 'What does Duplicate really do?' — the Duplicate action is unowned. Verify what Duplicate actually does (post_syndication.html:213-217) and relabel/explain it so its purpose is obvious to the user (or remove if redundant). Add this to the polish scope.
close_reason: Studio IA polish via ui-craftsman (browser read-back + slop test pass): 'Event Hub'->'Event Workspace' (kicker/title/cross-links); post-create vocab unified to 'promo post' + single empty-state across 5 sites; sync badges now legible by BEHAVIOR — state(i) 'Shared across N channels' (broadcast), state(ii) 'Synced from <peer> · editing detaches', state(iii) 'Custom'; persistent 'Channels' link (navbar + studio rail) + '+ New' event affordance in rail header; confusing Duplicate button removed (endpoint retained). Fresh review of the sync-badge logic folded 4 findings: silent-blank badge (ADR-008 D3), the 2-branch-missing-state-ii oscillation shape on the inline Switch bar (now 3-branch), count-wording clarity, + count test. 782 syndication tests green; ruff/format/djlint clean. Commits 9d8e3c6(approx)+fe04fd3.

title: Integration / harness: driven /ui-craft browser pass over both composers + additive Typefully-gap critique
design:
### Context
This is the integration/harness bead: it depends on A, B, C, D and constitutes the parent-re-verify altitude for the composed surface. Per the parent's Harness target and the memory `parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift`, a per-child green does not substitute for the driven composed read-back. Unit/view tests are the floor; the driven browser flow is the goal-faithful signal for "the composer feels right and matches the agreed Typefully properties."

### Firmness
FLEXIBLE — harness bead. The Typefully-gap critique is additive and does not gate the pass/fail verdict.

### Rationale
`external:` Parent Harness target specifies a driven browser-automation pass (CDP, browser-automation skill) over both composers. `direct:` `.claude/harness.md` templates/Alpine fit profile: Alpine-driven re-render, sync toggle, and modal behaviors are invisible to view tests and only surface live. `reasoned:` The composed parent-re-verify altitude is the only signal that can confirm the 8-item conjunction holistically; individual child harness targets are the floor but cannot confirm conjunction-level properties (e.g. that the single top row and the sync toggle are present AT THE SAME TIME in the same DOM).

### Alternatives

| Alternative | Decision | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Screenshot-based verification | Rejected | `external:` parent design explicitly states "The agent must DRIVE the flow (type into the card, toggle sync, trigger the discard modal, switch tabs, hit Publish), not screenshot static states." |
| Manual dogfooding only | Rejected | `reasoned:` too slow; not reproducible; does not produce a binary pass/fail record. |

**What would invalidate this design:** If the driven inspection passes but a real dogfooding author hits a composer flow the inspection didn't drive (deep-link to a single channel tab, refresh mid-edit losing autosave state, a sync source that became synced after selection) — the harness drove too narrow a flow set; widen the driven flows rather than trusting the green. ### canonical_refs

- ADR-012 D3 (four-predicate harness target; children-jointly-cover-parent rule)
- ADR-005 D7 (bead-authoring primitives + conjunction-coverage; parent-re-verify discipline)
- ADR-008 D8 (FIRM — signal-shaped invalidation; no numeric thresholds)

**Signal:** A driven browser-automation session (CDP) over the live composed surface — both event and post composers — that DRIVES all 8 observations in the acceptance contract (not screenshots; typed interactions, toggle actions, modal triggers, picker interactions). title: Per-channel sync FROM another channel with detach-on-edit, discard-confirm, and cycle guard (D4)
design:
### Context
The current `copy_from` operation (`syndication/services.py` ~line 789) mints an **independent snapshot** — it copies the source's content into the target projection's `content_version` row and the two are thereafter independent. The live-derive mechanism in the engine only resolves to the publishable's canonical (`content_version`), NOT a peer channel's version. Therefore "sync FROM another channel" (a live binding to a peer) is NOT free with current code.

### LOAD-BEARING OPEN MECHANISM — live (a) vs snapshot (b) resolution

**Option (a) LIVE:** The synced projection shares the source channel's `content_version` row (existing single-row broadcast). A directional `sync_source` field is added to the projection model recording which channel is the source. On detach-on-edit, the projection gets its own new `content_version` row and `sync_source` is cleared. On re-sync, the projection's FK is pointed back to the source's row (after confirm). Cycle guard: a projection with a non-null `sync_source` cannot be a source for another projection.

- Pro: source edits propagate live to all synced channels without a re-sync action.
- Con: adds a schema field (`sync_source` FK on `SyndicationProjection`); FK pointing two projections at the same `content_version` row means concurrent edits to different projections collide on the same row — requires careful save logic.
- Schema impact: one new nullable FK field, one migration.

**Option (b) SNAPSHOT (recommended):** On (re)sync, re-run `copy_from` — copy the source's current content into the target's existing `content_version` row. No new field on the projection model. No live propagation; the synced channel diverges from the source the moment an edit is made (detach-on-edit is still implemented by just allowing the edit to proceed, since the snapshot is already independent).

- Pro: no schema change; re-uses the existing `copy_from` path; the `sync_source` concept is UI-only (held in Alpine state or a lightweight session value for the duration of the composer session); detach is free (the snapshot is already independent, the user just edits it); the cycle guard is also UI-only (disable already-synced channels in the source picker).
- Con: source edits after the initial sync do NOT propagate to the synced channel; the author must explicitly re-sync to pull in updates. This is the Typefully model (their "sync" is also a one-time copy at toggle-on).
- Schema impact: none; `makemigrations --check` stays clean.

**Recommendation: option (b) snapshot**, for the following reasons:
- `reasoned:` ADR-008 D2 — simplest thing that works; no second caller yet earns the added complexity of a live-binding FK + concurrent-save logic.
- `direct:` Typefully's own sync toggle is a one-time copy at toggle-on (per UX characterization in parent design); "sync" in their model means "start from this source" not "stay live with this source." The UX contract (toggle / detach / discard-confirm / cycle guard) is fully satisfiable with snapshots.
- `reasoned:` the cycle guard is trivially implemented in Alpine state (disable channels whose sync-source toggle is ON in the source picker dropdown) without any backend enforcement beyond input validation.
- `direct:` if the author re-enables sync, the "discard your edits?" confirm + re-`copy_from` is already the correct UX; there is no UX difference between (a) and (b) from the author's perspective at toggle-on time.

This recommendation should be treated as the child's design decision to confirm at implementation start — NOT pre-locked by the parent epic. If implementation finds that live propagation is needed for a concrete use case the parent did not anticipate, option (a) remains available (one migration, careful save logic).

Note: the cycle-guard acceptance bullet's enforcement model branches on this (a)-vs-(b) resolution — under (b) snapshot it is UI-only + endpoint scope validation; under (a) live-binding the backend can validate `sync_source` against the projection model. The acceptance clause must be read accordingly.

### Firmness
FLEXIBLE (inherited from parent D4, per ADR-016 D2 evolution). The discard-confirm on destructive re-sync is FIRM per ADR-008 D3 (fail loud, no silent overwrite of user edits).

### Rationale
`external:` User direction — ToS divergence means no single canonical feeds every channel; the differentiator vs Typefully's single-primary. `external:` Typefully's per-channel sync toggle + "Discard text and sync?" modal is the proven UX to adopt. `direct:` builds on the existing `copy_from` + `customize` + `reset_to_canonical` ops; the current one-shot "Copy from" dropdown is the seed for the sync toggle. `reasoned:` re-sync is destructive → fail-loud confirm per ADR-008 D3.

### Alternatives

| Alternative | Decision | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Live binding (option a) with `sync_source` FK | Available but not recommended for V0 | `reasoned:` ADR-008 D2 — more schema + concurrent-save complexity; no current use case requires live propagation; deferred. |
| Abstract named content variants as sources | Rejected | `reasoned:` ADR-008 D2 — more concept + schema; no second caller yet earns the register layer; `direct:` ADR-016 D2 Invalidation names the promotion path (deferred, not killed). |
| Per-field sync (inherit/override per field) | Rejected | `reasoned:` whole-channel sync is what Typefully does and what the backend already models (whole `content_version`); per-field is more machinery without a present need. |

**What would invalidate this design (option b):** If authors regularly re-sync channels and find that the source has changed since their last sync, leading to unexpected content (they expected a live link, not a stale snapshot) — then option (a) live binding becomes warranted; promote `sync_source` to a schema field and implement live propagation.

### canonical_refs
- ADR-016 D2 (sync-from-any-channel; live binding vs snapshot mechanism left open to child)
- ADR-016 D4 (`kinds` per connection — cycle guard ensures only independent channels are offered as sources)
- ADR-008 D2 (no speculative abstraction — snapshot recommended over live-binding for V0)
- ADR-008 D3 (fail loud — discard-confirm before destructive re-sync)
- ADR-003 (cheap foresight — `ContentVersion.name` already supports the named-register shape the deferred D4 branch would use; no additional foresight needed here)

## Harness target

**Signal:** `uv run pytest syndication/tests/ -k "sync or copy_from or detach" -v` for the backend sync/copy path; PLUS a scoped driven browser check: navigate to a secondary channel in the event composer (after Child C lands), (1) toggle sync ON for a source channel, assert content matches source, (2) type a character, assert the sync indicator shows "custom", (3) toggle sync ON again, assert the discard-confirm modal appears, (4) attempt to pick an already-synced channel as a source, assert it is not offered in the picker.

**Expected green:** Backend tests pass (copy_from path exercised, no illegal transitions); the driven check observes all four behaviors (content match after sync, detach indicator on edit, modal on re-sync, cycle guard enforces non-synced source only).

**Rationale:** Covers parent-signal dimensions (4a) sync-from-channel toggle + detach, (4b) discard-confirm modal driven, and (4c) cycle guard driven. Per `.claude/harness.md` Alpine fit profile, the sync toggle / modal / cycle-guard behaviors are Alpine-driven and invisible to view tests; the driven browser check is the goal-faithful signal. The backend copy_from test is the floor for "the snapshot mechanism works."

**Invalidation:** If the driven check passes but a real author discovers that re-syncing a channel that has been edited does NOT show the discard modal (e.g. because the Alpine state tracking "has this channel been edited" is reset on tab switch) — the driven test didn't cover the tab-switch-then-re-sync flow; add it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new nullable `sync_source` self-FK on `PlatformProjection` (→ the source `PlatformProjection` within the same publishable's projection set) persists which channel each channel follows; the migration is present and committed and `makemigrations --check` is clean.
- Each secondary channel tab in BOTH the event and post composers shows a sync control naming its current source. The default source is the canonical — the Switch own-page tab for events, the restored abstract "Source" anchor for posts (ADR-010 D1, parent D1).
- Turning sync ON for a source copies that source's CURRENT content into the channel as an independent copy (one-time `copy_from` snapshot) and persists `sync_source`; the "Synced from <channel>" toggle state survives a full page reload (driven-browser-verified).
- Typing into a synced channel detaches it — `sync_source` is cleared and the indicator flips to "Custom"; no confirmation on detach.
- Re-enabling sync fires a "discard your edits?" confirm modal BEFORE re-running `copy_from` against the source's then-current content (destructive; fail-loud per ADR-008 D3, never a silent overwrite).
- Cycle guard is BACKEND-enforceable (not UI-only): a projection whose `sync_source` is non-null is not offered as a source in any picker, AND the sync/copy-from endpoint rejects a source whose `sync_source` is non-null (raises, per ADR-008 D3). A projection is a legal source iff its own `sync_source IS NULL`.
- The post composer's canonical "Source" anchor is restored as the first tab and the default sync source; the Source-anchor assertions Child C rewrote away are restored / re-expressed as passing tests.
- Snapshot semantics verified: editing a SOURCE channel after a downstream channel synced from it does NOT change the downstream channel's content (no live propagation) — backend test.
- Existing render-regression + view tests pass; djlint clean; the syndication suite is green.
notes:
## Carried-in open item from Child C review (2026-06-04) — post canonical "Source" anchor

Child C's post-composer reshape (single top row) SILENTLY DROPPED the post's canonical "Source" anchor (the abstract master a post anchors at, since it has no native-home channel). This contradicts parent epic D1 ("the abstract 'Source' anchor for a Post, per ADR-010 D1") and ADR-010 D1 (FLEXIBLE: "A Post has no native-home channel, so its canonical is an abstract 'Source' anchor"). Two tests asserting the Source anchor were rewritten away in C; the contradiction is currently un-ratified.

D4 MUST resolve the post canonical-source model — it is load-bearing for sync-from-channel (events default-sync-from Switch/canonical; posts had "Source" as that default). Resolve by EITHER:
(a) restore a canonical "Source" anchor as the post composer's first tab + the default sync source (contract-faithful); OR
(b) consciously adopt a new post-canonical model (e.g. one channel designated canonical, or canonical-implicit-in-content_version) and EVOLVE ADR-010 D1 (FLEXIBLE → announce+proceed per ADR-013 D3) + parent epic D1 in place via /adr-write to record it.
Do NOT leave posts without a defined canonical/default-sync source. This is a design decision for D's --design, not a silent implementation choice.

## RESOLVED 2026-06-04 — sync mechanism + post canonical "Source" anchor

Supersedes the "LOAD-BEARING OPEN MECHANISM (a)-vs-(b)" section above and the carried-in Source-anchor deferral below. Both open questions are now closed:

**Sync mechanism = (c) snapshot-plus-persisted-pointer** (user decision via design-fork question; ADR-016 D2 evolved in commit 9286ec3). NOT pure-(a)-live and NOT pure-(b)-UI-only. Concretely:
- Add a nullable `sync_source` self-FK on `PlatformProjection` pointing at the source `PlatformProjection` (within the same publishable's projection set). One migration; cheap pre-launch per ADR-008 D1.
- Sync = one-time `copy_from(user, projection, source.content_version)` (existing op, syndication/services.py ~789) — mints an independent copy. Then set `projection.sync_source = source`. NO live propagation: the source's later edits do not flow until a manual re-sync. This is intentional — ToS-divergent destinations *want* divergence.
- The persisted pointer is what pure-(b) could not give: the "Synced from <channel>" toggle state survives reload, and the cycle guard is backend-enforceable.
- **Three render states**: (i) `content_version == shared canonical row` ∧ `sync_source IS NULL` → *synced from canonical* (default — Switch tab / Source anchor); (ii) own `content_version` ∧ `sync_source` set → *synced from that peer*; (iii) own `content_version` ∧ `sync_source IS NULL` → *custom/detached*.
- **Detach** = on edit, clear `sync_source` (and the projection already has / gets its own independent `content_version` via `customize`/`copy_from`). **Re-sync** = discard-confirm → `copy_from` again + re-set `sync_source`.
- **Cycle guard (backend)**: a projection is a legal sync source iff its own `sync_source IS NULL`. The picker hides non-null-sync_source projections AND the sync endpoint raises if asked to sync from one (ADR-008 D3 fail-loud). This replaces the decomposition-draft acceptance bullet that said "UI-only enforcement under option (b)".

**Post canonical "Source" anchor = (a) RESTORE** (contract-faithful; no ADR change — ADR-010 D1 already says a Post's canonical is an abstract "Source" anchor, FLEXIBLE). Child C dropped it in the single-top-row reshape; D restores it as the post composer's first tab and the default sync source. The two Source-anchor tests C rewrote away are restored / re-expressed.
close_reason: D4 — per-channel sync FROM another channel, snapshot+persisted-pointer mechanism (ADR-016 D2 resolved 2026-06-04). Added nullable sync_source self-FK on PlatformProjection (migration 0008); sync_projection_from service (one-time copy_from + persisted pointer, no live propagation); detach-on-edit wired into version_edit; discard-confirm modal before re-sync; cycle guard backend-enforced (service raises on non-null-sync_source source) + UI picker excludes synced channels. Post canonical 'Source' anchor RESTORED as first tab + default sync source (ADR-010 D1; the tests Child C dropped re-expressed). Both composers. 153 tests green (was 124; +29 across test_sync_mechanism + test_sync_ux_behaviors), djlint clean, makemigrations clean. Commits 1b72e9b + 9b84c46. Fresh-context DRIVEN browser verification: all four behaviors (sync-copies, detach, discard-confirm-modal, cycle-guard) live-functional & screenshot-verified incl. the Alpine modal. title: Extend the shell to capability-filtered multi-channel tabs across event + post composers (D3)
design:
### Context
D3 is the UI realization of ADR-016 D1 (Event/Post are separate entities) and D4 (`kinds` per connection). The `kinds` field already drives eager projection creation (`_eager_create_listing_projections` / `_eager_create_promotion_projections` in `syndication/services.py`). This child applies the same filter at render time to the tab list, and extends the Child A shell pattern to the post composer. No schema change is needed.

### Firmness
FLEXIBLE (inherited from parent D3). Invalidation: if authors want a unified campaign view composing listing + promo posts together, add a cross-composer campaign surface — but keep the per-publishable composers as the editing primitives.

### Rationale
`external:` ADR-016 D1 (Event/Post are separate entities) + D4 (`kinds` per connection — this is the UI realization). `direct:` `kinds` already drives projection creation; the tab-filter reads the same field from `PlatformConnection` — no new data contract. `reasoned:` removing the "promotion tab inside the event composer" resolves the awkward mixed-surface the earlier sketch had. `reasoned:` landing after Child A means the shell pattern is stable before it is applied to the post composer.

### Alternatives

| Alternative | Decision | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| One composer mixing listing + promotion tabs | Rejected | `external:` contradicts ADR-016 D1 (separate entities); `reasoned:` conflates two content types with different shapes (structured event vs message). |
| Hard-code channel names in the template | Rejected | `reasoned:` ADR-008 D2 — no speculative abstraction; but also: hard-coding breaks when a new platform is added; `direct:` `kinds` is already the runtime source of truth. |

**What would invalidate this design:** If a platform-connection can have `kinds = []` (neither listing nor promotion) and it must still be surfaced — then add a catch-all tab or an admin-visible warning rather than silently hiding the connection.

### canonical_refs
- ADR-016 D1 (Event/Post separate entities), D4 (`kinds` per connection)
- ADR-008 D2 (no speculative abstraction — filter at render time using existing field, no new abstraction layer)
- ADR-008 D1 (refactor hard — apply shell pattern fully to post composer, no conditional shim)

## Harness target

**Signal:** Child C MUST ADD `syndication/tests/test_hub_fragment_branching.py` cases with a `PlatformConnection(kinds=['promotion'])` fixture asserting on `response.content` (assertContains/assertNotContains, NOT response.context) that Telegram is ABSENT from the event composer tab row and PRESENT in the post composer tab row; FetLife (both) and Switch (both) appear in both. The harness is RED until these new tests exist AND pass. Run via: `uv run pytest syndication/tests/test_hub_fragment_branching.py -v`.

**Expected green:** The NEW branching test cases added by this child pass: Telegram absent from the event composer tab row (assertNotContains on response.content) and present in the post composer tab row (assertContains on response.content); FetLife (both) and Switch (both) confirmed present in both composer tab rows; `makemigrations --check` exits 0.

**Rationale:** Covers parent-signal dimension (3) capability-filtered tabs — Telegram absent from event composer. The view/fragment-branching test is the fastest goal-faithful signal for template-conditional rendering: it catches the filtering logic without requiring a driven browser session. Per `.claude/harness.md` templates fit profile, fragment-branching tests are the right altitude for "which channels appear in which template." The driven browser check for this dimension lives at Child E (composed verification), not here.

**Invalidation:** If the branching tests pass but a real operator's event composer still shows Telegram (e.g. because the fixture didn't match production `kinds` values) — the fixture was wrong, not the test; align the fixture with the actual seeded `PlatformConnection` data.
