title: Drop the Approve gate from the solo flow; one Publish CTA + autosave (D6)
design:
### Context
`edit_version` raises when all consumers are non-draft (services.py:1000); autosave must not fire after the projection exits `draft` — enforced at the template layer by gating the editable surface on `proj.status == 'draft'`. Child A's reshape MUST preserve this guard.

The engine (`syndication/engine.py`) has NO `draft → published` edge and materializes `frozen_content` only at `draft → ready`. A direct `transition_status(proj, "published")` from `draft` raises (illegal transition) and/or ships unfrozen content — an ADR-008 D3 violation. The solo Publish CTA must therefore drive an internal `draft → ready → published` sequence: the `approve_projection` service step runs first (materializes `frozen_content`), then `publish_projection` runs. The three-state model is preserved for future agent-drafted or collaborative-review flows; this child makes the two-step invisible to the user, not absent from the engine.

### Firmness
FLEXIBLE (inherited from parent D6). Invalidation: if solo authors want a staged/review-all-before-batch-push step, re-surface `ready` as an opt-in. The implementation constraint (internal two-step) is FIRM within this child — it is enforced by `_LEGAL_TRANSITIONS` in the engine.

### Rationale
`external:` ADR-016 D5's own Invalidation clause predicted this ("why two steps?"). `external:` Typefully has no approve gate. `reasoned:` the dead-end `ready` state is friction for a solo author with no collaborators. `reasoned:` freeze rule unchanged — `published` never carries un-frozen content (ADR-008 D3). `direct:` `approve_projection` (~line 1047, `syndication/services.py`) + `publish_projection` (~line 1074) already exist; wiring the Publish CTA to call both in sequence is lower-risk than restructuring the engine. `direct:` autosave rides the `version-edit` endpoint (`syndication:version-edit`, views.py:991 → `edit_version` services.py:990, in-place body mutation); autosave is a debounced HTMX trigger on that endpoint, NOT on `customize` (which branches a new ContentVersion row — a separate detach action).

### Alternatives

| Alternative | Decision | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Add a `draft → published` edge to the engine | Rejected | `direct:` violates `_LEGAL_TRANSITIONS` invariant; `frozen_content` is only materialized at `draft → ready`; a direct edge would ship unfrozen content (ADR-008 D3 violation). |
| Keep Approve visible but label it "Publish" | Rejected | `reasoned:` same two-click friction; misleads users; does not simplify the mental model. |
| Remove autosave, keep explicit Save | Rejected | `external:` Typefully has no explicit save; `reasoned:` autosave is the UX contract the parent epic commits to; explicit save creates state-consistency concerns (unsaved edits on tab switch). |

**What would invalidate this design:** If the internal two-step (`ready → published`) imposes perceptible latency (two serial DB writes + freeze computation visible as UI stutter) — expose the freeze as a background step or pre-compute at autosave time, rather than blocking the Publish click.

### canonical_refs
- ADR-016 D5 (solo-flow direct publish; three-state model preserved for agent/collaborative flows)
- ADR-008 D3 (fail loud on data integrity — no published row with null `frozen_content`)
- ADR-016 D1 (three-state engine invariant; `ready` is the freeze point)
- ADR-017 D1, D2 (authz seam — unchanged by this child)

## Harness target

**Signal:** `uv run pytest syndication/tests/ -k "publish or approve" -v` to confirm the publish lifecycle tests pass and no `approve` view is exercised in the solo path; PLUS a direct DB assertion in a test: after the Publish CTA is invoked on a `draft` projection, assert `proj.status == "published"` AND `proj.frozen_content is not None` (freeze was materialized before status flipped to published); PLUS a rendered-content assertion (`assertNotContains(response, 'Approve')` on the event_syndication fragment for a `draft` projection) confirming zero Approve controls in the DOM after the CTA change.

**Expected green:** All matched tests pass; the DB assertion confirms `frozen_content` is non-null on the published row; no test invokes `approve_projection` as a separate user-facing call (it is called internally by the Publish path, not as an explicit author action).

**Rationale:** Covers parent-signal dimension (5) one Publish CTA / zero Approve / no user-visible ready. The DB-state assertion is the goal-faithful signal for the implementation constraint (internal two-step, freeze materialized) — a passing UI test that skips the freeze check would miss the ADR-008 D3 invariant. Per `.claude/harness.md`, view-test context assertions are insufficient for lifecycle correctness; the DB-state check is the floor signal.

**Invalidation:** If the DB assertion passes but a subsequent integration run shows `frozen_content` being null on some `published` rows (e.g. due to a race condition in the two-step) — the single-call test didn't cover concurrency; add a concurrent-invocation integration test.
acceptance_criteria:
- The "Approve" button and any user-visible "Approve" control are absent from the event and post composer surfaces.
- No user-visible `ready` state is surfaced to the author in the solo flow (the three-state engine model is preserved internally; `ready` is never rendered as an author-facing step).
- A single Publish CTA is present and correctly labeled.
- Clicking Publish on a `draft` projection drives an internal `draft → ready → published` transition sequence (freeze at `ready`, then `published`) — NOT a direct `draft → published` call. Verified by inspecting `syndication/engine.py` `_LEGAL_TRANSITIONS` and confirming `frozen_content` is non-null on the published projection row.
- Autosave replaces the explicit per-field Save button; edits are persisted without a manual save action.
- Existing render-regression and view tests pass; djlint clean; `makemigrations --check` clean.
- Known scope caveat (carry verbatim): Publish does not yet invoke platform adapters (kb-jgda); this child wires Publish to the existing publish service, it does not fix adapter dispatch.
- The autosave trigger is absent/disabled for projections not in `draft` status — the edit-in-place surface becomes read-only once Publish advances the projection to `ready`/`published` (carries forward the existing `status=='draft'` edit guard into the redesigned surface).
close_reason: D6 — drop Approve gate: removed user-facing Approve from event_syndication, post_syndication, AND review_all (the latter caught by fresh-context review — it was missed in the first pass). One Publish CTA driving internal draft→ready→published via new publish_projection_direct (freeze at ready, never direct draft→published — engine has no such edge). Autosave replaces explicit Save: focus-preserving (hx-swap=none + debounced trigger + 'Saved' indicator), gated on status=='draft' so it never fires post-publish (edit_version raises on non-draft consumers). Three-state engine model + approve_projection preserved for future collaborative flow + the internal step + failed-Retry. Review findings resolved: review_all Approve removed (fixed); two-step non-atomic partial-failure lands in recoverable failed/ready state (acceptable per ADR-008 D3/D4); can_publish==can_edit at v0 so CTA gate change is harmless (ADR-017 D2). 710 syndication tests green, djlint + makemigrations clean. Commits 14acb3f, aa6ad28. Composed driven verification at kb-ide0.5.

title: Build the edit-in-place composer shell (Switch listing, event composer only)
design:
### Context
Note: `templates/syndication/fragments/event_syndication.html` currently has NO `studio_swap` handling (a `dry-partial-merge-collapses-render-contexts` failure mode); this child introduces `studio_swap` gating to the restructured template to cover both standalone and HTMX-fragment render paths.

D1 (canonical-as-first-tab), D2 (edit-in-place card), and D5 (single top row) share a single DOM surface — the event composer shell. They cannot be landed green independently: shipping the single top row over an intact textarea is a red intermediate; shipping edit-in-place without removing the facts-block duplication still violates D1. The parent's Decomposition notes flagged this explicitly: land them together, scoped to ONE channel (Switch listing on the event composer), to de-risk the load-bearing edit-in-place surface before tabs and sync layers are added.

### Firmness
FLEXIBLE (inherited from parent D1, D2, D5). The Invalidation clauses from each parent decision are carried forward:
- If dogfooding reveals that the card-as-form is too cramped for 25 event fields (D1 invalidation), a structured-edit affordance reachable from the canonical tab is the fallback — not a full revert.
- If the engine's platform-specific rendering proves too rich to make editable in place without a client-side renderer rewrite (D2 invalidation), fall back to a minimal post-shaped editor + live adjacent preview (Typefully two-pane), which still kills the stacked-stale-preview problem.
- If tabs + CTA + status don't fit one row at narrow viewports without truncation harm (D5 invalidation), allow a responsive second row at small breakpoints only.

### Rationale
`external:` ADR-010 D1 — canonical is presented as the Switch channel tab (the master); others sync-or-diverge. This child realizes that decision on the DOM. `direct:` `event_facts.html` and the Switch listing tab in `event_syndication.html` both render the same canonical object — the duplication the redesign removes. `direct:` previews are server-rendered through the engine today (`_channel_preview.html`); edit-in-place keeps engine rendering but makes the surface an input that re-renders live via Alpine, not a client-side renderer rewrite. `reasoned:` landing D1+D2+D5 as one slice, one channel, ensures each subsequent child (B, C, D) has a stable shell to extend rather than a partially-converted intermediate.

### Alternatives

| Alternative | Decision | Warrant |
|---|---|---|
| Land D1/D2/D5 as three separate children in sequence | Rejected | `direct:` they share one DOM surface (`event_syndication.html` + the facts fragment slot); any intermediate state has one decision partially applied over the other's DOM surface, which cannot be green-tested in isolation. |
| Scope to all channels from the start | Rejected | `reasoned:` loads D3 (capability filtering) into the same slice; D3 cannot be green until multiple channels render; the shell itself would remain unverifiable until D3 is proven. `external:` parent Decomposition notes: "Land [D1+D2+D5] scoped to ONE channel first." |
| Remove facts block but keep textarea + preview | Rejected | `reasoned:` violates D2; removes one duplication while leaving the deeper WYSIWYG problem untouched; does not give the harness a meaningful intermediate signal. |

**What would invalidate this design:** If the structured event fields (`_event_form_fields.html`, ~25 fields) cannot be embedded inside the styled listing card without unacceptable layout cost at the card's intrinsic width — then keep the card-as-form affordance for promotion-shaped content only, and surface the structured edit inside a drawer/tab-panel reachable from the listing tab rather than inline.

### canonical_refs
- ADR-016 D1 (event/post as separate entities; canonical as first tab)
- ADR-010 D1 (Switch own-page tab is the master)
- ADR-008 D1 (refactor hard, no back-compat shim — delete facts fragment, no conditional preservation)
- ADR-008 D2 (no speculative abstraction — whole-card edit-in-place, not per-field dynamic injection)

## Harness target

**Signal:** `uv run pytest syndication/test_render_regressions.py syndication/tests/test_hub_fragment_branching.py -v` to confirm no regressions; PLUS a scoped driven browser check (browser-automation skill, single session): navigate to the event composer, confirm the top row is a single bar (tabs left, Publish right via DOM assertion), type into a field inside the Switch listing card and assert the card re-renders live (non-stale content visible), assert no `event_facts` block is present in the DOM. The driven browser check MUST navigate the composer both via direct URL (standalone path) and via in-studio rail click (HTMX path) to confirm both render paths satisfy the acceptance.

**Expected green:** All regression tests pass (`syndication/test_render_regressions.py`, `syndication/tests/test_hub_fragment_branching.py`); the driven browser check observes: (a) exactly one nav row in the composer header, (b) a live cursor inside the styled listing card with content reflecting typed input on re-render, (c) no element matching the event-facts block selector present in the DOM, (d) both standalone and HTMX-fragment render paths satisfy the acceptance.

**Rationale:** Covers parent-signal dimensions (1) no duplicated facts block, (2) edit-in-place with live cursor, and (5) single top row — the three dimensions this child is responsible for. Per `.claude/harness.md` templates/Alpine fit profile: Alpine-driven re-render behavior is invisible to view tests (context assertions pass on broken templates; Alpine directives are inert without `x-data`); the driven browser check is the lowest-altitude signal that is goal-faithful for edit-in-place re-render. The regression suite is the floor for "no unintended breakage."

**Invalidation:** If the driven check passes (DOM assertions satisfied) but a real author reports that the card re-render lags visibly or loses cursor position on fast typing — the driven test drove too coarse a flow; add a typed-burst interaction to the driven script and observe cursor continuity.
acceptance_criteria:
- The event composer surface renders a single top row: channel tabs left-aligned, Publish CTA right-aligned — no second navbar row underneath the first.
- The Switch listing tab IS the editor: the platform-styled card contains typed structured inputs (not a free textarea). Typing in any field re-renders the card live (Alpine reactive) without a page reload.
- The read-only "event facts" block (`event_facts.html`) and the "Edit event" detour link no longer appear on the composer surface.
- The canonical Switch listing content appears exactly once — as the first/anchor tab — not duplicated above the tab row.
- The existing render-regression and view tests pass (`uv run pytest syndication/`), djlint passes, `makemigrations --check` is clean.
- The Publish button in this slice routes to the existing publish endpoint without error (lifecycle change deferred to Child B; the button is wired, not re-designed).
- Scoped to the Switch listing channel only — other channel tabs are unchanged or hidden pending Child C.
- Both render contexts are exercised: the event composer renders correctly via the standalone full-page path AND when loaded as an HTMX fragment inside the studio shell; any navigation/cross-link added to the redesigned shell must not unconditionally bake in studio-context behavior — apply the `studio_swap` gating pattern (as `_post_hub_body.html` / `post_syndication.html` already do) if cross-links are introduced.
notes:
## Design decision (user, 2026-06-04) — listing edit-in-place shape

For the structured Switch LISTING tab, edit-in-place = **fields ARE the card, NO separate preview**. The ~structured EventForm inputs are styled to read as the Switch listing itself (title large serif, dates inline, description, accent hairline); there is NO separate engine-rendered "Preview" block for the Switch-listing draft case — the card the user edits IS the listing representation (WYSIWYG by construction). This resolves the ambiguity in acceptance bullet 2's "re-render the styled surface live": for the structured listing there is nothing separate to re-render (you edit the styled fields directly). The literal type-into-the-rendered-bubble live-WYSIWYG applies to the freeform POST/promotion surfaces (Children C/D), not the structured listing.

Child C MUST inherit this shape when applying the shell pattern to the post composer for any structured-listing channel.

Commits de44d37, 10d6225. Composed driven /ui-craft verification deferred to kb-ide0.5 per design.

title: Redesign the syndication composer as a single edit-in-place multi-channel surface (Typefully-grade)
design:
## Context

The syndication composer (the per-Event and per-Post multi-channel content editor) currently reads as a stack of separate slabs: a structured "event facts" block + an "Edit event" form detour at the top, then — below it — a tabbed board where each platform projection has a freeform `<textarea>` and a *separate, read-only, stacked-below* styled preview. The canonical event therefore appears twice (as the facts block AND as the Switch/Listing tab), editing is a generic textarea decoupled from what the user will actually see, and the publish path forces an "Approve" step into a dead-end `ready` state before a second "Publish" click.

We converged (this brainstorm) on a Typefully-grade redesign — grounded in a fresh read of Typefully's actual composer (the editor *is* the styled post, with a live edit cursor; per-channel sync toggle; discard-confirm on re-sync; single top row; Schedule/Publish as the one CTA; no approve gate). The redesign is NOT a Typefully clone: Switch's differentiator is ToS-divergent destinations (FetLife long/explicit, Telegram short/tamer, Switch editorial), which forces a per-channel *choosable* sync source that Typefully (single-primary) doesn't have.

Why now: the composer is the core authoring surface for the syndication MVP (epic kb-a4u), about to be dogfooded; its current shape is the most-cited UX weakness. The backend machinery this redesign rides on already exists (content_version FK + customize/copy_from/reset, connection.kinds, the status engine) — this is largely a UI/IA reshape plus making the engine-rendered card an edit surface.

## Decisions

### D1: One composer surface — the canonical IS the first tab; no separate "event up top" (FLEXIBLE)

Collapse the "event facts block + Edit-event detour + separate Switch/Listing tab" into a **single surface**: the canonical content is the **first/anchor tab** (the Switch own-page tab for an Event; the abstract "Source" anchor for a Post, per ADR-010 D1), edited directly. No duplicated facts block, no separate edit-event form route.

- **Rationale:** `direct:` the canonical currently renders twice (facts fragment `templates/syndication/fragments/event_facts.html` + the Switch listing tab in `event_syndication.html`) — a duplication users read as redundancy. `external:` ADR-010 D1 already states the canonical is *"presented as the Switch channel tab (the master); other channels sync-or-diverge from it"* — this realizes a decision already on the books. `reasoned:` one surface = one mental model; the editing target and the source-of-truth are the same object.
- **What would invalidate:** dogfooding shows authors want the structured event form as a distinct dense data-entry surface separate from the channel preview (i.e. the card-as-form is too cramped for 25 fields) — then keep a structured-edit affordance reachable from the canonical tab rather than forcing all editing into the card.

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Keep "event facts up top" + composer below (current) | `direct:` renders the canonical twice; `reasoned:` two editing entry points for one object, the redundancy the redesign exists to remove. |
| Canonical as a non-editable header, channels below | `reasoned:` re-introduces the edit-event detour; the canonical is the most-edited object, hiding its editor behind a link is backwards. |

### D2: Edit-in-place — the platform-skinned card IS the editor (FLEXIBLE)

The editing surface is the **platform-styled card/bubble itself**, edited in place with a live cursor (the listing card for listing kind; the chat-bubble/post for promotion kind). No separate `<textarea>` + read-only stacked preview. The surface re-renders live as you type.

- **Rationale:** `external:` Typefully's editor IS the styled post (verified via user screenshots — live edit cursor inside the rendered Bluesky/LinkedIn post); the separate-editor-plus-preview is the single most un-Typefully part of the current UI. `reasoned:` WYSIWYG collapses the "edit here / see there" split into one object, removing the duplication and the context switch. `direct:` previews are server-rendered through the engine today (`_channel_preview.html`) — the build keeps engine rendering but makes the surface an input that re-renders live (Alpine), rather than rebuilding rendering client-side.
- **What would invalidate:** the engine's platform-specific rendering proves too rich to make editable in place without a client-side renderer rewrite (cost balloons) — then fall back to a minimal post-shaped editor + a live adjacent preview (Typefully's actual two-pane), which still kills the stacked-stale-preview problem.

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Keep textarea + separate styled preview (current) | `reasoned:` the duplication + non-WYSIWYG split the redesign exists to remove. |
| Literal contenteditable on a server-rendered preview only | `reasoned:` for the *structured listing* the fields need typed inputs, not a contenteditable blob; edit-in-place means typed-fields-in-the-card for listing, contenteditable-bubble for promotion. |

### D3: Posts and Events are separate composers; channels filtered by capability via `connection.kinds` (FLEXIBLE)

Two composers, not one mixed surface. The **event composer** shows only **listing-capable** channels; the **post composer** shows only **promotion-capable** channels — filtered by the existing `PlatformConnection.kinds` JSON list (`listing` / `promotion`). Telegram (`promotion`-only) never appears in the event composer; FetLife (both) appears in both; Switch (both) appears in both.

- **Rationale:** `external:` ADR-016 D1 (Event/Post are separate entities) + D4 (`kinds` per connection) — this is the UI realization, no schema change. `direct:` `kinds` already drives eager projection creation (`syndication/services.py` `_eager_create_listing_projections` / `_eager_create_promotion_projections`). `reasoned:` removes the awkward "promotion tab inside the event composer" the earlier sketch had.
- **What would invalidate:** authors want a single unified surface that composes the listing and its promo posts together (e.g. a campaign view) — then add a cross-composer campaign view, but keep the per-publishable composers as the editing primitives.

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| One composer mixing listing + promotion tabs | `reasoned:` conflates two content types (structured event vs message) with different shapes; `external:` contradicts ADR-016 D1 separation. |

### D4: Per-channel "sync FROM another channel" as a live binding (FLEXIBLE — canonicalized in ADR-016 D2 evolution)

Each secondary channel carries a **sync toggle** choosing **which channel it syncs from** (live binding), defaulting to the canonical (Switch). Editing a synced channel **detaches** it (custom); flipping sync back on **discards the channel's edits** behind a "discard your edits?" confirm modal. A channel may sync only from an *independent* (non-synced) channel (cycle guard).

- **Rationale:** `external:` user direction — ToS divergence means no single canonical feeds every channel; the differentiator vs Typefully's single-primary. `external:` Typefully's per-channel sync toggle + the "Discard text and sync?" modal (user screenshots) is the proven UX to steal. `direct:` builds on the existing `content_version` FK + `customize` / `reset_to_canonical` ops (`syndication/services.py`); the current one-shot "Copy from" dropdown is the seed. `reasoned:` re-sync is destructive → fail-loud confirm per ADR-008 D3.
- **LOAD-BEARING OPEN MECHANISM (resolve at child-design, flagged by adversarial review 2026-06-03):** the as-shipped `copy_from` mints an *independent copy* (a snapshot), and the live-derive mechanism only resolves to the publishable's *canonical* — NOT a peer channel's version. So "sync FROM another channel" is NOT free with current code. The child bead must choose: **(a) live** — synced projection shares the source's `content_version` row (existing single-row broadcast; a source edit propagates), needs a recorded directional `sync_source` field + detach-on-edit; or **(b) snapshot** — re-`copy_from` on (re)sync (no new field, no live propagation). The epic does NOT pre-decide; the UX contract (toggle / detach-on-edit / discard-confirm / cycle guard) holds either way. Do NOT assert "no new schema" until (a)-vs-(b) is settled.
- **What would invalidate:** facilitators want a reusable named register decoupled from any publishing channel (a "short-censored" base several channels follow that is itself never published) — then promote the source from a channel-handle to a first-class named `ContentVersion` in the dropdown (the deferred branch named in ADR-016 D2).

| Alternative | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Single canonical source for all (Typefully primary model) | `external:` user — ToS divergence breaks single-source; FetLife-long can't feed Telegram-short. |
| Abstract named content variants as sources (not channels) | `reasoned:` ADR-008 D2 — more concept + schema; channel-as-source is the simpler thing that fits and no second caller yet earns the register layer. Deferred, not killed (ADR-016 D2 invalidation names the promotion path). |
| Per-field sync (inherit/override per field) | `reasoned:` whole-channel sync is what Typefully does and what the backend already models (whole content_version); per-field is more machinery without a present need. |
| Treat the binding mechanism as settled ("reuses copy_from, no new schema") | `direct:` adversarial review 2026-06-03 verified `copy_from` is a one-shot copy and live-derive only targets the canonical — the claim was false; mechanism is genuinely open (see LOAD-BEARING note above). |

### D5: Single top row — tabs left, Publish right (FLEXIBLE)

One top bar: channel tabs left-aligned, the Publish CTA right-aligned. Not two stacked navbars (the current title-row + tab-row split).

- **Rationale:** `external:` Typefully (tabs/toggles top-left, Schedule top-right). `reasoned:` one row = less chrome, more writing surface.
- **What would invalidate:** the tab set + CTA + status don't fit one row at narrow viewports without truncation harm — then allow a responsive second row at small breakpoints only.

### D6: Drop the Approve gate from the solo flow — Publish is the one CTA (FLEXIBLE — canonicalized in ADR-016 D5 evolution)

In the solo/human flow, **draft publishes directly** — no "Approve" button, no user-surfaced `ready` state. One **Publish** CTA. Autosave replaces the explicit per-edit Save. The three-state `draft→ready→published` model is preserved for future agent-drafted/collaborative review, and `frozen_content` is still materialized before publish (freeze-at-publish).

- **Rationale:** `external:` ADR-016 D5's own Invalidation clause predicted this ("why two steps?"); `external:` Typefully has no approve gate (base flow draft→published). `reasoned:` the dead-end `ready` state is friction for a solo author. `reasoned:` freeze rule unchanged → `published` never carries un-frozen content (ADR-008 D3).
- **Implementation constraint (adversarial review 2026-06-03):** the engine (`syndication/engine.py`) has **no `draft → published` edge** and materializes `frozen_content` only at `draft → ready`. The solo Publish CTA must therefore drive an **internal `draft → ready → published`** (freeze at the ready step) — NEVER a direct `transition_status(proj, "published")` from draft, which raises and/or ships unfrozen published content.
- **What would invalidate:** solo authors want a staged/review-all-before-batch-push step — re-surface `ready` as an opt-in.
- **Scope caveat (carried, not solved here):** there is a known pre-existing gap that Publish does not yet invoke the platform adapters (publish flips status without posting — see kb-a4u progress memory / kb-jgda). "Publish really posts" is separate open backend work; this epic owns the *composer UI*, and its Publish wires to the existing publish service as-is.

## Acceptance contract

The redesigned composer, observed live in a browser by an authenticated operator, satisfies ALL of:

1. **No duplication:** the canonical content appears once — as the first/anchor tab — with no separate "event facts" block or "Edit event" form detour on the composer surface.
2. **Edit-in-place:** the user types directly into the platform-styled card/bubble (live cursor in the rendered surface); there is no separate `<textarea>` + stacked read-only preview. Edits re-render the styled surface live.
3. **Separate, capability-filtered composers:** the event composer shows only listing-capable channels; the post composer only promotion-capable; a promotion-only channel (Telegram) is absent from the event composer.
4. **Sync-from-channel + discard guard:** a secondary channel has a sync toggle naming its source channel; editing it detaches to custom; re-enabling sync fires a "discard your edits?" confirm before reverting; a synced channel is not offered as a sync source (cycle guard).
5. **Single top row:** tabs left-aligned, Publish right-aligned, one bar.
6. **One CTA, no approve:** there is a single Publish CTA and no "Approve" control / no user-visible `ready` step; saving is automatic.
7. **No regressions:** existing render-regression and view tests stay green (`uv run pytest syndication/`), djlint clean, `makemigrations --check` clean (no unintended schema drift).

## Harness target

**Signal** — A live, *driven* browser-automation pass (CDP, the `browser-automation` skill) over the redesigned composer on a running instance, executed as a `/ui-craft` build→screenshot→read-back→critique loop per surface (event composer, post composer), PLUS one fresh-context adversarial comparison agent that walks the *actual flow* against the documented Typefully reference behaviors (this epic's `--design` + the Typefully UX characterization) and names residual UX gaps. The agent must DRIVE the flow (type into the card, toggle sync, trigger the discard modal, switch tabs, hit Publish), not screenshot static states.

**Expected green** — GREEN is the binary conjunction of these driven observations (each must be *driven*, not screenshotted): (1) edit-in-place — type into the styled card, observe a real cursor in the rendered surface and live re-render; (2) single top row, tabs-left/Publish-right; (3) capability-filtered tabs — the event composer shows NO promotion-only channel (Telegram); (4a) the sync-from-channel toggle names a source and detaches on edit; (4b) re-enabling sync fires the discard-confirm modal — driven by actually toggling off, editing, toggling on; (4c) **cycle guard driven** — attempt to pick an already-synced channel as a source and observe it is not offered; (5) one Publish CTA, zero Approve control, no user-visible "ready" step; (6) no separate textarea+stacked-preview; (7) no duplicated "event facts up top"; (8) the `/ui-craft` slop-test passes (no AI-slop reflexes). Green = all of 1–8 demonstrated. The **Typefully-gap critique is ADDITIVE, not part of the pass/fail gate**: the fresh-context comparison agent surfaces residual UX gaps and files them as follow-up beads (deliberate divergences from Typefully — structured listing fields, channel-as-source, per-channel ToS variants — are explicitly NOT gaps); it does not render a green/not-green verdict, so the "deliberate-vs-missing" judgment never gates the harness.

**Rationale** — Per `.claude/harness.md` (templates / Alpine fit profiles) and memories `parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift`, `alpine-3-x-directives-mouseenter-click-class-x`, `django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow`: UI/HTMX/Alpine behavior and rendered-output regressions are invisible to view tests (context assertions pass on broken templates; Alpine directives are inert without `x-data` and only surface live). The goal-faithful altitude is a *driven* live browser flow at the composed/parent-re-verify level — exactly because the originating concern is that prior verification passes screenshotted surfaces but never went through the UX flow. Unit/view tests are the floor (acceptance bullet 7), not the goal-faithful signal for "the composer feels right and matches the agreed Typefully properties."

**Invalidation** — If the driven inspection passes but a real dogfooding author hits a composer flow the inspection didn't drive (deep-link to a single channel tab, refresh mid-edit losing autosave state, a sync source that became synced after selection) — the harness drove too narrow a flow set; widen the driven flows rather than trusting the green. (Signal-shaped, no numeric threshold per ADR-008 D8.)

## Decomposition notes

Guidance for the decomposition pass, not a fixed recipe (adversarial review 2026-06-03 flagged shared-DOM entanglement):

- **D1 + D2 + D5 are one DOM surface** (the single composer shell: canonical-as-first-tab, edit-in-place card, single top row). They cannot land independently green — a child shipping the top row over the old textarea is a red intermediate. Land them together as the **first slice, scoped to ONE channel** (Switch listing on the event composer) — this de-risks the load-bearing edit-in-place surface before tabs/sync layer on.
- **D6 (drop Approve / autosave)** is the most separable — it's a lifecycle/CTA change, can land early or in parallel; carries the engine `draft→ready→published` internal-transition constraint above.
- **D3 (capability-filtered tabs)** layers onto the shell once multiple channels render.
- **D4 (sync-from-channel)** layers LAST and carries the load-bearing open mechanism (live-vs-snapshot) — its child design must resolve (a)-vs-(b) before claiming a schema posture.
- The **harness target runs at parent-re-verify altitude** on the composed surface (per `parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift`), not as per-child screenshots — a per-child green does not substitute for the driven composed read-back.

## canonical_refs

- [ADR-016 D1–D6](ADR-016-outbound-syndication-architecture-event-post-projections.md) — syndication entity + projection + lifecycle + connection model; D2 (sync-from-any-channel live binding) and D5 (solo-flow direct publish) were evolved in place 2026-06-03 for this epic.
- [ADR-010 D1](ADR-010-event-based-product-posture.md) — canonical is the Switch own-page tab (the master); others sync-or-diverge; real-world-action posture.
- [ADR-008 D1, D2, D3](ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md) — refactor hard / no back-compat shim (pre-launch clean reshape); no speculative abstraction (channel-as-source over named-register; whole-channel over per-field sync); fail-loud (discard-confirm on destructive re-sync, no silent overwrite).
- [ADR-017 D1, D2](ADR-017-authorization-edit-publish-policy.md) — edit/publish authority via the single authz seam; unchanged by this redesign.
- [ADR-003](ADR-003-cheap-foresight-patterns.md) — `ContentVersion.name` already supports the named-register shape the deferred D4 branch would use.
- `.claude/harness.md` — templates + Alpine fit profiles; the live-browser-read-back-at-composed-state mechanism this epic's Harness target adopts.
- Typefully composer UX characterization (this brainstorm, 2026-06-03) — reference behaviors the harness compares against; NOT a clone target.

title: Align on how someone becomes an organizer (claim-only is the current sole route)

title: CI test job red: makemigrations/check --deploy fail Django system checks E006/E007 (PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True but IMPRESSUM_*/TURNSTILE_* unset in CI env)
design:
Discovered 2026-06-02 while shipping kb-va4a. Now that kb-va4a unblocked the pytest step, the test job PROGRESSES to the next step — `uv run python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` — which runs Django system checks first and fails:

  (a_core.E006) PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True but required legal env vars are empty: IMPRESSUM_NAME, IMPRESSUM_ADDRESS, IMPRESSUM_EMAIL
  (a_core.E007) PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True but Turnstile env vars are missing: TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY

These are deliberate fail-loud guards (custom checks for the public-read posture, ADR-008 D3 shape) firing because the test job in .github/workflows/test.yml does NOT set those env vars while PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED defaults True. NEWLY EXPOSED, not introduced — the step runs after pytest under `bash -e`, so it was masked the whole time the 2 Telegram tests (kb-va4a) were red. Same env-coupling CLASS as kb-va4a, but at the settings/system-check layer instead of a test. The subsequent `check --deploy` step is also gated behind this and never ran.

Fix options (do NOT weaken the E006/E007 guards — they are correct): (a) set PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=False in the test job's env block — the suite does not exercise the public-read gate, so this is likely the minimal correct fix (ADR-008 D2); OR (b) provide placeholder IMPRESSUM_NAME/ADDRESS/EMAIL + Cloudflare TURNSTILE test keys in the test job env (NOT the real operator identity — dummies only). Verify both makemigrations --check AND check --deploy go green with the chosen fix. canonical_refs: ADR-008 D3 (guards are correct fail-loud; CI env is what's incomplete), ADR-008 D2 (minimal fix). Related env-coupling: kb-va4a.
acceptance_criteria:
- CI Tests workflow 'test' job passes its makemigrations --check AND check --deploy steps on main HEAD.
- Fix is in CI workflow env config (or a CI-only settings default), NOT by weakening or removing the a_core.E006/E007 system checks.
- gitleaks/bandit/lint/pytest steps remain green (no regression).

CI Tests 'test' job green: makemigrations --check + check --deploy both pass; pytest + lint + security (gitleaks/bandit/pip-audit) all green (run 26832577784). title: Studio cross-links silently no-op on standalone composer pages (hx-target=#studio-main absent)
design:
## Context
Discovered-from kb-9f1h parent re-verify (2026-06-02). kb-9f1h.3 extracted shared body partials (`_event_hub_body.html` / `_post_hub_body.html`) used by BOTH the standalone full page AND the in-studio HX fragment. That merge pulled the in-shell-rewired cross-links (which carry `hx-target="#studio-main"`) into the STANDALONE composer path — where `#studio-main` does not exist.

## The defect
Two cross-links carry `hx-target="#studio-main"`:
- `templates/syndication/_post_hub_body.html:19` — the post composer's "Event hub ↗" back-link.
- `templates/syndication/fragments/post_syndication.html:17` — the post syndication board's "Event hub ↗" link.

Both render in BOTH contexts. On a STANDALONE composer page (reached by deep-link / refresh / typing `/syndication/posts/<pk>/` directly — a real, documented entry path), `#studio-main` is absent. HTMX intercepts the click (hx-get present → preventDefault), tries to swap into the missing `#studio-main`, fires `htmx:targetError`, and does NOTHING — the `href` fallback never fires. Result: a silent UI no-op. This is BOTH a regression from the pre-epic plain-`<a href>` navigation AND an ADR-008 D3 silent-fallback violation. The in-studio flow works (verified by kb-9f1h.5); only the standalone path is broken, which is why the composed read-back missed it.

## Decision (FLEXIBLE)
Make the cross-links context-aware: **swap within `#studio-main` when rendered in the studio shell; full-navigate (plain `<a href>`) when rendered standalone.**
- Thread a `studio_swap` (or `studio_context`) boolean into the shared body partials: the fragment includes (`event_hub_fragment.html`, `post_hub_fragment.html`) pass it True; the full-page includes (`event_hub.html`, `post_hub.html`) leave it falsy. Gate the back-link's `hx-get`/`hx-target`/`hx-push-url` on it; the `href` is always present as the standalone behavior.
- The board sub-fragment (`post_syndication.html`) is loaded via a SEPARATE `hx-get` (`hx-trigger="load"`) from inside the body — its rendering context must also know `studio_swap`. Thread it through that section's hx-get (e.g. a `?studio=1` query param the board view reads, or equivalent) so the board's "Event hub ↗" link is likewise context-aware. Pick the simplest correct mechanism; do NOT over-build (ADR-008 D2).
- **canonical_refs:** ADR-008 D3 (no silent fallback — a user click must do something visible); parent kb-9f1h D2 (swap contract is for the in-studio context); .claude/harness.md:220 (composed read-back missed this because it only exercised the in-studio path).

## Harness target
**Signal:** browser read-back via `browser-automation` against `runserver` :8009 (the studio_readback.mjs probe is a starting point), testing the cross-link in BOTH contexts: (A) IN-STUDIO — open /studio/, click a Post row, then click the composer's "Event hub ↗" → it SWAPS #studio-main to the event composer AND window.location pushes to /syndication/events/<pk>/ (no full reload). (B) STANDALONE — navigate directly to /syndication/posts/<pk>/, click "Event hub ↗" → the browser NAVIGATES (full page) to /syndication/events/<pk>/ (window.location changes, a real event-hub full page renders). Plus a `response.content` test asserting the standalone post_hub page's cross-link is a plain navigable `<a href>` (no bare hx-target=#studio-main without an href, or context-gated so standalone omits the swap attrs).
**Expected green:** in-studio click swaps in-shell; standalone click navigates (NOT a silent no-op); neither context leaves the user with a dead click.
**Rationale:** the defect is precisely that one rendering serves two contexts with one (wrong-for-standalone) behavior. The goal-faithful signal must exercise BOTH contexts live — a single-context test (in-studio only) is what let the regression through at kb-9f1h.5. ADR-008 D3 fail-loud: a click that silently does nothing is the failure.
**Invalidation:** if the standalone test only asserts the `href` attribute is PRESENT (without confirming HTMX doesn't intercept-and-no-op), it can pass while the real click still dead-ends — the live standalone click must actually change window.location. If a future refactor removes the standalone full-page composer entirely (studio-only), this whole concern dissolves and the gate is re-scoped.

## Origin
Discovered-from kb-9f1h parent re-verify round 1 (F2/F6). See parent's notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- In the STUDIO context (composer loaded into #studio-main via the rail), clicking a composer's 'Event hub ↗' cross-link swaps #studio-main to the event composer AND pushes window.location to /syndication/events/<pk>/ (no full reload).
- In the STANDALONE context (composer reached directly at /syndication/posts/<pk>/ via deep-link/refresh/typed URL), clicking 'Event hub ↗' performs a real browser NAVIGATION to /syndication/events/<pk>/ (window.location changes, full event-hub page renders) — NOT a silent no-op (ADR-008 D3).
- Both affected links handled: _post_hub_body.html back-link AND post_syndication.html board link.
- A test asserts the standalone post_hub cross-link is navigable (context-gated so standalone omits the bare hx-target=#studio-main, or otherwise degrades to href navigation). Verified live in BOTH contexts via browser read-back. djlint clean; full suite green.
close_reason: Cross-link standalone-context regression fixed (commit 6dd7c2e). Threaded a studio_swap flag: _post_hub_body.html + post_syndication.html emit hx-get/hx-target=#studio-main/hx-push-url only in-studio (post_hub_fragment.html includes with studio_swap=True), plain navigable <a href> standalone (post_hub.html); board sub-fragment threaded via ?studio=1 -> fragment_post_syndication reads request.GET. Verified live in BOTH contexts: in-studio click swaps #studio-main (rail persists, window.location /syndication/events/46/, no reload); standalone click does real full-page navigation. +6 tests; full suite 1991 passed; djlint clean. Verdict:pass via orchestrator read-back (diff verified + both-context live read-back).

title: 2 syndication publish tests fail in CI for missing TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (env coupling)
design:
Discovered while pushing kb-33do (2026-06-02). The CI test job has 2 failures, both pre-existing kb-q4u9 work, NOT introduced by kb-33do:
- syndication/test_version_ops.py::PostOwnedProjectionPublishProbeTest::test_per_channel_publish_uses_own_frozen_body
- syndication/test_version_ops.py::PostOwnedProjectionPublishProbeTest::test_publish_all_ready_uses_own_frozen_body_per_projection

Both raise `ValueError: Cannot publish Telegram promotion projection NNN: no bot token available — set connection.credentials['bot_token'] or settings.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN. (ADR-008 D3 — fail loud)`. They PASS locally (local .env carries TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) and FAIL in CI (no token in the CI env). Classic env-coupling: the tests depend on a real settings token instead of providing one in-test.

FIX: make the tests independent of the ambient env — `@override_settings(TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="test-dummy")` (or set connection.credentials['bot_token']) in setUp/the test, so they pass deterministically in CI regardless of .env. The publish path is already httpx-mocked; only the token resolution needs an in-test value. canonical_refs: ADR-008 D3 (the fail-loud guard is correct — the TEST is what's wrong, not the code).
acceptance_criteria:
- Both PostOwnedProjectionPublishProbeTest tests pass in CI (and locally) WITHOUT depending on an ambient TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN in .env — the token is supplied in-test via override_settings or connection.credentials.
- No change to the publish code's fail-loud guard (ADR-008 D3); the fix is test-only.
close_reason: Env-coupling fixed: class-level @override_settings(TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="test-dummy-token") on PostOwnedProjectionPublishProbeTest makes token resolution deterministic regardless of ambient .env (committed d309b0c, test-only, +2 lines). Verified: RED demo (empty-token override raises the ADR-008 D3 fail-loud ValueError, the local proxy for CI's no-token state — env-clearing can't reproduce it because settings.py Env.read_env repopulates from .env); GREEN (both target tests pass); full bare 'uv run pytest' = 1991 passed, 0 failures, so the CI test job is green on this HEAD. Diff verified against pre-dispatch SHA. ADR-008 D3 guard untouched. Adversarial-review skipped: trivial test-only 2-line change, empirically verified RED->GREEN + full-suite-green.

title: CI lint job red: syndication app fails ruff (~800 errors, pre-existing kb-q4u9)
design:
Discovered while pushing kb-33do (2026-06-02). title: Integration gate: composed-state browser read-back of the full studio sequence
design:
## Context
Child of kb-9f1h. The integration / parent-re-verify-altitude gate: the composed-state browser read-back of the full studio sequence — i.e. the parent's `## Harness target` verbatim. Depends on kb-9f1h.1 + .2 + .3 (verifies their conjunction). See parent --design for the full narrative.

## Decisions

### Composed-state read-back is the load-bearing gate (harness.md:220)
Per harness.md:220, the load-bearing browser read-back for a multi-child UI epic runs on the FINAL composed state — a per-child screenshot passes while cross-child wiring stays broken (the kb-q4u9 case: a post's "publish-all-ready" fired the event-scoped endpoint; post-composer cards had no nav link — both invisible until a composed read-back). This child verifies the conjunction of .1 (gating/authz/service) + .2 (fragment swap + URL-push contract) + .3 (rail/rows/empty-state) actually composes. May add a seed/fixture helper; no production-code claim.

## Harness target
**Signal:** `browser-automation` against `manage.py runserver` (127.0.0.1:8009) with seeded fixtures (a claimant with ≥1 Event + ≥1 Post; a separate zero-publishables claimant; a zero-claims user), running this 6-step sequence and inspecting rendered DOM + post-click `window.location.pathname` (NOT response.context):
(1) navbar Studio link present for the claimant, ABSENT for a non-claimant;
(2) open studio → rail lists ≥1 Event + ≥1 Post as peers, Post row shows parent-Event subtitle;
(3) click Event row → composer renders in #studio-main AND `window.location.pathname === "/syndication/events/<pk>/"`;
(4) click Post row → composer renders in #studio-main AND `window.location.pathname === "/syndication/posts/<pk>/"`;
(5) zero-publishables claimant → empty-state CTA renders (not a blank list);
(6) zero-claims user hitting /studio/ → 403/redirect (not an empty workspace).
Active row reflects the post-navigation URL.
Concrete predicates: navbar gating via `document.querySelector('nav a[href="/studio/"]')` non-null for the claimant / null for the non-claimant; row-click navigation via `window.location.pathname === "/syndication/events/<pk>/"` (and `/posts/<pk>/`) after clicking + waiting for the swap; empty-state via a text/selector match on the CTA; zero-claims via HTTP status / redirect on a direct `/studio/` fetch.
**Expected green:** every assertion in the 6-step sequence holds against live DOM + the actual pushed URL (both row types push the REAL composer path; zero-publishables → empty-state; zero-claims → 403/redirect; navbar link present for claimant and absent for non-claimant via the querySelector predicate).
**Rationale:** this IS the parent's harness target at the composed-state altitude mandated by harness.md:220. It is the integration gate over the sibling conjunction — same altitude as the parent because no single sibling asserts the post-click window.location across BOTH row types together with the gating conjunction (so it is parent-faithful verification, not duplication of a sibling signal). Memory parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift is the warrant for a fresh composed gate distinct from per-child greens.
**Invalidation:** the present-tense boundary from the parent — a row-click that renders composer content in #studio-main but leaves window.location UNCHANGED means inline-load, not true navigation; the URL-push assertion is the falsifiability anchor and must not be dropped. If later refactored to the true-master-detail one-route model (parent D2 alternative), the URL shape changes (query-param vs path) and this sequence must be re-authored.

## canonical_refs
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md — D3 (fail-loud zero-claims observed live)
- .claude/harness.md:220 — composed-state read-back altitude for multi-child UI epics
- (bd memory) parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift — warrant for a fresh composed gate distinct from per-child greens

## Origin
/decompose kb-9f1h round 1 — see parent's `## Decomposition record`.
close_reason: Integration gate PASS (commit 40c99a8). Independent fresh-context browser read-back of the full studio sequence against the live composed app — all 6 steps green: navbar gating (link present for claimant, null for zero-claims); rail lists 2 events + 1 post as peers w/ Post parent-Event subtitle; Event row click -> window.location /syndication/events/47/ + composer in #studio-main (no nested html/body, true navigation); Post row click -> /syndication/posts/4/; zero-publishables claimant -> empty-state CTA; zero-claims user -> HTTP 403 fail-loud. No cross-child conjunction drift. Durable re-runnable probe at scripts/studio_readback.mjs (manual; seed-pinned pks; not CI-wired — no JS test framework in repo). Verdict:pass via fresh-subagent read-back.

title: /ui-craft two-pane studio build: shell + publishables rail + peer rows + empty-state
design:
## Context
Child of kb-9f1h. The /ui-craft build of the Typefully-style inner two-pane studio surface (parent D1/D2/D6). Owns the build→screenshot→critique→patch loop. Depends on kb-9f1h.1 (studio view + merge service + context processor) and kb-9f1h.2 (composers return layout-less fragment on HX-Request, so swapping into #studio-main doesn't nest). See parent --design for the full narrative.

## Decisions

### Two-pane shell + rail (parent D1/D2)
Studio shell template (new, e.g. templates/syndication/studio.html) with a named `#studio-main` main pane and the empty profile-switcher + nav-section slots left in place (cheap foresight, ADR-003 — kb-5ok6 wraps later at zero rework). Rail partial; row component + empty-state component as reusable cotton primitives in templates/cotton/kb/. event_hub.html/post_hub.html get the rail include (overlaps .2's edits to those files — serial).
Rail rows: FLAT peers (parent D1), type badge, Post parent-Event muted subtitle ("Launch teaser · ↳ Spring Munch"); row click hx-get real path / hx-target #studio-main / hx-push-url real path (parent D2). Active row reflects the current URL.

### Empty-state (parent D6)
Empty-state CTA for the claimant-with-zero-publishables case (distinct from the zero-claims 403 in .1) routing to event-create — never a blank list.

### Build cautions (memories)
- Tailwind v4 cascade (memory tailwind-v4-component-layer-loses-to-utilities): kb-* primitives in @layer components lose to utilities — verify computed style in-browser; use unlayered rules / id selectors to override a utility.
- Alpine (memory alpine-3-x-directives-mouseenter-click-class-x): any @click/:class/x-show is inert without an ancestor x-data — the rail/row interactivity needs an x-data wrapper on the swapped partial root.

## Harness target
**Signal:** /ui-craft build→screenshot→critique loop via `browser-automation` against `manage.py runserver` (127.0.0.1:8009) as a seeded claimant with ≥1 Event + ≥1 Post: rendered rail lists Event AND Post rows as flat peers with type badges; a Post row shows its parent-Event muted subtitle with the literal separator intact; the zero-publishables claimant sees the empty-state CTA. PLUS a `response.content` assertion that each rendered row carries `hx-target="#studio-main"` and `hx-push-url` set to its REAL composer path (static attribute-presence — verifying the wiring is emitted; the LIVE click→window.location push is .4's gate, not asserted here), AND that the row whose path matches the current URL carries the active-state class (active-row-reflects-URL, asserted programmatically on rendered markup, not left to screenshot eyeballing). Screenshots read studio-quality + brand-aligned; built from cotton/kb primitives. Pair with `uv run djlint --check` clean + a `response.content` render-regression assertion (kb-33do.3 reformat-mutates-output caveat) on any new/edited template.
**Expected green:** rail renders peer rows correctly (badge + subtitle); each row's `hx-target`/`hx-push-url` attributes are present and point at the real composer path; the active row carries its active class matching the current URL; empty-state CTA renders; no rendered-junk bleed (multi-line {# #} comment / collapsed `·` separator / wrapped href); ui-craft slop-test passes.
**Rationale:** covers parent-signal dimensions "rail lists ≥1 Event AND ≥1 Post as peers with Post parent-Event subtitle" + "empty-state CTA renders" + the "active row reflects URL" sub-behavior. Screenshot/critique is the goal-faithful altitude for the visual-quality surface — a Client test can't see the Tailwind v4/daisyUI cascade or rendered-junk (harness.md:220; memories django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow, django-multiline-hash-comment-renders-raw, djlint-reformat-mutates-rendered-output). The hx-push-url/active-class assertions are STATIC attribute-presence on rendered HTML — the per-SURFACE altitude; the cross-child composed wiring (live click → actual window.location push) is .4's gate. The .3/.4 line (review F4): .3 asserts the attribute is EMITTED; .4 asserts the URL actually CHANGES on a live click.
**Invalidation:** per harness.md:220 a per-child screenshot passes while cross-child wiring (the live row-click swap + real window.location push) stays broken — so .3 asserts only attribute-PRESENCE, never the post-click window.location (that is .4's falsifiability anchor); if ui-craft starts asserting window.location here it is overreaching into .4's dimension. If the separator renders as `·` collapsed (no spaces), the reformat caveat bit — the literal-separator render assertion catches it.

## canonical_refs
- docs/decisions/ADR-016-outbound-syndication-architecture-event-post-projections.md — D1/D2 (flat peer rows + parent-Event subtitle; view-unification)
- docs/decisions/ADR-003-cheap-foresight-patterns.md — empty switcher/nav slots at zero cost for kb-5ok6
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md — D3 (visible empty-state, no blank dead-end)
- docs/decisions/ADR-004-htmx-vs-island-default-plus-tripwire.md — D1 (HTMX+Alpine rail/swap)

## Origin
/decompose kb-9f1h round 1 — see parent's `## Decomposition record`.
acceptance_criteria:
- A two-pane studio shell renders: a persistent left rail + a named #studio-main main pane, with empty profile-switcher + nav-section slots left in place (cheap foresight, ADR-003).
- The rail lists the claimant's publishables as a FLAT list — Events and Posts as peers, no nesting — each row a type badge + title; a Post row shows its parent Event as a muted subtitle (literal · / ↳ separator preserved). The active row reflects the current URL.
- Each rendered row carries hx-get of its REAL composer path, hx-target='#studio-main', and hx-push-url to that real path (asserted as attribute-presence on rendered HTML; the live window.location push is kb-9f1h.4's gate).
- A claimant whose primary Profile has zero publishables sees a welcome/empty-state CTA routing to event-create, never a blank list.
- Built from reusable cotton/kb components; the surface reads studio-quality + brand-aligned (ui-craft slop-test passes); no rendered-junk bleed; djlint --check clean.
close_reason: Two-pane studio surface shipped (commit 20aff21). studio.html two-pane shell (rail + #studio-main, cheap-foresight switcher/nav slots); studio_rail_row + studio_empty_state cotton primitives; flat peer rows (Event/Post badge, title, Post parent-Event subtitle, active hairline) with hx-get/hx-target=#studio-main/hx-push-url real path + Alpine active-state sync; navbar Studio link gated on user_primary_profile; empty-state CTA (never blank). Resolved the .2 carry-forward: extracted _event_hub_body.html/_post_hub_body.html shared partials for full-page+fragment. 27 new tests (response.content). Read-back verified live (peers list, row swaps + active + URL push, empty-state, gating, deep-link). djlint clean, full suite 1983 passed. Verdict:pass via orchestrator read-back + gate run. Deferred: mobile rail (hidden < sm) to be filed as follow-up.

title: HX-Request fragment branching on event_hub/post_hub + cross-link rewiring
design:
## Context
Child of kb-9f1h. Makes the existing full-page composers swappable into the two-pane studio shell without DOM corruption (parent D2 swap contract). Depends on kb-9f1h.1 (shares syndication/views.py; the studio view from .1 must stay functional). See parent --design for the full narrative.

## Decisions

### HX-Request fragment branching (parent D2)
event_hub (syndication/views.py:91-109) and post_hub (:353+) currently render full pages with NO HX-Request branching. Add branching using the established idiom already in this file: `request.headers.get("HX-Request")` (views.py:461,550,694+). HX-Request → render a layout-less fragment template (composer body only); normal GET → the full page. Both event_hub.html and post_hub.html currently `{% extends "layouts/_default.html" %}` (:1-4) — swapping that whole page into #studio-main = nested <head>/<body> = the defect parent D2 guards; the fragment branch must return the body only.

### Cross-link rewiring (parent D2)
fragments/post_syndication.html:15-18's "Event hub ↗" is a plain `<a href>` full-navigate; rewire to hx-get the real event-hub path, hx-target="#studio-main", hx-push-url the real path. Same for the symmetric back-link. `#studio-main` is the parent-design swap-contract target id (shared contract; the shell that defines it is built in kb-9f1h.3).

## Harness target
**Signal:** `uv run pytest syndication/tests/test_hub_fragment_branching.py` (new) — event_hub + post_hub requested with `HX-Request: true` return content NOT containing `<html`/`<body` (layout-less); the same paths on a normal GET DO contain the full layout; the post cross-link + back-link content carries `hx-target="#studio-main"` AND `hx-push-url` set to the real composer path (not the fragments/ endpoint). All via `response.content.decode()` / assertContains (NOT response.context — hollow per memory).
**Expected green:** HX-Request → fragment (no nested head/body); normal GET → full page; cross-links carry hx-target + real-URL push; the full suite (including .1's test_studio_foundations.py) stays green after these same-file edits to syndication/views.py.
**Rationale:** covers the parent-signal dimension "selecting a row opens its composer in the studio main pane" at the swap-contract-mechanics altitude (layout-less fragment so the #studio-main swap doesn't nest; cross-links swap within the shell). A content-assertion altitude is correct for the fragment-SHAPE contract; the live-swap visual + the actual window.location push are kb-9f1h.4's composed gate. Per harness.md:220 the per-child signal here is the content assertion; the composed read-back is deferred to .4.
**Invalidation:** a content assertion passes if the fragment merely omits `<html>` while still double-rendering a partial layout block — watch that the HX fragment is the composer body only; if .4's composed read-back shows duplicated chrome in the swapped pane, this signal was too shallow.

## canonical_refs
- docs/decisions/ADR-004-htmx-vs-island-default-plus-tripwire.md — D1 (HTMX-default; fragment-branching is squarely the default path, no React-island tripwire)
- parent kb-9f1h --design D2 swap contract — the broken-fragment-swap = nested head/body defect is a render-STRUCTURE bug, caught by the .4 composed read-back + harness.md:220 rendered-junk failure class (NOT ADR-008 D3, which governs missing/invalid DATA — a category mismatch flagged in review F3)

## Origin
/decompose kb-9f1h round 1 — see parent's `## Decomposition record`.
acceptance_criteria:
- event_hub and post_hub, requested with HX-Request, return a layout-less body fragment (no <html>/<body>); a normal GET returns the full {% extends %} page (deep-link/refresh works).
- The post→event-hub cross-link (fragments/post_syndication.html:15-18) and the symmetric back-link carry hx-target='#studio-main' + hx-push-url to the REAL composer path (/syndication/events/<pk>/ or /posts/<pk>/), swapping within the studio shell rather than full-navigating away.
- The studio view added in kb-9f1h.1 remains functional (full suite, including .1's test_studio_foundations.py, stays green after .2's same-file edits to syndication/views.py).
- Assertions are on response.content.decode() (not response.context — hollow per memory).
close_reason: HX-Request fragment branching shipped (commit 798b7f9). event_hub/post_hub return layout-less body fragments on HX-Request (event_hub_fragment.html, post_hub_fragment.html) and full pages on normal GET; in-shell cross-links (post_syndication board link + post_hub_fragment back-link) rewired to hx-target=#studio-main + hx-push-url to real composer path, standalone pages keep full-navigate. 10 tests assert no <html>/<body> on HX + fragment carries title (not stub) + full layout on normal GET + cross-link attrs. Full suite 1956 passed. Verdict:pass via orchestrator read-back. Carry-forward to .3: extract a shared body partial (full-page vs fragment duplication) + ensure all intra-composer cross-links swap in-shell.

title: Studio backend foundations: merge service + context processor + studio route/view + zero-claims fail-loud
design:
## Context
Child of kb-9f1h (unified publishables index / organizer studio front door). Pure-Python/backend foundations the /ui-craft surface (kb-9f1h.3) and the composed-state e2e gate (kb-9f1h.4) consume. No UI polish here. See parent --design for the full 7-decision narrative.

## Decisions

### Merge service (parent D5)
`get_publishables_for_profile(profile)` — Python-level merge of two querysets (Event lives in events.models, Post in syndication.models — spans two apps; both carry updated_at: events/models.py:336, syndication/models.py:196). Sort by updated_at desc. NO UNION SQL, NO pagination (ADR-008 D2 — add on a real volume signal). Lives beside `_get_primary_profile_for_user` (syndication/services.py:171-189).
**ADR-012 NON-filter (load-bearing, scope-check + review F1):** organizers/views.py:38 uses `Profile.objects.visible()`; this service must NOT apply a visibility filter. Visibility is a public-RENDER concept; an owner always sees their own assets. ADR-012's read-side-only scope header is the warrant — this is owner-management, not outbound syndication.

### Context processor (parent D3)
`user_primary_profile` in a_core/context_processors.py (established module: feature_flags, legal_contact_processor at :1-23), registered in a_core/settings.py:141-147. Returns Profile or None; NEVER raises (must NOT call the raising `_get_primary_profile_for_user` — wrap the zero-claims case as None). This is the global-template-state mechanism the navbar reads (the existing view-scoped viewer_is_claimant pattern at organizers/views.py:36+ is not reusable in a global nav element).

### Studio route + view (parent D2/D4) — route placement RESOLVED (review F2)
Register the `/studio/` route at ROOT in a_core/urls.py with flat URL name `studio` (NOT under the `syndication:` namespace — syndication/urls.py:16 sets `app_name="syndication"`, but the navbar uses flat names like `{% url 'event-list' %}` at navbar.html:21, and a root-level generic `/studio/` home also fits the ADR-003 cheap-foresight framing better than nesting under syndication). The view itself may live in syndication/views.py. Claimant-gated: zero-claims → 403/redirect (fail loud, ADR-008 D3 — never a synthesized empty 200). View may rely on a Profile existing because it is claimant-gated. Passes `get_publishables_for_profile(primary_profile)` to the template. The shell/rail templates are kb-9f1h.3's job; this child renders a minimal placeholder template (or the view is template-agnostic and .3 supplies the template).

### Gating warrant (review F11)
The studio front door is a LISTING surface — the gate is "is this user a claimant at all?" (ADR-014 D1, ProfileClaim presence), NOT "does this user have edit/publish authority over a specific Event?" (ADR-017 D1). ADR-017 D1 becomes relevant later if the studio gates per-Event editing; it is not the front-door gate.

## Harness target
