title: Unified publishables index (flat left-nav listing events + posts as peers) + sync-toggle control polish
design:
## Context

Split from epic kb-q4u9. That epic shipped per-publishable workspaces (each Event and Post individually reachable; a Post links out from its Event hub), but never built the top-level **unified flat list** that the epic's D1 describes. The brainstorm surfaced a sharper framing than "add a list": **organizers have no front door at all** — the navbar (`templates/cotton/navbar.html`) carries only Listings / My profile / Log out, and neither `/me/` nor the organizer profile page links a claimant to their workspace. Organizers reach the composer by typing `/syndication/events/<pk>/` or following internal breadcrumbs. So this surface is the missing organizer entry point, and the flat publishables list is the shape we put there.

Reference models inspected live (browser read-back): **Hipsy** (`hipsy.nl/app/events`) = the eventual *outer* organizer dashboard — persistent left nav of organizer sections (Dashboard / Events / Sales / Reviews / Org) + a profile switcher pinned top-left + contextual right rail. **Typefully** = the *inner* two-pane layout for the compose section — left pane lists the publishables, main pane is the composer. The current Switch composer is a single centered column with empty side gutters, leaving literal room for a left pane.

The decision: build only the Typefully-style two-pane for the syndication surface now; the broad Hipsy-style dashboard is real but future (filed as kb-5ok6).

## Decisions

### D1 — Flat list of publishables; Events and Posts as peers, no structural nesting (FLEXIBLE)
Each row is one publishable with a type badge. A Post row shows its parent Event as a *muted subtitle* ("Launch teaser · ↳ Spring Munch") — labelling for orientation, not a tree. Selecting any row opens its composer.
- **Firmness:** FLEXIBLE — rests on ADR-016 D1/D2, both FLEXIBLE; this is the UI realization of the publishable-primitive view-unification, reversible if that model moves.
- **Rationale:** ADR-016 D2 (2026-06-01 note) canonicalizes the flat-list-of-publishables as a *view/interface* unification of Event + Post over the parallel-FK pattern. ADR-016 D1 establishes the two as separate peer entities where a Post carries a non-null FK to its Event (verified: `syndication/models.py` Post.event FK, on_delete=CASCADE) — so the subtitle is safe, and the peer (not nested) presentation matches the entity model.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  | Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
  |---|---|---|
  | Nest Posts under their Event (tree) | `direct:` ADR-016 D2 — "The 'publishable primitive' the syndication UI unifies (one flat list, one composer shell) is a view/interface unification … not a new content-model base class" | Contradicts the canonicalized flat-list unification; recreates the hierarchy the publishable view deliberately flattens |
  | Two separate lists (Events tab, Posts tab) | `reasoned:` a type split is nesting-by-another-name and forces the organizer to know a thing's type before finding it | Loses the unified-index value |
- **What would invalidate:** if a Post is ever made independent of an Event (the ADR-016 D1 "what would invalidate" path — collapse to a single entity / drop the Event FK), the subtitle convention loses meaning and rows need a different orientation cue.

### D2 — IA: persistent left rail + HTMX main-pane swap; real URLs preserved (FLEXIBLE)
The left publishables rail is a shared template include present on the composer pages. Each publishable keeps its real URL (`/syndication/events/<pk>/`, `/syndication/posts/<pk>/`). Clicking a row swaps the studio main pane and pushes the real composer URL. Route + template named generically toward a future `/studio/` home, with **empty profile-switcher and nav-section slots** left in the layout (cheap foresight per ADR-003 — kb-5ok6 wraps this later at zero rework).

**Swap contract (the load-bearing mechanics an implementer must not guess):**
- The studio shell defines a named main pane (e.g. `#studio-main`). Row clicks are `hx-get` of the publishable's real composer URL, `hx-target="#studio-main"`, `hx-push-url="true"` set to that **real composer path** (not the fragment endpoint), so `window.location` reflects the canonical URL.
- `event_hub` / `post_hub` views must return a **body fragment without the base layout** when `HX-Request` is present (the repo already runs `HtmxMiddleware` and uses a fragment pattern — see `templates/syndication/fragments/`), and the full page (rail + shell + composer) on a normal GET, so deep-linking/refresh works. Swapping a full `{% extends "layouts/_default.html" %}` page into a div is a defect (nested `<head>`/`<body>`) and must fail loud in review, not render broken DOM (ADR-008 D3).
- Existing intra-composer cross-links (the `post_hub` → event-hub back-link, the "Event hub ↗" link in `fragments/post_syndication.html`) must swap **within the studio shell** (hx-targeted to `#studio-main` + push the real URL), not full-navigate away — otherwise they break the two-pane model. The active row in the rail reflects the current URL.
- **Rationale:** user-confirmed. Reuses the existing composers via HX-Request branching (~90% of the Typefully feel at a fraction of an SPA refactor); ADR-004 D1 makes HTMX the default rendering strategy; ADR-008 D2 favours the simplest thing over a fragment-extraction rebuild.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  | Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
  |---|---|---|
  | True master-detail, one `/studio/` route owning both panes; composer becomes a swapped fragment with its own routing | `reasoned:` requires composer to become a standalone embeddable fragment + bespoke history/deep-link handling; larger build for marginal feel gain over HX-Request branching | Over-builds against working full-page composers |
  | Index page, no persistent pane (list → navigate away to composer) | `reasoned:` cheapest, but the list disappears once composing — not the two-pane model the user asked for | Fails the stated UX goal |
  | Full organizer dashboard with the list as one panel now | `direct:` ADR-008 D2 — "If two implementations diverge at the third call site, *then* extract — not before" | Speculative chrome (Sales/Reviews/etc.) with no second caller yet; deferred to kb-5ok6 |
- **What would invalidate:** a second distinct surface needing the same dashboard chrome — then kb-5ok6's shell earns its abstraction and `/studio/` is built out; OR the HX-Request fragment branching proving too entangled with the existing composer templates, pushing toward the true-master-detail alternative.

### D3 — Reached via a navbar "Studio" link, claimant-gated via a context processor (FLEXIBLE)
A persistent navbar entry (label TBD by /ui-craft — "Studio" / "Workspace") shown only to claimants.
- **Gating mechanism (specified — existing pattern is view-scoped `viewer_is_claimant` context, not reusable in the global navbar):** add a context processor exposing `user_primary_profile` to all templates — it returns the claimant's primary Profile or **`None`** for non-claimants (it must NOT call the raising `_get_primary_profile_for_user`; it wraps the zero-claims case as `None`). The navbar renders the Studio link iff `user_primary_profile` is non-None. This is the cheapest global-template-state mechanism and doubles as the zero-claims guard for D4.
- **Rationale:** the brainstorm's core finding is the absence of any entry point; a claimant-gated navbar link is the minimal durable fix. Gating policy is governed by existing ADR-017 D1 (authz = claimant of the EventOrganizer Profile) — no new policy, only a template-surfacing of it.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  | Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
  |---|---|---|
  | Link from `/me/` only | `reasoned:` buries the workspace under account settings; organizers are a primary persona | Weaker discoverability |
  | Per-view context injection (the existing `viewer_is_claimant` pattern) | `reasoned:` the navbar renders on every page; injecting per-view would require touching every view — a context processor is the one-place fit | Doesn't scale to a global nav element |
- **What would invalidate:** if non-claimant collaborators (co-organizers without a claim) need workspace access, the gate widens from ProfileClaim-presence to an authz role.

### D4 — Scoped to the claimant's primary Profile; zero-claims fails loud; multi-Profile switcher deferred (FLEXIBLE)
The studio view lists publishables of the primary Profile. Two distinct states must not be conflated:
- **Zero-claims user** (no ProfileClaim): never sees the navbar link (D3); a direct hit on the studio URL **403s or redirects** — fail loud, never synthesize an empty workspace (ADR-008 D3). The studio view may rely on a Profile existing because it is claimant-gated.
- **Claimant with a Profile but no publishables**: the empty-state CTA (D6). This is the only "empty" case.
- The profile-switcher slot from D2 stays empty for now; scoping is the single primary Profile.
- **Rationale:** ADR-008 D2 — most claimants have one Profile; a switcher is unbuilt UI with no current demand. ADR-008 D3 — the zero-claims path must be an explicit error/redirect, not a fabricated empty view.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  | Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
  |---|---|---|
  | Show all claimed Profiles' publishables merged | `reasoned:` ambiguous per-row ownership, and create-new has no target Profile | Confusing without a switcher |
  | Treat zero-claims as the empty state | `direct:` ADR-008 D3 — "raise, log with reason, render visible error state. Never zero-fill or synthesize missing fields" | Synthesizes a workspace for someone with no Profile |
- **What would invalidate:** real users claiming multiple active Profiles — then the switcher ships and scoping becomes per-selected-Profile.

### D5 — Ordering: flat, most-recently-updated first, via a new merge service; lifecycle grouping deferred (FLEXIBLE)
No grouping. A cheap at-a-glance status hint per row if free.
- **Merge mechanism (specified — Events and Posts are two models, not one queryset):** a new service `get_publishables_for_profile(profile)` returns the merged Event + Post list sorted by `updated_at` desc. At V0 scale this is a Python-level merge of two querysets (both models carry `updated_at`); **no UNION SQL and no pagination at V0** (ADR-008 D2 — add when a real volume signal demands it). Lives in `syndication/services.py` alongside `_get_primary_profile_for_user`.
- **Rationale:** Typefully groups by lifecycle (Drafts / Scheduled / Posted), but Switch's publish status lives **per-channel on each PlatformProjection** (ADR-016 D2/D5), not on the publishable — there is no clean single bucket to group a publishable into yet. Recency is unambiguous and needs no new aggregation.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  | Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
  |---|---|---|
  | Group by lifecycle (draft/ready/published) | `reasoned:` status is per-projection; a publishable with mixed-status channels has no single bucket | Requires an aggregation rule that doesn't exist; premature |
  | Order Events by event date | `reasoned:` Events and Posts have different time semantics (start vs created_at), so a single date axis mixes apples/oranges | Recency (`updated_at`) is the one shared, meaningful axis |
- **What would invalidate:** introducing a publishable-level publish status (a roll-up of channel states) — then lifecycle grouping becomes well-defined and may beat recency; OR list volume large enough that the in-Python merge needs a pageable UNION.

### D6 — Empty state: welcome + "Create your first event" CTA (FLEXIBLE)
For a claimant whose primary Profile has zero publishables (distinct from the zero-claims case in D4), render a welcome panel routing to event-create — never a blank list.
- **Rationale:** ADR-008 D3 — visible state over silence; an empty list with no affordance is a dead end for a new organizer.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  | Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
  |---|---|---|
  | Blank list / no special state | `direct:` ADR-008 D3 — "render visible error state" / no silent dead-ends | New organizer has no path forward |
  | Empty rail + composer placeholder text only | `reasoned:` the create action is the one thing a zero-publishable organizer needs; burying it in placeholder copy hides it | Weak call-to-action |
- **What would invalidate:** onboarding moves event-creation to a dedicated flow reached before the studio (then the studio is never seen empty).

### D7 — Sync affordance polish (finding 9 of the kb-q4u9 re-verify): single toggle, /ui-craft-review-gated (FLEXIBLE, optional)
The per-channel control ships as separate SYNC · CUSTOMIZE · RESET text links (`templates/syndication/fragments/event_syndication.html`). Fold to a single toggle expressing synced/diverged state **only if /ui-craft's review agrees it reads better**. Tail item; does not gate the bead.
- **Rationale:** cosmetic; a genuine toggle may read clearer than three peer links, but the call belongs to the design pass, not pre-decided here.
- **Alternatives rejected:**
  | Alternative | Warrant | Why rejected |
  |---|---|---|
  | Mandate the toggle now | `reasoned:` pre-deciding a cosmetic before the /ui-craft pass risks a worse affordance than the current explicit links | Keep it review-gated |
  | Drop the polish entirely | `reasoned:` the two-buttons-as-toggle smell was a real re-verify finding; worth a look during the build | Keep as optional |
- **What would invalidate:** /ui-craft review finds the explicit Customize/Reset links read clearer than a toggle (then the change is dropped).

## Build approach

The composer + studio surface is built via **/ui-craft** — studio-quality, brand-aligned, building reusable composable components (the publishables-rail, the row, the studio shell) and reusing/improving existing cotton primitives (`templates/cotton/`, `templates/cotton/kb/`) rather than one-off template markup.

## Acceptance contract

- A navbar "Studio"-style link, visible only to a claimant (context-processor-gated on a non-None primary Profile), opens a workspace surface.
- That surface renders a **flat list of the claimant's primary-Profile publishables — Events and Posts as peers, no nesting** — each row selectable, a Post row showing its parent Event as a subtitle.
- Selecting an Event row and selecting a Post row each opens its composer in the studio main pane, with `window.location` pushed to that publishable's **real composer path** (`/syndication/events/<pk>/` or `/syndication/posts/<pk>/`).
- A claimant Profile with no publishables shows a welcome/empty-state CTA; a zero-claims user hitting the studio URL is refused (403/redirect), not shown an empty workspace.
- (optional, /ui-craft-review-gated) the per-channel sync affordance reads as a single synced/diverged toggle.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Browser read-back via `browser-automation` against the running app (`127.0.0.1:8009`), with seeded fixture state: a claimant user whose primary Profile has **≥1 Event and ≥1 Post**, and a separate claimant whose Profile has **zero publishables**. Inspect rendered DOM + `window.location` (not Django view `response.context`, which memory `django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow` flags as hollow). Sequence: (1) load app as the seeded claimant → assert navbar Studio link present; (2) open it → assert the rail lists ≥1 Event row AND ≥1 Post row as peers, Post row showing its parent-Event subtitle; (3) click the Event row → assert composer for that Event renders in the main pane AND `window.location.pathname === "/syndication/events/<pk>/"` (the real composer path, not a fragment endpoint); (4) click the Post row → same assertion against `/syndication/posts/<pk>/`; (5) load as the zero-publishables claimant → assert the empty-state CTA renders (not a blank list).
- **Expected green:** every assertion in that sequence holds against the live rendered DOM and the post-click `window.location`.
- **Rationale:** this is a navigation/IA surface whose intent is *reachability + correct peer listing + correct composer routing*. A Client/unit test asserting on `response.context` (or merely that an hx-get returned 200) would pass even if the rail never rendered, the swap target was misw ired, or `hx-push-url` pushed the fragment endpoint instead of the real composer URL — the goal-faithful altitude is a real browser observing rendered DOM + the actual pushed URL, which is exactly what the repo's composed-state e2e pattern (kb-q4u9 read-back; harness.md composed-state altitude) and this bead's own acceptance call for. /ui-craft owns the build→screenshot→critique loop on top of this.
- **Invalidation (present-tense observable boundary, not only future refactor):** the signal is measuring the wrong thing if a row-click renders composer content in the main pane but `window.location` does **not** change to the real composer path — that indicates inline-load without true navigation/push-URL, so the URL assertion is the falsifiability anchor and must not be dropped. Separately, if the studio is later refactored to the true-master-detail one-route model (D2 alternative), the URL shape changes (query-param vs path) and the read-back sequence must be re-authored.

title: AgeGateMiddleware 302-redirects HTMX fragment requests, breaking the syndication board
design:
## Symptom

The event syndication board loads its sections via HTMX fragment GETs (event_facts, event_posts, event_syndication). HTMX sends `Accept: text/html` and `HX-Request: true`. AgeGateMiddleware intercepts these fragment requests and 302-redirects to /age-check/ unless an `age_gate=ok` cookie is present. HTMX then swaps the age-check HTML INTO the section, so the user sees a broken/empty board instead of the fragment.

Discovered during kb-cxyz (composer two-pane build) — the craftsman had to manually set `age_gate=ok` via CDP to get the fragments to load in a fresh automation session.

## Impact

Any session that reaches the event hub without having passed the age gate (cookie missing/expired) gets a broken syndication section with no error surface — a silent-failure / ADR-008 D3 concern.

## Fix direction

Exempt HTMX fragment requests from the age gate: check for the `HX-Request` header in AgeGateMiddleware and pass through (the parent page that embeds the fragments is itself age-gated, so the fragments don't need independent gating). Verify no other middleware has the same HTMX-blindness.

## canonical_refs
- ADR-008 D3 (no silent fallbacks on data integrity — render visible error, never silently swap wrong content)

title: Swap django-template-partials → Django 6.0 native partials
design:
## Context

Django 6.0 (released Dec 2025) ships native `{% partialdef %}` / `{% partial %}` template tags and the `template.html#partial-name` render shorthand — evolved directly from Carlton Gibson's `django-template-partials` package via a Google Summer of Code project (mentored by Gibson). We're on Django 6.0.4, so the third-party package is now redundant.

## Inventory (file-scanner output)

- **Config (3 lines in `a_core/settings.py`)**: `template_partials.apps.SimpleAppConfig` in `INSTALLED_APPS`, `template_partials.loader.Loader` wrapping the cached → cotton → filesystem → app_directories chain, `template_partials.templatetags.partials` in template `builtins`.
- **Dependency**: `django-template-partials>=25.1` in `pyproject.toml`; resolved to 25.3 in `uv.lock`.
- **Templates (1 file)**: `pages/templates/pages/home.html` — `{% load partials %}` at line 2; two partialdef blocks: `test-partial` (lines 17–21, success-alert HTML for an HTMX test) and `skeleton-partial` (lines 41–45, skeleton loader for an HTMX test).
- **Python (1 file)**: `pages/views.py` — two staff-gated debug views (`test_partial_view`, `test_skeleton_hx`) calling `render(request, "pages/home.html#test-partial")` and `render(request, "pages/home.html#skeleton-partial")`. Routed in `pages/urls.py` at `/debug/hx/test-partial` and `/debug/hx/test-skeleton`.
- **Docs (3 design plans)**: `docs/plans/2026-04-17-v0-design.md`, `2026-04-17-phase-0.3-internal-events-design.md`, `2026-04-17-phase-0.4-map-invite-design.md` — each mentions `django-template-partials` in passing.

**No migration cliffs**: zero usage of `inline=True`, zero cross-template `get_template("...#...")` calls, zero Python imports from `template_partials`. Native syntax matches the package's syntax exactly.

## Migration steps

1. Drop `django-template-partials>=25.1` from `pyproject.toml`; run `uv lock` to regenerate.
2. Remove `template_partials.apps.SimpleAppConfig` from `INSTALLED_APPS` in `a_core/settings.py:101`.
3. Remove `template_partials.loader.Loader` wrapper from template loaders in `a_core/settings.py:152` (keep the cached → cotton → filesystem → app_directories chain — the package's wrapper is no longer needed; native partials work through the standard loaders).
4. Remove `template_partials.templatetags.partials` from template `builtins` in `a_core/settings.py:167`.
5. Drop `{% load partials %}` from `pages/templates/pages/home.html:2` (native tags are template builtins in Django 6.0).
6. Update three design docs to drop the `django-template-partials` mentions (replace with "Django native partials" where relevant — the docs are forward-looking design plans, not historical records).

Templates and Python `render(..., "...#partial-name")` calls stay untouched — native syntax is identical to the package's.

## canonical_refs

- ADR-008 D1 (delete on sight — no backward-compat shims, no deprecation path) and D2 (no speculative abstraction — third-party package is no longer needed since the framework absorbed the functionality).
- Carlton Gibson's official migration guide: <https://github.com/carltongibson/django-template-partials/blob/main/Migration.md>
- Django 6.0 release notes: <https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/releases/6.0/>
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance

1. `django-template-partials` is absent from `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` (verify with `grep -i template-partials pyproject.toml uv.lock` returning no matches).
2. `a_core/settings.py` contains no references to `template_partials` (no `template_partials.apps.SimpleAppConfig` in INSTALLED_APPS; no `template_partials.loader.Loader` in template loaders; no `template_partials.templatetags.partials` in builtins).
3. `pages/templates/pages/home.html` has no `{% load partials %}` line; the two `{% partialdef %}` blocks (`test-partial`, `skeleton-partial`) remain unchanged.
4. `pages/views.py` `render(request, "pages/home.html#test-partial")` and `render(request, "pages/home.html#skeleton-partial")` calls work against Django 6.0's native `#partial` shorthand — verified by HTMX endpoint probe (see harness target).
5. Three design plans in `docs/plans/` (v0-design, phase-0.3-internal-events-design, phase-0.4-map-invite-design) updated to drop `django-template-partials` mentions.
6. Full `uv run pytest` suite green; `uv run djlint --check . --extension=html` green; `uv run python manage.py check` reports no issues.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** Four-part composition: (a) `uv run python manage.py check` — catches settings.py loader/builtins rip incompleteness at startup per ADR-008 D3 (fail loud). (b) `uv run djlint --check pages/templates/pages/home.html` — catches `{% load partials %}` removal mismatch. (c) `uv run pytest` — full regression sweep (pre-commit gates this anyway). (d) Live browser probe via `runserver`: log in as staff, GET `/debug/hx/test-partial` and `/debug/hx/test-skeleton`, inspect the HTMX swap targets.
- **Expected green:** `manage.py check` reports "System check identified no issues (0 silenced)"; `djlint --check` exits 0; `pytest` exits 0 with no new failures; both HTMX endpoints return HTTP 200 with the partialdef block's actual HTML rendered inline (the daisyUI success-alert markup for `test-partial`; the skeleton-card markup for `test-skeleton`) — NOT raw `{% partialdef %}...{% endpartialdef %}` text leaking into the response body.
- **Rationale:** Per `.claude/harness.md` templates fit-profile, browser read-back is load-bearing on user-facing template changes — djlint and view-context assertions both miss two known failure classes (context-vs-content hollow, multi-line `{# #}` rendered raw). The two debug HTMX endpoints exist precisely to exercise partial rendering and are the most goal-faithful signal for this swap. `manage.py check` is the cheapest catch for a half-removed loader entry per ADR-008 D3 fail-loud posture.
- **Invalidation:** If either HTMX endpoint returns raw `{% partialdef %}` text in the response body, the native tag parser isn't picking up the syntax → swap is broken (likely a stale `{% load partials %}` or a settings-side regression). If `manage.py check` reports a template-backend issue (e.g. "Could not load loader"), the settings rip is incomplete. If pytest surfaces a new failure in any template-rendering test, the loader change has cascaded — investigate the loader chain rather than the touched template.

title: Redesign /events/: sticky filter sidebar + map-as-filter + unified card-expand
design:
## Context

The `/events/` page is the product's primary discovery surface. Live smoke-testing surfaced
that its three "preview" mechanisms (in-map cluster popup list, top-right htmx drawer, list
inline-expand) compete and overlap; the inline-expand semi-duplicates the collapsed card; the
map is a wide horizontal band that overweights location (a *secondary* discovery axis for
events vs. real-estate/hotels); and filters are not sticky, forcing scroll-hunting to edit them.

Reference inspiration: Hipsy (content-first left filter sidebar + right event list) for the
skeleton; Airbnb (sticky filters incl. map) for the stickiness; explicitly rejecting Hipsy's
city-name + radius-slider location control (abstract, poor UX) in favor of map navigation.

## Decisions

### D1 — Layout: sticky left filter sidebar + right scrolling list (FLEXIBLE)
Two-column on desktop (lg+): left column ~300–340px is a `position: sticky` filter sidebar; right
column is the single-column editorial card list. Mobile/tablet: sidebar collapses to a top
"Filters" sheet/disclosure; list full-width.
- Rationale: content-first frame fits events (Hipsy); sticky removes scroll-hunting to change a
  filter (Airbnb). `reasoned:` location is one axis among date/type/organizer, not the spine.
- Alternatives: (a) full side-by-side half-screen map split (Zillow/Airbnb) — `reasoned:` overweights
  location for events, eats the fold; (b) keep current stacked full-width band — `reasoned:` doesn't
  fix geometry (pin→card not co-visible) or sticky-filters.
- Invalidates if: users on common laptop widths report the list column feels cramped, or mobile
  filter-sheet usage shows people can't find filters.

### D2 — Map becomes a collapsible "Location" filter widget inside the sticky sidebar (FLEXIBLE)
The map is no longer a layout element; it is one filter group ("Area") in the sidebar, sized modestly
(~320px square), expanded-by-default on desktop (sticky → co-visible as the list scrolls), collapsible
to a one-line row. A `⤢` control opens a large map overlay for roomy browsing. Collapsed/active state
shows the chosen area as a clearable chip.
- Rationale: right-sizes location to its secondary importance while preserving the one Airbnb property
  worth keeping — co-visibility (so drag-to-filter is visible and pin clicks land on real cards).
- Alternatives: (a) map-as-separate-view toggle — `reasoned:` gives up co-visibility; (b) keep map a
  structural column — `reasoned:` overweights location.
- Invalidates if: a 320px map proves unusable for the common click/drag-filter case even with the
  fullscreen escape.

### D3 — Unify on ONE preview/interaction model; remove the drawer and in-map popup (FLEXIBLE)
Delete the top-right htmx `#drawer` and the in-map cluster popup list (the unreadable one). The list is
the single preview surface (card expand/contract). Map gestures FILTER the list:
- Drag/pan the map → filter the list to the visible bounds ("search as I move" — currently dead wiring,
  made real). Debounced; loop-guarded against programmatic camera moves.
- Click a cluster → ease to it + filter the list to that area.
- Click a single marker → filter the list to that marker's vicinity (its venue / event).
- Clear via a visible "Area · clear ×" affordance; clearing the area preserves all other filters.
- Rationale: filtering reloads the list to exactly the clicked set, so the target card is always present
  (immune to the pagination gap where a marker points at an event not on the current page). One mechanic,
  trustworthy. Removes two silent-failure-prone surfaces (drawer's `is_primary` 404 + htmx-global-scope
  ReferenceError, per bd memories).
- ADR-008 D1: delete the drawer view/template/wiring on sight (no compat shim).
- ADR-008 D3: bounds parse stays fail-soft for *user-input* query param (not data-integrity) — malformed
  bounds ignored, not raised.
- Alternatives: (a) pin→highlight-in-place — `reasoned:` stacked/sticky geometry + pagination make it
  unreliable; (b) pin→scroll+auto-expand — user rejected autoscroll/expand; (c) pin→move-to-top —
  `reasoned:` breaks when the event isn't on the current page.
- Invalidates if: "search as I move" feels jarring → fall back to an explicit "Search this area" button
  (Airbnb pattern).

### D4 — List card expand/contract shows ONLY additive content (FLEXIBLE)
The inline expand currently re-renders date numeral, time, venue, price + a "PREVIEW" eyebrow + its own
X button — all already on the collapsed card — inside a separate-looking panel. Redesign: expanded region
is a *continuation of the card body* (same surface, card's bottom border drops while open), showing only
what's NOT already visible: full (un-truncated) description, tags, and an actions row with a clear
"View full event →" CTA (+ external link if present). No second date numeral, no PREVIEW eyebrow, no X
(the rotating chevron + click-again collapses).
- Rationale: "the card itself expands with more info," not "a new panel appears" (user's exact ask).
- Alternatives: keep current panel — `reasoned:` reads as a duplicate per live screenshot.
- Invalidates if: users miss the explicit collapse control (chevron insufficient).

### D5 — "From organizers you follow" section → a "Following" filter toggle (FLEXIBLE)
Remove the hard-coded following SECTION above the list. The `?filter=following` machinery already exists
in the view. Add a "Following" toggle to the sidebar filters (auth users only); when active the list is
the followed set. Add `filter` to the preserved filter-query-string so pagination/sort links keep it.
Delete the `following_events` computation (ADR-008 D1).
- Rationale: a section that ignores the active filters/map is incoherent once filtering is the model;
  following is conceptually a filter.
- Alternatives: keep section + add filter — `reasoned:` redundant, ADR-008 D2 (one path).
- Invalidates if: users want a persistent "from people you follow" spotlight regardless of filters.

### D6 — Hero slims to make room for the working layout (EXPLORATORY)
The full editorial masthead ("What's happening in Berlin." at 112px) competes with the app-zone. Slim it
(smaller headline + issue/date eyebrow retained) above the filter+list zone; keep brand identity without
owning the fold.
- Rationale: preserve editorial brand asset while ceding fold space to filters+list.
- Invalidates if: slim hero reads as generic / loses the editorial voice that differentiates the brand.

## Acceptance contract

- Desktop: left filter sidebar is sticky (stays in view while the right list scrolls); contains tags,
  period (from/to), price, Following toggle (auth), and a collapsible Area/map widget.
- The top-right map drawer and the in-map cluster popup list no longer exist (deleted).
- Dragging/panning the map filters the list to the visible area; clicking a cluster or single marker
  filters the list; a visible "clear area" control resets only the area filter (other filters preserved).
- Clicking a list card expands it in place showing only additive content (full description, tags,
  View-full-event CTA); collapsed card content is not duplicated; the card+expansion read as one surface.
- No "From organizers you follow" section; a "Following" filter toggle exists for authed users and
  survives pagination/sort.
- Mobile (375px): list is full-width; filters reachable via a sheet/disclosure; map collapsed/toggle.
- No JS console errors on /events/ at 375 and 1280.

## Harness target

- **Signal:** (a) `uv run pytest events/ organizers/` for view-layer logic (bounds filters the *list* qs;
  `filter=following` preserved in pagination query string; following section removed); (b) browser-automation
  screenshots + console-error read at 375px and 1280px on http://localhost:8000/events/ (sticky-sidebar
  scroll behavior, map-collapse, card-expand de-dup, drawer/popup absence).
- **Expected green:** pytest green AND screenshots confirm sticky sidebar, collapsible map that filters the
  list, de-duplicated card expand, following-as-filter, zero console errors.
- **Rationale:** UI layout/interaction correctness is visual and stateful — unit tests cover the view query
  changes but cannot see stickiness, co-visibility, or the expand-as-continuation read; the screenshot loop
  is the goal-faithful altitude. Unit-only would pass with the layout visibly broken.
- **Invalidation:** if the dev server / browser-automation is unavailable, fall back to explicit manual
  user verification at both viewports (state so; do not claim visual success).

## canonical_refs

- docs/decisions/ADR-004-htmx-vs-island-default-plus-tripwire.md — map↔list coordination via the
  client event-bus (events:selection-changed / hover-changed / filter-changed / bounds-changed); this
  redesign rewires those events, removing the drawer consumer.
- docs/decisions/ADR-008-code-posture-refactor-hard-fail-loud.md — D1 delete drawer/popup on sight (no
  compat shim); D2 one filter path (following as filter, not section+filter); D3 fail-soft on user-input
  bounds param is acceptable (not data-integrity).
acceptance_criteria: Desktop: sticky left filter sidebar (tags/period/price/Following toggle/collapsible Area-map) stays in view as the right list scrolls. Top-right map drawer + in-map cluster popup deleted. Map drag/cluster/marker click filters the list; clear-area resets only area filter. List card expands in place showing only additive content (full desc + tags + View-full-event CTA), no duplication of collapsed-card content. No 'From organizers you follow' section; Following is a filter surviving pagination. Mobile 375px: list full-width, filters via sheet, map collapsed. No JS console errors at 375/1280.
close_reason: /events/ redesign complete across 4 commits (3f7cf85 sticky sidebar + Following filter; 7d1af05 card-expand de-dup; 6d23c0e map-as-area-filter + drawer removal; 62b754b parent-re-verify fixes). Parent re-verify (adversarial-review of cumulative diff) run + findings fixed. Full suite green (1712). Honest gaps: live map-drag not auto-exercisable (puppeteer canvas) + 375px mobile not screenshot-verified — flagged to user for manual check.

title: Syndication API lacks a projection generation endpoint (design vs impl gap)
description: Reconcile the syndication API surface with ADR-016's stated generation-endpoint design: either add the generation endpoint (+ mode param + co-equal CLI verb) or evolve ADR-016 to record that eager-create + override-edit supersede it.
notes: discovered-from: kb-a4u.7 adversarial review F1. The parent kb-a4u design + ADR-016 describe a projection GENERATION endpoint with a 'mode' request param (mode=rule_based default; mode=agent_assisted when an agent supplies its composed body) — e.g. the web 'Generate projection' button and agent-driven generation. But the built API (syndication/api.py) has NO generation endpoint: projection POST verbs are only approve/publish/mark-published/batch-publish-ready. v0 reality: rule_based generation runs EAGERLY at projection-create time (engine.generate_projection via eager-create), and agent_assisted 'generation' currently happens via the override-edit path (save_projection_override writes override_data['body'] + flips provenance to manual). DESIGN QUESTION: is the explicit generation endpoint still needed, or has it been superseded by eager-create + override-edit? If superseded, evolve ADR-016 in place to drop the generation-endpoint + mode-param language (route via /adr-write). If still needed (e.g. re-generate rule_based on demand, or a first-class agent_assisted generate verb distinct from override), add the endpoint + a co-equal CLI verb. Surfaced because the switch-cli generate-projection verb had to be removed (it was faking generation by calling /approve/).

title: Projection content model: resolve live-canonical-fallback vs stable-snapshot tension (ADR-016 D2 + parent acceptance 4)
description: Discovered during kb-a4u.10 adversarial review. syndication/engine.py render_projection() falls back to re-deriving the body from the LIVE canonical source_event/source_post when override_data['body'] is absent (engine.py ~L247-251). This is a live-view behavior. It collides with parent epic kb-a4u acceptance criterion (4), which requires projections to be STABLE SNAPSHOTS: 'canonical Event/Post updates do NOT cause already-generated projections to silently re-render... the projection's rendered output is stable — reflects the projection's stored content at generation time, not the post-mutation canonical value.' If render falls back to live canonical, a post-generation canonical edit WOULD change an already-generated projection's render, violating (4). ROOT TENSION: ADR-016 D2 is phrased inconsistently — kb-a4u.10's NOTES quote it as 'effective content = LIVE canonical + per-field override_data (absent key = canonical)' (a live model), while engine.py's docstring + parent acceptance (4) describe an editable-copy/snapshot model. These cannot both hold. For rule_based projections override_data['body'] is always written at generation so the fallback never fires — but manually-created (provenance=manual) projections hit the live fallback. Needs: (1) an ADR-016 D2 clarification via /adr-write on whether projections are live-with-overrides or generation-time snapshots; (2) engine.py render_projection aligned to the resolved model; (3) the acceptance-(4) stability test (mutate canonical, assert projection render stable) implemented to enforce it. Likely intersects kb-a4u.5 (projection-review override-edit UI) — the live-vs-snapshot answer determines whether the override UI edits a snapshot or layers over live.
acceptance_criteria: (a) ADR-016 D2 states unambiguously whether a projection's effective content is a generation-time snapshot or live-canonical-plus-overrides; (b) engine.py render_projection matches the resolved model (no hidden live-fallback if snapshot model wins); (c) a test mutates a canonical field after generation and asserts the projection render is stable per parent acceptance (4).
notes:
discovered-from: kb-a4u.10
CLOSE STATE (2026-05-27): hybrid content model shipped via commits 738fb72 + 825cde0 (2 adversarial-review rounds; load-bearing partial-freeze fixed). frozen_content JSONField captures the FULL effective structured field set at draft->ready (listing: title/description/start/end/dress_code/age_restriction/capacity/content_warnings/tickets_url/body; promotion: headline/post_body/cta/imagery/voice/body) so a ready/published projection is a self-contained artifact immune to later canonical edits. render_projection: draft->live, ready+->frozen, fail-loud if frozen_content missing. ready->draft re-open clears the snapshot. Hidden live-fallback removed. transition_status confirmed sole production status-writer. ADR-016 D2 evolved (8124ce7), parent acceptance (4) reframed (epic comment). 198 syndication + 1515 full-suite tests green. NOTE: _compose_listing_body still omits date/location from the composed body STRING — routed to FetLife adapter bead kb-a4u.15 (body-completeness, separate from freeze field-set which captures them).
close_reason: Hybrid projection content model shipped: draft tracks live canonical, freezes full structured field set at draft->ready, ready/published return frozen snapshot (immune to later canonical edits), re-open clears it. ADR-016 D2 evolved + parent acceptance (4) reframed. 2 review rounds, 198 syndication + 1515 full-suite green. Commits 738fb72+825cde0 (+ADR 8124ce7).

comments.author: jsnyde0
comments.text: RESOLVED (2026-05-27, user-confirmed) — hybrid content model, now canonical in ADR-016 D2 (commit 8124ce7). Build target: (1) render_projection returns LIVE canonical + override_data while status==draft; returns the FROZEN SNAPSHOT when status is ready/published/failed. (2) At the draft->ready transition, materialize the then-current effective content (canonical values + overrides at that instant) into a stored snapshot on the projection (implementer chooses the field shape — e.g. a frozen_content JSON blob, or materialize all fields into override_data; update migration in place, pre-launch squashable per ADR-008 D1). (3) Stability test per parent acceptance (4) reframe: generate projection (draft) -> edit a canonical Event field -> assert the DRAFT projection's rendered body reflects the edit (live tracking); then flip to ready -> edit canonical again -> assert the READY projection's rendered body is UNCHANGED (frozen snapshot). Remove the hidden live-fallback in render_projection that currently fires for manually-created projections — it must follow the same draft-vs-ready rule. Primary publish carrier context: the facilitator's agent fetches the (frozen, ready) projection and publishes externally; it must be handed a stable artifact.

title: Event D1 field completion: category (model field) + cover-image authoring (file-upload infra)
description: Carries the remainder of kb-a4u parent acceptance (1)'s full ADR-016 D1 field list that kb-a4u.3 could not land because the underlying substrate is absent. Two gaps: (1) category — ADR-016 D1 lists 'category' as a canonical Event field, but the Event model has no category field at v0; needs a model field + migration + form/schema wiring. (2) cover image — ADR-016 D1 lists 'cover image + optional gallery + video'; EventImage model exists (events/models.py:440, ImageField + is_cover) but authoring a cover image needs file-upload infrastructure (multipart POST handling, storage config, ImageField form widget) that does not exist in the codebase. Neither field gates the dogfooding flow (kb-a4u acceptance 10 names date/location/description/ticket-config, not category/cover-image), so they were split out per ADR-008 D4 rather than bloating kb-a4u.3. NOTE: per-event timezone was deliberately NOT included (v0 is single-city Berlin, TIME_ZONE=Europe/Berlin; per-event tz is a city-federation concern, deferred with rationale — not part of this bead).
design:
Close the two ADR-016 D1 Event fields deferred from kb-a4u.3 (documented as gaps in syndication/forms.py:41-43): category (no model field yet) + cover-image authoring (upload never wired into the syndication path).

## category — new model field
Add Event.category = CharField(choices, blank=True) on events/models.py (single category per event). Save-always (ADR-016 D5): blank allowed; completeness gated at draft->ready, never at save. Simplest-that-works per ADR-008 D2 — a CharField enum, NOT a Category FK model / taxonomy table (that would be speculative abstraction; extract from divergence later). Distinct from tags (M2M, already present).

v0 vocabulary (FLEXIBLE, pre-launch squashable per ADR-008 D1; project-owner-revisable): play_party, workshop, munch, performance, social, festival, other. Migration squashable pre-launch.

Wire through the co-equal seam (ADR-016 D3): add "category" to _EVENT_FIELDS (services.py:269); add to EventCreateIn/EventUpdateIn/EventOut (api.py); add a category ChoiceField to EventForm (forms.py); add the <select> to the authoring template. Web form and JSON API both author + read back category.

## cover image — wire upload into the authoring path
Model infra already exists: events/models.py EventImage (ImageField upload_to=events/, validate_image_size + FileExtensionValidator, is_cover bool, order); MEDIA_ROOT/MEDIA_URL configured. The gap is the AUTHORING affordance, not storage.
- Service helper (syndication/services.py) e.g. set_event_cover(user, event, uploaded_file): can_edit-gated (ADR-017 D2); creates/updates the single is_cover=True EventImage; single-cover invariant (setting a new cover unsets any prior cover); validates via the existing model validators (fail-loud on oversize/bad-extension per ADR-008 D3 — no silent drop).
- Web form: EventForm gets cover_image = ImageField(required=False); the event_create / event_edit templates use enctype=multipart/form-data; view passes the file to the service.
- API: a multipart cover-upload capability (e.g. POST /events/{id}/cover with file: UploadedFile = File(...)) — keeps create_event JSON-clean while preserving co-equal parity (an agent CAN set a cover). can_edit-gated, 403 generic body on denial.
- OUT OF SCOPE: projection rendering of the cover (frozen_content/adapters do not consume cover at v0) — note as possible follow-up, do not build.

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D1 (canonical Event field set incl. category + cover image), D3 (co-equal API), D5 (save-always); ADR-008 D1 (squashable migration), D2 (no speculative abstraction), D3 (fail-loud); ADR-017 D2 (can_edit gate).

## Harness target
Signal: uv run pytest (syndication suite) green. Expected-green: (1) category persists + reads back via BOTH web form and JSON API; (2) cover upload persists EventImage(is_cover=True) via BOTH web form and the API cover endpoint; (3) single-cover invariant holds (second upload unsets the first); (4) cover upload + category edit are can_edit-gated (non-claimant -> 403/PermissionError); (5) invalid image (oversize/bad ext) fails loud, not silent. Rationale: D1 field completion through the co-equal seam is the goal; a model-only test would miss the form/API/authz wiring. Invalidation: ADR-016 D1 field set changes, or category becomes a taxonomy entity.
Live-browser file-picker UX deferred to kb-a4u.17 dogfooding (consistent with kb-a4u.3/.5 — repo has no headless JS harness).

## Origin
discovered-from kb-a4u.3 (close-state split). Framed via /send-it 2026-05-28.

(b) category authored + read-back via web EventForm AND JSON API (EventCreateIn/Out + EventUpdateIn); "category" in _EVENT_FIELDS. (c) Cover image upload wired: web form (multipart) + API endpoint both create EventImage(is_cover=True) on an event via the can_edit-gated service. (d) Single-cover invariant: a second cover upload unsets the prior cover. (e) can_edit gate enforced on cover upload + category edit (non-claimant blocked). (f) Invalid image fails loud (oversize/bad-extension raises, no silent drop). (g) syndication/forms.py:41-43 stale "not built" notes removed. (h) uv run pytest syndication suite green; makemigrations --check clean.

Live file-picker UX deferred to kb-a4u.17 dogfooding.

title: Refactor syndication schema: add PlatformConnection, refront projection FK, add provenance + attribution fields
design:
## Context

The C3/C5 authoring-UX brainstorm (2026-05-26) refined ADR-016 D2 and added D4/D5. The as-built C1 schema (`syndication/models.py`, kb-a4u.1, closed 2026-05-26) predates these: it shipped `PlatformProjection.platform_id` as a `CharField` (with `'telegram-channel:<id>'` string-encoding) and has no `PlatformConnection` model, no `provenance`, and no agent-attribution reservation fields. This bead aligns the schema to the evolved ADR. Pre-launch, so a squashable migration per ADR-008 D1 (no backward-compat shim).

## Decisions (all canonical in ADR-016 D2/D4 — this bead implements, does not re-decide)

1. **Add `PlatformConnection` model** (per ADR-016 D4) — a specific syndication destination owned by an organizer. Fields: organizer/Profile FK (ADR-007 D2), `platform`, destination identifier, per-destination credentials, `enabled` flag, supported `kinds` (Switch page=listing, Ticket Tailor=listing, Telegram=promotion, FetLife=both). An organizer may hold multiple connections per platform. This model is simultaneously the organizer's syndication-targets setting and the per-organizer adapter credential store the adapter beads (kb-a4u.10–.16) consume.
2. **Refront `PlatformProjection.platform_id` → `connection` FK** to `PlatformConnection`. Remove the `platform_id` string.
3. **Add `provenance`** enum field ∈ {`rule_template`, `agent_supplied`, `manual`} (per ADR-016 D2 refinement) — flips to `manual` on human edit of an override.
4. **Add ADR-003 reservation fields** `generated_by` (nullable agent identity ref) + `last_generated_at` (nullable datetime). Empty for human-driven flows; the columns a future `ProjectionRevision` history table would key on.
5. Retain the existing `override_data` JSONField (effective content = live canonical + override_data; no stored generated/override two-field split).

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D2 (refined 2026-05-26), ADR-016 D4, ADR-007 D2, ADR-003, ADR-008 D1.

## Harness target
Signal: pytest — create a `PlatformConnection`, author an Event, assert eager-created projections FK to the connection (not a string) and carry default `provenance`; migration applies clean on an empty DB. Expected-green: projection.connection resolves to a PlatformConnection; provenance/generated_by/last_generated_at columns present; no `platform_id` field remains. Rationale: the schema refront is the load-bearing change C3/C5 and the adapters depend on; a model-level test is the goal-faithful altitude (a view test would pass even with the string FK still present). Invalidation: ADR-016 D4 connection field set changes.

title: German translations never compiled in prod build — .mo missing at runtime
description: locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/django.mo is gitignored (only django.po is tracked). The Dockerfile installs gettext (line 32) but never runs 'manage.py compilemessages', and neither entrypoint.sh nor bin/init.sh do either. Result: the production image has no compiled German catalog, so Django falls back to the English msgid for every {% trans %} string when LANGUAGE_CODE/Accept-Language is German — German UI is effectively broken in prod despite the DE .po being maintained (CI even gates on the .po being non-empty). Discovered while greening the takedown DE translation tests (kb-cyp session 2026-05-26); fixed in CI test.yml by adding a compilemessages step before pytest, but the prod build path was left untouched (deferred to avoid touching the deploy pipeline mid-session).
design: Add 'manage.py compilemessages' to the Docker build (after COPY of source, gettext already installed at Dockerfile:32) so the .mo lands in the image layer shared across init/app/qcluster/bot — same rationale as collectstatic-at-build-time per kb-cm5. Do NOT put it only in init.sh: init is a separate container whose filesystem writes never reach the app container (the kb-cm5 collectstatic lesson). Verify post-deploy: request a page with Accept-Language: de and assert a known German string renders.
acceptance_criteria: Production image contains locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/django.mo; a German-locale request to /takedown/ renders 'Inhalt melden' (not 'Report content'). compilemessages runs at image build, not runtime-init-only.

title: C15 Guard: syndication is NOT gated by visibility tier (unlisted/semi_public still syndicate)
design:
REPURPOSED 2026-05-26 (C3/C5 brainstorm): the original "visibility-tier projection gating" premise (unlisted→0, public→all) is GONE — syndication is visibility-tier-agnostic (ADR-016 revised carried-forward ADR-012 clause; C4 write-gate removed). This bead becomes an inverted regression guard at the integration altitude: assert that visibility tier does NOT suppress syndication anywhere in the pipeline.

The guard verifies, end-to-end across the adapters, that an `unlisted` event (and a `semi_public` event) still eager-creates draft projections for every enabled connection and can be advanced/published exactly like a `public` event — i.e. no adapter, generation step, or eager-creation path silently re-introduces a visibility gate. Read-side `visible_to` on switch.berlin is unaffected and out of scope here (that is ADR-012 read-side rendering, not syndication).

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D4/D5 + revised carried-forward ADR-012 clause (visibility does NOT gate syndication); ADR-012 (read-side only, orthogonal).

## Harness target
Signal: pytest integration test across enabled connections. Expected-green: an `unlisted` event and a `semi_public` event each eager-create the SAME draft projection set as a `public` event (one per enabled connection × supported kind), and each can reach `ready`/`published` with no tier-based suppression at any adapter or generation step. Rationale: guards against regression to a visibility gate — the failure mode is a future dev re-adding `if event.visibility == unlisted: skip` somewhere in the pipeline; this asserts the inverse. Invalidation: the visibility-syndication-agnostic decision is reversed (would itself route through /adr-write).

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1; repurposed from gating-test to inverted-guard 2026-05-26 after the visibility-tier-gating decision was reversed (kb-wrb dissolved).
acceptance_criteria: An unlisted event and a semi_public event each eager-create the same draft projection set as a public event (one per enabled connection x supported kind) and can reach ready/published with no tier-based suppression at any generation step or adapter. Read-side visible_to on switch.berlin is unaffected.

D4 note: the projections this test counts now FK to PlatformConnections and are eager-created per enabled connection x supported kind. The 'all four adapters generate' assertion should hold given enabled connections exist for each platform; ensure the test fixture sets up enabled connections so 'public -> all four generate' isn't masked by absent/disabled connections. Its Harness Expected-green (eager-create produces the same draft set + lifecycle reaches ready/published across all visibility tiers) is satisfied at the services/engine seam and does NOT require the adapter implementations to exist. The per-adapter 'visibility doesn't gate THIS adapter's publish path' assertion is carried into each adapter bead's own acceptance (kb-a4u.14/.15), per ADR-008 D2 extract-at-the-caller — not blocked here.

title: C13 Adapter: Telegram channel promotion (shape per C12 outcome)
design:
Telegram channel promotion adapter — the first promotion-kind, push-API adapter. Shape is fully resolved (no remaining C12 ambiguity): per the bead notes + ADR-016 D5, Telegram is a push-API platform — the publish verb performs the Bot API send and AUTO-CONFIRMS published(+message_id) or failed.

Built as a STANDALONE adapter function, test-green in isolation with a mocked Bot API — mirrors how kb-a4u.10 (publish_switch_own_page) and kb-a4u.15 (FetLife) were built. Live posting to a real channel is deferred to kb-a4u.17 dogfooding (no live bot/channel needed for test-green). Per ADR-008 D2: NO cross-platform dispatcher / adapter base-class — that abstraction emerges from divergence and is a separate concern (the publish flow does not yet route to any adapter; publish_switch_own_page is also standalone-and-unwired). If the publish→adapter dispatch gap is worth closing now that divergence exists, file it as a discovered-from follow-up, do NOT expand this bead.

## Shape (mirror publish_switch_own_page in syndication/adapters.py)
New function publish_telegram_promotion(projection) in syndication/adapters.py:
- Preconditions, fail-loud (ADR-008 D3), mirroring switch own-page ordering: status==ready (else raise, NO transition — draft→failed is illegal); kind==promotion (else raise); source_post present (else transition→failed + raise); connection.platform=="telegram".
- Resolve channel ref: projection.connection.destination_id. Resolve bot token: connection.credentials.get("bot_token") if present (per-channel override), else settings.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (the existing ingestion bot identity — see kb-a4u.13 note "reuse TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN for bot identity; per-channel destination/creds live on the connection"). Fail loud if no token or no channel ref.
- Body: render_projection(projection) (effective content = canonical + override_data).
- Bot API send via httpx: POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage {chat_id, text}.
- ADR-008 D4 retry policy: TRANSPORT errors (httpx ConnectError/ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout/RemoteProtocolError) → up to 2 retries (linear backoff) → then transition→failed + raise. HTTP 4xx/5xx response OR Telegram {ok:false} → NO retry → transition→failed + raise. (Data/API errors never retry.)
- On success (200 + ok:true): transition ready→published; store external_id=str(result.message_id); set syndicated_at; set external_url only if a valid t.me link can be built (else leave blank — ADR-008 D3, no synthesized URL). external_id is the authoritative platform ref.
- Adapter is a PURE publish-mechanic — no authz inside it (matches publish_switch_own_page; the can_publish gate lives at the caller/dispatch layer per the existing publish_projection seam).
- Visibility-agnostic (carry-forward from kb-a4u.16): the publish path must NOT gate on Event.visibility. Include an adapter-level test asserting this.

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D2 (promotion projection), D5 (push-API auto-confirm lifecycle); ADR-008 D2 (no dispatcher abstraction), D3 (fail-loud), D4 (transport retry vs no-retry on 4xx/5xx); ADR-017 (authz at caller, not adapter).

## Harness target
Signal: uv run pytest syndication/ green (new test_telegram_adapter.py). Expected-green: (1) happy path ready→published with external_id=message_id + syndicated_at on 200/ok:true; (2) status!=ready raises with no transition; (3) kind!=promotion raises; (4) missing source_post → failed + raise; (5) transport error → 2 retries (3 attempts total) → failed + raise; (6) HTTP 4xx or ok:false → no retry (1 attempt) → failed + raise; (7) visibility-agnostic (unlisted/semi_public event still publishes); (8) token resolves from connection.credentials[bot_token] when present else settings.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN. Mock the Bot API HTTP call (no network). Rationale: push-API auto-confirm adapter with retry semantics is the goal; mocked-HTTP isolation is the same pattern as switch/fetlife adapters. Invalidation: ADR-016 D5 lifecycle shape changes, or Telegram stops being push-API.
Live channel posting deferred to kb-a4u.17 dogfooding.

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1; framed for build via /send-it 2026-05-28 (C12 outcome resolved to push-API per bead notes).
acceptance_criteria: (a) publish_telegram_promotion(projection) exists in syndication/adapters.py. (b) Happy path: ready+promotion projection on a telegram connection, mocked Bot API 200/{ok:true,result:{message_id}} → status=published, external_id=str(message_id), syndicated_at set. (c) Fail-loud preconditions: status!=ready raises with NO transition; kind!=promotion raises; missing source_post → status=failed + raise. (d) ADR-008 D4 retry: transport error → up to 2 retries (3 attempts) → failed + raise; HTTP 4xx/5xx or {ok:false} → NO retry (1 attempt) → failed + raise. (e) Token resolution: connection.credentials[bot_token] when present, else settings.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN. (f) Visibility-agnostic: publish does NOT gate on Event.visibility (adapter-level test). (g) No cross-platform dispatcher/base-class introduced (ADR-008 D2). (h) uv run pytest syndication/ green; makemigrations --check clean (no model change expected).
notes:
## ADR-016 evolution alignment (2026-05-26)
D5: Telegram is a push-API platform — publish verb performs the Bot API send and AUTO-CONFIRMS published (+message_id) or failed (ADR-008 D3/D4 retry/fail-loud). D4: read bot token + channel ref from the PlatformConnection created in C12 (kb-a4u.13), NOT settings/env. D2: projection FKs to that connection; effective content = canonical + override_data. Added dep on kb-a4u.18.
Carry-forward from kb-a4u.16 (visibility-agnostic guard): this Telegram adapter must include a test asserting its publish path does NOT gate on Event.visibility. Pipeline-level guard is in syndication/test_visibility_agnostic.py; adapter-level assertion belongs here per ADR-008 D2.

Forced past open dep kb-a4u.13 (manual bot-as-admin + channel id): that is a LIVE-posting precedence, not a code-completion dep — live verification rides kb-a4u.17 dogfooding, consistent with kb-a4u.15 FetLife live-deferral.

title: C6 Pairing flow: agents/register browser flow bound to ProfileClaim (+ kb-eya reconciliation)
design:
Pairing flow. Mirror the MagicLinkToken (organizers/models.py) one-time-token envelope. **Reconcile with kb-eya** (TelegramLinkToken + bot-DM in ingestion/) — per ADR-008 D2 the default is mirror-the-envelope-and-diverge-with-rationale (do NOT force a shared base class before a third caller); name the divergence rationale in the impl. Binds the issued long-lived credential to the facilitator User via the ProfileClaim Profile<->User link.

## v0 issuance mechanics (decided 2026-05-27 — see ADR-016 D3 "v0 concrete shape")
- **Issuance = one-time pairing-token redemption (rung B), NOT raw key-paste.** `agents/register` mints a short-lived single-use pairing token (the MagicLinkToken envelope); the facilitator hands that token to their agent, which redeems it over the API for the long-lived Bearer key. The long-lived secret never transits the facilitator's clipboard — only the agent holds it. (Full agent-initiated browser device-flow with no paste is deferred until non-technical-facilitator BYO friction surfaces.)
- **Credential binds to the User, not a Profile.** One key = the registering facilitator's identity; authority resolves through that User's full ProfileClaim set (ADR-017 D1). No per-Profile keys.
- The key→short-lived-identity-token exchange and the (stubbed) verify-identity endpoint live in C2/kb-a4u.2; this bead owns the pairing/registration + credential→User binding.

## Authz-resolution consequence (ADR-017 D1 — resolution settled 2026-05-27)
The agent->User binding this bead implements is exactly what the authorization seam (ADR-017 D2 `can_edit`/`can_publish`) resolves an authenticated agent THROUGH: a paired agent holds no independent authority scope — it presents AS its owning claimant for authz purposes, inheriting that claimant's `EventOrganizer` authority via the ProfileClaim link, exactly as that user's web session would. ADR-017 D1 previously flagged this resolution as a deferred open question; the 2026-05-27 agent-credential convergence settled it and the resolution path is THIS bead (+ C2). Concrete shape: store the credential->User binding on the agent-credential record (a column or join from the issued Bearer credential to the registering User) so `can_edit(agent_principal, event)` resolves to that User's ProfileClaim set. Don't ship the credential record without this link, or the authz seam can't resolve agents.

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D3 (v0 concrete auth shape), ADR-014 D1, ADR-017 D1 (+ D2 — the authz seam this binding feeds).

## Harness target
Signal: pytest pairing->pairing-token-redemption->key-issue->identity-token-exchange->authorized Profile-scoped action. Expected-green: a paired agent (credential bound to the facilitator User) acts on the facilitator's behalf AND is rejected on an Event whose organizer Profile the User does not claim (authz resolves through the binding). Rationale: the agent-onboarding gate for BYO-agent dogfooding; the negative case proves the ADR-017 D1 resolution actually gates. Invalidation: ADR-016 D3 / ADR-014 D1 / ADR-017 D1 change.

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1. Authz-resolution linkage added 2026-05-26 from ADR-016/017 adversarial review (finding #6). v0 issuance mechanics folded 2026-05-27 from the agent-credential design convergence.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Web UI "Personal Agent" settings page with "Pair a new agent" -> displays a one-time Bearer API key + setup instructions (shown once); (b) the Bearer key -> identity-token binds to the facilitator User account via ProfileClaim Profile<->User link (ADR-014 D1); (c) switch-cli configure accepts the key (or manual config); (d) demonstrable: a paired agent calls a protected API endpoint on the facilitator behalf and succeeds; (e) test: pairing issues a key, key exchanges for identity token, token authorizes a Profile-scoped action.

## ADR-016 evolution alignment (2026-05-26)
Unaffected by the D2/D4/D5/D6 syndication-schema/publish-lifecycle changes — this is the pairing/identity-token flow (ADR-016 D3, ADR-014 D1), which the evolution did not touch. No note content change to design needed, no dep on kb-a4u.18. (Recorded for traceability.)

title: C5 Projection-review web UI: list, override-edit, status-flip, copy-to-clipboard
design:
Depends on C3 (review UI navigates from the authored Event/Post and extends `syndication/urls.py` which C3 creates; resolves R1-F3 + R1-F5 urls.py overlap by serializing after C3) and C4 (generation + status).

## Projection-review UX/IA (decided — C3/C5 brainstorm 2026-05-26; supersedes the prior design-first FLAG)

**The review board is a PANEL on the Event page, not a separate destination.** It is the `event_syndication` fragment of the Event hub (see kb-a4u.3) — the organizer never navigates "to the projections section." It renders the syndication status board: one row per projection (= per enabled connection x supported kind, eager-created per ADR-016 D4).

**Board row shape:** `connection (platform · destination) · kind · status-chip · provenance-tag · effective-copy preview · [expand → edit]`.
- **status-chip:** draft / ready / published / failed (ADR-016 D5).
- **provenance-tag:** derived from `provenance` (ADR-016 D2) — "template" / "from agent" / "edited" — gives the generated-vs-human signal with NO version machinery.
- **expand → edit:** inline per-field override editing (`override_data`); for promotion rows that's effectively the body. Effective content = live canonical + overrides, so non-overridden fields track the Event automatically.

**Status lifecycle UX (ADR-016 D5):**
- **Approve (draft -> ready):** explicit action, gated on completeness; the "missing X" state is shown on incomplete rows (also the save-and-resume cue).
- **Publish (ready -> published):** EXPLICIT action — per-row AND a batch "publish all ready" — never auto-on-ready. For push-API platforms the publish action performs the push; for no-API platforms (FetLife) the publish action surfaces copy-to-clipboard + deep link, the actor posts out-of-band, then attests via `mark-published` (a co-equal API verb, not a UI-only button — an agent calls the same verb and can verify before attesting).
- **failed:** prominent chip + the platform's actual error reason on expand + a manual retry action (failed-push governed by FIRM ADR-008 D3/D4 — no silent failures).

**Empty / error states (the originally-flagged gap), priority order:**
1. **No connections configured (first-run):** board shows "Connect platforms in settings to start syndicating ->" rather than an empty/broken panel.
2. **No promo Posts yet:** "No promo posts yet" + the inline [Add promo message] CTA.
3. **Connection broken/expired** (e.g. revoked Telegram token): surfaced at BOTH settings and every affected projection row ("can't publish — Telegram needs reconnecting"). Fail loud per ADR-008 D3.
4. **Seed/generation failure:** row shows "couldn't generate — missing X", NOT a silently-blank body (ADR-008 D3 — no zero-fill). Doubles as the WIP indicator.
5. **Content-policy flag** (kb-o0j clean_for_platform): pre-publish warning on the row ("may contain terms FetLife/Telegram reject — review") rather than letting the push fail downstream.

Per the alpine-3.x lesson (bd memories): the board is swap-heavy (status flips, generate, edit) — each swapped partial needs its own `x-data` root or directives go inert; verify in a live browser, not just unit tests.

## Dependencies
Depends on kb-a4u.18 (PlatformConnection schema + provenance field the board surfaces), kb-a4u.3 (the Event hub it's a panel of), kb-a4u.4 (generation + status engine).

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D2, D3, D4, D5; ADR-011 D1; ADR-004; ADR-008 D3, D4; kb-o0j (content-policy).

## Harness target
Signal: pytest status-flip + override-edit persist + provenance-tag render + mark-published verb + the five empty/error states + manual browser check (swap behavior + x-data). Expected-green: the board renders one row per eager-created projection with status/provenance, inline override-edit persists and flips provenance to manual, explicit publish + actor-attested mark-published work, and each empty/error state renders its specified affordance. Rationale: the board is the facilitator-facing control surface for projection lifecycle; the goal-faithful altitude is the rendered board + lifecycle actions (a model-only test misses the swap/x-data failure mode and the empty-state affordances). Invalidation: ADR-016 D2 override/provenance model or D5 lifecycle changes.

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1; review-UI IA decided in C3/C5 brainstorm 2026-05-26.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Projection-review UI lists projections per Event/Post; (b) per-projection override-edit view editing shadowed fields; (c) status-flip controls (draft->ready->published per legal transitions); (d) copy-to-clipboard affordance per projection (used by FetLife always + TT outcome-c); (e) "Generate projection" button per Event/Post invoking rule_based generation; test: status-flip persists, override-edit persists, copy-to-clipboard present for manual-assisted adapters.

title: C4 PlatformProjection generation engine: state-machine + override + clean_for_platform + eager visibility-agnostic creation (rule_based & agent_assisted)
design:
Generic projection substrate that adapters (C9/C11/C13/C14) plug into. Carries the state-machine, the live-canonical + override_data content model, fail-loud policy, the mode parameter, the clean_for_platform seam, AND eager projection creation.

## Content model (ADR-016 D2, refined 2026-05-26)
Effective projection content = **live canonical (Event/Post fields) + per-field `override_data`** (absent key = use canonical). There is NO stored generated_body/override two-field split. Consequence for the override-independence behavior: a field that HAS been overridden is stable when the canonical changes (the override shadows it); a field NOT overridden TRACKS the canonical automatically. Generation sets `provenance` (`rule_template` for mode=rule_based, `agent_supplied` for mode=agent_assisted; flips to `manual` later on human edit per C5) and the ADR-003 reservation fields `generated_by` (nullable) + `last_generated_at`.

## Eager creation (ADR-016 D4)
Generation exposes a "create draft projections for this Event/Post across the organizer's enabled connections" capability that the C3 authoring flow invokes: per enabled `PlatformConnection` × the kinds it supports (Event→listing-capable, Post→promotion-capable), create a `draft` projection FK'd to the connection. Respects `connection.enabled`.

## Syndication is visibility-tier-agnostic (ADR-016 carried-forward, REVISED 2026-05-26)
There is **NO visibility write-gate.** `Event.visibility` (ADR-012) governs read-side rendering on switch.berlin (`visible_to`) only — it does NOT gate outbound syndication. Eager creation is **uniform across all visibility tiers** (unlisted/semi_public/public produce the same draft set); the facilitator controls where the event actually goes via explicit publish (D5). The prior "unlisted → no external projections" gate (former R1-F11 fold) is REMOVED — it conflated read-side Switch visibility with outbound syndication and boxed in facilitators. Switch's own-event-page listing remains governed by the normal read-side `visible_to` rendering (not a syndication gate).

## Generation modes
mode=rule_based (default) deterministically generates a template body from canonical Event/Post fields into `override_data` seed, NO agent required, provenance=rule_template. mode=agent_assisted accepts an agent-supplied body/override and stores it (v0 semantics — no in-Switch voice-learning model at v0 per parent --design; the agent does the voice work and POSTs the result), provenance=agent_supplied. Both modes covered by the harness. Template seed is one-time at creation, not a re-runnable regenerate (ADR-016 D2).

clean_for_platform(text, platform_id) -> str identity-stub seam at syndication/cleaning.py, called before body assembly (kb-o0j fills real rules later in place — soft dep, not blocking).

## Dependencies
Depends on kb-a4u.18 (PlatformConnection + provenance/attribution fields generation writes), kb-a4u.1 (base schema), kb-a4u.2 (API skeleton).

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D2 (refined), D4, D5; ADR-008 D2/D3/D4; ADR-011 D1; ADR-003 (reservation fields). ADR-012 is orthogonal (read-side visibility only; does NOT gate syndication per ADR-016 revised carried-forward note).

## Harness target
Signal: pytest on (1) state-machine legal/illegal transitions; (2a) override-independence — set an override on a field, mutate that canonical field, assert projection rendered output STABLE; (2b) live-tracking — mutate a NON-overridden canonical field, assert projection rendered output CHANGES to track it; (3) mode=rule_based template generation sets provenance=rule_template; (4) mode=agent_assisted accepts+stores agent body, provenance=agent_supplied; (5) eager creation is visibility-tier-AGNOSTIC — unlisted/semi_public/public Events each produce the SAME draft set (one per enabled connection x supported kind); no tier gating. Expected-green: all green. Rationale: this is the substrate every adapter depends on; the 2a/2b split is the goal-faithful test of the refined live-canonical+override model; item (5) is a guard preventing regression to a tier-gate. Invalidation: ADR-016 D2 content model changes.

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1; content model + eager-creation aligned to ADR-016 D2/D4/D5 evolution 2026-05-26; visibility write-gate REMOVED 2026-05-26 (syndication visibility-agnostic per ADR-016 revised carried-forward).
acceptance_criteria: (a) Generation endpoint (POST) accepts mode=rule_based (default) | agent_assisted; rule_based produces a deterministic-template body from canonical Event/Post fields with NO agent; agent_assisted accepts an agent-supplied body and stores it; (b) clean_for_platform(text, platform_id)->str identity-stub seam exists and is called before body assembly; (c) status state-machine draft->ready->published->failed with legal-transition set enforced; failed-push fails loud per ADR-008 D4 (no silent retry on data-integrity; <=2 retries on transport then fail); (d) per-field override storage + apply (overrides shadow canonical values); (e) parent-acceptance-4 test: mutate a canonical field after generation, assert the projection rendered output (body from retrieval endpoint) is stable; (f) visibility write-gate: an unlisted Event generates NO external projections.
notes:
ENGINE CORE COMPLETE — commit ea6129c (2026-05-26). All 5 harness pytest checks green (27 tests in syndication/tests_engine.py; full suite 371 OK). Built: syndication/engine.py (generate_projection / render_projection / transition_status callables), syndication/cleaning.py (clean_for_platform identity stub seam). Override-independence via snapshot-into-override_data["body"] at generation time. Visibility write-gate blocks only `unlisted` (semi_public deferred to kb-wrb per scope-out). State-machine draft->ready->published->failed + failed->draft retry path; fail-loud per ADR-008 D4.

REMAINING (blocked on C2 = kb-a4u.2, the Django Ninja skeleton / open ADR decision): the HTTP generation POST endpoint + retrieval endpoint named in acceptance (a)/(e). The engine is a pure callable that C2's Ninja route and C7's CLI both wrap (co-equal-API per ADR-016 D3). Dep C4->C2 added 2026-05-26 to track this. Close C4 only after the HTTP route lands on the Ninja skeleton.
close_reason:
Engine brought up to revised acceptance. All 5 harness checks green (state-machine transitions; override-independence 2a; live-tracking 2b; rule_based→provenance=rule_template; agent_assisted→provenance=agent_supplied; visibility-tier-agnostic eager creation). Full syndication suite 79 pass.

Fixed the 5 stale-engine findings from the 2026-05-27 review comment: (1) removed _check_visibility_gate entirely — syndication is visibility-tier-agnostic per ADR-016 revised carried-forward; (2) replaced UnlistedVisibilityGateTest with VisibilityTierAgnosticTest; (3) provenance now set explicitly per mode (was silently defaulting agent_assisted to rule_template — ADR-008 D3); (4) added missing agent_assisted→agent_supplied test; (5) renamed cleaning param platform_id→platform.

--force rationale: the kb-a4u.2 (API skeleton) dependency edge is a decompose-time sequencing assumption that reality inverted — the engine is a pure service layer the API/HTMX views call INTO, not vice versa. The engine's own acceptance (5 engine/model-level pytest checks) is self-contained and verified green without the API layer. Review: the fresh-context adversarial review at kb-a4u.18 close produced these exact findings; this work implements them.
