title: C3 Event + Post CRUD endpoints + web UI authoring forms
design:
Core scope per ADR-011 D1 (must have web-UI affordance). Form precedents: organizers/forms.py, accounts/forms.py. No events/forms.py exists today. C3 creates `syndication/urls.py` (C5 later extends it — serial via the C3->C5 edge).

## Authoring UX/IA (decided — C3/C5 brainstorm 2026-05-26; supersedes the prior design-first FLAG)

**Mental model: Event-centric hub.** The organizer's primary object is the Event. The Event detail/edit page IS the single syndication hub — authoring, posts, and the projection-review board (C5) all live here; there is no separate "campaign composer" object and no separate "projections" destination. The one property worth borrowing from a campaign-composer UI — visibility of "what's going where" — is delivered by the on-page syndication board (C5), not by a new object.

**Fragment-seam composition (cheap foresight per ADR-003, within ADR-008 D2).** The hub page is a composition of independently-addressable, HTMX-swappable django_cotton components, each backed by its own endpoint and named by domain concept (`event_facts`, `event_posts`, `event_syndication`), NOT by layout position. The hub template composes them; it does not inline their query logic. This is correct HTMX hygiene anyway (status chips flip, projections regenerate, posts get added — all swaps), AND it makes a future reorg (e.g. promoting Posts to its own tab) a route+nav change, not a re-plumb. Do NOT build the tab/framework now (that would be ADR-008 D2 speculation). Per the alpine-3.x lesson (bd memories): each HTMX-swapped partial needs its own `x-data` root or directives go inert.

**Promo Posts are an inline add**, not a nav destination: an "Add promo message" action on the Event page creates a Post (+ eager promotion projections per D4). Keeps Posts feeling like an add-on to the Event.

**Connections + defaults settings surface.** C3 includes the organizer-facing UI to manage `PlatformConnection`s (per ADR-016 D4, schema from kb-a4u.18): connect a destination (Telegram channel, FetLife account, Ticket Tailor account; Switch own-page needs nothing), set per-destination credentials, toggle the `enabled` default. "Enabled" mostly means "connected." This is both the syndication-targets setting and the credential store the adapters consume.

**Save-always; completeness gated at draft->ready (ADR-016 D5).** Saving an incomplete Event is always allowed (it sits in `draft`); completeness is enforced at the `draft -> ready` transition, never at save. The fail-loud "missing X" state (ADR-008 D3) doubles as the save-and-resume affordance.

**Eager projection creation (ADR-016 D4):** authoring an Event eager-creates draft listing projections for each enabled listing-capable connection; authoring a Post eager-creates draft promotion projections for each enabled promotion-capable connection.

**Authorization (ADR-017 — supersedes the prior R1-F7 "no edit-gate" note):** authoring populates EventOrganizer + EventFacilitator through-tables (ADR-007 D2). Edit/publish is gated through the `can_edit`/`can_publish` seam (ADR-017 D2): a principal may edit iff they are a claimant of an `EventOrganizer` Profile of the Event (ADR-017 D1); `EventFacilitator`s are credited-only. The gate EXISTS in v0 — it is the predicate — and is trivially satisfied for the single-facilitator case (one organizer Profile, one claimant). This REPLACES the earlier "v0 ships co-host rows WITHOUT an edit-permission gate / deferred to follow-up bead F-authz" framing: co-*organizers* DO get edit via D1, and the F-authz follow-up was canonicalized as ADR-017 (kb-7oz, closed). C3 routes its edit/publish checks through the seam rather than inlining an `is_primary` check.

**Co-equal API (ADR-016 D3):** the authoring forms are HTML clients of the same logic the JSON API exposes; the web form submission and an agent's API call resolve to the same persistence (the HTML-vs-JSON-over-shared-logic mechanism is C2/kb-a4u.2's architecture call).

## Dependencies
Depends on kb-a4u.18 (PlatformConnection schema + projection FK refront + provenance/attribution fields). Depends on kb-a4u.1 (base schema), kb-a4u.2 (API skeleton).

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D1, D2, D3, D4, D5; ADR-017 D1, D2; ADR-011 D1; ADR-004; ADR-007 D2; ADR-003; ADR-008 D2, D3.

## Harness target
Signal: pytest form-submission persists all fields + manual browser check of the authoring hub page (UX). Expected-green: round-trip Event + Post via web UI persisting all ADR-016 D1 fields, with the Event page composing the event_facts / event_posts / event_syndication fragments and eager-creating draft projections per enabled connection. Rationale: core authoring is the wedge entry-point; the hub-composition + eager-creation is the goal-faithful behavior (a bare form test would miss the fragment seam and the eager fan-out). Invalidation: ADR-016 D1 field set or D4 eager-creation policy changes.

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1; authoring-UX IA decided in C3/C5 brainstorm 2026-05-26. Authorization paragraph corrected 2026-05-27 to reflect ADR-017 (the bead's prior "no edit-gate" note was superseded by ADR-017 lines 98/122).
acceptance_criteria: (a) Event CRUD endpoints (create/read/update/list/detail) backed by C2 skeleton; (b) Post CRUD endpoints scoped to an Event; (c) web UI Event authoring form carrying ALL ADR-016 D1 fields (parent acceptance 1 field list), HTMX+Alpine per ADR-004, populating EventOrganizer + EventFacilitator through-tables; (d) web UI Post authoring form scoped to an Event; (e) test: an Event authored via the web form persists all fields, and a Post authored persists with FK to Event. (Note: Post-authoring-via-agent-API path is satisfied here, not by C2 whose endpoints are stubbed.)

The prior 'co-host rows WITHOUT an edit-permission gate / policy deferred to F-authz' note is SUPERSEDED. ADR-017 D1: edit/publish authority = claimant of an EventOrganizer Profile (+ paired agent); EventFacilitators are credited-only. The gate IS the single can_edit predicate (ADR-017 D2) — trivially satisfied for v0 single-facilitator, but co-organizers DO get edit by being listed. Route all edit/publish checks through that predicate, not inline is_primary/claimant checks. kb-7oz closed.
CLOSE STATE (2026-05-27): Shipped via commits c76581c + 96ee496 + 1555eb3 (3 adversarial-review rounds folded — broken edit page, full D1 scalar field set, co-equal API parity, ADR-017 can_edit/can_publish seam, eager projection creation, PermissionError->403 generic-body, 169 syndication tests green, makemigrations clean). title: C2 HTTP API skeleton: Django Ninja + auth (Bearer->identity-token->verify-identity) + OpenAPI
design:
Decided (resolves R1-F10 + user-confirmed): API framework = **Django Ninja** (in-process, Django-routed callables → satisfies the co-equal-API same-handler/same-middleware constraint; auto OpenAPI at root nearly free; fits ADR-004 HTMX-not-SPA + ADR-008 D2). On pickup, route the framework choice through /adr-write (likely an in-place note on ADR-001 or a small new ADR; the API *contract* is ADR-016 D3, the *binding* is not yet canonical). Implement the Moltbook auth chain mirroring the MagicLinkToken one-time-token envelope (organizers/models.py). Endpoint bodies for Event/Post/Projection are STUBBED here (filled by C3/C4) — this bead lands skeleton + auth + docs only.

## v0 auth shape (decided 2026-05-27 — see ADR-016 D3 "v0 concrete shape")
- **Build legs 1–2: long-lived Bearer key → short-lived (~1h, single-use) identity-token exchange.** Real blast-radius reduction, cheap. The credential→User binding and pairing-token issuance live in C6/kb-a4u.6; this bead owns the exchange endpoint + protected-endpoint auth.
- **Stub leg 3 (`verify-identity`).** That endpoint is for a *third-party* service that receives a Switch token and must ask Switch to validate it ("Sign in with Switch"). v0 has no such consumer — the facilitator's own agent calls Switch directly and Switch verifies its own tokens — so verify-identity ships stubbed until an external consumer exists (ADR-008 D2). (Title retains verify-identity as the named surface; the v0 deliverable is a stub.)
- **Record an actor-marker on writes for provenance.** Web UI (session) and agent (Bearer) both resolve to the same User and the same `can_edit` — authority is identical (the agent is the user's delegate, ADR-017 D1). Record the request's auth method as an actor-marker so writes carry provenance (→ the reserved `generated_by`/`provenance` projection fields). Audit-only at v0; no authority difference, no rate-limit/confirmation-by-actor-type.

## canonical_refs
ADR-016 D3 (v0 concrete auth shape), ADR-001 D8, ADR-004, ADR-014 D1, ADR-017 D1, ADR-008 D2.

## Harness target
Signal: pytest on auth-rejection/acceptance (key→identity-token exchange, then protected endpoint) + `curl /api/docs` returns OpenAPI schema. Expected-green: protected endpoint 401 without a valid identity token, 200 with one; OpenAPI served at root; verify-identity present but stubbed. Rationale: auth + contract surface every other API child builds on. Invalidation: ADR-016 D3 auth mechanism changes.

## Origin
/decompose kb-a4u round 1. v0 auth shape (legs 1–2 built, verify-identity stubbed, actor-marker) folded 2026-05-27 from the agent-credential design convergence.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Django Ninja installed + registered; (b) API mounted under /api/ with OpenAPI/JSON-schema docs served at the API root; (c) auth chain: agents/register returns a one-time Bearer API key (mirroring MagicLinkToken envelope), identity-token-exchange endpoint (Bearer->short-lived identity token), verify-identity endpoint; (d) auth middleware enforces identity-token on protected endpoints; (e) test: unauthenticated request to a protected endpoint is rejected, authenticated request passes. Event/Post/Projection endpoint bodies are stubbed (filled by C3/C4).
notes:
UPDATE 2026-05-26 (C3/C5 brainstorm convergence): the API-framework binding is now canonical — ADR-016 D6 (Django Ninja; django-bolt rejected for breaking the co-equal-handler constraint). No need to route through /adr-write at pickup; build against Django Ninja per D6, with handlers over a shared service layer the HTMX views also use (so the co-equal test kb-a4u.9 can assert identical persistence/auth).
## D6 phrasing correction (2026-05-26, post-adversarial-review)
The earlier note's 'django-bolt rejected for breaking the co-equal-handler constraint' overstates ADR-016 D3 (which says co-equal *clients of one API surface*, not 'same callable'). Corrected framing per revised ADR-016 D6: build against Django Ninja because its in-process handlers let the JSON API and HTMX views share a SINGLE auth + service layer; django-bolt's separate Rust server with its own auth splits that layer, reintroducing the two-surface drift D3 forbids. The co-equal test (kb-a4u.9) asserts identical persistence/auth through that shared layer.
ADR residue (2026-05-27): token-lifecycle + uniform-vouching ruling folded into ADR-016 D3 in-place (commit 27db461, FLEXIBLE path). Identity token = reusable-within-~1h-TTL (not single-use); Bearer = displayed-once + revoke-via-enabled-flag; vouching enforced at every API door. Resume-plan step 5 complete.
close_reason: API skeleton shipped: Django Ninja at /api/ with OpenAPI docs; Bearer->identity-token auth chain (verify-identity stubbed per ADR-016 D3 leg-3); uniform vouching enforcement; reuse-within-TTL token lifecycle. Two adversarial-review rounds folded (load-bearing token-lifecycle + vouching gaps fixed). 110 tests green, makemigrations clean. ADR-016 D3 evolved in place. Commits 4e24f86+3a62384+c807707+27db461.

comments.author: jsnyde0
comments.text:
Adversarial review (2026-05-27, fresh-context) → REVISE. Token-lifecycle design ruling + fix list recorded here.

TOKEN-LIFECYCLE RULING (resolves the "one-time" vs "long-lived" tension in acceptance(c) vs ADR-016 D3):
- Bearer API key (AgentCredential) is LONG-LIVED + reusable for exchanges, per ADR-016 D3 ("long-lived secret stored by the agent"). "One-time" in acceptance(c) means DISPLAYED-ONCE at registration (raw key shown once, stored hashed — the MagicLinkToken envelope is the storage pattern, NOT single-use semantics). Use a revoke path (enabled flag / revoked_at), not consume-on-first-exchange.
- Identity token is ~1h TTL and REUSABLE within that window for multiple protected-endpoint calls. A 1h TTL is meaningless if the token dies after one request. Enforce expiry; do NOT consume-per-request.
- This is the v0 concrete shape of ADR-016 D3; route to /adr-write to canonicalize after the fix lands.

FIX LIST:
F1+F3 (load-bearing): remove consume-on-exchange from AgentCredential and consume-per-request from IdentityToken per the ruling above.
F2+F7 (security, load-bearing): /api/ in ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES skips LoginWallMiddleware's vouching gate (user.status=="vouched" or is_staff). The Ninja auth callables (IdentityTokenAuth + SessionMarkerAuth) must enforce that same invariant — reject non-vouched authenticated users (don't silently drop it, ADR-008 D3).
F4: give stub endpoints a declared Ninja response schema so the OpenAPI contract is stable for kb-a4u.3/.4 (the OpenAPI surface IS the contract). Keep the actor-marker working through the schema change.
F8: add negative tests — expired identity token rejected; same identity token VALID on a second call within TTL (the multi-call case currently untested); non-vouched user rejected; malformed/tampered token rejected.
F5/F6: acceptable for v0 (service-layer get_actor_marker seam is correct); ensure marker survives the F4 change.

title: C1 Data model: extend Event, add Post + PlatformProjection, cheap-foresight reservations
design:

Non-trivial: cheap-foresight column-level spec per ADR-003 F1-F9 (concrete names/types/nullability, NO behavior). title: Turnstile: forms un-submittable in DEBUG + silent error on claim form
description: The Turnstile widget is suppressed in DEBUG (commit f1b84aa) but the server still requires a valid token via clean_turnstile_token in both accounts/forms.py (OpenSignupForm) and organizers/forms.py (ClaimForm). Result: signup and claim forms cannot be submitted locally/dev at all. Separately, claim_start.html only renders the turnstile_token error inside {% if turnstile_site_key %}, so in DEBUG a failed token (or any non-field error) is completely invisible — a silent dead-end (also an ADR-008 D3 fail-loud concern in prod).
design: (a) DEBUG-only bypass: clean_turnstile_token returns the token unvalidated when settings.DEBUG is True — scoped so prod (DEBUG=False) and the Django test runner (DEBUG=False) are never weakened; symmetric with the DEBUG widget suppression. (b) claim_start.html: add a non_field/turnstile error alert so a failed CAPTCHA is never silent; signup.html already surfaces via its generic form.errors loop. Touches ADR-014 D3/D4 (Turnstile gate, FIRM) — bypass is DEBUG-scoped only, does not relax the production gate.
acceptance_criteria: Signup + claim forms submit locally with DEBUG=True and no Turnstile config. With DEBUG=False, both forms still require a valid token (unchanged). A failed/blank turnstile error renders visibly on the claim form. Full pytest suite green.
close_reason: DEBUG-only bypass in both clean_turnstile_token methods makes signup+claim submittable locally; claim_start.html now surfaces non-field/turnstile errors; 4 regression tests added; full suite green. Prod/CI (DEBUG=False) gate unchanged.

title: Switch v0 outbound syndication MVP — Event/Post/Projection + web UI + API + CLI + pairing + first projections (FetLife/TT/Telegram/Switch own page)
design:
## Context

Spawned from kb-dko (closed 2026-05-25) via the close-and-spawn pattern. The brainstorm converged on the v0 shape of Switch's outbound syndication architecture (see ADR-016). This bead is the impl-shaped successor; it carries the v0 build scope and an observable acceptance contract.

Switch v0's wedge is **syndication-first**: the labor-savings of authoring one canonical Event + one canonical Post and having the system generate cleaned, platform-shaped projections for each target. The dogfooding loop is the project owner running their own personal agent (BYO at v0) against the API, surfacing friction, feeding friction back into v0.5 design.

## Architecture (canonicalized in ADR-016)

Two canonical entities + per-platform projections + co-equal API contract. The full architecture lives in [ADR-016](../../docs/decisions/ADR-016-outbound-syndication-architecture-event-post-projections.md):

- **Canonical Event** — structured facts (datetime, location, capacity, ticket types, organizer, dress code, content warnings, visibility, etc.). Source of truth.
- **Canonical Post** — communication artifact (headline, body, imagery, CTA, voice). References an Event by FK. One Event has many Posts over its lifecycle (save-the-date → early bird → almost-sold-out → last-call). Posts and Events never share fields.
- **Per-platform projections** of kind ∈ {`listing`, `promotion`}. Each projection is an editable copy of its source (Event for listing, Post for promotion), with per-field overrides, status enum, external_id/external_url, and platform-specific action elements. Content-policy filtering invokes kb-o0j's cleaning-policy substrate at projection-generation time.
- **HTTP API as the co-equal client surface** — web UI and external personal agents consume the same endpoints. Moltbook-pattern auth: Bearer API key (via `agents/register` browser flow) → short-lived identity token → service-side `verify-identity`. No SDK; raw REST.

## ADR-011 D1 feature classification (core vs agent-extended)

Per ADR-011 Consequences, every agent-layer feature must be classified. v0 scope:

- **Core scope (must have web-UI affordance)**:
  - Event authoring + edit
  - Post authoring + edit
  - Projection review + status flip + per-field override edit
  - Agent pairing flow (`agents/register` browser-mediated)
  - **Rule-based projection generation** — a deterministic-template-driven baseline draft body, generated from canonical Event/Post fields, requiring NO personal agent. The facilitator can author + edit + publish a v0 event using only the web UI (BYO-agent is optional, not gating). This satisfies ADR-011 D1's value-proposition test: syndication is the v0 wedge, and a facilitator without an agent must still be able to syndicate.
- **Agent-extended scope (may be agent-only at v0)**:
  - **Agent-assisted projection generation** — voice-and-tone-aware, learned-preference projection drafts the facilitator's personal agent generates by calling the same generation endpoint with a different mode parameter. Web UI offers no equivalent (no in-Switch voice-learning model at v0).
  - `switch-cli` — CLI surface for shell-out from external agents; no equivalent web action because it's an agent-shaped tool.
  - `verify-identity` — downstream-service endpoint, not a facilitator-facing feature.

This classification binds child-bead authoring: child beads implementing core-scope features must ship a web-UI surface; agent-extended beads may ship API/CLI only. Both generation modes call the same `PlatformProjection` generation endpoint; the mode is a request parameter (`mode=rule_based` default; `mode=agent_assisted` when an agent invokes with an identity token).

## kb-o0j cleaning-policy substrate — v0 baseline + interface seam

kb-o0j (open) owns the per-platform content-policy substrate that projection generation invokes. **kb-o0j is not a blocking prerequisite for kb-a4u v0** — the v0 baseline is:

- **For FetLife**: no content-policy cleaning required (FetLife allows explicit content; pass canonical through with format adaptation only).
- **For Switch's own event page**: no cleaning required (Switch hosts canonical events; what's on the canonical Event renders directly).
- **For Telegram channel promotion**: no aggressive cleaning required for v0 (Telegram channels are not publicly indexed, no documented kink restrictions). Light-touch format adaptation only.
- **For Ticket Tailor**: no aggressive cleaning required per ADR-015 D1 + the Ticket Tailor kb-dko scout (no documented content restrictions; verify with TT directly as part of spike 5b).

**Interface contract for the filter slot** (named to avoid kb-o0j-vs-adapter integration drift):

```python
# kb_o0j/cleaning.py (eventually owned by kb-o0j)
def clean_for_platform(text: str, platform_id: str) -> str:
    """Apply per-platform content-policy filter. v0 default: identity (return text unchanged)."""
    return text  # v0 baseline; kb-o0j substrate replaces in-place when shipped
```

Each adapter calls `clean_for_platform(body, platform_id="fetlife")` (etc.) before assembling the final projection body. v0 ships the identity-function stub at this path; when kb-o0j substrate lands real rules, the function is updated in place without adapter changes. Per ADR-008 D2 — build the seam, not the speculative-rule library.

**This is a design seam, not a defer.** The seam is in scope at v0; the rules behind it are kb-o0j's job.

## Scope — what's in (v0)

**Tier-1 (build first), per the kb-dko convergence:**

1. **Data model** — Django models for `Event`, `Post`, `PlatformProjection` per ADR-016. Schema reserves shape (per ADR-003 cheap foresight) for: multi-Post-per-Event campaign sequencing, full ticket type taxonomy, buyer/attendee screening questions, recurrence pattern. **Column-level specification of the reservations is deferred to the migration child bead spawned by `/decompose`** — that bead authors the concrete column names/types/nullability per the ADR-003 discipline (see ADR-003 F1–F9 for the model of how concrete reservations should look). **Behavior** for those reservations ships in later epics; the v0 migrations land the columns and FK shapes only.

2. **HTTP API** — canonical surface exposing:
   - `Event` CRUD endpoints + listing/detail (visible to web UI and authenticated agents)
   - `Post` CRUD endpoints scoped to an Event
   - `PlatformProjection` endpoints — generation (POST to trigger; accepts `mode=rule_based|agent_assisted` parameter — see classification section above), retrieval, status transitions (`draft` → `ready` → `published` → `failed`), per-field override edits
   - `agents/register` — browser-mediated one-time flow returning a Bearer API key
   - identity-token exchange endpoint — Bearer key → short-lived identity token
   - `verify-identity` endpoint — for downstream services (kept minimal at v0 since Switch is largely self-consumed)
   - OpenAPI/JSON-schema documentation served at the API root (the API IS the contract until `skill.md` extraction in v0.5+)
   - **Co-equal-API integration test obligation per ADR-016 D3**: a test that asserts a web-UI HTMX form submission AND a `switch-cli` invocation for the same Event CRUD operation resolve to **the same Django view/handler** (introspected via test instrumentation, not just same-endpoint-URL), produce **identical DB state**, and traverse identical auth middleware. The test is what enforces no-private-fast-path; "verified by inspection" is not adequate.

3. **Web UI** — canonical authoring surface:
   - Event authoring form (all fields per ADR-016 D1)
   - Post authoring form (scoped to an Event)
   - Projection review UI — list view per Event/Post, edit-overrides view per projection, status-flip controls. Each projection adapter brings any adapter-specific affordances it needs (see item 5 per adapter).
   - **Copy-to-clipboard affordance** is a per-projection feature on the projection-review UI — available for any manual-assisted listing projection (FetLife always; Ticket Tailor when spike outcome is (c)).
   - "Generate projection" button on each Event/Post that invokes rule-based generation (mode=rule_based) — the core path that works without an agent.
   - Pairing flow page — initiates `agents/register`, displays Bearer API key once, instructions for the facilitator to configure their agent
   - Renders on the existing Django + HTMX + Alpine stack per ADR-004; React island only if a tripwire condition fires (none anticipated for v0 scope)

4. **CLI** — `switch-cli` (Python `uv`-managed) wrapping the HTTP API:
   - Same primitive verbs as the API (create-event, create-post, generate-projection, publish-projection, list-projections, etc.)
   - Authenticated via the identity-token exchange flow (CLI stores the Bearer key in `~/.config/switch/credentials`)
   - Intended for shell-out use from Claude Code / Codex / Paseo / nanoclaw / Pi-agent — the agent doesn't need a SDK, it can `subprocess.run(["switch-cli", "create-post", ...])`
   - **Round-trip test obligation**: a test that exercises the agent-shell-out pattern end-to-end — `switch-cli create-event ...` → verifies the same Event is reachable via the web UI and via the API directly.

5. **First projection adapters** (per ADR-008 D2 — the adapters are written directly per platform; the per-platform abstraction shape is a judgment call at impl time, **not** a deterministic outcome of building any specific platform second):

   - **FetLife listing** — manual-assisted. Switch generates the per-platform body (FetLife markdown + dress_code surfaced prominently + content-policy filter slot via `clean_for_platform(text, "fetlife")` — v0 identity baseline). The projection's lifecycle:
     - `draft` — Switch has generated a candidate body, facilitator hasn't approved.
     - `ready` — facilitator has approved; UI provides "copy to clipboard" affordance.
     - `published` — *polish-level affordance not gated at v0 acceptance*: facilitator manually pastes into FetLife, then returns to Switch and clicks "I've posted this" + pastes back the FetLife event URL. The status flip + URL paste-back UI is a v0.5+ refinement; v0 acceptance only requires that the projection can reach `ready` with the right body content.

   - **Ticket Tailor listing** — HTTP API integration (or manual-assisted depending on spike outcome — see below). Per ADR-015 D1, Switch hands event metadata to TT without entering the payment funds path (organizer-direct Stripe stays with TT). **External pre-condition (not a v0 deliverable):** the dogfooding facilitator must already have a TT account + Stripe connected per `kb-94h` before this adapter can push to TT. kb-94h is the organizer-onboarding playbook; its existence is sufficient — it does not need to be closed for kb-a4u to ship, but the project owner must complete its steps for themselves before dogfooding sub-check (d) is reachable.

     **TT POST /events spike — required as build-order step 5b before adapter implementation:** per the kb-dko scout, a public `POST /events` API endpoint may not exist (scout couldn't find one). The spike's deliverable: a verified answer to "does a public TT API endpoint exist for event creation?" with one of three outcomes documented:
     - **(a) Yes, public endpoint** — TT adapter proceeds against the documented API; acceptance criterion 3 TT holds at `status=published`.
     - **(b) No public endpoint, but TT support enables on request** — TT support contacted; resolution time captured; acceptance criterion 3 TT either holds at `status=published` (if enabled in time for v0) or shifts to outcome (c) shape.
     - **(c) No path** — adapter ships manual-assisted (Switch generates the body, facilitator pastes into TT's web UI). Same UI shape as FetLife adapter: copy-to-clipboard affordance on the projection-review UI; status caps at `ready` for v0. Acceptance criterion 3 TT shifts to mirror FetLife's shape.

     The spike outcome conditions acceptance criterion 3's exact shape. Without the spike, the TT adapter scope is undefined.

   - **Switch's own event page listing** — Switch's `/events/<slug>` HTMX page renders the canonical Event directly. Trivial in implementation terms; mostly a confirmation that "Switch is a listing platform like any other" — and the simplest projection (no external API, no per-platform content-policy cleaning, just canonical render).

   - **Telegram channel promotion** — Bot API integration. Promotion projection generates a Telegram channel post (text + optional photo + optional inline keyboard with `web_app` button for future RSVP-via-Mini-App; v0 uses URL button to the Switch listing). Status flips to `published` with the message_id as external_id.

     **Prerequisites — required as build-order step 5c before adapter implementation:** (a) A Switch-operated Telegram bot must be registered with BotFather and its token stored in Switch settings. (b) The bot must be added as admin to the facilitator's target Telegram channel by the facilitator (one-time configuration per channel). (c) The facilitator must register their channel with Switch via the Web UI's "Connect Telegram channel" affordance — Switch records the channel_id for later sending.

     **Telegram setup-outcome conditioning (analogous to TT spike):** Step 5c can fail externally — BotFather is third-party, bot-admin-add requires the project owner's manual Telegram action, channel-registration requires Switch UI to be built before 5c is testable end-to-end. Outcomes:
     - **(α) All three setup steps complete in time** — Telegram adapter ships as designed; acceptance criterion 3 Telegram holds at `status=published`.
     - **(β) Bot registered + channel-admin added but Switch channel-registration UI delayed** — adapter falls back to a config-file pinned channel_id (project-owner-only path), still hits `status=published`.
     - **(γ) BotFather-side or channel-admin-side block** — Telegram adapter ships manual-assisted: copy-to-clipboard for the Telegram-formatted body; project owner posts manually to their channel. Acceptance criterion 3 Telegram shifts to mirror FetLife shape (`status=ready`, manual paste).

6. **Pairing flow** — browser-mediated `agents/register`:
   - Facilitator logs into Switch web UI, navigates to "Personal Agent" settings
   - Clicks "Pair a new agent" → Switch displays a one-time API key + setup instructions
   - Facilitator copies the key into their agent's config (or runs `switch-cli configure` and pastes when prompted)
   - From that point, the agent has API access scoped to the facilitator's Profile. The pairing binds the Bearer API key → identity token to the facilitator's User account (which is linked to their Profile via ADR-014 ProfileClaim). Authorization mechanism is canonicalized in ADR-016 D3; identity substrate (Profile ↔ User link) is canonicalized in ADR-014.

## Build order (suggested — situational at impl time)

The ordering below is the orchestrator's current judgment of a minimal-blockage path. Each step is annotated with its dependency edges; the implementer should revisit ordering when implementation reveals constraint shifts. **Steps 5b and 5c are mechanically necessary** prerequisites (you can't write a TT adapter without knowing whether the API exists; you can't post to Telegram without a bot token) — the rest of the ordering is judgment-routed.

1. **Data model migrations** — Event, Post, PlatformProjection with cheap-foresight reservations (column-level shape authored in the migration child bead per ADR-003). Lands first because everything else depends on it.
2. **HTTP API skeleton** — endpoints stub'd with auth + OpenAPI docs.
3. **Web UI authoring** — Event + Post forms consuming the API + "Generate projection" button (rule-based mode). *Reorderable with step 5*: if the project owner prefers agent-first dogfooding (author events via `switch-cli` before the web UI exists), the CLI + pairing can land before web UI authoring. Default order assumes web UI first for legibility during pairing-flow design.
4. **First projection adapter — Switch's own event page** — cheapest; uses canonical render, no external integration. Validates the projection-record model end-to-end *for the trivial render case*. Does NOT validate per-platform abstraction shape — that emerges later.
5. **Pairing flow + `switch-cli` skeleton** — agent can now register and consume the API. Co-equal-API integration test (per scope item 2) lands here.
   - **5b. TT POST /events API spike** — *mechanically necessary before TT adapter implementation*. Outcome conditions acceptance criterion 3 TT (see Scope item 5, TT paragraph). Deliverable: a one-pager in `docs/research/` documenting the endpoint's status + chosen v0 path (a/b/c).
   - **5c. Telegram bot setup** — *mechanically necessary before Telegram adapter implementation*. Deliverable: a registered Switch bot, token in Switch settings, the project owner's Telegram channel added to Switch with the bot as channel admin. Setup-outcome (α/β/γ) conditions acceptance criterion 3 Telegram.
6. **Ticket Tailor listing adapter** — second listing-kind adapter. *Whether this drives per-listing-platform abstraction is a judgment call at impl time* per ADR-008 D2; the abstraction emerges from observed divergence, not from being-the-second.
7. **Telegram channel promotion adapter** — first promotion-kind projection.
8. **FetLife manual-assisted listing adapter** — third listing platform; refines the abstraction without changing it.
9. **Dogfooding cycle** — project owner publishes one configured event end-to-end. See "Dogfooding criterion" below for what "end-to-end" means concretely.

This ordering minimizes most blockage paths in the current judgment; revisit per learning at implementation. Per the recipe-leak guard: an ordering claim is suggested-not-deterministic.

## Dogfooding criterion (what "end-to-end" means)

For acceptance criterion 10, "one configured event end-to-end" means:

- **Configured event** — an event the project owner has authored on Switch with concrete date, location, description, ticket type configuration, etc. The acceptance gate is "the event is configured completely enough that, IF the project owner chose to run it, all six per-adapter states below would have been reached." This is independently observable at close time via the configured-event state in Switch's DB (intent to actually run is the project owner's call; not gate-relevant for v0 acceptance — the gate is "the system supports the workflow," not "a real-world event happened").
- **End-to-end through this stack** — the configured event passes through ALL of: (a) Event authored on Switch (web UI OR CLI/agent), (b) at least one Post authored on Switch, (c) listing projection on Switch's own event page reaches `status=published` with a public-accessible URL, (d) Ticket Tailor listing projection — either reaches `status=published` (if TT spike outcome (a) or (b)) OR reaches `status=ready` and the project owner manually pastes (if spike outcome (c)), (e) FetLife listing projection reaches `status=ready` and the project owner manually pastes it onto FetLife, (f) Telegram channel promotion projection — either reaches `status=published` with a visible message in the project owner's configured Telegram channel (if Telegram-setup outcome (α) or (β)) OR reaches `status=ready` and the project owner manually pastes (if outcome (γ)).
- **Friction observations captured** — a `bd memories` entry tagged `kb-a4u-dogfood` is created listing friction observations sufficient to seed v0.5 design. Sufficiency is orchestrator judgment, not a quota — the goal is "enough signal that the v0.5 backlog has substance," not a specific count.

acceptance_criteria:
Given a freshly-deployed Switch v0 with the project owner paired as the first facilitator (via browser-mediated agents/register flow producing a Bearer API key), THEN the system supports the following observable end-state, verified by dogfooding one configured event end-to-end per the "Dogfooding criterion" section of --design:

(1) Facilitator authors a canonical Event via the web UI carrying all ADR-016 D1 fields (title, datetime, end-datetime, timezone, recurrence shape reserved, location, organizer + co-host via ADR-007 D2 through-tables, capacity, age restriction, dress code, content warnings, category, tags, cover image, pricing model + ticket type shapes reserved, visibility per ADR-012, external links).

(2) Facilitator authors at least one canonical Post via web UI OR via personal agent calling the HTTP API; Post has FK to Event, distinct body, headline, imagery, CTA.

(3) System generates the v0 projections per the design's per-adapter scope, with the following exact end-states (each conditional clause references the per-adapter spike/setup outcome documented in --design):
- Switch own event page listing — kind=listing, status=published, external_url = /events/<slug>, public-accessible.
- Telegram channel promotion — if --design Telegram-setup outcome (α) or (β), kind=promotion reaches status=published with message_id stored as external_id and a message visible in the project owner's configured Telegram channel (includes URL button to the Switch listing); if outcome (γ), kind=promotion reaches status=ready with a Telegram-formatted body and copy-to-clipboard affordance functional (project owner manually pastes).
- FetLife listing — kind=listing, status=ready, body-with-dress-code-surfaced + content-policy filter applied (via clean_for_platform(text, "fetlife") — identity filter for v0 unless kb-o0j substrate has shipped applicable rules), copy-to-clipboard affordance functional. The project owner manually publishes by pasting into FetLife; v0 does NOT gate on status=published for FetLife (the "I've posted this" + URL paste-back affordance is v0.5+ polish).
- Ticket Tailor listing — if --design Build order step 5b spike outcome (a) or (b), kind=listing reaches status=published with external_id and event metadata pushed without entering payment funds path per ADR-015 D1; if spike outcome (c), kind=listing reaches status=ready with copy-to-clipboard affordance functional and the project owner manually creates the TT event using the Switch-generated body.

(4) Each projection has independently editable per-field overrides; canonical Event/Post updates do not cause already-generated projections to silently re-render. An automated test verifies this by: mutating a canonical field after a projection has been generated, then asserting the projection's rendered output (the actual body string returned by the projection-retrieval endpoint) is stable — reflects the projection's stored content at generation time, not the post-mutation canonical value.

(5) HTTP API exposes Event/Post/Projection CRUD + status transitions + agents/register + identity-token exchange + verify-identity, with OpenAPI/JSON-schema docs at API root. An integration test asserts a web-UI HTMX form submission AND a switch-cli invocation for the same Event CRUD operation resolve to the same Django view/handler (introspected via test instrumentation, not just same-endpoint-URL), produce identical DB state, and traverse identical auth middleware. The co-equal-API constraint (ADR-016 D3) is enforced by this test, not by "inspection."

(6) switch-cli wraps the API and exposes the same primitive verbs; a round-trip integration test exercises the agent-shell-out pattern (`switch-cli create-event ...` → verifies the same Event is reachable via the web UI AND via direct API call).

(7) Migrations land cheap-foresight schema reservations (multi-Post-per-Event campaign sequencing, full ticket type taxonomy, buyer/attendee screening questions, recurrence pattern) with concrete column-level specification authored under the migration child bead (spawned by /decompose); no v0 behavioral implementation of those reservations.

(8) Projections respect ADR-012 visibility tiers: an automated test verifies that an `unlisted` Event generates NO external projections by default, AND that a `public` Event successfully generates all four configured projection adapters. The `semi_public`-tier projection logic is acknowledged in --design but its acceptance gate is deferred to a follow-up bead spawned at /decompose time (see --design Scope-out section).

(9) Pairing flow per --design item 6 is functional: the project owner registers a personal agent via browser-mediated `agents/register`, receives a Bearer API key, configures their agent (via `switch-cli configure` or manual config), and demonstrates the agent calling the API on the facilitator's behalf. Authorization mechanism is ADR-016 D3 (Bearer → identity-token → verify-identity); identity substrate (Profile ↔ User link) is ADR-014 D1 ProfileClaim.

(10) Project owner dogfoods one configured event end-to-end per the "Dogfooding criterion" section of --design: configured event (authored on Switch with concrete date, location, description, ticket type configuration — the system supports the workflow regardless of whether the real-world event actually happens later); all six per-adapter end-states reached (Event + Post + Switch own page status=published + TT status per spike outcome + FetLife status=ready with copy-paste + Telegram status per setup outcome); friction observations captured to bd memories tagged `kb-a4u-dogfood` — sufficiency is orchestrator judgment, not a numeric quota.

Out of scope and deferred per ADR-016 D3 / kb-dko convergence / kb-a4u --design out-of-scope section.

comments.author: jsnyde0
comments.text: Acceptance criterion (4) REFRAME (2026-05-27, user-confirmed): the stability requirement is reframed from 'stable at generation time' to 'stable from the ready transition onward' per the hybrid content model now in ADR-016 D2. Correct behavior: a projection in DRAFT tracks live canonical (non-overridden fields update when the Event is edited); at draft->ready the effective content FREEZES into a stored snapshot; ready/published reads return the snapshot, not live canonical. So the acceptance-(4) test should: (i) assert a DRAFT projection reflects a post-generation canonical edit (live tracking in draft), AND (ii) assert a READY projection's render is STABLE against a subsequent canonical edit (frozen). Implemented by kb-a4u.20.

title: kb-m69 parent re-verify: ADR-008 D1+D3 cleanups
description:
Findings 3+9 from kb-m69 parent re-verify (adversarial reviewer agentId a8e4f4d7cd37cfc18, 2026-05-21). Two ADR-008 hygiene gaps.

**Finding 3 — NoSignupAdapter + redeemed_by/redeemed_at compat shim violates ADR-008 D1** (accounts/models.py:98-106 + accounts/adapter.py:63-143, esp. lines 75, 128-129).

ACCOUNT_ADAPTER is 'accounts.adapter.OpenSignupAdapter' (a_core/settings.py:203). NoSignupAdapter is a dead class. Its only role is to query/write the InviteCode.redeemed_by/redeemed_at field pair, which exists ONLY as compat scaffolding for the dead class per the docstring at accounts/models.py:98 ('Legacy fields — kept for compatibility with NoSignupAdapter (phase 0.4)').

ADR-008 D1 (FIRM until V1): 'No backward compatibility shims until V1 — delete on sight, no deprecation paths.'

Fix:
- Delete NoSignupAdapter class entirely.
- Delete InviteCode.redeemed_by and InviteCode.redeemed_at fields.
- Migration to drop both columns.
- Grep for any other reference to redeemed_by/redeemed_at and clean up.

**Finding 9 — silent getattr fallback in events/managers.py:77 violates ADR-008 D3** (events/managers.py:77 vs :50 inconsistency).

visible_to_url() uses 'status = getattr(user, "status", "open")' — silent default to 'open' if status missing. visible_to() (line 50) uses 'user.status' directly. ADR-008 D3 (FIRM): 'no silent fallbacks on data integrity.'

Fix: change events/managers.py:77 to 'status = user.status' (matching line 50). All User rows have status post-migration (kb-m69.1); the getattr default was defensive scaffolding without warrant.

Acceptance:
- NoSignupAdapter class gone.
- InviteCode.redeemed_by + redeemed_at fields gone (migration drops columns).
- accounts/adapter.py has only OpenSignupAdapter.
- events/managers.py:77 uses 'user.status' (no getattr default).
- pytest suite green (no new failures vs. baseline of 8 failed + 65 errors).
notes: discovered-from: kb-m69 parent re-verify (audit 2026-05-21). FIRM ADR-008 D1+D3.
close_reason: Closed

title: Profile-claim entry: auth-required, web-first, two-track verification, magic-link envelope
design:
## Decision-substrate

Per ADR-014 D1 + D2 + D3 + D4. Auth-before-claim adopted proactively from D2 invalidation predicate to preserve D3's (email, profile_id, user_id) scope triple — user_target is NEVER NULL.

## File-claims

- organizers/views.py (login-required claim entry view + magic-link redemption)
- organizers/urls.py
- organizers/forms.py (new — ClaimForm)
- organizers/models.py (MagicLinkToken + ClaimIntent — different from S3's ProfileClaim and S4's verified_domain)
- organizers/migrations/00NN_magic_link_token_and_claim_intent.py (new — both models + ClaimIntent cheap-foresight cols rejected_at/rejected_by_admin/rejection_reason/resolved_at)
- templates/organizers/profile.html (three CTA branches + anonymous Sign in link)
- templates/organizers/claim_*.html (new)
- templates/email/claim_magic_link.html (new)

## canonical_refs

- ADR-014 D1 (multi-claimant through-model)
- ADR-014 D2 (web-first + two-track + auth-required mitigation; CTA variants)
- ADR-014 D3 (magic-link envelope — (email, profile_id, user_id) triple)
- ADR-014 D4 (Turnstile)
- ADR-008 D3 (fail-loud on token misuse; explicit branch for user-IS-claimant, no silent omission)

## Origin

/decompose kb-m69 round 3 convergence (2026-05-21). Slot S8.
acceptance_criteria: Auth required before claim entry per ADR-014 D2 invalidation predicate. Anonymous visitors on public Profile page see 'Sign in to claim this profile' link → redirects to /accounts/signup/?next=/p/<slug>/claim/. Authenticated users see exactly one of three CTAs: 'Manage this profile' when not profile.is_claimed; 'Add me as a claimant' when profile.is_claimed AND request.user not in profile.active_claimants.all() per ADR-014 D2 line 67; 'You manage this profile' badge (no claim CTA, link to existing admin/edit) when request.user IN active_claimants. Claim form (login-required): email field (defaults to user.email, editable) + optional 'why claiming' free-text + Turnstile. Both tracks send magic-link first per ADR-014 D2 line 76. Email-domain fast-path matching → on click, ProfileClaim with verified_method='email_domain'. Admin-review fallback → on click, ClaimIntent row (NOT ProfileClaim — admin approves via S9 to materialize ProfileClaim). MagicLinkToken(token_hash, email, profile, user_target FK User NOT NULL, intent CharField email_domain|admin_review, expires_at, consumed_at) — auth-required entry preserves ADR-014 D3 (email, profile_id, user_id) scope triple. Hash storage SHA-256, single-use atomic consumed_at, fail-loud on already-consumed (ADR-008 D3). ClaimIntent(profile, user_target, submitted_email, reason_text, rejected_at nullable, rejected_by_admin nullable, rejection_reason blank, resolved_at nullable, created_at) — cheap-foresight soft-delete + resolution cols ship in this migration; populated by S9. Tests cover (a) anonymous → Sign in link not direct form, (b) authenticated unclaimed → Manage CTA, (c) authenticated claimed user-not-claimant → Add me CTA, (d) authenticated user IN active_claimants → You manage badge (no CTA), (e) fast-path matching → ProfileClaim with email_domain, (f) admin-review non-matching → ClaimIntent (NOT ProfileClaim), (g) magic-link expired rejected, (h) already-consumed rejected, (i) Turnstile-rejected no MagicLinkToken row, (j) cross-profile token-replay rejected (scope check).

title: Sister-platform payment-processor strategy decision (Stripe-cutover vs adult-friendly day-1)
design:
## Context

**Discovered from `kb-cyq` R2 synthesis (2026-05-21).** The long-term sister platform (kb-2ve Phase A D1: Hipsy-shaped revenue home for explicit canonical events) faces the same Stripe-vs-Verotel/Segpay payment-processor question as the tactical V0/V1 path, but with different trade-offs:

- **Stripe day 1** — cheap (1.5% + €0.25), mass-market UX, deferred risk; scheduled cutover when scale triggers attention. Inherits the same `kb-0cj` R0 finding that Stripe is already the structural processor under most of our scene's existing operators.
- **Adult-friendly processor day 1** (Verotel or Segpay) — higher fees (5–10% + scheme-reg + rolling reserve), niche-fit UX (kink-aware checkout language), lower banking-surprise risk. Sets the sister platform up as a structurally-resilient alternative to mainstream platforms from launch.

The decision shape is fundamentally different from kb-cyq's tactical V0/V1 path because:

1. **Sister platform is likely merchant of record** (kb-2ve Phase A characterized it as "Hipsy-shaped" which is MoR; confirm against kb-2ve Phase B definition when authored) — direct financial liability, not organizer-via-Stripe like TT.
2. **No "leave TT" cost** — the sister platform is greenfield; processor choice doesn't require migrating off another stack.
3. **Long-term horizon** — fee differences compound; lock-in is harder to unwind once attendees know the payment UX.

## Scope

Decide which payment processor the long-term sister platform uses at launch, and record the decision in ADR-015 D1 (FLEXIBLE addition planned in kb-cyq R2 ADR evolution).

**Decision inputs needed:**

1. **`kb-0cj` R1 deep-scouts** — Stripe EU-precedent depth + Verotel + Segpay deep-scouts (currently deferred; spawned by this bead when work begins)
2. **kb-2ve Phase B definition** — what's the sister platform's MoR posture, fee model, target organizer scale, EUR-only vs multi-currency? This bead has a soft dependency on kb-2ve Phase B; can claim work as soon as MoR posture is decided informally.
3. **Cutover-readiness beads A, B output** — operational learnings from V0/V1 (what actually breaks, what triggers a ban, how organizers respond)
4. **Audience-friction analysis** — does Verotel/Segpay's checkout UX harm conversion enough to outweigh ban-risk reduction? (Empirical data from existing adult-friendly platforms)

## Phase shape

- **R0** — synthesize across kb-0cj R0 + kb-2ve Phase B + cutover learnings; option-spec for Stripe / Verotel / Segpay / hybrid
- **R1** — deep-scouts on shortlisted options if needed

## Context

**Discovered from `kb-cyq` R2 synthesis (2026-05-21).** When both mainstream layers (TickeTailor AUP + organizer's Stripe ToS) go hostile simultaneously — and dedicated adult processors (Verotel/Segpay) impose 5–10% + scheme-reg setup costs — crypto payment rails are the only remaining option without leaving cleanable-Western-banking entirely.

The 2026 EU regulatory landscape under MiCA reshapes crypto-PSP availability: Coinbase Commerce exits EU 2026-03-31; new licensing requirements affect which providers can settle EUR. The audience-fit question is also genuinely open — tantra/sex-positive event attendees aren't crypto-native by default.

This bead is **exploratory** — research first, decide V1.5 inclusion second.

## Scope (exploratory — discovery-shape)

5. **Operational complexity** — KYC requirements per provider, volatility-hedging (auto-convert to EUR on purchase vs hold crypto), accounting/tax implications for organizers in DE

title: Payment processor risk + alternatives for explicit-event ticketing (Stripe upstream gate)
design:
## Context

**Discovered from `kb-cyq` R1 P0 TickeTailor deep-scout (2026-05-21).** That scout surfaced a load-bearing risk-surface shift not previously framed: **TickeTailor is not merchant-of-record** — organizer connects their own Stripe / PayPal / Square. Therefore the actual financial-existential gate for explicit-event ticketing on TickeTailor is **the underlying payment processor's adult-content policy, not TickeTailor's AUP.**

This re-shapes the V0/V1 risk model:

- Hipsy and Eventbrite ARE merchants of record → one policy gate (theirs)
- TickeTailor is NOT merchant of record → two stacked policy gates (TT's AUP + organizer's payment processor's ToS); the second is unaffected by which ticket platform sits above it
- Whichever path V1 takes (TickeTailor, custom-build, sister platform), **a payment processor sits at the base of the stack and its policy is the structural risk floor**

## Scope

This bead carries the **payment processor research and risk-mitigation strategy** for explicit-event-organizer ticketing across all V1 paths (TickeTailor tactical, sister platform long-term).

## Phase R0 status (2026-05-21, COMPLETE)

R0 discovery complete. Synthesis in [`docs/research/kb-0cj-r0-payment-processor-landscape.md`](../../docs/research/kb-0cj-r0-payment-processor-landscape.md).

**Load-bearing findings:**

1. **Stripe ToS (Jan 2024 update) explicitly added "fetish services"** to the prohibited list, alongside escorts/pornography/sexual-massages. Termination-for-convenience confirmed in the SSA. **WishTender (dominatrix-tip platform) was cut off March 2024 with no notice** — canonical EU/US-applies-globally precedent.

2. **No mainstream EU PSP is friendly.** Adyen explicitly classifies "fetish products" as PROHIBITED (strictest). Mollie, Klarna, GoCardless all prohibit. All downstream of Visa/MC scheme rules.

3. **MoR absorbers (Paddle / FastSpring / LemonSqueezy) are dead-ends** on two axes: adult-content bans AND product-type mismatch (digital-products-only; event-tix not in scope).

4. **Dedicated adult processors** (CCBill / Segpay / Verotel / Epoch / RocketGate) openly accept but cost 5–10% + $500–1000/yr scheme reg + 5–10% rolling reserve, and are subscription-content-shaped. **Verotel + Segpay are the only EU-native EUR-SEPA candidates.**

5. **Structural reality:** TickeTailor + Squarespace-Commerce + DICE + Shotgun + Yogo + Eventbrite all default to Stripe underneath. **Stripe is the structural processor under the vast majority of our scene** — including TNT Berlin, Shibari Studio Berlin, Sensual Hearts Temple, Tantric Kink Munich, European Tantra Festival. **The financial-existential risk is already present and unmitigated in the current state; this is not a Switch-introduces-risk problem.**

6. **Crypto fallback narrows.** Coinbase Commerce exits EU 2026-03-31 (MiCA). BTCPay (0%, self-hosted, no fiat-settle), NOWPayments (0.5-1%, MiCA-posture unclear), CoinGate (1%, MiCA-licensed, EUR settlement) are the realistic candidates. Audience-friction (tantra-workshop attendees aren't crypto-native) keeps crypto in fallback-rail territory, not primary.

## R2 synthesis (in parent `kb-cyq`)

The kb-cyq R2 synthesis (2026-05-21) ratifies this bead's R0 findings into V0/V1 path decisions. Key implications:

- **TickeTailor + Stripe is GO** for tactical V0/V1 — inherits the same risk every scene operator already runs.
- **Cutover-readiness is a V0/V1 deliverable** — spawned beads kb-y6w / kb-6y6 / kb-d9s cover Stripe-ban + TT AUP-removal + facilitator-agent metadata-logging.
- **Crypto-fallback exploratory** spawned bead kb-bw0 covers research into 2026 options.
- **Sister-platform processor decision** spawned bead kb-hm0 covers the kb-2ve Phase B question, with ADR-010 D1(d) evolution capturing the decision surface.

See `kb-cyq` `--design` body (R2 synthesis sections D1-D4) via `bd show kb-cyq`.

## Phase R1 deep-scouts (deferred, feeding cutover-runbook beads)

R1 P0–P2 priorities surfaced in R0 doc:

- **P0:** Stripe EU-precedent deep-dive (volume thresholds, EU-organizer ban records via ESWA / sifted.eu / FetLife). Feeds bead kb-y6w (Stripe-ban cutover runbook).
- **P1:** Mollie (Hipsy's stack + WC-Mollie footprint) — feeds Hipsy migration option in kb-6y6; **Verotel** (only EU-native openly-adult with public rates) — feeds onboarding playbook in kb-y6w.
- **P2:** Segpay backup + CoinGate as MiCA-compliant crypto failover — feeds bead D (crypto-fallback exploratory).

R1 deep-scouts dispatch on-demand when the spawned beads (kb-y6w / kb-6y6 / kb-bw0) need their inputs.

title: Research third-party ticket platform leverage for organizer-hub V1 short-term ticketing
design:
## Context

Seed bead from kb-6uj convergence + R1 adversarial review (2026-05-20). The kb-6uj backlog names the **organizer-hub epic** as next-up after legal-gate (`kb-dko` carries its full definition). One component of that epic is a **tactical short-term ticketing path** via a third-party platform — used during the period when the Phase A D1 sister platform (the long-term revenue home) isn't built yet.

The Switch facilitator agent creates the canonical event on Switch (full kink-explicit content) and auto-generates a "cleaned" version on the chosen third-party ticket platform — and ideally syncs attendee capacity bidirectionally.

This bead carries the **research and validation** for which third-party platform(s) to leverage during the tactical short-term period. **R2 converged 2026-05-21; adversarial-review revisions folded in 2026-05-21** — see decisions below.

## Scope clarifier

This is **not** a "third-party vs sister platform" decision research. D1 sister platform is positioned in kb-6uj's Bucket 3 as long-term core revenue infrastructure that will be built (sequencing TBD); third-party ticketing is the practical short-term path for organizer-hub V1. The two are not in competition.

The research output feeds the **ticketing-component scope** of `kb-dko` (organizer-hub epic definition).

## Research path summary

- **Phase R0 discovery** (2026-05-21) — four parallel niche-cluster scouts mapped ~80 organizers in our scene. Synthesis: [`docs/research/kb-cyq-r0-provider-landscape.md`](../../docs/research/kb-cyq-r0-provider-landscape.md).
- **Phase R1 P0** (2026-05-21) — TickeTailor logged-in CDP deep-scout. Output: [`docs/research/kb-cyq-r1-tickettailor-deepscout.md`](../../docs/research/kb-cyq-r1-tickettailor-deepscout.md). Surfaced payment-processor risk-surface shift → spawned `kb-0cj`.
- **Phase R1 P1** (2026-05-21) — Forbidden Tickets fallback scout. Output: [`docs/research/kb-cyq-r1-forbiddentickets-deepscout.md`](../../docs/research/kb-cyq-r1-forbiddentickets-deepscout.md). Verdict: US-only, no API, no EU traction — skip for V1 but interesting existence-proof for kb-2ve sister-platform inspiration.
- **`kb-0cj` R0 payment-processor landscape** (2026-05-21) — [`docs/research/kb-0cj-r0-payment-processor-landscape.md`](../../docs/research/kb-0cj-r0-payment-processor-landscape.md). Critical finding: Stripe is the structural processor under the vast majority of our scene (TickeTailor + Squarespace + Eventbrite + DICE + Shotgun + Yogo all default to Stripe). Stripe's Jan 2024 ToS explicitly added "fetish services" to prohibited list. No mainstream-EU alternative exists; only Verotel + Segpay are EU-native EUR-SEPA openly-adult.
- **Adversarial review** (2026-05-21) — REVISE verdict; 8 load-bearing findings folded back into this synthesis. Most-load-bearing: F1 evidence tightening, F2 Switch-as-aggregator risk surface clarification, F5 cleaning-flow scope, F6 ADR home for payment-processor decision moved to new ADR-015.

## R2 — load-bearing picture (2026-05-21, revised)

The risk surfaced on TickeTailor's AUP layer is **mirrored exactly one layer deeper on Stripe**. Both have hostile literal text + reactive-only enforcement + 20+ scene organizers running unbothered + termination-for-convenience clauses + canonical-precedent cases (WishTender for Stripe, lack-of-precedent for TT). **Same risk shape, stacked.**

**Stripe is already the processor under most of our scene** — TNT Berlin, Shibari Studio Berlin, Sensual Hearts Temple, Tantric Kink Munich, European Tantra Festival are all on Stripe right now. The Stripe-bans-fetish-services risk is **already present and unmitigated** in the current scene state. Switch building on this stack **in coordination-layer mode** (see D1 architecture, Mode A) does not introduce the risk; it inherits the same risk every scene operator already runs. If Switch ever moves to Stripe Connect platform mode (Mode B), the risk surface changes — see `kb-a2j` (bead F).

**Per F1 evidence tightening:** R1 evidence cites ~12 operators "currently selling on TT" but the meaningful subset for Switch's use-case (publishing *explicit canonical events cleaned to TT*) is ~4–5 — Seren Sins BDSM Dungeon Social (London), Townhouse Wirral BDSM Play Event (UK), Cherry Noir BDSM Club (Philadelphia), Seani Love "Rituals of Kink" (Berlin/London). The other ~7+ (Fox Den Tantra, GAY-TANTRA, Dance Meets Tantra, Wheel of Consent, etc.) already use coded/tantra-framed language that wouldn't trigger AUP §"sexually explicit imagery" — they're existence-proofs for the cleaning approach, not for the raw-explicit-tolerance ceiling. GO decision still holds, but evidence is narrower than the v3 synthesis claimed.

**No mainstream-EU escape exists.** Adyen is stricter than Stripe (explicit "fetish products" prohibited). Mollie / Klarna / GoCardless all prohibit adult/sexual content. MoR absorbers (Paddle / FastSpring / LemonSqueezy) double-fail (adult bans + digital-products-only). Visa/MC scheme rules are upstream of all of them.

**Only viable alternative processors** are dedicated adult: Verotel + Segpay are the EU-native EUR-SEPA candidates at 5–10% + $500–1000/yr setup + rolling reserve + subscription-shaped. **They do not plug into TickeTailor** (TT supports only Stripe/PayPal/Square natively) — going Verotel/Segpay means leaving TickeTailor. → cutover-readiness path, not primary path.

**Crypto is fallback-rail only** — Coinbase Commerce exits EU 2026-03-31 (MiCA); BTCPay / NOWPayments / CoinGate viable for emergency cutover; tantra/workshop attendees aren't crypto-native. → exploratory bead, V1.5 candidate.

## R2 — Decisions

### D1. Tactical V0/V1 path: TickeTailor + organizer's own Stripe + Switch-owned vetting layer, Mode A coordination-layer

GO. Same risk-shape Stripe already imposes on the scene (in coordination-layer mode); no upside to custom-build or routing differently when the existential gate is identical Visa/MC scheme rules every alternative inherits.

**Architecture — explicit mode clarification (post-F2):**

- **Mode A coordination-layer (V0/V1 choice).** Switch facilitator agent helps each organizer set up their *own direct Stripe account*; the ToS counterparty relationship is organizer→Stripe. Switch never holds a Stripe Connect application, never aggregates payment routing, never appears as ISV/platform in Stripe's risk model. The "already-present-risk" framing applies. Detail in `kb-a2j` (bead F).
- **Canonical authoring layer:** Switch holds the explicit canonical event (full kink/sex-positive vocabulary, imagery, dress-code, consent prereqs).
- **Cleaning layer:** Switch facilitator agent generates a "cleaned" projection per the versioned cleaning policy (see `kb-o0j`, bead G). First-N events per organizer-cluster pair go through organizer human review before publish; trust-escalation threshold N defined in cleaning-policy bead.
- **Vetting layer:** Switch-owned, upstream of TickeTailor — facilitator agent handles application/Telegram-bot/member-portal-style gating where organizer requires it. **Decouples vetting from ticket platform (R0 finding F2).**
- **Cleaned target:** TickeTailor event via API (event_series + bundles path). TickeTailor publishes an MCP server (`developers.tickettailor.com/docs/mcp`); **R2 defers explicit position on MCP-vs-REST integration** (per F8) — V0 uses REST per the R1 doc's confirmed API surface; MCP evaluation can happen in implementation if needed.
- **Payment processor:** organizer's own Stripe — Switch is not in the funds path; TickeTailor is not merchant-of-record either; organizer owns the Stripe relationship. Organizer onboarding through Stripe KYC has its own friction-surface — see `kb-94h` (bead H).
- **Capacity sync:** TT webhooks (`order.created`, `issued_ticket.created`) push to Switch facilitator agent in seconds; Switch PATCHes capacity changes back when organizer raises cap.

### D2. Cutover-readiness as V0/V1 deliverable, not blocker

Both AUP-layer (TT) and processor-layer (Stripe) enforcement are reactive with no notice (WishTender precedent). V0/V1 ships with cutover capability across three fallback paths:

**Fallback paths (priority-ordered):**

1. **Cleaned event removed under TT AUP** → migrate to Hipsy (MoR transfers to Hipsy) OR Eventbrite with conscious-coded framing, asterisk-censored if needed à la Wet Playground Barcelona (MoR transfers to Eventbrite) OR self-hosted (WordPress + Modern Events Calendar + WooCommerce à la Karada House / SM Kurse / Kinky Deviants Vienna pattern — organizer's Stripe relationship preserved). Choice depends on cleaning ceiling required and organizer preference.
2. **Stripe banned organizer** → migrate organizer to Verotel or Segpay (EU-native EUR-SEPA dedicated adult processor). Requires leaving TickeTailor since TT doesn't natively support those processors — paired with self-hosted ticketing or custom adult-friendly platform.
3. **Both layers hostile** → full reconstruction on adult-friendly stack (Verotel/Segpay + self-hosted), OR crypto fallback if exploratory bead (kb-bw0 below) converges on viable option.

**Spawned beads (V0/V1 deliverables):**

- **kb-y6w (A)** — Stripe-ban cutover runbook + Verotel/Segpay onboarding playbook
- **kb-6y6 (B)** — TickeTailor AUP §removal cutover runbook + Hipsy/Eventbrite/self-hosted migration paths
- **kb-d9s (C)** — Switch facilitator agent metadata-logging for cutover reproducibility
- **kb-bw0 (D)** — Exploratory: crypto payment-rail fallback in 2026 (BTCPay / CoinGate / NOWPayments). P2 / V1.5 candidate.

**Adversarial-review-spawned beads (V0/V1 architecture + readiness):**

- **kb-a2j (F)** — Switch platform-level Stripe risk: confirms Mode A coordination-layer architecture for V0/V1, documents Mode B boundary, risk-mitigation playbook. Prerequisite for D1 architecture being load-bearing.
- **kb-o0j (G)** — Switch facilitator cleaning policy schema + versioning + per-platform target rules + trust-escalation threshold N. Closes acceptance item (2). Upstream of kb-d9s.
- **kb-94h (H)** — Organizer Stripe onboarding playbook for explicit-event business KYC. V1 launch readiness; without it first organizer could brick at Stripe setup.

### D3. Sister-platform (kb-2ve) processor decision → kb-hm0 + new ADR-015

The long-term sister platform faces the same Stripe-vs-Verotel/Segpay choice. Either:
- Build with adult-friendly processor day 1 (higher fees, niche-fit UX, lower banking risk), OR
- Stripe day 1 (cheap, mass-market UX) + scheduled cutover when scale triggers attention.

**Per F6 — payment-processor strategy is an infra/ops decision, not product-posture.** Wrong fit for ADR-010 (which carries product-posture decisions). **Decision lands in new standalone ADR-015 "Payment-processor strategy for explicit-event ticketing"** (TBD via `/adr-write`) — D1 FLEXIBLE captures the decision surface; kb-hm0 (sister-platform processor strategy) lands the actual decision into ADR-014 D1 when sister-platform scope clarifies.

### D4. Acceptance items 2–6 close-out

- **(2) Cleaning-flow design:** Vocabulary substitution per-cluster + imagery scoping + per-platform cleaning targets + trust-escalation threshold N + re-review-on-AUP-removal mechanism — all formalized in **kb-o0j (G)**. Acceptance item (2) closed via that bead's deliverables (schema + per-platform rule sets + implemented gate).
- **(3) Payment flow ownership / MoR:** **Organizer**, via own Stripe (Mode A coordination-layer per D1). TickeTailor is not MoR; Switch is not in the funds path. Chargebacks hit organizer's Stripe directly. Clear ownership; no Switch financial liability for ticket sales in this mode.
- **(4) Failure-mode handling:** covered by D2 (cutover-readiness beads kb-y6w / kb-6y6 / kb-d9s / kb-bw0).
- **(5) Migration path to sister platform:** TT exports attendee CSV; full event read-back via API. Migration shape = export → ingest → re-onboard attendees with notification. **Low friction precisely because TT doesn't lock organizer data.** Sister-platform-side import schema is downstream of kb-2ve Phase B.
- **(6) Decision:** **TickeTailor + organizer's own Stripe (Mode A coordination-layer) + Switch facilitator agent for cleaning/vetting/sync**, with cutover-readiness beads kb-y6w/kb-6y6/kb-d9s/kb-bw0 + sister-platform processor question landed in kb-hm0 + ADR-015 (new standalone) + V0/V1 readiness beads F/G/H from adversarial review.

## Why this is its own bead

Distinct from the organizer-hub epic definition (`kb-dko`) — that bead defines the epic scope assuming this research has converged. This bead is upstream of `kb-dko`'s ticketing-component scope: research output feeds organizer-hub V1 ticketing scope.

title: Explore: do ADRs distinguish planned vs implemented status?
design:
## Decision: option (b) — no change needed (2026-05-21)

Existing pattern suffices. ADRs document **target architecture** (per global ADR-011 D1: 'ADRs reflect target architecture, not as-is state'). Implementation status is orthogonal to that semantic and is already tracked elsewhere — beads cite ADRs via canonical_refs, and reverse-lookup (`bd search <ADR-ref>` or `bd list` with grep on canonical_refs) yields the implementation surface for any given decision.

Adding a planned-vs-implemented field to ADR conventions would:

- Muddy the global ADR-011 D1 semantic ('reflect target') by re-injecting as-is state into the artifact whose whole point is to be target-stable.
- Duplicate state that already lives in bd (where status mutates as work moves through ready/in_progress/closed).
- Risk drift between ADR-asserted status and actual bd state.

Firmness (FIRM / FLEXIBLE / EXPLORATORY) already encodes 'how strongly held'; that's the only dimension the decision-artifact itself needs to carry. Whether a FIRM decision has shipped is a question for the bead substrate, not the ADR.

## Rationale carried forward

If a future case shows reverse-lookup is too lossy (e.g., an ADR's implementing beads are closed but the implementation is incomplete because they were closed-as-superseded, or a beadless ADR has been documented but never implementer-claimed), revisit. The signal would be: someone asks 'is ADR-NNN actually live?' and the bd substrate doesn't yield a clean answer in <60s. As of 2026-05-21 no such case has surfaced.

## canonical_refs

- `~/.claude/docs/decisions/ADR-011-adrs-reflect-target-architecture.md` D1 — current ADR semantics; this decision aligns with rather than mutates D1.
- `kb-6uj` — origin / where the question was surfaced during Phase A staging brainstorm.

title: Sort Phase A long-term vision into prioritized epic backlog
design:
## Context

kb-2ve closed (2026-05-20) with the Phase A long-term-vision picture landed:

- **D1** Two-platform end-to-end (Switch Berlin native + sister platform Hipsy-shaped for PSP-resilience)
- **D2** Two-flow outbound event syndication, agent-mediated
- **D3** Deep social-network within ADR-009 D4 + UGC guardrails (FetLife/Diversia-shaped depth long-term)
- **D4** Personal-agent layer for every profile (MCP-shaped agent-callable surface)
- **D5** (EXPLORATORY) Cross-organizer community discovery

Phase A established *what the maximalist long-term version looks like*. **What was never done** is the original user-intended reduce step: mapping the Phase A picture onto pragmatic release slices. This bead carried that exercise.

## Why this is its own bead, not kb-2ve

kb-2ve was overloaded once already (Phase A vision + Phase B kb-fx9 routing). The reduce-to-pragmatic-slices exercise is a different shape that integrates with ADR-002's phase ladder and ADR-005's bundle structure. Clean provenance: kb-2ve = vision + routing; this bead = staging.

## Convergence (2026-05-20, /brainstorm + R1 adversarial review)

### Framing reduction

Originally framed as a **per-decision version-staging table** (D1→V0/V0.x/V0.5/V1/post-V1/future). During the Socratic loop, the user reframed away from rigid version-staging toward an agile, product-led shape: climb to legal gate, publish, outreach to closest facilitators first then widen out, prioritize epics just-in-time as signal arrives. **The output became a lightly-sorted epic backlog, not a version table.**

### Strategic call — supply-side wedge first

**Firmness: FLEXIBLE** (load-bearing — would constrain post-0.5 capacity allocation for many cycles).

Two-sided marketplace cold-start: solve the supply side (organizers/facilitators) first because they get value standalone (write-once event entry, outbound syndication, ops automation). Users follow because their V0 prop is the easier one ("find interesting events").

- **Rationale (reasoned):** Two-sided marketplaces typically grow one side first. Demand-side prop in this domain ("find events") is table-stakes; facilitator-side prop ("save hours of cross-posting + manage RSVPs in one place") is differentiated and standalone-valuable. Solving facilitator pain unblocks the harder side.

- **Alternatives considered:**

  | Alternative | Why rejected |
  |---|---|
  | Demand-side first (seed users with discovery, hope supply follows) | `reasoned:` Domain has latent demand already (existing attendees on FetLife/Diversia/Hipsy) — but those attendees are already on platforms that work for them as discovery layers. Building a user-first discovery platform competes head-on with FetLife/Diversia/Hipsy on their own ground without differentiation, since Switch can't yet offer events the others don't have. The Airbnb-Craigslist seeding pattern (seed demand via external aggregation) needs a moat (Airbnb had hosts; Switch has nothing yet for demand-first attendees). The differentiation has to come from supply-side first. |
  | Both sides at once | `reasoned:` V0 capacity (solo) insufficient; would dilute both sides and produce a half-built version of each. ADR-008 D2 (no speculative abstraction) pushes against fan-out at this stage. |

- **What would invalidate this:** Concentric facilitator outreach signal shows the hypothesized pains (cross-posting, RSVP management, ticketing) aren't acute, OR facilitators surface a different more acute pain we should target instead.

### Pre-0.5 — no Phase A staging

Pre-0.5 work follows ADR-002's phase ladder (FIRM up to legal gate at 0.5). **Phase A decisions enter the picture from 0.5 onward.**

Note on the ADR-002 D5 0.3 organizer-peer: the first organizer-peer at 0.3 (FIRM per ADR-002 D5) tests *foundational platform schema* — event entry, basic browsing, schema feedback. This is **not** the organizer-hub epic. The organizer-hub epic (Phase A D2 + D4 organizer-cut) is a structural upgrade *on top of* the foundational platform and only enters scope post-0.5. The 0.3 schema work should be foundation-shaped (an event has a title, a time, a venue, attendees), not Phase-A-shaped (no syndication targets, no agent layer surface, no third-party platform integration in the schema yet).

### Sorted epic backlog

Buckets are **work-bundles, not decision-bundles** — Phase A decisions D1–D5 don't map 1-to-1 onto buckets; they get *sliced* and slices go into different buckets.

**Bucket structure: FLEXIBLE. Bucket contents: EXPLORATORY.** Re-shuffling expected at every stage as facilitator signal arrives. These are not firm commitments to ship anything.

Relationship to ADR-005's Bundle A/B/C: these three buckets are an **epic-layer roadmap** sitting *above* ADR-005's implementation-layer Bundle A (code) / Bundle B (ops & soak) / Bundle C (post-observation design) decomposition. When Bucket 1's organizer-hub epic actually ships, it will likely span across one or more of Bundle A / B / C depending on scope — this bead does not pre-commit. ADR-005 is FLEXIBLE and may evolve in place when the bucket-to-bundle relationship sharpens.

**Bucket 1 — Next-up after legal-gate: Organizer-hub epic**

Pulls from D2 (outbound event syndication) + D4 organizer-cut (personal agent layer for the facilitator). Candidate concrete contents:

- Write-once event entry on Switch as canonical source
- RSVPs + screening questions managed on Switch
