kind: anti-pattern
scope: global
created: 2026-05-26
---

Adversarial-reviewer subagents — even with rule-2 "findings-only, no verdict" explicitly in the brief — will emit a VERDICT: REVISE / VERDICT: PASS closing line under default-prose-habit pressure. The closing-summary instinct is strong; a rule lower-listed in the brief gets pattern-overridden by the trained shape of "adversarial review writeups end with a verdict."

**Why:** kb-a4u R1 reviewer (2026-05-26) included `VERDICT: REVISE` at the end of its findings list despite the brief's rule 2 explicitly prohibiting any verdict line. Orchestrator ignored it (per skill discipline). R2 brief was sharpened: the rule-2 prohibition was re-foregrounded with R1's specific violation cited as an example of what NOT to do. R2 reviewer obeyed (no verdict line). The sharpening worked — but only because R1's violation was the priming example.

**How to apply:** When dispatching an adversarial-reviewer subagent, structure the brief so the "no verdict" rule is FOREGROUNDED, not buried as rule N-of-M. Concrete tactic: open the brief's rules section with "Rule 1: emit findings only — no closing verdict line. Reviewers default-habit to verdict-shaped summaries; this prohibition is the most-violated rule, so verify your output ends with the last finding, not with VERDICT: X." If the reviewer violates anyway, the orchestrator must ignore the verdict line (no fold; the violation is a primer for the next dispatch's brief, not a signal to fold). Companion to [[adr-clause-hallucination-by-reviewers]] (reviewer hallucinates clause-ids under fold-pressure); both are reviewer-default-prose failure modes the orchestrator must catch.

Alpine 3.x directives (@mouseenter, @click, :class, x-show, x-bind, etc.) are INERT unless the element has an x-data ancestor. $store and Alpine.store() are globals and work anywhere, but directives are scoped — Alpine only walks DOM subtrees rooted at an x-data node. Symptom: directive appears in rendered HTML (verified via outerHTML), Alpine is loaded and initialized ($store works when called directly), Alpine.version reads fine — but @mouseenter/@click do nothing. Fix: add x-data='{}' (empty object is fine) to the closest sensible wrapper. For HTMX-swapped subtrees, put x-data on the swapped partial's root element so Alpine reinitializes on re-render. Discovered on switch.berlin /events/ kb-0da (commits e9863f0 + 47b2173, 2026-05-11): event cards had @mouseenter and :class for hover sync, but the partial _event_list.html had no x-data wrapper. Reviewer signed off ('Alpine loaded in _base.html → directives resolve') without testing actual hover behavior on a deployed page — code review can't catch this; only live browser-automation verification can. Lesson: when adding Alpine directives, grep up the ancestor chain in the rendered DOM for x-data BEFORE assuming directives will fire.

kind: anti-pattern | scope: workspace | created: 2026-05-21

"Risk X is already present in the existing scene → we don't introduce it by building on top" is a valid framing for coordination-layer architectures (Mode A) but a category-error for aggregator-platform architectures (Mode B). Aggregator platforms engage platform-compliance review independent of individual-merchant risk states.

Why: kb-cyq R2 v3 synthesis used "already-present-risk" framing as if it covered all of Switch's possible architectures. Adversarial review F2 caught that framing only holds in Mode A (organizer→Stripe direct, Switch as guide); Mode B (Switch-owned Stripe Connect aggregating many organizers) re-engages the risk via platform-compliance pathway. Watchdogs reporting "Switch facilitates fetish events" route through Stripe's platform team regardless of individual merchant-account states.

How to apply: Whenever an architecture decision pivots on inheriting-existing-risk framing, name the architectural mode explicitly. If aggregation is in scope, the inheritance argument does not survive without a separate platform-compliance analysis. Applies to payment processors (Stripe Connect), identity providers, content-moderation pipelines, any vendor that evaluates risk at platform-tier. Canonical case: ADR-015 D1 + kb-a2j (2026-05-21).

kind: anti-pattern | scope: workspace | created: 2026-05-22

When a model auto-creates a user-owned record at signup (Profile, default workspace, etc.) and that model has a visibility/status enum that gates rendering, the default status MUST keep the owner reachable to themselves. Defaulting to a moderation-pending status silently breaks "user sees their own thing."

Why: kb-m69.4 auto-created Profile(kind=person) on signup with status='candidate' (the curation-queue default for admin-imported Profiles). The kind=person path forgot that the auto-created Profile's owner IS the verified claimant via verified_method='auto_self' — no admin curation needed. Result: signed-up users couldn't see their own profile until kb-m69.11 flipped the auto_self default to status='approved' and added a unit test. Generalizes beyond Profile: any auto-create-on-signup record with a curation/moderation status field has this trap.

How to apply: When auto-creating any user-owned record at signup or first-action, decision-substrate must answer: (1) is the owner pre-verified by the creation context itself? If yes, default to a status that renders to the owner. (2) Does the user have a way to view their own record under the default status? If no, the default is wrong. Add a unit test asserting "owner can view their own freshly-created record" as a load-bearing post-condition.

kind: procedural-lesson | scope: workspace | created: 2026-07-07 | updated: 2026-07-07 (RESOLVED for PyPI/uv)

RESOLVED 2026-07-07: in-cage `uv run pytest` works again for DB-less suites. Root cause of the original block: iron-proxy's egress allowlist is BAKED into the cage image (the install_cmd in ~/.config/rip-cage/tools.yaml writes /etc/iron-proxy/proxy.yaml with a hard-coded domains list; default-deny, MODE-INDEPENDENT — a host missing there is 403'd even under network.mode: observe, and /etc/rip-cage/egress-rules.yaml is a separate non-choking layer, which is why the two lists diverged). Fix: added pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, registry.npmjs.org, objects.githubusercontent.com, switch.berlin to the baked list; `rc build` + destroy/recreate of personal-switch-berlin. Verified in-cage: `curl -x http://127.0.0.1:8888 https://pypi.org/simple/` → 200; `uv run --directory /workspace/tools/switch-cli pytest` → 124 passed (uv sync pulled the full venv through the mediator).

**Diagnosis recipe (keep):** a DIRECT curl to a blocked host shows `tls handshake eof` (the egress firewall); the honest signal is routing through the mediator (`curl -x http://127.0.0.1:8888 <url>`) and reading `tail /tmp/rip-cage-mediator-iron-proxy.log` for `action:reject status_code:403 host:<host>`. If a needed host 403s at the mediator, the fix is HOST-SIDE: add it to the baked domains list in ~/.config/rip-cage/tools.yaml, `rc build`, destroy+recreate the cage. Don't burn time retrying uv sync in-cage.

**REMAINING LIMIT — Django suite needs Postgres:** `pytest syndication/` (or any suite needing the dockerized Postgres+pgvector) still cannot run in-cage — no docker inside a cage, no postgres in the image. Hand those runs to the host (`docker compose run --rm app uv run pytest syndication/`), as done for kb-k2ds.2/.3 (1404 passed host-side). An in-cage test-services strategy (native postgres baked as a TOOL, nested podman, microVM reframe) is under evaluation — see the pre-brainstorm from the 2026-07-07 session.

**Also NOT in the baked allowlist (deliberate):** api.telegram.org — switch-cli's Telegram path is MTProto over raw TCP, which doesn't traverse an HTTP CONNECT mediator anyway; caged Telegram work needs its own design pass. Related: [[challenge-driven-dogfood-as-design-main-thread]].

kind: project-anchor | scope: workspace | created: 2026-06-15

THE MAIN THREAD of Switch work (as of 2026-06-15) is a graph of CHALLENGE epics (Challenge 0, 1, 2 ...) — NOT the ~50 scattered feature/bug/payment-research beads on the board. Strategic pivot, driven by the user feeling lost: we shipped the syndication COMPONENTS (generation engine, WYSIWYG composer/studio, Switch/FetLife/Telegram adapters, destination picker, coverage tracker, switch-cli) but never WALKED the journey, so nothing felt smooth or like how he'd actually use it. We are switching FROM feature-spec planning ('build features we think we need') TO challenge/journey-driven planning ('walk a real user journey end-to-end; build only what the walk makes us wish for').

THE METHOD — dogfood-as-design: one real end-to-end outcome = one Challenge epic. WALK it as the user actually would. For the dogfood, the AGENT (Claude Code) literally IS the user's distribution agent: it drives the EXISTING endpoints + switch-cli, writes and tones the copy itself, drops drafts into the studio for the user to review/greenlight, places the drafts, and reports what landed / what's left to do by hand. Walking over the existing surface (NOT pre-building) reveals which gaps actually hurt enough to wire into the product vs which are fine left as 'the agent does it over the existing API'. Children are created AS THE WALK REVEALS THEM — never pre-spec'd / pre-decomposed. This is the journey analog of ADR-008 D2 'extract from the third diverging caller, not the first'.

REAL-USE DISCIPLINE (learned 2026-06-15 from the first Challenge 0 walk attempt): a walk only teaches if it mirrors real use. The first attempt did NOT — the agent INVENTED the event (real use: the event already exists; the agent promotes it), and it ran against a half-synthetic fixture (a made-up event + a two-channel Telegram+FetLife setup that was never actually connected), so fixture-noise drowned the real friction. The honest version starts from a FRESH account with nothing set up and walks the genuine onboarding-to-publish arc. RULE: if a walk needs invented events / hand-wired fixtures / synthetic identities to proceed, that is a smell — stop and re-derive the journey toward real use before pushing through.

CADENCE — lean/agile: orient + design ONE walk together with the user, file a follow-up 'co-design the next challenge' checkpoint bead, walk, repeat. Confirm scope with the user before executing a walk.

SECOND DESIGN TARGET (added 2026-06-15) — THE HARNESS-AS-PRODUCT: the agent harness we build to drive Switch (skills/CLIs/hooks/subagents) is ITSELF a product we'll ship to our users (and later other harnesses: pi, Codex, standalone). Canonicalized EXPLORATORY in ADR-019. Core rule: CAPABILITY IN THE CLI (switch-cli), CONVENIENCE IN THE SKILL (Claude-only wrappers) — so capability is reachable by pi/Codex/humans/CI, never Claude-only. Portability seam = the existing co-equal REST contract + CLI (ADR-016 D3), no per-harness SDK. Dependency isolation = capability-ladder (ADR-018 D4) + a cheap-foresight PRIMITIVE LEDGER at docs/harness-primitive-ledger.md (tracks name|lever|deps|portability per primitive). TWO DISTINCT harnesses, do not conflate: operator's personal substrate (via publish-harness) vs the Switch PRODUCT harness (for users) — publish-harness inspires only. Build NO publishing/adapter machinery now (ADR-008 D2 / ADR-003). The challenge walks are where ADR-019 gets grounded.

CURRENT SPINE: Challenge 0 = kb-k2ds (P1) — RE-SCOPED 2026-06-15 to the honest journey: a FRESH account onboards from ZERO (no connections/events/posts) to a PUBLISHED promo on the user's REAL synced Telegram. Telegram-ONLY; FetLife/multi-channel deferred to Challenge 1. Journey: real web signup -> connect Telegram (QR) + sync -> ENABLE channels for promotion -> create event -> publish event -> write + tone promo post -> greenlight -> place saveDrafts in real channels -> report landed/left. Multi-actor (human: signup + QR scan; agent: everything else). The walk = kb-k2ds.1 (design-checkpointed; live walk deferred to a session where the user is at their phone). Next planning checkpoint = kb-z50e (co-design Challenge 1 = fan out to FetLife / more channels / a real recurring event, parked behind the walk).

GAPS in the agent-driven Telegram loop (probed 2026-06-15; (1)+(2) confirmed over the live CLI/REST surface, independent of any fixture): (1) FRONT-DOOR is blind and silent — create-post returns NO fan-out info, list-projections is a hard-coded stub, there is NO studio-link verb and NO find/list-events verb; an agent cannot get from event-exists to drafts-exist + studio-link over the CLI. Generation IS wired eager at post-create (_eager_create_promotion_projections) but it silently no-ops when no connection has 'promotion' in kinds. (2) ENABLE-FOR-PROMOTION missing — synced channels land with kinds=[] (promotion off); no agent- or user-reachable verb to enable a channel for promotion was found, only the raw DB field. (3) TONING — clean_for_platform() is an identity stub, real ToS/explicit-language rules deferred to kb-o0j; agent-assisted copy mode CAN carry toned copy. (4) REPORT — approve / publish / coverage are separate page navigations; no single greenlight->publish->report. The Challenge 0 walk will confirm which of these actually hurt in real use.

HOW TO APPLY: when a new agent asks 'what's next' / runs /roadmap-tldr, the Challenge-N graph IS the answer — surface it as the spine; the scattered backlog stays parked unless a live challenge needs it. Do NOT pre-decompose a challenge. Canonical refs: ADR-019 (harness-as-product target — capability-in-CLI, primitive ledger), ADR-018 (Telegram tiered delivery bot/saveDraft/deep-link), ADR-016 (composer surface + co-equal REST contract), ADR-011 (agent-extended scope). Sibling discipline: dogfood-workflow + substrate-thick/process-thin (ADR-012 D1).

scope: global

A cheap-foresight seam (ADR-003) authored as a single named resolution point but with ZERO live callers is dead code that defeats the very intent it was added for: the future change it was supposed to make a one-value edit is still a rewrite, because no behavior flows through the seam. 'Defined' is not 'load-bearing.' Worse than not adding the seam, because the ADR records the foresight as delivered when it isn't.

**Why:** kb-96tn.5 (commit 728e880) added edit_after_publish_policy(platform) at services.py:636 — commented 'the SINGLE named resolution point' per ADR-016 D5 / ADR-003. But the dirty affordance read proj.is_dirty directly at all three render sites; the policy function had no non-test caller. Per-bead review passed (function existed, defaulted correctly, unit-tested in isolation). Only fresh-context parent re-verify caught that flipping the policy value would change NOTHING rendered. Repair child kb-96tn.11 (commit 14c506a) wired the three sites through it; the proving test stubs a non-default policy and asserts the dirty banner changes.

**How to apply:** A cheap-foresight seam's acceptance is 'a non-default value changes observable behavior,' NOT 'the resolver exists and is unit-tested.' When closing a bead that introduces an ADR-003 seam: grep the seam name for a live (non-test) caller on the behavior path BEFORE close; write the proving test as 'stub the seam to a non-default value, assert the affordance changes' (the isolation unit test passes on dead code — that is the trap). Sibling of [[parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift]] and [[adr-enum-vocabulary-drift-invisible-per-bead]].

kind: project-anchor | scope: workspace | created: 2026-06-02

The CI 'test' job's check --deploy (test.yml, kb-eqr) is a FAST pre-merge mirror that runs at --fail-level WARNING with NO frontend build and NO built image — it catches settings regressions (DEBUG, CSRF, SECRET_KEY length/W009) only. The AUTHORITATIVE deploy gate is deploy.yml's check --deploy (line ~244), which runs inside the built Docker image but at the DEFAULT fail-level (ERROR) — so WARNING-level checks do NOT gate there. Net: no check --deploy anywhere fails on a WARNING; the test.yml gate is stricter (WARNING) but artifact-incomplete, the deploy.yml gate is artifact-complete but laxer (ERROR).

Two consequences:
1. The test-job check --deploy step had NEVER run to completion before kb-7t0s (2026-06-02) — it was masked behind earlier red steps under 'bash -e'. This is the recurring 'bash -e cascade' pattern: kb-va4a (Telegram tests) unmasked kb-7t0s's E006/E007, which when fixed unmasked django_vite.W001. Expect more masked failures to surface as upstream steps go green.
2. The prod manifest guarantee is NOT either check --deploy — it's the Dockerfile frontend build stage (builds static/dist into the image, fails the build loud if npm build fails). django_vite.W001 is silenced in the test-job gate only via CI_SKIP_VITE_MANIFEST_CHECK (a_core/settings.py, set only in test.yml's check --deploy env).

Why it matters: when adding a new prod-safety system check, decide deliberately whether it should gate at WARNING (add to test.yml's gate, ensure the artifact it needs exists or scope-silence it CI-only) or ERROR (deploy.yml catches it). Don't assume deploy.yml's check --deploy enforces WARNINGs — it doesn't.

kind: procedural-lesson
scope: workspace
created: 2026-06-02
---

A "CI green on HEAD" acceptance bullet is NOT satisfiable by a pytest+djlint proxy. The CI workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) runs MULTIPLE jobs/steps: lint (ruff check . + ruff format --check + djlint), test (full bare `uv run pytest` + makemigrations --check + check --deploy + makemessages), and security (gitleaks full-history + bandit + pip-audit). Verify EACH, with the EXACT CI command.

**Why:** kb-33do.5 integration gate verified only pytest+djlint+test_settings and reported green; I closed the parent on a "CI green" bullet. The push revealed CI red on ruff (~800 syndication errors, kb-f17n), gitleaks (2 history secrets, kb-9wk5), and 2 Telegram-token tests that pass locally via .env but fail in CI (kb-va4a). All pre-existing, none caught by the narrow gate, forcing a reopen + scope correction.

**How to apply:** When a bead's harness target / acceptance says "CI green," (1) read .github/workflows/*.yml and enumerate every gating step; run each locally with its exact command; (2) run bare commands as CI does (`uv run pytest`, not a local `--ignore`'d invocation) — local convenience flags mask collection/coverage gaps; (3) reproduce CI's environment — tests depending on a local .env value (API/bot tokens) pass locally and fail in CI; override_settings/mock the value in-test; (4) for "is main CI actually red and why," check the real run via `gh run view <id> --log-failed` per job, don't trust a stale triage note. Local-green ≠ CI-green. Linked: [[nested-uv-subproject-breaks-root-pytest-collection]], [[django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow]].

kind: anti-pattern
scope: workspace
created: 2026-05-22
---

Running collectstatic in an init Docker service is only correct if the output directory is a volume the app (gunicorn) service mounts. If STATIC_ROOT lives on the init container's container-local filesystem, /app/staticfiles is empty in the gunicorn container — every /static/* URL 404s.

**Why:** kb-cm5 (2026-05-22) — bin/init.sh ran python manage.py collectstatic --noinput in the init service; init exits, its FS is ephemeral and never shared. The app container's /app/staticfiles was empty. Vite manifest was baked into the image at build time (Dockerfile COPY of static/dist/), so HTML <link> and <script> tags resolved correctly — masking the 404s in the rendered HTML. Login-wall middleware also redirected anonymous static-asset requests away from the asset, double-masking the failure.

**How to apply:** (1) Default: run collectstatic at image build time in the Dockerfile, not in a runtime init script. Files land in the image layer shared by every container started from it. kb-x14's fail-loud SECRET_KEY guard is a *runtime* guard; collectstatic doesn't use crypto, so a dummy SECRET_KEY=x DATABASE_URL=postgres://x:x@x/x at build time is acceptable (commit d359137 shape). (2) If you keep collectstatic at runtime, STATIC_ROOT MUST be a named volume (or bind mount) declared in docker-compose.yml and mounted at the same path on both init and app services. (3) Smoke probe after deploy: curl -I https://<host>/static/dist/assets/<known-asset>.css MUST return 200 text/css from anonymous context. HTML rendering correctly is not sufficient evidence — the manifest is image-baked.

kind: feedback | scope: workspace | created: 2026-06-13

The syndication composer is WYSIWYG: the user EDITS the live styled platform preview directly — type into the rendered post body, cursor in the real styling, Typefully-style. Editor and preview are ONE surface. Never a separate textarea + read-only render, never an editor/preview split.

**Why:** This is a RECURRING regression — the user has had to correct it 'every time'. Agents keep re-deriving an editor/preview split (e.g. _channel_editor.html textarea gated against read-only _channel_preview.html per kb-kgza.10; bead kb-6yyp was even scoped FIRM 'READ-ONLY, no editing controls' — the exact opposite of the user's vision) because 'type in a box, see a preview elsewhere' is the conventional default. The product vision is modeled explicitly on Typefully: live-edit-the-preview. Re-deriving the split wastes cycles and frustrates the user badly.

**How to apply:** When building or touching the syndication composer, the styled per-platform post body IS the editable surface (contenteditable or equivalent). Do NOT add a separate textarea. Do NOT render a read-only preview as a distinct element. Collapse editor and preview into one. Overflow-into-thread (Typefully's segment auto-split as you cross the char limit) is cheap-foresight-only until a thread-native platform (Twitter/Bluesky — named as later targets) is added: shape the content data/naming to hold an ordered set of segments, but do NOT build splitting logic now. This governs the ADR-016 composer surface and overrides bead kb-6yyp's original read-only premise.

kind: procedural-lesson | scope: global | created: 2026-07-07

The configure-cage skill (+ the recipe fragments in rip-cage's examples/) IS rip-cage's install/config UX — for the operator's future selves AND for other users adopting rip-cage. When a cage-layer lesson is learned in ANY project session (an egress footgun, a posture gotcha, a new default host set), fold it into the skill/recipe docs in the rip-cage repo the same day — a lesson that lives only in one project's memories leaves every other adopter to re-hit it. **Why:** 2026-07-07 the mode-independent mediator-allowlist choke cost a caged agent ~40 failed uv-sync attempts; the fix generalized to every future cage, so it was folded into the skill's Footguns (not just this repo's memory). **How to apply:** after resolving any rip-cage config issue, ask 'is this project-specific or cage-layer?' — cage-layer goes into configure-cage SKILL.md / the relevant examples/ recipe (it's git-tracked product surface, commit it in rip-cage); project-specific stays in the project's .rip-cage.yaml comments + bd memories. Composability is the product: capability in recipes, judgment in the skill, per-project deltas in .rip-cage.yaml.

kind: anti-pattern
scope: global
created: 2026-06-14
---
When building a per-object coverage/status/reconciliation surface over a domain enum of N values (delivery tiers, states, kinds), the model must account for ALL N. A tier the model silently forgets does not error — it falls into the default/absence bucket and renders as a permanent ghost (e.g. an eternal `pending` indistinguishable from "never processed"), a silent ADR-008 D3 integrity gap.

**Why:** kb-56c2 (2026-06-14, round-1 adversarial-review blocker). ADR-018 D1 defines THREE delivery tiers {bot (Bot-API, web-observable), agent (saveDraft, reported), public (deep-link, human-posts-manually)}. The coverage tracker's initial design modeled only the two machine-observable writers; `pending` was computed as "selected destination with no placement record." Public-tier destinations are NEVER machine-observable — they can never get a record — so every selected public destination became a PERMANENT silent `pending` ghost, visually identical to never-distributed. Folded as FIRM D6: public tier = human-action affordance (deep-link "open & post manually" + send-checklist), explicitly EXCLUDED from the pending reconciliation — never `placed` (fabricated, same class as a "sent" badge), never `pending` (silent ghost).

**How to apply:** Before shipping any coverage/status surface, list every value the source enum can take (read the ADR/model that defines it — here ADR-018 D1's three tiers) and write down, per value, which bucket it lands in. Any value with no explicit mapping is the ghost. A value that is categorically UNOBSERVABLE must render as an explicit honest non-state (an affordance / "outside our observation"), not absorb a default machine state. Inverse-direction sibling of [[adr-enum-vocabulary-drift-invisible-per-bead]] (that = an implementer ADDS an (N+1)th enum value; this = a model DROPS one of the canonical N). Cross-ref ADR-008 D3.

kind: anti-pattern | scope: global | created: 2026-06-12

A verification tool whose DEFAULT request shape does not satisfy the condition the code-under-test gates on will silently DODGE the gate and return a FALSE GREEN — it never reproduces what the real client hits. Canonical instance: curl defaults to Accept star/star; a middleware/view that only acts on text/html (content negotiation, an age gate, a format branch) is invisible to a bare 'curl -A UA url' — the request sails past the gate and returns the ungated body, confirming behavior the real text/html client never gets.

Why: kb-t93r (2026-06-12, Switch prod P1). AgeGateMiddleware redirects only text/html requests without an age_gate cookie to /age-check/. I verified the kb-6d7o Telegram OG card with 'curl -A TelegramBot' and got the correct event card every time — a false green — because curl Accept star/star never contained text/html, so the gate never fired. Every REAL social unfurler (Telegram/Twitter/FB) sends Accept text/html and was 302d to the age-check interstitial, scraping 'Age Verification — Switch Berlin' instead of the event on every platform. The bug surfaced ONLY by driving real Telegram web (browser-automation, CDP 9222) and reading the rendered card; the user push to self-verify live is what caught what curl structurally could not. The decisive cheap repro needed BOTH the crawler UA AND -H Accept text/html.

How to apply: Before treating a curl/HTTP-client probe as green for crawler-/format-/content-negotiation-gated behavior, name the request attribute the gate keys on (Accept header, UA substring, cookie, Sec-Fetch, Content-Type) and set it EXPLICITLY to the real client value — do not let the tool permissive default stand in for the real condition. When ground truth is a third-party renderer (link-preview unfurler, embed), drive the REAL client (browser-automation against the live service). A unit test pinning the gate code path (accounts/tests.py::test_agegate_social_crawlers_bypass_gate with HTTP_ACCEPT text/html) guards the logic but NOT the false-green class. Sibling to overselling-validation-before-representative-case-demonstrated and implementer-subagent-self-report-unreliable-verify-diff; all evidence-before-assertion failures. Cross-ref .claude/harness.md Fit profiles Crawler-facing / Accept-gated behavior.

kind: anti-pattern
scope: global
created: 2026-05-22
---

A data-migration backfill that introduces a new visibility/status/tier field MUST preserve the de-facto visibility the row had before the field existed. A "pessimistic default" for rows missing source signal is a labeling lie in the opposite direction: it hides rows that were already publicly visible under the old schema.

**Why:** events.0013_event_visibility.backfill_visibility defaulted rows with no RawMessage source linkage to semi_public (kb-m69.2, 2026-05-21). All 32 prod events were admin-created without source linkage. Pre-migration, /events/ rendered them to anonymous viewers. Post-migration, with EVENT_VISIBILITY_TRUSTED_STATUSES=("vouched",) and 0 users on prod, nobody could see them. The migration's fail-loud branch (ADR-008 D3) fired only on unknown source_type, not on no source — the latter took the silent pessimistic default. Resolution required a bulk UPDATE to restore public.

**How to apply:** When writing a data migration that introduces an enum gating render/access: (1) Identify the pre-migration observable visibility of each row class (anonymous can see it? logged-in can? URL-keyed?). That is the floor for the post-migration default — never go below it without an explicit data-cleanup step. (2) The "no source signal" branch is a third arm alongside known/unknown — name it explicitly. Either raise (fail-loud, ADR-008 D3) and triage, OR map to the de-facto-prior tier. (3) Add a post-migration assertion: rows visible to anonymous pre-migration count == rows visible to anonymous post-migration. (4) Companion at signup-time auto-create is [[auto-created-records-reachable-default]]; this entry is its data-migration sibling.

kind: procedural-lesson | scope: global | created: 2026-06-02

When decomposing an epic, an acceptance bullet describing a CROSS-ELEMENT AGGREGATE surface (a unified index, a global nav, a dashboard rollup) is the one most likely to end up owned by no child — each element-scoped child satisfies it only at a reduced altitude (e.g. per-item reachability instead of the aggregate surface).

Why: kb-q4u9's decomposition coverage map mapped acceptance bullet 1 ('a flat list of publishables is navigable; selecting one opens its composer') to the composer child, but that child satisfied it only at per-workspace reachability — the unified events+posts index the bullet actually described was owned by no child. The /decompose conjunction-coverage probe did not catch it because that probe is harness-SIGNAL-scoped ('what behavior fires on the parent harness target without firing on any child harness target?'), and a cross-aggregate bullet accepted at reduced altitude usually carries no dedicated harness signal, so it sits outside the probe's frame. It surfaced only at parent re-verify and was split to a follow-up. The fix is judgment + the existing parent-re-verify net, NOT a new probe arm in /decompose (that would be process-thickening / recipe-leak).

How to apply: When decomposing, before trusting the coverage map, scan the parent's acceptance bullets for any describing a surface that SPANS multiple elements (index / nav / rollup / aggregate). For each, name the specific child that owns the FULL surface — not merely per-element reachability. If no child owns the aggregate, that is a missing child, not a covered bullet. Do not lean on the conjunction-coverage probe alone for these — it checks harness signals, and aggregate bullets frequently lack one.

kind: procedural-lesson
scope: global

When a decomposition flags a "load-bearing open mechanism" as a binary choice — option (a) vs option (b) — the resolution at implementation time may be a THIRD point that is neither: a hybrid that takes the cheap structural half of one and the persistence half of the other. Pre-framing the choice as strictly (a)|(b) can anchor the implementer onto the recommended pole and miss the midpoint that actually fits.

**Why:** kb-ide0 / kb-ide0.4 (2026-06-04, ADR-016 D2 sync mechanism). The epic flagged the sync-from-channel binding as "(a) LIVE — shared content_version row + sync_source FK, live propagation" vs "(b) SNAPSHOT — re-copy_from on resync, no new field, no live propagation", recommending (b). The actual resolution was a third option — "snapshot + persisted pointer": snapshot semantics (no live propagation, copy on resync) PLUS a persisted sync_source FK so the toggle state survives reload. Pure-snapshot (b) could not persist the toggle across a page reload (UI-only state is lost); pure-live (a) carried unwanted shared-row collision risk. The midpoint kept (b)'s no-propagation simplicity and borrowed (a)'s one persisted field. The decomposition's binary framing under-specified this.

**How to apply:** When authoring a "resolve (a)-vs-(b) at child design" note in a decomposition, add an explicit prompt: "or a hybrid taking <cheap-half-of-a> + <persistence-half-of-b>?" Name at least the axis the binary collapses (here: persistence-of-toggle-state vs propagation-of-content). The implementer should re-derive the option space, not just pick the recommended pole. The recommendation is a prior, not a fork-closure. Linked: [[decompose-cross-aggregate-acceptance-bullet-needs-an-owner]].

Django autoescape does NOT protect a value interpolated into an Alpine directive expression (`@click`/`x-on`/`:attr="...{{ value }}..."`). Autoescape turns `'` into `'` for HTML-TEXT safety, but the browser HTML-decodes the attribute value back to `'` BEFORE Alpine's JS parser evaluates the expression string — so a user-controlled value breaks out of the JS string literal and injects into the Alpine expression. Stored self-XSS even with autoescape on.

**Why:** kb-sbhs.3 (2026-06-12). A theme-tag value was interpolated into an Alpine `@click` expression on the tag chip. Autoescaped `'` rendered as `'`, but the live browser decoded it to `'` before Alpine eval, injecting into the expression. Fresh-context review caught it; neither the deterministic suite NOR the prior live read-back did. Fixed by moving the value out of the expression into a `data-tag`/`dataset` attribute and reading it via `event.target.dataset` — no user value ever lands inside an Alpine expression string.

**How to apply:** NEVER interpolate a user/stored value directly into an Alpine expression attribute. Pass it via a plain `data-*` attribute and read `el.dataset.*` inside the handler; or `|escapejs` only if it must be a JS string (and understand the attribute-decode still applies). Autoescape guards HTML text, not the JS-expression-in-attribute context. Test the apostrophe/quote value end-to-end in a LIVE browser — a `response.content` assertion sees the escaped `'` and false-greens; the decode-then-eval happens browser-side only. Related: [[alpine-3-x-directives-mouseenter-click-class-x]] (directives inert without x-data) is a different Alpine trap on the same surface.

When migrating an FK to an M2M-through with an is_primary=True compat property (see events/models.py:283 Event.organizer), every caller that uses the bare M2M handle .add() is a latent bug. .add() creates a through row using the through-model's field defaults (is_primary=False); the compat property filters on is_primary=True and returns None; downstream template {% url %} resolves None → empty string → NoReverseMatch → 500.

**Why:** kb-cm5 session (2026-05-22) — events/management/commands/seed_visibility_demo.py used event.organizers.add(organizer) (the standard M2M shortcut). It created 6 events with no primary EventOrganizer row. /events/ 500'd as soon as the seed ran because the list template hits event.organizer.slug in a {% url 'event-detail' org_slug=event.organizer.slug %} call. The compat property + setter was designed for the ~30 pre-existing call sites; the M2M handle is the un-mediated bypass. Fixed in commit 2d22f20 by switching the seed to event.organizer = organizer (the setter handles is_primary=True via get_or_create) AND patching the 6 existing rows.

**How to apply:** (1) Grep for \.organizers\.add( and \.organizers\.set( across the codebase whenever the compat property exists. Each call site is either intentionally adding a co-organizer (in which case is_primary=False is correct) or confused-shortcut for primary-set. The latter is the bug — replace with event.organizer = profile. (2) The general pattern: any model.<m2m_field>.add(x) against a through-table with a compat_property that filters on a through-field default is suspect. Audit at compat-property-creation time, not at first 500. (3) Stronger fix (deferred under ADR-008 D2): override the through model's manager add() to raise on the compat-property's discriminator — but that's behavioral speculation. For V0, grep-and-audit is sufficient. (4) The compat property itself should raise (not return None) when the M2M has rows but no primary — that state is data corruption per ADR-008 D3, not "no organizer."

Restoring an OLD pg_dump (taken before a Django RenameModel-style migration) hits 'InconsistentMigrationHistory: migration X is applied before its dependency Y' when forward-migrating. Cause: when you ship a RenameModel migration like organizers 0007_rename_organizer_to_profile, Django (or your hands) inject the new migration into the 'dependencies' of OLDER migrations that have FKs to that renamed model. The snapshot's django_migrations table records those older migrations as applied — but the CURRENT files on disk show them depending on a not-yet-applied later migration → consistency check fires. Cleanest fix: (1) Generate the rename migration's SQL via a Python shell with 'unittest.mock.patch.object(MigrationLoader, check_consistent_history, lambda *a, **kw: None)' and migration.apply(state, schema_editor, collect_sql=True) — pure sqlmigrate is also blocked by the same check. (2) Run that SQL directly via psql (BEGIN ... COMMIT). (3) Also CREATE INDEX explicitly for any FK fields (db_index=True is default but collect_sql doesn't always emit the index DDL). (4) Manually INSERT INTO django_migrations (app, name, applied) VALUES (...). (5) Now run 'manage.py migrate' — consistency restored, remaining migrations apply normally. Encountered on kb-vp8 restore 2026-05-13; snapshot at 83 migrations, current code at 90, organizers 0007 was the bridge. Single quotes in SQL through SSH heredocs MANGLE — write SQL to a local file and pipe via 'cat sql | ssh host docker exec -i ... psql' instead.

A Django {# ... #} comment is stripped ONLY when single-line. A {# ... #} spanning multiple lines is NOT a comment — Django renders it as literal page text. Use {% comment %}…{% endcomment %} for anything multi-line.

**Why:** In the kb-wz8m syndication epic a multi-line {# comment bled visible raw text across multiple syndication partials and the GDPR consent modal. No test caught it: test-Client assertions check that expected markers are present, never that junk is absent, so raw-comment bleed is structurally invisible to the suite — only the ui-craft browser read-back saw it. RECURRED kb-sbhs.2 (2026-06-12) in the destination-picker template (commit 82f1ce7) — again caught only by the live browser read-back, exactly as predicted. Third+ occurrence; the recurrence rate is the signal: treat a multi-line {# #} as a live-read-back-mandatory smell on EVERY new template, not a once-learned lesson.
**How to apply:** Never write a {# #} comment that wraps to a second line — convert to {% comment %}. When reviewing templates, scan for {# followed by a newline before the closing #}. Treat a browser read-back (not the test suite) as the catch for rendered-junk regressions. Linked: [[django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow]].

Django view tests that assert on response.context[...] pass even when the template consuming that context is broken — they verify the view computed the right data, not that the user sees it. For any acceptance bullet that is observable HTML, assert on response.content.decode() / assertContains(response, ...), not response.context.

**Why:** Recurred across the kb-wz8m syndication epic — adversarial review flagged "hollow against template bugs" on both the board UI and Review-all; a test file closed carrying ~18 context-only assertions. The lesson was applied to newer tests but never recorded, so it re-surfaced per bead.
**How to apply:** When writing/reviewing a syndication or events view test whose acceptance is user-facing, grep the test for response.context[ — each is a candidate to pair with a .content/assertContains assertion. Context assertions are fine for non-rendered invariants (authz booleans, redirect targets); the trap is using them as a proxy for "the page shows X." Linked: [[django-multiline-hash-comment-renders-raw]].

`djlint --reformat` is NOT whitespace-only. It can change rendered output in ways invisible to BOTH `djlint --check` AND pytest: (1) collapsing a rendered separator " · " to bare "·" (literal text inside an element), (2) wrapping an href/attribute value across lines, injecting newlines INTO the attribute value.

**Why:** kb-33do.3 reformatted 18 templates. The implementer's diff-inspection self-review concluded "all whitespace-only, no semantic change" — WRONG on 2 of 18 (connections_list.html separator collapse; events/list.html sort-tab href line-wrap). A fresh-context adversarial review falsified that and found both. Same invisible-to-tests class as [[django-multiline-hash-comment-renders-raw]] and [[django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow]]: tooling-driven template change that marker-present assertions and the linter cannot see.

**How to apply:** Treat `djlint --reformat` as a behavioral change, not a format change — never self-certify a reformat diff as "whitespace-only." After any reformat: (1) lock rendered behavior with assertions on response.content/assertContains (NOT response.context) — see syndication/test_render_regressions.py; (2) for literal-text separators (" · ", " | "), prefer a filter ({{ x|join:" · " }}) so the separator is data, not reformat-fragile source; (3) fence attribute values djlint wants to wrap with single-line {# djlint:off #}; (4) fresh-context review the diff, not author self-inspection. Linked: [[django-multiline-hash-comment-renders-raw]], [[django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow]].

A DRY extraction that unifies a standalone-page render path AND an embedded/fragment render path into one shared template partial can silently carry context-specific behavior (an hx-target, an hx-push-url, a swap attribute, a base-layout assumption) into the context where it is wrong. The element renders identically in both contexts but only *behaves* correctly in one.

**Why:** kb-9f1h.3 extracted `_post_hub_body.html` / `_event_hub_body.html` shared by both the standalone composer full-page AND the in-studio HX fragment. The extraction pulled the in-shell-rewired cross-links (`hx-target="#studio-main"`, _post_hub_body.html:19 + fragments/post_syndication.html:17) into the standalone path. On a directly-loaded /syndication/posts/<pk>/ page (#studio-main absent — a real entry path: deep-link, refresh, typed URL), HTMX intercepts the click (hx-get -> preventDefault), the target is missing, fires htmx:targetError, and does nothing — the href fallback never runs. Silent UI no-op + ADR-008 D3 silent-fallback violation. Fixed in kb-9f1h.7 by threading a `studio_swap` context flag that gates swap-attrs vs plain href (and ?studio=1 to thread the board sub-fragment). The in-studio flow was green (kb-9f1h.5 composed read-back), so per-child AND composed read-back both passed — only the fresh-context parent re-verify, reasoning about the standalone context, caught it.

**How to apply:** When extracting a shared partial used by 2+ render contexts (standalone page vs HTMX/embedded fragment; full-page vs swapped-in), audit every behavioral attribute (hx-*, swap target, base-layout assumption, JS-init hook) for context-dependence. If an attribute is correct in only one context, gate it on a context flag passed by the includer — do not let the merge bake in one context's behavior. The standalone deep-link path is a documented entry path, not an edge case. Sibling of [[alpine-3-x-directives-mouseenter-click-class-x]] (DOM-present but inert; only a live browser in the right context surfaces it) and [[parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift]] (the net that caught this).

Editing a migration file that prod (or any long-lived DB) has ALREADY applied — squash-style, instead of adding a NEW migration — silently diverges that DB's real schema from the migration graph. The graph records the migration as applied, so Django never reconciles; the divergence is invisible until the first LATER migration runs real DDL/queries against the assumed-but-missing columns.

**Why:** kb-vixx (2026-06-03). syndication/0001_initial was edited in place across 3 commits during the kb-a4u epic (cb8a2ea create, e940abb platform-to-connection FK refront + new PlatformConnection table, 738fb72 added frozen_content to the CREATE TABLE). Prod applied an early 0001 on 2026-05-26; the later edits never reached prod's schema because 0001 was already recorded applied. Prod's syndication_platformprojection froze at the late-May shape (platform_id string, NO connection_id, NO frozen_content, NO platformconnection table) while the graph claimed 0001-0004 applied. 0005 was the first migration with real DDL/backfill to touch the table, raising ProgrammingError column generated_by/frozen_content does not exist, wedging the prod deploy init container for ~4 days. CI never caught it: fresh test DBs build from the current internally-consistent files, so test.yml migrate/check --deploy were green — only the real prod DB carried the divergence. Sibling of [[data-migration-backfill-default-regresses-prior-visibility]] and [[migration-introducing-unhandled-rows-lands-with-its-code-path]] (all green-on-fresh-DB, broken-on-real-prod); see also [[django-migrate-after-restore-from-old-snapshot-gotcha]].

**How to apply:** (1) NEVER edit a migration already applied to a long-lived environment — add a new migration. ADR-008 D1 permits squashing PRE-launch, but only when every live DB is wiped/rebuilt in lockstep; in-place edit + a prod that already ran the old version is the trap. (2) When a deploy migrate fails with column X does not exist but CI is green, suspect applied-migration divergence — compare prod ACTUAL schema (information_schema.columns) + django_migrations rows against the current files, do not just patch the failing op. (3) Idempotent ops (DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS + state_operations) patch a single drifted drop but cannot fix a SELECT against a missing column or a missing table — those need schema reconciliation. (4) When the drifted tables are EMPTY and nothing FKs into them (verify: grep cross-app migration deps + FK refs), the clean fix is rebuild: DROP the tables + DELETE FROM django_migrations WHERE app=X + re-migrate from current files. Confirm row counts are 0 first. (5) The deploy init container stderr is NOT in the GH Actions log by default (up -d only prints service init didnt complete successfully) — kb-vixx added an if:failure() log-dump step to deploy.yml; until such a step exists, ssh -i ~/.ssh/switch-berlin-deploy switch@switch.berlin then docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs init.

gh CLI 'gh secret set NAME --body -' DOES NOT read stdin — it sets the secret value to the literal string '-' (one hyphen). The pipe is silently discarded, exit code 0 makes it look successful, and gh secret list shows the secret as 'updated' with no value verification possible (GH API never returns secret values). To actually pipe stdin into a secret, use one of: (a) omit --body entirely — gh defaults to reading stdin; (b) --body-file - which explicitly reads stdin. Burned switch.berlin prod 2026-05-13 (kb-vb7): host-side agent set DATABASE_URL and SECRET_KEY each to literal '-', deploy.yml rendered DATABASE_URL=- into .env, Django crashed with dj_database_url.UnknownSchemeError, self-heal sed-without-n let the broken value through and ALTERed the postgres role with a garbage password literal. Two compounding bugs: (1) gh flag misuse, (2) plain 'sed s|p|r|' echoes input on no-match, so =garbage and -z guards never fire. Fix for sed: use 'sed -nE s|p|r|p' so output is empty on no-match. Always validate scheme prefix with a 'case' statement BEFORE running sed.

kind: procedural-lesson | scope: global | created: 2026-06-12

The /send-it -> /decompose -> /harness compose chain (and the leaf-path /harness quick recipe) is INVENTORY-FIRST: it reads .claude/harness.md fit profiles before authoring a bead's harness-target Signal. So a fit profile is the LOAD-BEARING piece that converts the chain from 'runs but cold-scans, may author a proxy signal' to 'authors the ground-truth signal' — and the adversarial-reviewer then grades that Signal for alignment (its #1 criterion). Adding a fit profile is therefore the highest-leverage substrate write for making agents self-verify: it changes what the verification-primitive chain will AUTHOR for that surface, not just what's documented.

**Why:** kb-t93r (2026-06-12). curl false-greened an Accept-gated OG-card bug; only driving real Telegram caught it. After fixing, the question was 'would updating harness.md make future agents self-verify by default?' Analysis: the workflow chain covers signal-AUTHORING — once the crawler-facing/Accept-gated fit profile exists, a future OG-card bead's /harness compose authors 'drive real Telegram via browser-automation', not 'curl returns og tags', and the reviewer flags a proxy. So lever (2) 'bake ground-truth into the harness target' IS structurally covered for any render/card work that runs the /harness step — GIVEN the fit profile exists (it didn't before; that's what made kb-t93r's verification cold-scan to curl).

Two residual leaks the chain does NOT close (both behavioral-floor, not substrate-fixable): (1) SKIP-THE-STEP — nothing forces the /harness consult; a leaf-sized fix (most bugs; kb-t93r was one) correctly skips /decompose and an agent can hand-roll a harness target without ever reading the fit profile. (2) RUN-AS-WRITTEN != AUTHORED — the harness-target Signal is a proxy GRADIENT, not an execution interlock; a bead can correctly say 'drive real Telegram' while the closer greens it with curl and calls it done (the exact kb-t93r execution failure). The harness skill already names this: 'Gradient, not proof; done = harness green AND acceptance met.'

**How to apply:** When you add/strengthen a harness.md fit profile, recognize you've changed what /harness compose AND /harness quick will AUTHOR for that surface (both are inventory-first) — that is the structural lever for self-verification, more than any exhortation. But it bites only if (a) the /harness step actually runs and (b) the authored signal is executed as written; those two are the behavioral floor that only a disposition norm closes (CLAUDE.md: 'before claiming a user-facing/external-rendered behavior verified, exercise the real client, not a proxy whose default request shape may differ'). Lever (2) authors the right signal; lever (3) makes the step run and the signal get executed. Complementary, not redundant. Sibling of [[curl-default-accept-dodges-content-negotiated-gate]]; the disposition-norm is the generic form.

kind: procedural-lesson (herdr dispatch hygiene, 2026-07-07). Amending a typed-but-unsent worker launch line in a herdr pane: kill-line keys are NOT trustworthy blind — Ctrl+U (herdr key syntax is 'Ctrl+X'; 'C-x' form is rejected with invalid_key) left the old wrapped command in the buffer and a second send-text APPENDED to it. Hetzner Storage Box API (Cloud) — quirks discovered while provisioning kb-eac (BX11). Key facts for any future session that touches Hetzner Storage Boxes:

- Host: api.hetzner.com (NOT api.hetzner.cloud — different host than the rest of Hetzner Cloud API). Same Bearer token (HETZNER_API_KEY) works for both.
- Robot panel was deprecated 2025-07-30; everything is API-managed now. Existing Robot-era boxes were migrated to Hetzner Console.
- POST /v1/storage_boxes payload shape (the docs are misleading — verified by trial):
  * 'ssh_keys' is TOP-LEVEL, array of OpenSSH-format public-key strings (NOT names of /v1/ssh_keys resources, despite Python SDK appearance). Got 'invalid input: must be a valid public key' when sending names.
  * 'labels' is TOP-LEVEL too (silently dropped if nested inside access_settings).
  * 'access_settings' on POST is silently ignored — must call POST /v1/storage_boxes/{id}/actions/update_access_settings post-create to flip ssh_enabled / reachable_externally / etc.
  * 'password' is required at create. Used only for Console UI / SMB / WebDAV; restic uses SSH-key auth.
- No public endpoint to add SSH keys to an EXISTING box. add_ssh_key/set_ssh_keys actions return 404. update_access_settings silently drops ssh_keys field. PUT /v1/storage_boxes/{id} only accepts name/description. If keys need to change → delete + recreate.
- SSH on port 23 (not 22). SFTP-only — no shell. Test from VPS: 'sftp -i ~/.ssh/<key> -P 23 -o BatchMode=yes -b /dev/null u<NNN>@u<NNN>.your-storagebox.de'.
- DNS for u<NNN>.your-storagebox.de takes ~30–60s to propagate to recursive resolvers after create (authoritative is instant via ns1.first-ns.de).
- Pricing as of 2026-05: BX11 €3.80 gross/€3.20 net per month at fsn1 (1 TB, no setup fee).
- Working create payload reference (jq+curl pattern with secret-isolated password):
  jq -n --arg pass "$PASS" --arg pubkey "$PUBKEY" '{location: "fsn1", name: "X", password: $pass, storage_box_type: "bx11", labels: {...}, ssh_keys: [$pubkey]}' | curl -X POST https://api.hetzner.com/v1/storage_boxes ...

On an HTMX autosave surface whose view filters to SUBMITTED keys (to avoid wiping untouched fields under partial POSTs), exposing a previously-hidden checkbox as editable SILENTLY breaks setting it back to False. An unchecked HTML checkbox is ABSENT from the POST body — so the submitted-keys filter treats "user unchecked it" identically to "field not in this partial form" and never writes False. The box can be turned on but never off; the bug is invisible in tests that only assert turning it ON.

**Why:** kb-y209.1 (2026-06-11, event composer field-parity). Moving is_free / sliding_scale / registration_required from hidden inputs to editable checkboxes in the `hx-swap="none"` autosave card (`_channel_editor.html`, filter at `syndication/views.py` ~374-377) collided with the submitted-keys wipe-guard the surface relies on for partial autosave POSTs. The guard is correct and load-bearing for text fields; checkboxes break its assumption that "absent key = untouched." Fix: emit a hidden companion input (`<input type="hidden" name="X" value="false">` placed BEFORE the checkbox `name="X"`) in the FULL form only, so an unchecked box still submits X=false while the partial-form wipe-protection stays intact for the text path. The tension (submitted-keys protection vs. checkbox-can-go-False) is real; the companion input is the resolution that keeps both.

**How to apply:** Before exposing any boolean/checkbox field as editable on an autosave surface that filters to submitted keys, ask "can the user set this back to False?" — by default no, because unchecked checkboxes do not POST. Add a hidden companion input with the same name and value="false" immediately before the checkbox (HTML last-value-wins gives checked->true, unchecked->false), scoped to the full form so the partial-POST wipe-guard is untouched. Test BOTH directions: check->persist True AND uncheck->persist False (the uncheck case is the one that silently fails); pair with the existing no-wipe-of-other-fields assertion (ADR-008 D3). Request-side sibling of [[htmx-swap-none-discards-returned-fragment-oob-only]] (same autosave surface / same submitted-keys filter, but the discarded leg there is the server RESPONSE; here it is the absent checkbox in the REQUEST).

kind: anti-pattern | scope: global | created: 2026-06-08

A Django view that returns a full rendered fragment as its HTTP response to an HTMX request whose triggering element carries hx-swap=none has its response body SILENTLY DISCARDED — HTMX honors 'none' and swaps nothing into the DOM. The server can compute the entirely correct new state (a dirty marker, a re-publish CTA, an updated badge) and it never reaches the page. The ONLY delivery that survives hx-swap=none is an out-of-band swap: markup carrying hx-swap-oob=true (or outerHTML:#id).

**Why:** kb-nexw.2 (2026-06-08, syndication composer, commit d5c2069). Editing the canonical of a PUBLISHED Switch listing surfaced no dirty/Re-publish marker. event_hub_edit computed the right dirty state and returned a full fragment — but the autosave form posts hx-swap=none (_channel_editor.html, the focus-preserving debounced-autosave pattern), so HTMX threw the whole response away. Body-form paths in the same surface already emitted state as hx-swap-oob; the EventForm autosave path returned-instead-of-OOB'd. Fix: emit _channel_dirty_oob.html as an OOB fragment. The focus-preservation requirement (hx-swap=none + debounced trigger) and the state-delivery requirement are in direct tension, and OOB is the only resolution.

**How to apply:** On any autosave-style form using hx-swap=none (debounced 'input changed delay:Nms', focus-preserving), the server CANNOT deliver any state change by returning a fragment — the response is discarded by design. Every piece of state the request mutates that the user must SEE (dirty markers, badges, CTAs, counts) must be emitted as hx-swap-oob markup. Audit: for each hx-swap=none form, confirm its view's response is OOB-only. The trap is invisible to a Django view test asserting on response.content — the OOB markup IS in the body and the test passes; the discard happens browser-side, so only a live browser read-back catches it. Sibling of [[optimistic-ui-flip-lies-under-shared-row-broadcast]] (which names OOB as the truthful-delivery remedy — this is the delivery-MECHANISM failure underneath it) and [[dry-partial-merge-collapses-render-contexts]]. Cross-ref [[django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow]] and .claude/harness.md Templates section.

scope: global

---
An implementer subagent's narration of WHAT IT DID is unreliable and can be flatly false — it may report work as pre-existing when its own diff proves it just wrote it (or claim it did work it didn't). The orchestrator must verify the git diff / actual artifacts, never accept the implementer's self-report of its actions as the basis for a verdict or close-reason.

**Why:** kb-9f1h.1's implementer reported "everything was already implemented when I started." The git diff (commit 0012342) showed it had just written the merge service, the context processor, the /studio/ route+view, AND 10 foundation tests. The orchestrator caught it by reading the diff (close_reason: "implementer mis-narrated as pre-existing; diff verified real") and stamped verdict:pass on the verified artifact, not the narration. Had it trusted the report, it might have skipped verification or mis-recorded provenance.

**How to apply:** After any implementer-subagent dispatch, run `git diff <pre-dispatch-sha>..HEAD` (or inspect changed files) before stamping a verdict or writing a close-reason — the diff is ground truth, the subagent's situational self-model is not. Execute-role mirror of [[adversarial-reviewer-verdict-line-despite-rule-2-prohibition]] (reviewer-subagent emits a prohibited verdict line under prose-habit); both are subagent-self-narration failure modes the orchestrator must independently check against artifacts.

kind: procedural-lesson | scope: global | created: 2026-06-06

A bead inherited from a prior session/epic carries a ROOT-CAUSE diagnosis (and often a file:line fix location) in its --design that was never re-confirmed against current code. Before walking such children, dispatch a fresh-context debugger to CONFIRM each root-cause hypothesis live, then rewrite the beads' --design/--acceptance against the confirmed root — do NOT execute against the inherited diagnosis.

**Why:** kb-kgza round 3 (2026-06-06). The orchestrator ran substrate-repair-before-execution: a debugger live-confirmed the 4 inherited beads' hypotheses, which caught two diagnosis errors that would have produced wrong/dead code. (1) kb-kgza.11's inherited note ('the publish view doesn't read selected_pk back') was flatly REFUTED — the server already reads+validates it (views.py:664-669, landed kb-shzi.2); acting on it would have added redundant dead reads. Closed NOT-A-BUG + regression-lock test (commit 84020df). (2) kb-kgza.13's inherited fix location was WRONG — the re-freeze gap lives in engine.py:105 (transition_status, the single status-writer), not services.py:1455 as the bead claimed; a services-only fix would have missed the adapter + mark_published paths (commit 84ea361). Both errors were invisible without a live repro.

**Why (cont., kb-v93q, 2026-06-07):** A /compound-DISCOVERED bead can be stale-on-ARRIVAL — not because its diagnosis decayed, but because its parent epic FINISHED the described work in a later child AFTER the retrospective filed the bead. kb-kgza round-3 /compound filed kb-v93q claiming three composer widgets still needed extracting; but kb-kgza.9 (commit f23072e) had ALREADY extracted all three into shared includes earlier in the same epic — the retrospective named them from the epic's DRY-posture --design, not from current state. /recall's load-bearing-surprise probe caught it before any re-extraction; residual real work was only the surface-wide regression guard (the bead's distinctive value). Generalizes the rule beyond hand-off beads: ANY discovered/inherited bead's premise is a HYPOTHESIS — re-verify it against current HEAD at pickup, especially a /compound-discovered child whose siblings kept shipping after it was filed.

**How to apply:** For any inherited/hand-off bead whose --design asserts a root cause or fix location, treat that as a HYPOTHESIS, not a fact. Before first execution dispatch on the epic, dispatch one fresh-context debugger to (a) live-repro each claimed symptom, (b) confirm or refute the stated root, (c) confirm the fix LOCATION (single chokepoint vs scattered). Rewrite --design/--acceptance against confirmed roots; some beads may resolve to NOT-A-BUG (close + regression-lock so the refuted diagnosis can't silently regress). For a /compound-discovered bead, the pickup re-verify is cheap (/recall load-bearing-surprise probe / a grep for the artifact the bead says is missing) and must run BEFORE sinking in — a discovered bead's premise reflects the substrate at filing time, which its own younger epic-siblings may have already invalidated. Pre-dispatch counterpart to [[parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift]] (post-close net) and [[implementer-subagent-self-report-unreliable-verify-diff]] (verify what was done, not what was claimed).

Anti-pattern (global, 2026-06-04): An inline hand-copy of a shared template partial (kept 'in sync by comment', not by {% include %}) silently drifts and re-introduces the exact bug the partial was the single source of truth for. Each partial fix must be manually mirrored into every inline twin — and the mirror is forgotten, so the twin lags one fix behind.

Why: kb-shzi (2026-06-04, syndication composer). The inline Switch-listing sync bar (event_syndication.html ~156-235) is a hand-copy of the three-state badge whose single source is _sync_bar.html — it even carries a 'must match _sync_bar.html' comment. That manual-sync contract broke twice at the SAME seam: (1) kb-lprn — inline copy missing states (ii)/(iii) -> 2-branch badge oscillation; expanded to 3-branch to match. (2) kb-shzi.6 — inline copy's forms missing the selected_pk hidden input _sync_bar.html already had -> re-introduced the tab-jump-to-leftmost bug kb-shzi.2 thought fixed. Both times the fix landed in the partial not the twin; both times only fresh-context parent re-verify caught the lag. Same root at form level: kb-shzi.2 threaded selected_pk into 3 forms, kb-shzi.6 had to thread 13 — the other 10 lagged.

How to apply: When fixing a bug in a shared partial, grep for inline copies of that widget BEFORE closing — a 'must match X' comment is the tell that an un-DRYed twin exists. Either (preferred) replace the inline copy with an include so there is structurally one source, or if the inline copy must stay (wraps platform-specific structure like the Switch event-edit form) treat every partial fix as a required two-site edit AND add a content test asserting the twin carries the same load-bearing markers (state-branch count, hidden inputs) as the partial. A comment is not a sync mechanism. Sibling of dry-partial-merge-collapses-render-contexts and parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift.

Why (cont., kb-kgza round 3, 2026-06-06): Recurred again at the same composer seam. (a) FAILURE arm: kb-kgza.12 form-scoped the document-scoped `from:` autosave triggers in _channel_editor.html but the identical trigger one file over in post_syndication.html:239 lagged — caught only at parent re-verify (kb-kgza.14, commit 9b4cdf3). (b) SUCCESS arm: the generic dirty-banner copy was hand-twinned at FIVE sites; kb-kgza.10 took the preferred exit — extracted one _dirty_label.html snippet used at all five (commit 24defa8), so no twin can drift. Confirms the rule: prefer structural single-source (include) over the two-site-edit-plus-content-test arm. And when the manual-mirror arm is unavoidable, the standing regression guard must be SURFACE-WIDE (directory/codebase grep), not per-file — a per-file guard lags exactly like the twin (see .claude/harness.md §Templates: "class-of-bug regression guard must scan the whole surface").

scope: workspace
created: 2026-05-22
---

Any login-wall / vouching-gate middleware that 302s anonymous requests to a login page MUST allow-list /static/ (and /media/ if applicable) BEFORE the redirect logic, otherwise the login page itself renders unstyled — the redirect catches CSS requests on the way to rendering the login form.

**Why:** accounts/middleware.py:LoginWallMiddleware.ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES (commit 15d5614) initially omitted /static/. Anonymous request to /accounts/signup/ rendered HTML correctly, but anonymous follow-up requests for /static/dist/assets/app-*.css 302'd to /accounts/login/ (HTML redirect — Content-Type text/html), the browser dropped it as not-CSS, and the page rendered unstyled. Invisible to authenticated users; invisible to anyone with cached statics.

**How to apply:** (1) Audit any middleware that does return redirect(login_url) on anonymous: confirm /static/, /media/, /favicon.ico, /robots.txt are in its always-public allowlist BEFORE that branch fires. (2) Add an integration test that requests a known static asset URL as AnonymousUser and asserts 200 text/css (or whatever MIME), NOT a 302 to login. accounts/tests.py got such a test in commit 15d5614 — replicate the shape for any new login-wall-style middleware. (3) When you add a NEW LOGIN_REQUIRED-style middleware, the prefix allowlist is the first thing to populate, not an afterthought.

maplibre-gl 5.x removed the callback signature from GeoJSONSource.getClusterLeaves(clusterId, limit, offset, cb) and getClusterExpansionZoom(clusterId, cb). In 5.x these methods now ONLY return a Promise — if you pass a callback as the trailing argument, it is silently ignored, no error is thrown, the returned Promise is discarded, and nothing visibly happens. Discovered live on switch.berlin/events/ via browser-automation (kb-6ow, 2026-05-11): the kb-k7a cluster-popup fix used the callback variant (static/js/events/map.js lines 194 and 237) and silently no-ops on prod — clicking the IKSK cluster neither opens the events-list popup nor zooms to expand. Fix: await src.getClusterLeaves(cid, pc, 0).then(...) and same for getClusterExpansionZoom. Same pattern as the alpine-3-x-directives lesson: code review can't catch the silent-API-drop; only live browser-automation verification can. When bumping a library major version, grep the codebase for every method the upgrade notes mention and verify in a running browser, not in unit tests.

kind: procedural-lesson | scope: global | created: 2026-06-02

A data migration that introduces rows a not-yet-written code path cannot safely handle (e.g. a generalized FK whose new null-branch existing services read un-guarded) must land in the SAME unit as the code that makes those rows safe — never in an earlier, independently-shipped child.

Why: kb-q4u9 first decomposed schema-generalize + data-backfill into one child (kb-q4u9.1). Adversarial review caught that minting post-owned ContentVersion rows (event=null) while every service still reads content_version.event un-None-guarded leaves a RED intermediate state between that child closing and the service-rewrite child landing — a per-bead-green child that breaks the suite the moment its own migration runs against live code. Fix: split into schema-only child A (no post rows exist after A, all event-path code stays green, A independently shippable) + data-backfill child B landing atomically with the publishable-scoped service rewrite.

How to apply: When /decompose splits a schema generalization from its data backfill, test each proposed child for independent-greenness — does the earlier child's migration introduce a row shape that surviving (not-yet-rewritten) code reads without a guard? If yes, the backfill is NOT independently shippable: fold it into the child that rewrites the readers, or keep the new branch unreachable (no rows) until the readers land. Discriminating question: 'after this child closes, does any un-rewritten code path read a field this child's migration just made null/divergent?'

kind: anti-pattern | scope: workspace | created: 2026-06-02

A fully-green test suite does NOT validate a dependency major/minor-version bump when the dependency is mocked at the test boundary. The mock furnishes whatever attribute/kwarg the old code used, so removed/renamed APIs pass silently.

**Why:** kb-z2ly bumped pydantic-ai 1.84->1.105 to clear a CVE. The implementer ran `uv run pytest` (1991 passed) and concluded "no code change needed." A fresh-context adversarial review against the ACTUALLY-INSTALLED library source caught two hard runtime breaks the mock hid: `Agent(result_type=...)` was removed (now `output_type=`, raises UserError) and `AgentRunResult.data` was removed (now `.output`, raises AttributeError). The ingestion tests mock `ingestion.extraction.Agent`, so `mock_result.data` and the constructor call never touched the real 1.105 API — green CI was a false negative.

**How to apply:** When bumping a dependency across more than a patch, (1) find its real usage sites and cross-check every API call against the installed package source in .venv (not memory, not the mock); (2) verify with a real-library smoke check that needs no network — e.g. construct the object with the new kwargs in `uv run python -c "..."` to prove the signature is accepted; (3) de-blind the mocks so they mirror the real current API (rename `mock_result.data`->`.output`), so the test class stops being structurally blind to this break going forward. Pairs with [[ci-green-means-full-ci-job-set-not-pytest-proxy]] — both are "the green signal you trusted didn't cover what you assumed."

A self-contained nested sub-project (own pyproject/.venv/uv.lock, e.g. tools/switch-cli) silently breaks the PARENT repo's bare `uv run pytest` at COLLECTION time — ModuleNotFoundError for the sub-project's package (not installed in the root env) before any test runs. Root pytest with no testpaths and no --ignore descends into it.

**Why:** kb-33do.6 — CI runs bare `uv run pytest` (.github/workflows/test.yml:117). tools/switch-cli tests errored at collection with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'switch_cli'", a CI-red cause invisible until the exact CI command ran, pre-existing since the sub-project landed (bbd9bdc). Local --ignore=tools runs had masked it.

**How to apply:** When adding a nested standalone sub-project, immediately add --ignore=<dir> to the root [tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts (config-layer fix, ADR-008 D1 — do NOT install the sub-package into the root env). Verify with bare `uv run pytest --collect-only` (the CI command, not a local --ignore'd invocation). Coverage consequence: the excluded sub-project's tests then DON'T run in main CI; if they need coverage, give them their own CI job.

kind: anti-pattern
scope: global
created: 2026-05-26
---

Numeric thresholds in acceptance criteria (--design or --acceptance) introduce recipe-leak even when paired with "this is a minimum, not a quota" disclaimer. The disclaimer renders the author's intent; the threshold renders the system's behavior to downstream readers, implementers, and reviewers. The number wins.

**Why:** kb-a4u R1 fold-in (response to brainstorm-skill F6 finding) introduced "friction observations captured (≥3)" into the Dogfooding criterion, paired with the disclaimer "Three is the minimum acceptance bar; not a quota." R2 F1 caught the contradiction: the gate exists in text whether or not the prose disclaims it, and downstream readers pattern-match on the number, not the disclaimer. R2 reframe replaced both with "sufficient to seed v0.5 design — orchestrator judgment, not a quota" — moving the gate from arithmetic to judgment.

**How to apply:** When folding an adversarial-review finding that names "more/at least N" or "X-or-more" of anything (friction observations, test cases, ADR-citations, canonical_refs entries), pause: does the gate need to be a number? If you're about to write a number followed by a "not a quota" disclaimer, you've identified the leak — replace the number with the judgment criterion the disclaimer was trying to express. Companion to [[adr-clause-hallucination-by-reviewers]] (reviewer-side ADR placement leak) and [[adr-enum-vocabulary-drift-invisible-per-bead]] (implementer-side enum leak); this entry is the author-side / fold-in-side numeric leak. Three mirror-instances of the same general pattern: a structured artifact (clause-id, enum-value, count-threshold) reads locally coherent but introduces drift the disclaimer cannot undo.

kind: anti-pattern
scope: global
created: 2026-06-04
---

An optimistic client-side state flip (e.g. an Alpine `.once` flag flipping a badge to "Custom" on first keystroke) is only truthful in states where the edit actually DETACHES the edited row from its source. In a canonical-shared / single-row-broadcast state — where several channels point at ONE shared row and editing BROADCASTS to all sharers rather than forking — the optimistic flip LIES: it flashes the detached label, then snaps back on the next server render because no detach happened.

**Why:** kb-ide0.5 / kb-lprn (2026-06-04, syndication composer). The "Custom" badge was to flip instantly on detach-on-edit. In the event-composer state (own ContentVersion + sync_source set), editing clears sync_source → genuinely detaches → optimistic flip correct. But in the post/event canonical-shared state (promotion channels share one canonical ContentVersion per ADR-016 D2), editing broadcasts to all sharers — it does NOT detach — so the optimistic "Custom" badge flashed then reverted. A first naive .once-flag attempt was stashed for exactly this reason. The truthful states and the lying states look identical at the markup level; the difference is the row-sharing semantics underneath.

**How to apply:** Before adding an optimistic UI flip on a state transition, ask "does this edit fork/detach the underlying row, or broadcast to a shared row?" (1) Optimistic flip is only safe on states where the edit detaches. (2) For shared-row-broadcast states, do NOT flip optimistically — drive the indicator from the server response (OOB swap / small hx-swap target returning the authoritative state) so the badge can never out-run the truth. (3) When one widget renders across BOTH detach and broadcast states (same template, different data), a blanket optimistic flag is wrong for half the states — make the flip state-aware or server-driven, never a context-blind .once. Linked: [[alpine-3-x-directives-mouseenter-click-class-x]], [[django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow]].

kind: anti-pattern
scope: global
created: 2026-06-11
---
A progressive/composer-first redesign that re-homes a flow into a new curated surface can leave the OLD full-capability surface intact in code but UNREACHABLE — its only entry link lives in a fragment the new shell never composes. "Parity exists in code but is undiscoverable." The capability is present, fully tested in isolation, and a feature gap is reported against it — because no live path reaches it. The orphaned surface also masks the real gap: a reviewer greps, finds the full form, and wrongly concludes "parity already shipped."

**Why:** kb-y209 (2026-06-11, event edit/hub field-parity). The composer-first hub (`_event_hub_body.html` -> `event_syndication`) became the live event-EDIT surface, rendering 9 editable fields + 16 hidden + cover omitted. A full 26-field edit page (`event_edit.html` -> `_event_form_fields.html`, route `event-edit`) ALREADY EXISTED with complete parity — but its only link lived in the dormant `event_facts` fragment, which the live hub never composes. So the user hit "can't set cover / can't edit 16 fields" against a feature that was 100% built one orphaned route away. The fix was NOT reviving the stranded page (explicitly rejected) but bringing the live composer to parity; the stranded page stayed dead. A naive "does parity exist?" grep would have answered yes and closed the bug as not-a-bug.

**How to apply:** After any composer-first / progressive-disclosure redesign that re-homes an edit/create flow, audit the OLD surface: is it still routed, and is its route reachable from the live shell (grep the new shell's composed includes for the old route's url-name / link)? Two failure modes: (1) the old surface is dead weight that confuses future readers into thinking a capability ships when no live path reaches it — delete it (ADR-008 D1, no compat shims) or explicitly re-link it; (2) when triaging a "feature X is missing" report, do NOT stop at "the code for X exists" — confirm a LIVE user path reaches it, because an orphaned-but-complete surface reads as present to a grep and absent to the user. Sibling of [[cheap-foresight-seam-shipped-dead-defeats-its-own-intent]] (a behavioral seam with no live caller; this is a whole UI surface with no live entry) and [[ui-label-names-mechanism-not-implemented]] (the gap-between-code-and-user-reality family). Catch leg: only a live browser walk of the new shell — or a route-reachability grep — surfaces it; isolation tests on the orphaned surface stay green.
