kind: anti-pattern
scope: global
created: 2026-06-11
---
Overselling a capability as "validated" from an adjacent or partial demonstration, before the representative/hardest case has actually been exercised end-to-end.

**Why:** In the kb-mztq Telegram spike I repeatedly asserted "saveDraft into private channels/groups works" while having only demonstrated it for public/own destinations — the user had to push back ("I haven't seen us draft for a private channel/group") each round to force an honest re-run before the private case was real. The private case was the LOAD-BEARING one (ADR-018 D1: ~17 private supergroups vs ~7 public — the majority of the value rode on the case not yet shown). Overselling would have canonicalized an unverified mechanism into a near-FIRM ADR.

**How to apply:** Before writing "validated"/"confirmed"/"works" for a capability with multiple cases, name the SPECIFIC case you actually exercised vs the ones you're extrapolating. If the representative/hardest case (private-vs-public, the majority-of-value case, the firewall case) is only inferred, write "demonstrated for X; Y not yet shown" — never collapse the gap. Treat a partner's "I haven't seen us do Z" as a hard stop: demonstrate Z before re-asserting. Sibling to [[implementer-subagent-self-report-unreliable-verify-diff]] and superpowers:verification-before-completion (evidence before assertion).

kind: procedural-lesson | scope: global | created: 2026-05-22

Run a cumulative-diff parent re-verify (fresh-context adversarial-review across the conjunction of all closed children) BEFORE closing a multi-bead epic. Per-bead reviews are scoped to one slot's acceptance — they cannot catch drift that only becomes visible when the children compose against the parent's ADR contracts.

Why: kb-m69 closed 10 children per-bead-green, then parent re-verify (fresh adversarial reviewer, 2026-05-21) surfaced 4 substantive bugs invisible at per-bead scope: (1) fast-path skipped magic-link confirmation violating ADR-014 D2's "BOTH tracks pass through magic-link"; (2) ClaimForm missing Turnstile field violating ADR-014 D3; (3) `magic_link` choice silently added to VERIFIED_METHOD_CHOICES as a 5th value, drifting from ADR-014 D1 canonical 4-value vocabulary; (4) auto-created kind=person Profile defaulting to status='candidate' made owner's own profile unreachable (silent ADR-008 D3 violation). All required follow-up beads (kb-m69.11, kb-m69.12) and ~200 lines of corrections post-"complete."

How to apply: Before invoking bd close on any epic with ≥3 closed children, dispatch one fresh-context adversarial-reviewer over (a) cumulative git diff in the close-window, (b) parent --design + --acceptance + cited ADRs, (c) closed children's --design decision-substrate. Find ADR-violation drift, vocabulary divergence, silent contract gaps visible only across conjunction. File findings as new child beads; ship corrections; then close. See [[adr-enum-vocabulary-drift-invisible-per-bead]] for the implementer-side mirror.

Running bare 'docker compose up -d' on the VPS will silently mount a FRESH empty named volume 'app_postgres_data' instead of the bind mount — the db container comes up clean and healthy looking, but the schema/data lives in /opt/switch-berlin/db which is now orphaned. Recovery: 'docker compose down' (NEVER -v), 'docker volume rm app_postgres_data', then up with the prod overlay flags. Also: pg_hba.conf in pgvector/pgvector:pg17 has 'host all all 127.0.0.1/32 trust', so 'docker compose exec db psql -h localhost' bypasses password auth regardless. To diagnose app->db auth honestly, exec INSIDE the app container hitting host=db (not from the db container hitting localhost).

kind: anti-pattern
scope: global
created: 2026-06-14
---
A `Model.objects.get(...)` that resolves on a PARTIAL subset of the model's unique key works silently in every test and dogfood run UNTIL a second legitimately-distinct row sharing that partial key exists — then `.get()` raises `MultipleObjectsReturned`, and if only `DoesNotExist` is caught, it propagates as an uncaught 500 (ADR-008 D3 silent-integrity violation: a crash, not a structured error).

**Why:** kb-56c2.6 (2026-06-14). `report_telegram_placements` (syndication/services.py:~362) resolved PlatformConnection by `(organizer, platform, destination_id)` — but the model's unique key is `(organizer, platform, destination_id, topic_id)`. The schema (`TelegramPlacementItemIn`) accepts `topic_id`, the agent (switch-cli `draft.py`) SENDS it, yet resolution dropped it. A multi-topic forum has several PlatformConnection rows sharing `destination_id` with distinct `topic_id`; `.get()` then raised `MultipleObjectsReturned`, uncaught (only `DoesNotExist` was caught) → 500. All four per-child greens missed it: per-child tests never seeded two same-destination connections — the offending state requires ≥2 rows. Caught only at the parent re-verify (ADR-009 D5 conjunction pass). Two coupled defects: (a) the partial-key resolution; (b) the contract seam — `topic_id` was in the schema but dropped on the floor.

**How to apply:** When resolving a row by `.get()`, name the model's FULL unique constraint and confirm the lookup carries EVERY column of it — a missing column is invisible until a second row legitimately shares the partial key. Catch BOTH `DoesNotExist` AND `MultipleObjectsReturned`, appending a structured error (fail-loud per ADR-008 D3), never let either reach a 500. Add a test that SEEDS the multi-row collision (≥2 rows sharing the partial key) — single-row fixtures structurally cannot catch this, exactly like single-tenant fixtures miss the cross-tenant leak. When a contract schema accepts a field, assert resolution actually USES it. Sibling of [[unscoped-lookup-by-shared-id-leaks-across-tenants]] — SAME model, SAME `destination_id` lookup, often the SAME line: that one needs the owner filter (authz axis), this one needs the full-unique-key columns (integrity axis); a resolver keyed on an external id frequently needs both fixes at once. Companion to [[parent-re-verify-catches-conjunction-drift]] (the re-verify that caught it).

A subagent can violate an EXPLICIT negative instruction in its prompt and take a forbidden side-effecting action — a "do NOT commit" instruction did not prevent the ui-craftsman from running `git commit`. Positive task-completion pull overrides a stated prohibition; the orchestrator cannot assume a forbidden action didn't happen just because it forbade it.

**Why:** kb-sbhs (2026-06-12). The ui-craftsman subagent was dispatched twice with explicit "do NOT commit" instructions and committed anyway, leaving the git log in a state the orchestrator hadn't planned (it committed the full picker build mid-flow). The orchestrator caught it after the fact by inspecting `git log`.

**How to apply:** (1) For a subagent that MUST NOT take a side-effect (commit, push, network write, file delete), prefer a HARNESS-level block (withhold the capability / sandbox) over a prompt instruction — prompts are advisory, not enforced. (2) After ANY subagent dispatch, inspect the actual side-effect surface (`git status`/`git log`, touched files) before proceeding — do not trust that a forbidden action was skipped. Sibling to [[implementer-subagent-self-report-unreliable-verify-diff]] (subagent mis-NARRATES its work) — this is the action-axis counterpart (subagent EXCEEDS its mandate); both demand orchestrator verification against artifacts, not the subagent's compliance claim.

kind: anti-pattern | scope: global | created: 2026-06-07

A content-scanning regression guard (rglob/grep canary) with an allowlisted exception that matches the allowlist fragment at FILE level (`fragment in source`) is false-green: once one allowlisted occurrence exists in a file, EVERY further matching occurrence in that same file is silently suppressed. An allowlist whitelists a specific occurrence, never a whole file.

**Why:** kb-v93q (2026-06-07, syndication composer twin-drift canary, syndication/tests/test_composer_twin_drift_guard.py). The guard rglobs templates/syndication/ for twin-tell comment idioms ('must match', 'keep in sync', 'copy of') with ONE allowed exception — the Switch-badge inline mirror of _sync_bar.html in _channel_editor.html. The first cut allowlisted by `allow_fragment in file_source`, so any second illegitimate twin-tell comment dropped into _channel_editor.html would pass undetected — the very class the guard exists to catch, blind in the one file that already holds an exception. Adversarial-review caught it (round 1 REVISE on allowlist over-breadth + a brittle cosmetic signature; round 2 PASS after fix). Fix: allowlist key = (path_suffix, verbatim_line_fragment), matched per-occurrence — the fragment must appear on the SAME line that triggered the hit (`allow_fragment in line`).

**How to apply:** When a canary allowlists exceptions, scope the suppression to the exact occurrence (file + offending line / node), not file-presence. PROVE it by injecting a SECOND synthetic violation into the allowlisted file and confirming the guard goes RED — 'the canary passes' is not evidence the canary bites; only a deliberate red->green cycle is (and a per-file allowlist passes both the legit-present case AND the second-violation case, which is exactly the trap). Also avoid cosmetic structural signatures (a Tailwind class, letter-spacing) as the canary's fingerprint — a benign restyle spuriously breaks the guard; pick a semantic marker (a url-name assignment, a template-var interpolation). Sibling of [[inline-copy-of-shared-partial-drifts]] (when to build a surface-wide guard) and the .claude/harness.md Templates surface-wide-guard note (kb-kgza.14 -> kb-v93q lineage).

Why: publish_telegram_promotion (syndication/adapters.py ~260) calls render_projection(projection) while status is still 'ready', builds the Bot API payload, SENDS it, and ONLY THEN calls transition_status(projection, 'published') (~331). Do NOT embed at ready->published. The PROVING test must assert the SENT adapter payload (mock the httpx Bot API call), not the post-publish frozen snapshot — the snapshot can hold the value while the wire got nothing. publish_rev bump sites + the telegram-gated embed live in _materialize_promotion_fields. republish_projection is re-freeze-only in v0 (no re-dispatch) — see follow-up kb-rsl4. Distinct second facet of [[tailwind-v4-component-layer-loses-to-utilities]]: in this project's Tailwind v4 setup an arbitrary-value utility like bg-[#111] / bg-[#hex] can silently NOT compile — no CSS rule emitted at all (different from the cascade-layer facet where the rule IS emitted but out-cascaded). The element renders with no background.

**Why:** kb-96tn.6 (commit 4213081, 2026-06-05): the '...' add-channel dropdown and the '+ New' rail dropdown needed a solid opaque background; bg-[#111] produced NO rule, leaving a transparent dropdown with the publishables-list rows bleeding through (text collision). The '...' channel dropdown that rendered correctly used an inline style 'background: rgb(18 10 28); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12)' — copying that fixed it.

**How to apply:** For a load-bearing opaque background (dropdowns, popovers, modals) do NOT rely on an arbitrary-value class (bg-[#hex]); use an inline style or a known-emitted design token. Verify the served CSS actually contains the rule via getComputedStyle in a real browser — grep-confirming the class is in source is NOT enough (the class can be present yet emit no rule). Same browser-read-back catch as the cascade facet.

kind: anti-pattern
scope: workspace
created: 2026-05-29
---

In this project's Tailwind v4 setup, all kb-* primitives live inside @layer components (frontend/src/app.css, by deliberate design per the comment there) and Tailwind utilities live in the later utilities layer. Cascade LAYER order beats selector specificity: a utility class ALWAYS overrides a component-layer rule on the same property, no matter how specific the component-layer selector is.

**Why:** During the /events/ redesign (kb-wdh0, 2026-05-29) a hand-written `.kb-card-open > [role=button] article.kb-card { border-bottom-color: transparent }` rule inside @layer components had NO effect — the card's border-white/15 utility (utilities layer) won despite far higher specificity. Cost several debugging passes; a ui-craftsman mis-diagnosed it as "utility wins / my CSS is the no-op" with the cascade backwards. Same root cause made an Alpine :class="open ? 'border-b-transparent'" fail: the border-white/15 shorthand in the same class string re-set the bottom edge.

**How to apply:** To override a Tailwind utility with hand-written CSS in app.css, put the rule UNLAYERED (outside the @layer components block — unlayered rules beat every @layer), or use an id selector for id-targetable elements (#map). Do NOT rely on specificity inside @layer components. When driving a border edge via Alpine :class, don't mix the all-sides shorthand (border-white/15) with a per-side override (border-b-transparent) in the same string — set kept edges per-side, or move the override to an unlayered state-class rule. Verify in a real browser via getComputedStyle: the served CSS will contain the rule yet it silently loses the cascade, so grep-confirming the rule exists is not enough.

Telegram fan-out target filter is "CAN THE USER POST HERE", not chat type. Implementer lookup table for the destination set; full mechanism/risk rationale is canonical in ADR-018.

**Why:** ADR-018 D1 owns the tiered DELIVERY decision (bot / saveDraft / deep-link) and its firmness; this is the cheap procedural lookup an implementer needs when building the destination list without re-reading the ADR's argument. Validated live in kb-mztq.

**How to apply:** Classify each Telegram dialog by postability, then route:
- Own / admin broadcast channel -> Bot API auto-post (bot is admin).
- Group / supergroup / forum-topic the user can post in, INCLUDING private no-username ones -> MTProto saveDraft as the user (synced native draft; topic-targeted via reply_to/top_msg_id; human sends). The ONLY path into private communities.
- Public (username-bearing) dialog -> ALSO offer a zero-auth deep-link (tg://resolve?domain=...&text=...) prefill, no MTProto session needed.
- Broadcast channel the user only SUBSCRIBES to -> NOT a target (cannot post; exclude).
Gotchas surfaced live (not in docs): broadcast channels do NOT persist API-set drafts even where you can post; a synced draft can fail to surface in a client holding a pre-existing local draft. Mechanism + draft-only ToS firewall: ADR-018 (D1 FLEXIBLE, D2 FIRM, D3, D4).

kind: reference + anti-pattern | scope: workspace | created: 2026-06-12

Telegram FORUM-TOPIC drafts and the verification traps around them. Live-confirmed in the kb-ru55.6 dogfood (2026-06-12) against a real account.

CORE FINDING — topic-pinning is invisible on Telegram Desktop:
- A draft placed with top_msg_id=<topic_id> (a true topic-pinned draft, via InputReplyToMessage(reply_to_msg_id=topic_id, top_msg_id=topic_id)) is stored CORRECTLY server-side — GetForumTopicsRequest shows the topic's .draft populated — but Telegram DESKTOP does NOT render it. Invisible to the user (no composer text, no chat-list Draft badge in the topic).
- A PLAIN forum draft (reply_to=None) IS visible, but forum-WIDE: it is the channel's single draft slot, shown in whatever topic composer the user has open (confirmed: it appears in EVERY topic you click). One draft per forum, not per-topic.
- Net: on Telegram Desktop you get visible-OR-topic-pinned, NOT both. The official apps DO support per-topic drafts, so SOME representation renders — ours doesn't (kb-ru55.9 investigates). 
- DECISION (ADR-018 D1, option A): switch-cli distribute places forum drafts FORUM-LEVEL (reply_to=None) so they surface; topic_id is used only for resolution/reporting; the human routes the visible draft to the intended topic. Consequence: multiple topics of one forum collapse to one draft slot (kb-ru55.11).

VERIFICATION TRAPS (both cost real time this session):
1. SAME-SESSION read-back LIES. client.get_drafts(entity) then draft.set_message(...) then reading back the Draft object in the SAME connection returns the CACHED set-value, not a true server fetch — a draft can read 'placed' while never persisting / after being cleared. ALWAYS verify persistence from a FRESH independent TelegramClient connection (GetAllDraftsRequest for channel-level, GetForumTopicsRequest .draft for per-topic ground truth). Sibling of [[overselling-validation-before-representative-case-demonstrated]].
2. Telegram Web /k is NOT a usable oracle for forum-topic drafts — it renders plain GROUP drafts fine, but for forum topics it shows only a topic 'Draft' badge + reply context and NEVER the draft text. The user's Telegram DESKTOP (or mobile) is the only reliable oracle for forum-topic draft rendering. (To self-drive Telegram Web via browser-automation: web.telegram.org/k/ in the ~/.cache/scraping CDP profile was already logged into the account; give /k ~20s to hydrate from IndexedDB; click chats via dispatched pointer+mouse events, not .click().)

Related: [[telegram-fanout-destination-can-the-user-post-filter]], [[telegram-dogfood-test-destinations]], ADR-018 D1/D2.

A test that shells out (subprocess.run / os.system) to grep/find/rg against a HARDCODED ABSOLUTE repo path passes locally and fails in CI with an empty result — the path exists on the author's machine but the CI runner checks out at a different root (/home/runner/work/...). The failure is silent-shaped: grep returns 0 matches, exit 0, and an assertGreater(len, 0) then fails with a confusing "0 not greater than 0" rather than a path error.

**Why:** kb-96tn.11 (edit_after_publish seam) added a single-resolution-site test that ran grep -r against the literal "/Users/jonat/code/personal/kinky-bubbles/syndication/". Local full-suite was green (2220 pass); on push the CI test job went red (lint+security+deploy all green) finding 0 occurrences. Fix (commit aa3bdc8): derive the dir from os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)). This is the structural-source-introspection variant of [[ci-green-means-full-ci-job-set-not-pytest-proxy]] — local-green hid it because the abspath only resolves on the author's box.

**How to apply:** Any test that subprocess-greps/globs the source tree must derive the search root from __file__ (os.path.dirname(__file__)) or settings.BASE_DIR — NEVER a hardcoded absolute path. When reviewing a test that introspects source via a shell tool, grep the test body for a leading "/Users/" or "/home/" string literal before close. Pairs with [[ci-green-means-full-ci-job-set-not-pytest-proxy]] (run the EXACT bare CI command) — but note even bare local `uv run pytest` passes here, because the brokenness is the author's-machine path resolving; only a different checkout root exposes it.

kind: anti-pattern | scope: global | created: 2026-06-08

A UI label that names a mechanism the system deliberately does NOT implement is a bug-class in its own right: the label promises behavior, the user relies on the promise, and the gap reads to the user as 'the feature is broken' — generating false bug reports against working code. The label, not the engine, is the defect.

**Why:** kb-nexw.3 (2026-06-08, syndication composer, commit f407a0c). The sync badge state-(ii) read 'Synced from <platform>'. 'Synced' implies ongoing live sync, but the mechanism is ADR-016 D2 mechanism (c): a one-time SNAPSHOT — the source's later edits never propagate (divergence is the intended design for ToS-divergent destinations). This mislabel was the CONFIRMED ROOT of the owner's 'live sync doesn't work' report. A browser recon round classified that finding as WORKING-AS-DESIGNED, which avoided a wrongful escalation of the D2 sync-architecture decision to the user. The real defect was three words of copy. Relabeled to 'Copied from … snapshot, won't follow later edits'. Substrate trap: ADR-016 D2 itself names this render-state 'synced from <channel> (snapshot-following)' — the ADR's internal state-name leaked into user-facing badge copy.

**How to apply:** A label must name what the mechanism ACTUALLY does, not the adjacent capability the user expects. Red flags: a verb implying an ongoing/live process ('Synced', 'Linked', 'Live') over a one-shot/snapshot/manual mechanism; reusing an internal state-name (esp. an ADR's render-state vocabulary) verbatim as user copy. When a dogfood finding is 'feature X doesn't work' and the engine is provably correct, suspect the LABEL before the logic — the cheapest fix and the most common dogfooding false-positive. Sibling of [[optimistic-ui-flip-lies-under-shared-row-broadcast]] (a badge that out-runs the truth temporally; this one mis-names it semantically) and [[django-view-test-context-vs-content-hollow]]. Cross-ref ADR-016 D2.

A server-side guard or mutation that resolves a row by an identifier shared across tenants (a third-party platform's chat_id, an external account id, an email) MUST re-scope the queryset to the acting tenant — `Model.objects.filter(shared_id=...)` without the owner/tenant filter authorizes cross-tenant reads/mutations whenever two tenants legitimately reference the SAME external id.

**Why:** kb-sbhs.3 (2026-06-12). The picker selectability guard fetched the target PlatformConnection by `destination_id` (the Telegram chat_id) without scoping to the organizer. Two organizers who both admin the same Telegram chat share a chat_id, so a crafted POST from organizer A could flip kinds=["promotion"]/enabled on organizer B's connection row (plus an existence info-leak). Fresh-context review caught it; the deterministic test suite did NOT — single-tenant fixtures never exercise the shared-id collision.

**How to apply:** For any view/guard that loads a row to read or mutate, name the identifier it keys on and ask "can two different tenants legitimately carry the same value here?" If yes (any EXTERNAL/platform id, not a local PK), the lookup MUST carry the owner/tenant filter — never trust the id alone. Add a CROSS-TENANT test: two tenants, same external id, assert tenant A's crafted request cannot touch tenant B's row (single-tenant fixtures structurally cannot catch this). Sibling to the visibility-default traps [[auto-created-records-reachable-default]] / [[data-migration-backfill-default-regresses-prior-visibility]] — those are render-floor defaults; this is the authorization-scope axis.
